Πολλοί από εμάς, στα νιάτα μας, έχουμε φανταστεί τον ιδανικό γάμο. Έχουμε οραματιστεί να είμαστε παντρεμένοι με κάποιον που μας αγαπά άνευ όρων και δέχεται με χαρά κάθε ιδιορρυθμία μας. Στην Εφεσίους 5:22-33 βρίσκουμε έναν τέτοιο γάμο. Εδώ ο απόστολος Παύλος συγκρίνει τη σχέση του συζύγου με τη σύζυγο με την οικεία σχέση του Ιησού Χριστού με τη νύφη Του, την Εκκλησία. Μεταβαίνει τόσο εύκολα από τη σχέση του συζύγου και της συζύγου στη σχέση του Χριστού και της νύφης Του, ώστε μένουμε να αναρωτιόμαστε ποια από τις δύο είχε ως κύριο θέμα του. Στο εδάφιο 22, συμβουλεύει τις γυναίκες να …υποτάσσεστε στους δικούς σας άντρες, όπως στον Κύριο. Έπειτα, στο εδάφιο 25, συμβουλεύει τους άντρες να …αγαπάτε τις γυναίκες σας, όπως και ο Χριστός αγάπησε την εκκλησία….

Ο Παύλος συνοψίζει αυτό το απόσπασμα δηλώνοντας: Αυτό το μυστήριο είναι μεγάλο· εγώ όμως μιλάω για τον Χριστό και την εκκλησία. –Εφεσ. 5:32. Αυτός ο εντυπωσιακός παραλληλισμός μάς οδηγεί να πιστεύουμε ότι ο γάμος προορίζεται να αντανακλά πλήρως την έντονη, αυτοθυσιαστική σχέση που έδειξε ο Χριστός, όταν εξασφάλισε μια νύφη για τον εαυτό Του. Αυτή η εικόνα είναι τόσο ισχυρή, ώστε μπορούμε μόνο να πιστεύουμε ότι από τον καιρό της δημιουργίας ο Θεός σχεδίασε τον γάμο να αντανακλά την παθιασμένη αγάπη Του για εμάς.

Ο Παύλος έγραψε: Οι άντρες, αγαπάτε τις γυναίκες σας, όπως και ο Χριστός αγάπησε την εκκλησία και παρέδωσε τον εαυτό του γι’ αυτήν· –Εφεσ. 5:25. Καθώς παρατηρούμε τη ζωή του Ιησού κατά τη σύντομη παραμονή Του εδώ στη γη, δεν βλέπουμε παρά αυτοθυσία για το καλό των άλλων. Δεν βρίσκουμε ούτε ίχνος ιδιοτέλειας. Αυτή η ανιδιοτελής παράδοση της ζωής Του είναι που κάνει το Ευαγγέλιο τόσο δυναμικά ελκυστικό για τόσο πολλούς.

Στη Β΄ Κορ. 5:14, ο Παύλος έγραψε: Επειδή, η αγάπη του Χριστού μάς συσφίγγει…. Αυτή είναι η φύση του Ευαγγελίου. Η μεγάλη αγάπη του Χριστού για εμάς μάς παρακινεί να Τον αγαπήσουμε κι εμείς. Αυτή η αμοιβαία αγάπη οδηγεί σε μια ζωή αφοσιωμένης υπηρεσίας, την οποία μερικές φορές αποκαλούμε υπακοή. Αν εσύ, ως σύζυγος, επιθυμείς μια γυναίκα που να χαίρεται να σε υπηρετεί αφοσιωμένα, μάθε να αγαπάς όπως αγάπησε ο Χριστός.

I. Ο Χριστός αγάπησε με «θυσιαστική αγάπη»

Το δεύτερο κεφάλαιο της προς Φιλιππησίους επιστολής αποκαλείται μερικές φορές η «μεγάλη κένωση» του Χριστού. Η ελληνική λέξη κενόω που βρίσκεται στο εδάφιο επτά (αλλά κένωσε τον εαυτό του), σημαίνει «αδειάζω». Ερχόμενος στη γη, ο Ιησούς άφησε κατά μέρος τη θέση Του κοντά στον Πατέρα και εισήλθε στη ζωή στον πλανήτη Γη μέσω μιας αμφισβητήσιμης σύλληψης (από ανθρώπινη σκοπιά), ως γιος μιας ταπεινής, παρθένας, χωριατοπούλας. Αυτή ήταν η υπόληψη που επέλεξε να έχει. Επέλεξε να ταυτιστεί με την πεσμένη ανθρωπότητα, παρότι είχε κάθε δικαίωμα να αξιώσει ισότητα με τον Θεό.

Στον κήπο της Γεθσημανή, ο Ιησούς έδειξε «θυσιαστική αγάπη» όταν …προσευχήθηκε, λέγοντας: Πατέρα μου, αν είναι δυνατόν, ας παρέλθει από μένα αυτό το ποτήρι· όμως, όχι όπως θέλω εγώ, αλλά όπως εσύ. –Ματθ. 26:39. Με τη ζωή Του και τον θυσιαστικό θάνατό Του, μας έδειξε ότι η οικειότητα στη σχέση μπορεί να βρεθεί μόνο όταν χάσουμε τον εαυτό μας μέσα σε αυτή τη σχέση. Η μεγάλη μάστιγα της εποχής μας είναι η φιλαυτία και η αυτοαπορρόφηση. Ο Παύλος έγραψε στον Τιμόθεο: …ότι στις έσχατες ημέρες θα έρθουν καιροί δύσκολοι. Επειδή, οι άνθρωποι θα είναι φίλαυτοι… –Β΄ Τιμ. 3:1-2

Βλέπουμε αυτή την προφητεία να εκπληρώνεται με την εμφάνιση των μέσων κοινωνικής δικτύωσης. Ενώ ισχυρίζονται πως είναι μια πλατφόρμα όπου οι άνθρωποι μπορούν να συνδεθούν, στην πραγματικότητα είναι μια πλατφόρμα για την προβολή του εαυτού. Αυτή η εμμονή με τον εαυτό είναι «επικίνδυνη», επειδή στρέφεται ενάντια στην οικειότητα μέσα στη σχέση και μπορεί να αποβεί μοιραία για τον γάμο. Η οικειότητα στον γάμο προϋποθέτει δύο ανθρώπους πρόθυμους να εγκαταλείψουν την προσωπική τους ταυτότητα και να υιοθετήσουν μια νέα κοινή ταυτότητα.

II. Ο Χριστός αγάπησε με «πιστή αγάπη»

Και πριν από τη γιορτή του Πάσχα, επειδή ο Ιησούς ήξερε ότι ήρθε η ώρα Του να αναχωρήσει από αυτόν τον κόσμο προς τον Πατέρα, έχοντας αγαπήσει τους δικούς Του που ήταν μέσα στον κόσμο, τους αγάπησε μέχρι τέλους. –Ιωάν. 13:1. Ο Χριστός έδειξε πιστή αγάπη, ακόμη και απέναντι στην απόρριψη. Ο Ιωάννης έγραψε ότι Ήρθε στους δικούς του, και οι δικοί του δεν τον δέχτηκαν. –Ιωάν. 1:11

Ο Ματθαίος έγραψε: Και όλο αυτό έγινε, για να εκπληρωθούν οι γραφές των προφητών. Τότε, όλοι οι μαθητές τον άφησαν και έφυγαν. –Ματθ. 26:56. Είναι ένα πράγμα να αγαπάμε εκείνους που μας αγαπούν κι εκείνοι. Ο Ιησούς είπε ότι ακόμη και οι τελώνες κάνουν τόσο. Ο Ιησούς έδειξε αγάπη σε όσους Τον μισούσαν, σε όσους Τον πρόδωσαν, σε όσους Τον αρνήθηκαν, και προσευχήθηκε ακόμη και για εκείνους που Τον σταύρωσαν. Η αγάπη Του στηριζόταν σε μια δέσμευση διαθήκης. Ήταν …το Αρνίο το σφαγμένο από καταβολής κόσμου. –Αποκ. 13:8. Δεν άφησε τίποτε να Τον αποτρέψει από τον αιώνιο σκοπό Του.

Η κοινωνία μας έχει χάσει την κατανόηση της διαθήκης· γι’ αυτό έχουμε τόσους διαλυμένους γάμους. Ακόμη και πολλές εκκλησίες που ασπάζονται τη «θεολογία της διαθήκης» όσον αφορά τη σωτηρία, δεν εφαρμόζουν αυτές τις ίδιες αρχές της διαθήκης στον γάμο. Ο Μαλαχίας δηλώνει ξεκάθαρα ότι ο γάμος είναι διαθήκη—…κι όμως αυτή είναι η σύντροφός σου και η γυναίκα της διαθήκης σου. –Μαλ. 2:14. Η αγάπη της βιβλικής διαθήκης είναι αγάπη που διαρκεί, είτε ανταποδίδεται είτε όχι.

Η πιο δραματική αποκάλυψη της αγάπης της διαθήκης βρίσκεται στους Προφήτες. Το μήνυμα των προφητών είναι κυρίως εκείνο ενός παθιασμένου εραστή, του «Θεού», που καλεί την άπιστη σύζυγό Του, τον «Ισραήλ», να επιστρέψει σ’ Αυτόν—…επιστρέψτε, επιστρέψτε από τους πονηρούς δρόμους σας· επειδή, γιατί να πεθάνετε, οίκος Ισραήλ; –Ιεζ. 33:11. Ο Ησαΐας έγραψε: Ζητήστε τον Κύριο, ενώ μπορεί να βρεθεί· επικαλεστείτε τον, ενώ είναι κοντά. Ας εγκαταλείψει ο ασεβής τον δρόμο του, και ο άδικος τις σκέψεις του· και ας επιστρέψει στον Κύριο, και θα τον ελεήσει· και στον Θεό μας, επειδή θα συγχωρήσει άφθονα. –Ησ. 55:6-7

Παρότι ο Ισραήλ επαναστάτησε ενάντια στον Κύριο ξανά και ξανά, βλέπουμε την αγάπη του Θεού προς αυτόν σταθερή και αμετάβλητη. Ο Θεός έμεινε πιστός στην υπόσχεση της διαθήκης Του, παρόλο που η νύφη Του γονάτισε μπροστά σε ειδωλολατρικούς βωμούς. Αυτή η ιδιότητα της πιστής αγάπης της διαθήκης έφερε τον Λυτρωτή. Ο Θεός έδωσε μια υπόσχεση στον κήπο της Εδέμ—Και θα βάλω έχθρα ανάμεσα σε σένα και στη γυναίκα, και ανάμεσα στο σπέρμα σου και στο σπέρμα της· αυτό θα σου συντρίψει το κεφάλι, κι εσύ θα του πληγώσεις τη φτέρνα. –Γεν. 3:15. Αυτή η υπόσχεση εκπληρώθηκε στον Χριστό περίπου τέσσερις χιλιάδες χρόνια αργότερα.

Την ημέρα του γάμου μας υποσχόμαστε να αγαπάμε «μέχρι να μας χωρίσει ο θάνατος». Αυτή είναι μια υπόσχεση που δίνεται με πίστη. Κανείς δεν μπορεί να γνωρίζει την ημέρα του γάμου του τι μπορεί να κοστίσει αυτή η υπόσχεση μέσα σε μια ολόκληρη ζωή. Το κόστος είναι άσχετο με τη δέσμευση, αν υπάρχει μια σταθερή, διαρκής αγάπη, ριζωμένη στην αιώνια πιστότητα του Θεού, με Εκείνον ως μάρτυρά μας.

III. Η αγάπη του Χριστού αγκάλιασε τα παθήματα

Ένα χαρακτηριστικό της γενιάς μας, που είναι προσηλωμένη στον εαυτό της, είναι η ιδέα ότι δεν θα έπρεπε να χρειάζεται να υποφέρω μέσα σε μια σχέση. Αυτό είναι προϊόν της ηδονιστικής κοινωνίας μας, που επιδιώκει την ευχαρίστηση. Η νοοτροπία αυτή εισχωρεί στην αναβαπτιστική κουλτούρα μας καθώς γινόμαστε ολοένα πιο εύποροι και οι διαχωριστικές γραμμές ανάμεσα σε εμάς και τον κόσμο γίνονται ολοένα πιο δυσδιάκριτες. Το αποτέλεσμα αυτής της νοοτροπίας είναι ότι νέοι άνθρωποι μπαίνουν στον γάμο σκεπτόμενοι: «ο σύντροφός μου θα με υπηρετεί, κι εγώ θα μπορώ να ζω σαν πρίγκιπας ή πριγκίπισσα».

Η αναβαπτιστική πίστη και κληρονομιά μας διατηρήθηκε μέχρι τις μέρες μας από άντρες και γυναίκες που καταλάβαιναν ότι η σχέση με τον Χριστό συνεπάγεται να σηκώνουμε σταυρό. Υπάρχουν πολλές ιστορίες οικογενειών που εγκατέλειψαν την πατρίδα τους και όλα όσα είχαν για χάρη του Ευαγγελίου.

Η έννοια του να αγκαλιάζει κανείς τα παθήματα μέσα στη σχέση διδάσκεται ξεκάθαρα στην επιστολή του Πέτρου. Ο Πέτρος έγραφε σε μια εκκλησία που υπέμενε τη μανιασμένη πυρά του διωγμού. Την παρότρυνε να συλλογιστεί το παράδειγμα του Χριστού, που υπέφερε για έναν σκοπό πέρα από τον εαυτό Του. Αφού, λοιπόν, ο Χριστός έπαθε για μας κατά τη σάρκα, οπλιστείτε κι εσείς με το ίδιο φρόνημα… –Α΄ Πέτρ. 4:1. Στο δεύτερο κεφάλαιο, ο Πέτρος γράφει: Επειδή, αυτό είναι ευάρεστο, αν κάποιος υποφέρει λύπες, πάσχοντας άδικα για συνείδηση προς τον Θεό. –Α΄ Πέτρ. 2:19. Λίγα εδάφια παρακάτω δηλώνει: Επειδή, σ’ αυτό κληθήκατε· δεδομένου ότι και ο Χριστός έπαθε για μας, αφήνοντάς μας υπόδειγμα, για να ακολουθήσετε τα ίχνη του· –Α΄ Πέτρ. 2:21.

Αφού μας καλεί στο δεύτερο κεφάλαιο να είμαστε πρόθυμοι να μιμηθούμε το παράδειγμα του Χριστού στα παθήματα, ο Πέτρος προχωρά στο τρίτο κεφάλαιο λέγοντας: Παρόμοια και οι γυναίκες, να υποτάσσεστε στους δικούς σας άντρες· ώστε, αν μερικοί απειθούν στον λόγο, να κερδηθούν χωρίς τον λόγο με τη διαγωγή των γυναικών· καθώς θα παρατηρούν την αγνή διαγωγή σας με φόβο. –Α΄ Πέτρ. 3:1-2. Οι Χριστιανοί όλων των εποχών θεωρούσαν μεγάλη τιμή το να υποφέρουν κάνοντας το καλό. Μόνο τα τελευταία χρόνια άρχισε να θεωρείται «κακοποίηση» το να υποφέρει κανείς κάνοντας το καλό. Υπάρχουν τουλάχιστον τρεις δυνάμεις που διαμορφώνουν αρνητικά την αντίληψή μας για τα παθήματα.

1. Μια εγωιστική κοινωνία που επιδιώκει την ευχαρίστηση

Η πρώτη έχει ήδη περιγραφεί παραπάνω: πρόκειται για την ηδονιστική κοινωνία (την αφοσίωση στην ευχαρίστηση ως τρόπο ζωής) μέσα στην οποία ζούμε.

2. Το ευαγγέλιο της υγείας, του πλούτου και της ευημερίας

Η δεύτερη είναι το ευαγγέλιο της υγείας, του πλούτου και της ευημερίας που κηρύττουν πολλές ευαγγελικές εκκλησίες. Υπονοείται ότι, αν επιλέξουμε να ακολουθήσουμε τον Χριστό, η ζωή μας θα ξεχειλίζει από σωματική ευεξία και υλική αφθονία. Αυτή η αντίληψη βασίζεται στις υποσχέσεις προς τον αρχαίο Ισραήλ στην Παλαιά Διαθήκη για μια γη που έρρεε γάλα και μέλι. Πιστεύουμε ότι η υπόσχεση αυτή εκπληρώνεται στην εποχή της εκκλησίας με μια ζωή που ξεχειλίζει από τον καρπό του Πνεύματος: αγάπη, χαρά, ειρήνη κ.λπ. Είναι δυνατόν αυτοί οι καρποί να αφθονούν μέσα στα παθήματα. Μάλιστα, όταν οι άλλοι βλέπουν καρπό μέσα στα παθήματα κάποιου, τότε αυτός γίνεται περισσότερο αισθητός και εκτιμάται περισσότερο.

3. Το φεμινιστικό κίνημα

Η τρίτη επιρροή που διαμορφώνει σήμερα την άποψή μας για τα παθήματα προέρχεται από το φεμινιστικό κίνημα, το οποίο διακηρύσσει με τόλμη ότι καμία γυναίκα δεν θα έπρεπε να υποφέρει ή να στερείται οτιδήποτε μέσα στον γάμο. Έτσι, έχουμε μια κοινωνία γυναικών με δική τους καριέρα, δικό τους μισθό και δικό τους τραπεζικό λογαριασμό. Πόσο διαφορετική είναι αυτή η εικόνα από τη μαρτυρία πιστών γυναικών όπως η Σάρρα, η οποία …υπάκουσε στον Αβραάμ, αποκαλώντας τον κύριό της· και της οποίας εσείς γίνατε θυγατέρες, εφόσον κάνετε το καλό και δεν φοβάστε κανέναν τρόμο. –Α΄ Πέτρ. 3:6

Τα παθήματα για χάρη της σχέσης ξεκίνησαν με τον Χριστό και μιμήθηκαν χιλιάδες πιστοί Χριστιανοί στη διάρκεια της εποχής της εκκλησίας. Τα λόγια του αποστόλου Πέτρου και η μαρτυρία πιστών Χριστιανών μάς καλούν να αγκαλιάσουμε τα παθήματα ως ένδειξη της γνησιότητας της πίστης μας.

IV. Ο Χριστός αγάπησε με αγάπη που αγιάζει

Το σχέδιο του Θεού όταν μας δημιούργησε ήταν να είμαστε άγιοι όπως είναι άγιος Εκείνος, ώστε να μπορούμε να απολαμβάνουμε στενή κοινωνία μαζί Του. Όμως η ανθρωπότητα επαναστάτησε εναντίον του Θεού, κι έτσι Εκείνος υποσχέθηκε έναν λυτρωτή. Στο μεταξύ, εισήγαγε ένα εφεδρικό σχέδιο, που είχε σκοπό να εμποδίσει την ανθρωπότητα να καταστρέψει τον εαυτό της, και αυτό ήταν «ο Νόμος».

Ωστόσο, ποτέ δεν ήταν πρόθεση του Θεού η σχέση μας μαζί Του να διέπεται από νόμο. Επιθυμεί να έχει μαζί μας μια σχέση αγάπης, γι’ αυτό έστειλε σε εμάς τον Υιό Του και μας κατέκλυσε με την αγάπη Του. Τώρα ανταποδίδουμε την αγάπη Του, όχι από φόβο για την κρίση, αλλά ως ανταπόκριση αγάπης στη δυνατή αγάπη Του. Αυτή η έννοια διατυπώνεται πιο ξεκάθαρα στην προς Ρωμαίους: Επειδή, εκείνο που ήταν αδύνατο στον νόμο, καθότι ήταν ασθενής διαμέσου της σάρκας [περιοριζόταν σε όσα μπορούσαν να επιτευχθούν με τη σάρκα], το έκανε ο Θεός, στέλνοντας τον δικό του Υιό με ομοίωμα σάρκας αμαρτίας και για χάρη της αμαρτίας, καταδίκασε την αμαρτία στη σάρκα [ικανοποίησε τις δίκαιες απαιτήσεις του νόμου]· ώστε το δικαίωμα του νόμου [η πλήρης και ολοκληρωμένη εκπλήρωση του νόμου] να εκπληρωθεί σε εμάς, που δεν περπατάμε σύμφωνα με τη σάρκα, αλλά σύμφωνα με το Πνεύμα. –Ρωμ. 8:3-4

Ο Ιησούς πέτυχε με την αγάπη ό,τι δεν θα μπορούσε ποτέ να επιτευχθεί με τις αυστηρές απαιτήσεις ενός ποινικού κώδικα. Ανύψωσε τον πήχη της δικαιοσύνης. Επειδή, σας λέω ότι, αν η δικαιοσύνη σας δεν περισσεύσει περισσότερο από τη δικαιοσύνη των γραμματέων και των Φαρισαίων, δεν θα μπείτε σε καμία περίπτωση μέσα στη βασιλεία των ουρανών. –Ματθ. 5:20. Μας έδειξε πώς να ζούμε και πώς να αγαπάμε. Ο θυσιαστικός θάνατός Του ικανοποίησε τις ποινικές απαιτήσεις του νόμου. Μέσω της ανάστασής Του, της ανάληψής Του και της έκχυσης του Αγίου Πνεύματος, έδωσε στους πιστούς τη δύναμη να ζουν και να αγαπούν όπως Εκείνος.

Ο Παύλος μάς συμβουλεύει να σχετιζόμαστε μέσα στον γάμο με τον ίδιο τρόπο: Οι άντρες, αγαπάτε τις γυναίκες σας, όπως και ο Χριστός αγάπησε την εκκλησία και παρέδωσε τον εαυτό του γι’ αυτήν· για να την αγιάσει και να την καθαρίσει με το λουτρό του νερού διαμέσου του λόγου· για να την παραστήσει στον εαυτό του ένδοξη εκκλησία, χωρίς να έχει κηλίδα ή ρυτίδα ή κάτι τέτοιο, αλλά να είναι αγία και χωρίς ψεγάδι. –Εφεσ. 5:27. Ο Ιησούς ήρθε στη γη για να εξασφαλίσει μια νύφη για τον εαυτό Του. Δεν ήταν μια όμορφη, λαμπερή νύφη που περίμενε με λαχτάρα τον ερχομό Του. Η αμαρτία την είχε παραμορφώσει και ζούσε σε ανταρσία εναντίον Του—Ήρθε στους δικούς του, και οι δικοί του δεν τον δέχτηκαν. –Ιωάν. 1:11. Με την υπομονετική, επίμονη αγάπη Του, μεταμόρφωσε τη νύφη Του σε μια ένδοξη, λαμπερή νύφη, που στέκεται με δέος μπροστά Του και Τον λατρεύει και Τον δοξάζει με χαρά.

Έχει η γυναίκα σου κηλίδες και ρυτίδες; Υπάρχουν κάποιες συμπεριφορές που θα ήθελες να ήταν διαφορετικές; Ή μήπως υπάρχουν φόβοι και ανασφάλειες που εμποδίζουν την ελευθερία και τη χαρά της; Θα μπορούσες να απαιτήσεις να αλλάξει και να την επιπλήττεις επειδή δεν ανταποκρίνεται στις προσδοκίες σου. Αυτή η προσέγγιση θα ήταν ανάλογη με εκείνη του νόμου. Θα μεγέθυνε τους περιορισμούς της και θα αύξανε τις ανησυχίες της. Ή θα μπορούσες να την αγαπάς παρά τις κηλίδες και τις ρυτίδες της. Με λόγια συμπόνιας και ενθάρρυνσης θα μπορούσες να την παρακινήσεις να ξεπεράσει τους φόβους της, όπως ακριβώς ο Χριστός αγιάζει τη νύφη Του με τον λόγο Του. Ο Ιησούς έδειξε ότι η αγάπη μπορεί να πετύχει όσα δεν μπορούν ποτέ να πετύχουν οι σκληρές απαιτήσεις. Ο Παύλος δίδαξε ότι αυτή είναι μια θεμελιώδης αρχή του γάμου. Προορίζεται να είναι μια σχέση στην οποία η κινητήρια δύναμη είναι η αγάπη.

V. Το μεγάλο μυστήριο

Ο Παύλος ολοκλήρωσε την πραγματεία του για τον γάμο λέγοντας: Αυτό το μυστήριο είναι μεγάλο· εγώ όμως μιλάω για τον Χριστό και την εκκλησία. –Εφεσ. 5:32. Στη βιβλική γλώσσα, μυστήριο δεν είναι κάτι που δεν μπορεί να γίνει κατανοητό, αλλά κάτι που μπορούν να καταλάβουν μόνο όσοι δέχονται και αγκαλιάζουν την Αλήθεια με πίστη. Αποκαλύπτεται στους ειλικρινείς Χριστιανούς· παραμένει καλυμμένο για τους άλλους.

Ως πιστοί στον Ιησού, έχουμε το προνόμιο να κατανοούμε μια οπτική του γάμου που πολλοί δεν μπορούν καν να αρχίσουν να συλλαμβάνουν: ότι η θυσιαστική αγάπη ανοίγει την πόρτα στην οικειότητα, ότι η αγάπη της διαθήκης είναι το κλειδί για μια ζωή μακρόχρονης πληρότητας, ότι η προθυμία μας να υποφέρουμε για τη σχέση αποδεικνύει τη γνησιότητα της αγάπης μας και, τέλος, ότι ο πιο αποτελεσματικός τρόπος να επισπεύσουμε την αλλαγή στον σύζυγό μας είναι η αγάπη άνευ όρων.

Αυτές οι αρχές έχουν αποδειχτεί στον χρόνο και βασίζονται στη Βίβλο. Είναι θεμελιώδεις για το Ευαγγέλιο και αποτελούν αναπόσπαστο μέρος της αναβαπτιστικής θεολογίας μας, που βασίζεται στη βασιλεία. Όταν εφαρμόζονται πιστά, θα μεταμορφώσουν κάθε γάμο.

Mile after mile sped by as Carol drove the old Chevy along the busy interstate highway toward home. Between intervals of silence and conversation, Carol and her two sisters, Elaine and Gloria, lifted their voices in song, giving thanks and praise to their Creator. How thankful they were for the opportunity to spend the evening with their friends at Pine Creek Church and to receive another inspiring message from God’s Word.

Suddenly their smooth travel was interrupted by signs of trouble. “Now what can be wrong with this car?” Carol worried out loud as she guided the stalled car to the side of the road. “Oh, no, girls, we’re out of gas! I was in such a hurry this evening that I forgot to check the gauge. I thought the tank was almost full when we left home, and… Oh no!” wailed Carol again. “Dad put the cell phone on the counter for me to take along, and I forgot that also!”

“Whatever are we going to do now?” exclaimed Elaine. “Here we are, stranded in the dark, no gas, no phone, and seven more miles to our exit! And another thing, people just don’t stop very quickly these days and offer help. They know that most everyone carries a phone. This seems almost impossible to me!” she mournfully uttered from the back seat.

As the girls lapsed into silence, the old Chevy seemed to shake in protest as a long row of trucks whizzed by. “You know,” said Gloria, “I was just remembering Brother Lester’s message this evening. How can we forget so quickly! Maybe God has allowed this to happen to us so our faith might be increased as we place our trust in Him. Let’s take this to the Lord in prayer. Let’s look for a miracle from God’s hand.”

Together the girls bowed their heads and pled for the Lord’s protection and help.

“You know, I feel better already,” smiled Elaine. “I was so worried and fearful, but since we prayed and committed everything to God, I have confidence that He will watch over us. I’m so glad we have a God who hears all of our cries. What would we do without His comforting Holy Spirit? Let’s sing again.”

“Joys are flowing like a river,
Since the Comforter has come;
He abides with us forever,
Makes the trusting heart His home.
Blessed quietness, holy quietness,
Blest assurance in my soul!
On the stormy sea Jesus speaks to me,
And the billows cease to roll!”

-Manie P. Ferguson, 19th century

As the girls sang song after song, their hearts were deeply stirred. How quiet and peaceful they felt, even though they were stranded on a dark highway thirteen miles from home. Car after car, and truck after truck sped by without stopping. Then they noticed a pickup truck, with two dirt bikes on the back, slowing down. It pulled off the road several hundred feet ahead of them, and slowly began to back up. The girls’ voices were stilled in silence as they desperately cried out to God from the bottom of their hearts. When the truck came to a halt, two husky, long-haired men jumped out. Carol rolled her window down as a man wearing a red-checked flannel jacket approached.

“What’s the trouble here, girls?” he asked, glancing over the car.

“We’re out of gas,” Carol quickly replied.

“Well, I’d say we’re pretty lucky. We have a can of gas with us. How far do you need to go yet?”

“About thirteen miles.”

“Good. We’ll just pour some of our gas into your tank and you can be on your way again. No payment necessary.”

“O thank you so much,” responded Carol. “We were praying that God would send us help, and He did more than we could ever have thought! Thanks so much.”

“Yes, yes”, replied the man gruffly, “You’re pretty lucky we came along. We’re just glad to help you out.”

Several minutes later, the girls were on their way again. “You know,” said Carol, “when I saw that truck pull over, I was scared and glad at the same time. I began to scold myself again for not having that cell phone with me. But then I asked God to help me completely trust in Him and not be afraid. After all, isn’t He much more dependable than any cell phone? This has been such a faith booster for me. How different this may have turned out, if we had depended solely on our cell phones or “good luck” as those men called it. It must grieve our Father’s heart tremendously when we do not place our trust in Him.”

“It’s just as Brother Lester preached this evening”, added Gloria. “Remember some of those verses? I waited patiently for the LORD; and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry … And he hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God… Blessed is that man that maketh the LORD his trust, and respecteth not the proud, nor such as turn aside to lies. –Psa 40:1-4. This makes me so happy I just want to keep singing and thanking the Lord!”

Again, the girls raised their voices in song:

“His eye is always watching,
His ear is keen to hear;
His love is all-sufficient
To calm the gravest fear.
Then trust Him in shine and shade;
Trust Him, be not afraid:
He’s walking close beside thee;
His hand will safely guide thee;
His wings securely hide thee;
Then trust! Be not afraid.”

-Charles H. Gabriel, 1856-1932

캐럴이 낡은 쉐보레를 몰고 붐비는 고속도로를 따라 집으로 향하는 동안, 수많은 마일이 빠르게 지나갔습니다. 침묵과 대화가 번갈아 이어지는 가운데, 캐럴과 두 자매 일레인과 글로리아는 목소리를 높여 노래하며 창조주께 감사와 찬양을 드렸습니다. 파인 크리크 교회에서 친구들과 저녁 시간을 보내고, 하나님의 말씀에서 또 한 편의 감동적인 메시지를 들을 기회를 얻은 것이 얼마나 감사한 일이었는지요.

갑자기 순조로운 여정에 문제가 생겼다는 징후가 나타났습니다. “이 차에 대체 무슨 문제가 생긴 거지?” 캐럴은 걱정스러운 듯 소리 내어 말하며 멈춰 선 차를 도로 가장자리로 몰았습니다. “아, 안 돼, 얘들아, 기름이 떨어졌어! 오늘 저녁에 너무 서두르느라 연료 게이지를 확인하는 걸 잊었어. 집을 나설 때 탱크가 거의 가득 찼다고 생각했는데, 그리고… 아, 안 돼!” 캐럴이 다시 탄식했습니다. “아빠가 내가 가져가도록 휴대전화를 조리대 위에 놓아두셨는데, 그것도 깜빡했어!”

“이제 대체 어떻게 해야 하지?” 일레인이 외쳤습니다. “우리는 어두운 곳에 꼼짝없이 갇혀 있고, 기름도 없고, 전화도 없는데, 출구까지는 7마일이나 더 남았어! 게다가 요즘 사람들은 멈춰서 도와주겠다고 나서질 않아. 다들 거의 누구나 휴대전화를 가지고 있다고 생각하니까. 난 이게 도무지 믿기지 않아!” 그녀는 뒷좌석에서 슬픈 목소리로 말했습니다.

소녀들이 말없이 조용해지자, 낡은 쉐보레는 긴 줄을 이룬 트럭들이 쌩쌩 지나가는 데 항의라도 하듯 흔들리는 것 같았습니다. “있잖아,” 글로리아가 말했습니다. “오늘 저녁 레스터 형제님의 설교가 생각났어. 우리가 어떻게 그렇게 빨리 잊을 수 있을까! 어쩌면 하나님께서는 우리가 그분을 신뢰할 때 믿음이 자라도록 이런 일이 일어나게 하셨는지도 몰라. 주님께 기도로 아뢰자. 하나님께서 베푸실 기적을 기대하자.”

소녀들은 함께 고개를 숙이고 주님의 보호와 도움을 간구했습니다.

“있잖아, 벌써 마음이 한결 나아졌어.” 일레인이 미소 지었습니다. “아까는 너무 걱정되고 두려웠지만, 기도하고 모든 일을 하나님께 맡긴 뒤로는 그분이 우리를 지켜 주실 거라는 확신이 들어. 우리의 모든 부르짖음을 들으시는 하나님이 계시다니 정말 기뻐. 그분의 위로하시는 성령님이 안 계셨다면 우리는 어떻게 했을까? 다시 노래하자.”

“위로자 오신 뒤로
기쁨 강물처럼 흘러넘치네;
그분은 우리와 영원히 함께하시며,
신뢰하는 마음을 거처로 삼으시네.
복된 고요함, 거룩한 고요함,
내 영혼에 복된 확신을 주시네!
폭풍 치는 바다에서 예수님이 내게 말씀하시니,
파도가 더는 일렁이지 않네!”

-매니 P. 퍼거슨, 19세기

소녀들은 노래를 거듭 부르며 마음이 깊이 감동되었습니다. 집에서 13마일 떨어진 어두운 고속도로에 발이 묶였는데도, 마음이 얼마나 고요하고 평안한지요. 승용차도 트럭도 한 대 한 대 쌩쌩 지나갔지만 멈추지 않았습니다. 그러다 흙길용 오토바이 두 대를 뒤에 실은 픽업트럭 한 대가 속도를 늦추는 것이 보였습니다. 그 트럭은 수백 피트 앞에서 도로를 벗어나더니 천천히 후진하기 시작했습니다. 소녀들은 목소리를 멈추고 마음 깊은 곳에서 하나님께 간절히 부르짖었습니다. 트럭이 멈춰 서자 건장하고 머리가 긴 남자 두 명이 뛰어내렸습니다. 빨간 체크무늬 플란넬 재킷을 입은 남자가 다가오자 캐럴은 창문을 내렸습니다.

“얘들아, 무슨 일이야?” 그가 차를 살피며 물었습니다.

“기름이 떨어졌어요.” 캐럴이 재빨리 대답했습니다.

“그럼 우리가 꽤 운이 좋다고 해야겠네. 우리에게 기름통이 있거든. 아직 얼마나 더 가야 하지?”

“약 13마일이요.”

“좋아. 우리 기름을 탱크에 좀 부어 줄 테니 다시 가면 되겠네. 돈은 안 내도 돼.”

“정말 정말 고맙습니다.” 캐럴이 대답했습니다. “하나님께 도와 달라고 기도했는데, 하나님은 우리가 상상한 것보다 훨씬 더 큰 도움을 보내 주셨어요! 정말 감사합니다.”

“그래, 그래.” 남자가 퉁명스럽게 대답했습니다. “우리가 지나가서 정말 운이 좋았지. 도와줄 수 있어서 기쁘네.”

몇 분 뒤, 소녀들은 다시 길을 나섰습니다. “있잖아,” 캐럴이 말했습니다. “그 트럭이 길가에 멈추는 걸 봤을 때 무섭기도 하고 기쁘기도 했어. 휴대전화를 가지고 오지 않은 걸 또 자책하기 시작했지. 하지만 그때 하나님께 온전히 그분을 신뢰하고 두려워하지 않도록 도와 달라고 기도했어. 어쨌든 그분이 어떤 휴대전화보다 훨씬 더 믿을 만하시지 않겠어? 이번 일은 내 믿음을 정말 크게 북돋아 줬어. 우리가 휴대전화나 그 남자들이 말한 ‘운’만 믿었다면 얼마나 다른 결과가 되었을지 몰라. 우리가 하나님을 신뢰하지 않을 때 우리 아버지의 마음이 얼마나 크게 아프실까.”

“오늘 저녁 레스터 형제님이 설교하신 내용이 바로 그거야.” 글로리아가 덧붙였습니다. “그 구절들 기억나? 내가 여호와를 간절히 기다렸더니 그가 내게 몸을 굽히사 나의 부르짖음을 들으셨도다… 새 노래 곧 우리 하나님께 올릴 찬송을 내 입에 두셨도다… 여호와를 신뢰하며 교만한 자와 거짓에 치우치는 자들을 따르지 아니하는 자는 복이 있도다. –시편 40:1-4. 이 말씀을 생각하면 너무 기뻐서 계속 노래하고 주님께 감사하고 싶어!”

소녀들은 다시 목소리를 높여 노래했습니다.

“그분의 눈은 늘 지켜보시고,
그분의 귀는 귀 기울여 들으시네;
그분의 사랑은 넉넉하여
가장 큰 두려움도 가라앉히네.
그러니 햇빛 속에서도 그늘 속에서도 그분을 신뢰하라;
그분을 신뢰하고 두려워하지 말라:
그분은 네 곁에 가까이 걸으시며;
그 손이 안전하게 너를 인도하시리라;
그 날개가 안전하게 너를 감싸시리라;
그러니 신뢰하라! 두려워하지 말라.”

-찰스 H. 가브리엘, 1856-1932

The cold, grey days of winter are being transformed into the warm, sunny days of spring. The first flowers of the year are persistently pushing their way up out of the cold earth towards the warmth of the sun. It never seems to get old—this exciting feeling in the springtime air. There’s the warmth and light of sunny days. There’s the cheery, lilting music of the song birds as they once more take up housekeeping with seemingly boundless energy. And we are again blessed with another season to plant seeds with the expectation of another crop of food to enjoy.

This year I will turn 48 years of age. My how that sounds old to me. I remember that as a youth I thought that folks who were 50 were old. Now I am almost there. For me, this is a clear reminder that we all are getting older and that we will not live forever. Next, comes a number of sobering thoughts: “What have I done for the furtherance of God’s Kingdom? Am I remaining faithful to Him in all that I do? Lord, what wilt thou have me to do—this year?” Let’s, each one, prayerfully seek the Lord about His present and future will for our lives. Let’s encourage and exhort each other to remain faithful in relationship with, and in service for, our Master.

In this issue we have an excellent article on marriage, which we felt can take the place of an article on Discipleship this time. When we meet with couples who have struggled with extreme marriage problems for years, we usually find that something is not working in a godly way at a foundational level. We feel that this marriage article is quite thorough in its evaluation of building and maintaining a Biblical foundation. Lord willing, we plan to have ongoing articles relating to this subject.

Die kalten, grauen Wintertage verwandeln sich in die warmen, sonnigen Frühlingstage. Die ersten Blumen des Jahres bahnen sich unermüdlich ihren Weg aus der kalten Erde hinauf zur Wärme der Sonne. Dieses aufregende Gefühl in der Frühlingsluft scheint nie alt zu werden. Da sind die Wärme und das Licht sonniger Tage. Da ist die fröhliche, beschwingte Musik der Singvögel, die sich wieder mit scheinbar grenzenloser Energie häuslich niederlassen. Und uns ist erneut eine Jahreszeit geschenkt, in der wir Samen säen können, in der Erwartung einer weiteren Ernte von Lebensmitteln, die wir genießen dürfen.

Dieses Jahr werde ich 48 Jahre alt. Meine Güte, das klingt für mich alt. Ich erinnere mich, dass ich als Jugendlicher dachte, Leute mit 50 seien alt. Jetzt bin ich fast so weit. Für mich ist das eine deutliche Erinnerung daran, dass wir alle älter werden und nicht ewig leben werden. Dann folgen einige ernste Gedanken: „Was habe ich zur Förderung des Reiches Gottes getan? Bin ich Ihm in allem, was ich tue, treu? Herr, was willst Du, dass ich dieses Jahr tue?“ Lasst uns alle im Gebet den Herrn um Klarheit über Seinen gegenwärtigen und zukünftigen Willen für unser Leben bitten. Lasst uns einander ermutigen und ermahnen, in der Beziehung zu unserem Meister und im Dienst für Ihn treu zu bleiben.

In dieser Ausgabe haben wir einen ausgezeichneten Artikel über die Ehe, von dem wir fanden, dass er dieses Mal an die Stelle eines Artikels über Jüngerschaft treten kann. Wenn wir Paare treffen, die seit Jahren mit extremen Eheproblemen zu kämpfen haben, stellen wir gewöhnlich fest, dass auf grundlegender Ebene etwas nicht auf gottgemäße Weise funktioniert. Wir sind der Meinung, dass dieser Artikel über die Ehe die Errichtung und Bewahrung eines biblischen Fundaments sehr gründlich untersucht. So der Herr will, planen wir weitere Artikel zu diesem Thema.

As a man was dying, his thoughts went back.
Will I leave a good mark, that none can attack?
I forsook all, on the alter I went
Keeping nothing back, not even a cent.
I wanted to do, all that was right.
I sometimes prayed, all through the night.
It was easy? I cannot say.
But rather a battle, I fought everyday.
Few understood why I lived this way.
Giving up everything was foolish they’d say.
They couldn’t have seen the peace inside.
A peace that I thought, no one could hide.
A life on the run, was not my desire.
But they wanted my body, to put in the fire.
From cave to cave, I would call home
Knowing one day, I’d never more roam.
As I look back, I wouldn’t change a thing.
It has been a great honor serving my king.
But I must go now, the smoke is too thick.
My body to ashes, as the flames lick.
There is one thing, I need to ask.
Will I die in vain, or will you take up the task?
Jesus is looking for A people today
That will stand the test, and not go astray.
Giving our life is part of the cost.
Will you make that decision, before time is lost?
The church is struggling, the world has come in.
They killed our Jesus, and love their sin.
Let’s not give in, there’s too much at stake.
But rather let’s fight! There’s a kingdom to take!

–Barry Grant

And I sought for a man among them, that should make up the hedge, and stand in the gap before me for the land, that I should not destroy it: but I found none. –Ezekiel 22:30

The account of the little Dutch boy who heroically stuck his finger in the hole in the dike comes to mind as we consider such a verse. He couldn’t leave the spot for fear of erosion, so he waited the long night through until someone came along in the morning to rescue him from his plight. Many men have performed astounding feats on impulse when the moment so required. Lives were rescued, towns were saved, and enemies defeated because someone filled a role that was needed. Books are written, and monuments erected in honor of those whose benefaction has touched us. These are considered the heroes of history and they are remembered for their staunch bravery and steadfast faithfulness.

But the gaps in life are not always so obvious and the results not always measurable. Solomon informs us of the account of …a little city, and few men within it; and there came a great king against it, and besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it: Now there was found in it a poor wise man, and he by his wisdom delivered the city; yet no man remembered that same poor man. –Ecc 9:14-15. Though we have many thorough descriptions in the Bible of pious men who stood in the gap for God, there are, no doubt, hordes of others who overcame tremendous odds on a spiritual level yet received no recognition in this life.

The problem lies not so much in that, standing in the gap is beyond our capabilities or finances, but in the reality that often the job bears no title, ordination, or recognition. It is to be filled by volunteers with enough vision and care to sacrifice their own agenda for the sole cause of filling the hole in the hedge. It often does not lie within the realm of the physical, but within the borders of the spiritual. While the poor we have with us always and spiritual nobility will stoop to help them, we must consider that God probably has more in mind here than needing someone to organize bread lines and soup kitchens. He is looking for a man clad in a robe of “purple principles” that won’t be shed when the temperatures get hot.

King Darius signed the fateful degree that was designed to escort Daniel to a luncheon with the lions. Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime. –Dan 6:10. What a slight thing it would have been for Daniel to close the shutters before he prayed. But Daniel was not filling the gap by his presence in the high governmental position that he held. The gap lay in the dearth of godly witnesses in Babylon. Thus, the hole between heaven and earth was to be fulfilled by prayer at the open window while sacrificing his “seat in the senate.”

The underlying reason that so many gaps exist and there are so few men to fill them is because we often get our personal, earthly vision of circumstances confused with the eternal purposes of God. We are busily occupied with good things and feeling quite useful. Martha was zealously active in filling what she perceived as the imminent gap in the household, while Mary was sitting in the eternal one. It is incredibly easy to get caught up in the activity trap of a busy life. We may give intensive care to efficiently climb to the top of the ladder, only to discover that it is leaning against the wrong wall. Many people are very busy, but not very effective. Many have labored industriously for years in the Lord’s work, only to arrive at the finish line and realize that the things, which mattered most, had eluded them. Some, while giving their lives to serve others, allowed their marriage to suffer, or their children to disrespect them. Others have given “Corban” to their church while neglecting their relationship with their own parents.

The man in the gap must be wise, and wisdom must understand wherein the true gap lies. In this we must be driven by a purposed, biblical vision. Life will afford many opportunities to abandon our course. If we actively seek to live the expectations handed to us by our family, friends, associates, church agendas, and life’s circumstances, we will be driven by people rather than biblical principles. While this may seem legitimate on the surface, we may reap the bitter disappointment of finding ourselves dangling at the end of the wrong rope.

So, what does the gap of God’s concern look like? Some would say that this gap consists where any need arises. The poor we have with us always and certainly herein is an opportunity to do good. But the better part chosen by Mary had nothing to do with helping the poor or feeding the hungry. Likewise, the woman with the precious alabaster box of ointment of spikenard could have sold it and supplied the poor for quite a while with the sum of its value. But the real gap could not be filled by caressing the cripple, but by crowning the Christ. In the Garden of Eden there was no gap, for man walked in perfect harmony with his Creator. It was sin that created the gap and rankled the relationship. Also, there will be no breach at the end of time when the Lamb receives His bride. Until then, we have a large gap that exists because this earth refuses to glorify its Creator. To stand in that gap must be the chief purpose of all who aspire to bear His name.

This calls for a complete transformation in relationship to our God. The atonement of Christ’s blood makes it judicially possible. The comfort of the Holy Spirit makes it emotionally satisfying, but it is in the realm of our surrender and glorification of God that animates the scene. The Prodigal Son is a prime example of a soul who had brought a world of trouble upon himself by forsaking the position that he held as a son of his father. At the bottom of his restoration was nothing more than a re-establishing of the father-son relationship which had existed from his birth.

It appears to me that God is not so much looking for souls with their hands waving in the air shouting, “Here am I send me!” Rather His eyes search for the humble souls who bow their wills before the Almighty and recognize Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created. –Revelation 4:11. There is no lack for Sons of Sceva who imagine they are filling an important role in their willingness to broadcast the “Jesus” that they have heard of. In 1997, some 800,000 men arrived at a Promise Keepers rally in Washington D.C in response to the theme of “Standing in the Gap.” These men may have had good intentions of representing God to a nation in swift departure from spiritual underpinnings, but it takes more than just a willing heart. God doesn’t need of a large mass of bodies to stuff into a hole. He is looking for qualified men, and few have been promoted to such a position.

If all God wanted was men to show up at a rally or publicly proclaim their faith on the streets, He, no doubt, could have found many desiring such a good work. But to stand in the gap between God and the world will only be sanctioned by God for those who deserve to be there. It is the universal pride of man that drives man to believe that he must only desire to be useful and then he will be used. In God’s house there are some vessels to honor and some to dishonor, yet to deserve an honorable place is much more difficult than to desire one.

It is very common in our day to receive mail bearing the message, “Get the credit you deserve.” It is no secret that the credit that many deserve is zero credit. But we have all been impacted by the subliminal message that everybody deserves credit. Our society is promoting that all immoral, imprudent, and improvident people deserve the same care as the moral and industrious. If the slothful individual deserves a good wage and the spendthrift deserves financial security, then the Apostle Paul certainly has no right to lay any qualifications upon the widows who should receive support from the church. Neither has he any right to reject any sincere soul who desires the office of a Bishop, just because he does not meet the qualifications. But God noticed a few souls …in Sardis which have not defiled their garments; and they shall walk with me in white: for they are worthy. –Rev 3:4

These are men in the gap. Not because they had energy to burn, but because they had a vision for purity. This was no mere accident, for men who wish to attain to preeminence with God must do it by…

…Purpose

By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter; Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season; Esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt: for he had respect unto the recompence of the reward. By faith he forsook Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king: for he endured, as seeing him who is invisible. –Heb 11:24-27

A true vision for the work of God will come with a price tag. The rich young ruler would have loved to be a ruler in the kingdom of Christ as well as on his estate, but he couldn’t hold both. This principle provided the first hurdle for him and for everyone else who would desire such a noble work. As a young man, Moses made his decision and chose his loyalties. He was prepared to be rejected by Egypt, but he never dreamed he would also be so flippantly discarded by his own people.

It was forty years in the lonely furnace that purged his pride and pruned his prowess. There he graduated from the seminary of silence, equipped and prepared to stand in the gap as the meekest man on the face of the earth. He became an intercessor for men to God. As an advocate of men and of God, he preached and prayed, he walked and wept, he lived and loved his God and his brethren. All this while, he deemed himself inadequate for the position. While the children of Israel were at the very core of his heart, his fear and focus never left his God. When we seek to be respected by men, our purpose is clouded over and our position in the gap forfeited. Many good pastors, parents, and pilgrims have made this mistake and received their script from their wife, their children, their friends, or their church. Perhaps it seems like the loving, caring, and most respectful thing to do. But God requires absolute fidelity and there can be no compromise. What a man “wants to be” is driven by his visionary purpose, but what he “turns out to be” rests upon his…

…Priorities

This is a true saying, If a man desire the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work. A bishop then must be blameless, the husband of one wife, vigilant, sober, of good behaviour, given to hospitality, apt to teach; Not given to wine, no striker, not greedy of filthy lucre; but patient, not a brawler, not covetous; One that ruleth well his own house, having his children in subjection with all gravity; –1Ti 3:1-4. Our purpose forms our destination, but our priorities pave the road to get us there.

Unfortunately, some men are promoted to the ministry by popular opinion, but God chooses his men based upon their priorities and eternal qualifications. Men who are governed by their possessions, passions, or position will be useless to serve for God’s purpose. They love to be called Pastor, Reverend, or Father. They love to be esteemed as zealous, knowledgeable, steadfast, or compassionate. For am I now seeking the favor of men, or of God? Or am I striving to please men? If I were still pleasing men, I should not be a servant of Christ. –Gal 1:10 ASV

Fortunately, God is not a respecter of persons, and a stone fit for the wall will not be left in the way. The aged, the poor, the maimed, and the halt are all prime candidates for the position of filling the gap. Those with broken dreams, broken bodies, and broken hearts can stand unhindered in the hedge beside Noah, Abraham, Joseph, Moses, Daniel, Esther, Ruth and a countless battalion of others. These are all stellar representatives of God to this world. They all have turned their back on frivolity, fame, familiarity, and fortune and have become the heroes of heaven. They stand shoulder to shoulder in the hedge and form the “Embassy of the Eternal.” They loved, while others hated. They gave all, while others received. They were mocked and misunderstood, reviled and ridiculed, weary and weeping.

For we are unto God a sweet savour of Christ, in them that are saved, and in them that perish: To the one we are the savour of death unto death; and to the other the savour of life unto life. And who is sufficient for these things? –2 Co 2:15-16. Those whose sole purpose and priorities are governed by God.

내가 그들 가운데서 한 사람을 찾아 성벽을 쌓아 올리고, 이 땅을 위하여 내 앞에 무너진 틈에 서서 내가 그것을 멸하지 않게 할 자를 찾았으나, 찾지 못하였다. –에스겔 22:30

제방의 구멍에 손가락을 영웅적으로 집어넣었던 네덜란드 소년의 이야기는 이 구절을 생각할 때 떠오릅니다. 그는 물이 더 새어 나갈까 두려워 그 자리를 떠날 수 없었고, 아침에 누군가 와서 곤경에 빠진 자신을 구해 줄 때까지 긴 밤을 견뎠습니다. 많은 사람이 그 순간에 요구된 일을 충동적으로 해내며 놀라운 위업을 이룬 적이 있습니다. 누군가 필요한 역할을 맡았기에 생명이 구해지고, 마을이 보존되고, 적이 패배했습니다. 우리의 마음을 움직인 선행을 베푼 이들을 기리는 책이 쓰이고 기념비가 세워집니다. 이들은 역사의 영웅으로 여겨지며, 굳센 용기와 변함없는 신실함으로 기억됩니다.

그러나 삶의 틈이 언제나 그처럼 분명한 것은 아니며, 그 결과를 언제나 측정할 수 있는 것도 아닙니다. 솔로몬은 다음과 같은 이야기를 들려줍니다. …작은 성읍이 있고 그 안에 사람이 적은데, 큰 왕이 와서 그 성읍을 에워싸고 그에 대하여 큰 보루를 쌓았더라. 그 성읍 안에 가난하나 지혜로운 사람이 있어 그의 지혜로 성읍을 구하였으나, 그 가난한 사람을 기억하는 자가 없었더라. –전도서 9:14-15. 성경에는 하나님을 위해 무너진 틈에 섰던 경건한 사람들에 대한 상세한 기록이 많지만, 영적인 차원에서 엄청난 역경을 이겨 내고도 이 땅에서 아무런 인정을 받지 못한 이들이 그 밖에도 수없이 많았을 것입니다.

문제는 무너진 틈에 서는 일이 우리의 능력이나 재정 능력을 넘어서는 데 있다기보다, 그 일이 흔히 직함도, 안수도, 인정도 따르지 않는다는 현실에 있습니다. 그 일은 충분한 비전과 배려를 지닌 자원봉사자들이 자신의 계획을 희생하여 오직 성벽의 구멍을 메우는 일에 힘쓸 때 채워집니다. 그 일은 흔히 물질적인 영역이 아니라 영적인 영역에 속합니다. 가난한 이들은 언제나 우리와 함께 있고 영적으로 고귀한 이들은 그들을 돕기 위해 몸을 낮추겠지만, 하나님께서 여기서 생각하시는 일이 단지 누군가에게 배식 줄과 무료 급식소를 운영하게 하는 것보다 더 크다는 점을 생각해야 합니다. 하나님께서는 기온이 오르면 벗어 던질 “자주색 원칙”의 옷을 입지 않은 사람을 찾고 계십니다.

다리오 왕은 다니엘을 사자들과 함께 점심을 먹게 하려는 운명의 조서에 서명했습니다. 다니엘은 조서에 왕의 도장이 찍힌 것을 알고도 자기 집으로 들어갔으며, 그의 다락방 창문은 예루살렘을 향해 열려 있었다. 그는 전에 하던 대로 하루에 세 번 무릎을 꿇고 자기 하나님 앞에 기도하며 감사드렸다. –다니엘 6:10. 다니엘이 기도하기 전에 덧문을 닫았더라도 별일 아니었을 것입니다. 그러나 다니엘은 자신이 맡았던 높은 정부 직책에 있다는 사실만으로 무너진 틈을 메우고 있던 것이 아닙니다. 틈은 바빌론에 경건한 증인이 부족한 데 있었습니다. 그러므로 하늘과 땅 사이의 구멍은 열린 창가에서 기도하고 자신의 “원로원 의석”을 희생함으로써 메워야 했습니다.

그토록 많은 틈이 있고 이를 메울 사람이 그토록 적은 근본적인 이유는 우리가 개인적이고 세상적인 시각으로 상황을 바라보면서 하나님의 영원한 목적과 자주 혼동하기 때문입니다. 우리는 좋은 일에 분주히 몰두하며 자신이 꽤 쓸모 있다고 느낍니다. 마르다는 집안에 당장 생겼다고 생각한 빈자리를 채우느라 열심히 움직였지만, 마리아는 영원한 것에 자리를 잡고 있었습니다. 바쁜 삶의 활동이라는 덫에 빠지기는 놀라울 만큼 쉽습니다. 우리는 사다리 꼭대기에 효율적으로 오르려고 온 힘을 쏟다가, 그 사다리가 엉뚱한 벽에 기대어 있음을 깨달을 수도 있습니다. 많은 사람이 매우 바쁘지만 그리 효과적이지는 않습니다. 많은 사람이 여러 해 동안 주님의 일에 부지런히 힘썼지만, 결승선에 이르러 가장 중요한 것들이 자신에게서 빠져나가 버렸다는 사실을 깨닫습니다. 다른 이들을 섬기느라 삶을 바친 사람들 가운데는 결혼 생활이 어려움을 겪게 하거나 자녀들이 자신을 존중하지 않게 내버려 둔 이들도 있습니다. 또 어떤 이들은 부모와의 관계를 소홀히 하면서 교회에 “고르반”을 드렸습니다.

무너진 틈에 선 사람은 지혜로워야 하며, 지혜는 참된 틈이 어디에 있는지 알아야 합니다. 이를 위해 우리는 목적이 분명한 성경적 비전에 이끌려야 합니다. 삶에는 우리의 길을 버릴 기회가 많이 찾아옵니다. 가족과 친구, 동료, 교회의 계획, 삶의 여건이 우리에게 기대하는 바를 적극적으로 이루려 한다면, 우리는 성경적 원칙이 아니라 사람들에게 이끌릴 것입니다. 겉으로는 그럴듯해 보여도, 결국 엉뚱한 밧줄 끝에 매달려 있음을 깨닫고 쓰라린 실망을 맛볼 수 있습니다.

그렇다면 하나님께서 마음을 두시는 틈은 어떤 모습일까요? 어떤 이들은 어떤 필요든 생기는 곳에 그 틈이 있다고 말할 것입니다. 가난한 이들은 언제나 우리와 함께 있으니, 물론 그들을 돕는 것은 선을 행할 기회입니다. 그러나 마리아가 택한 더 좋은 몫은 가난한 이들을 돕거나 굶주린 이들을 먹이는 것과는 아무 관계가 없었습니다. 마찬가지로 귀한 나드 향유가 든 옥합을 지닌 여인은 그것을 팔아 그 값으로 한동안 가난한 이들을 먹여 살릴 수도 있었습니다. 그러나 참된 틈은 불구자를 어루만져서가 아니라 그리스도께 왕관을 씌워 드림으로써 메울 수 있었습니다. 에덴동산에는 틈이 없었습니다. 사람이 창조주와 완전한 조화를 이루며 걸었기 때문입니다. 죄가 틈을 만들고 관계를 손상시켰습니다. 또한 시간이 끝나 어린양께서 신부를 맞이하실 때에는 아무런 균열도 없을 것입니다. 그때까지 이 땅이 창조주께 영광 돌리기를 거부하기 때문에 커다란 틈이 존재합니다. 그 틈에 서는 것이 그분의 이름을 지니고자 하는 모든 이의 으뜸가는 목적이어야 합니다.

이를 위해서는 하나님과의 관계가 완전히 변화해야 합니다. 그리스도의 피로 이루신 속죄로 인해 법적으로 그것이 가능해집니다. 성령의 위로가 정서적인 만족을 주지만, 우리를 움직이는 것은 하나님께 자신을 내어 드리고 하나님께 영광을 돌리는 영역입니다. 탕자는 아버지의 아들로서 누리던 지위를 저버림으로써 스스로 온갖 문제를 불러온 영혼의 대표적인 사례입니다. 그가 회복되는 일의 핵심은 태어날 때부터 존재했던 아버지와 아들의 관계를 다시 세우는 것에 지나지 않았습니다.

하나님께서는 “내가 여기 있나이다. 나를 보내소서!”라고 외치며 손을 흔드는 영혼을 그토록 찾으시는 것은 아닌 듯합니다. 오히려 그분의 눈은 전능하신 하나님 앞에 자기 뜻을 굽히고 다음을 인정하는 겸손한 영혼을 찾으십니다. 주님, 주께서는 영광과 존귀와 권능을 받으시기에 합당하십니다. 주께서 만물을 창조하셨고, 만물이 주의 뜻으로 말미암아 존재하며 창조되었습니다. –요한계시록 4:11. 자신들이 들은 “예수”를 전하려는 의지만으로 중요한 역할을 맡고 있다고 여기는 스게와의 아들들은 부족하지 않습니다. 1997년, “무너진 틈에 서기”라는 주제에 호응하여 약 80만 명의 남성이 워싱턴 D.C.에서 열린 프라미스 키퍼스 집회에 모였습니다. 이들은 영적 기반에서 급속히 멀어지는 나라에 하나님을 나타내려는 좋은 의도가 있었을지 모릅니다. 그러나 선한 마음만으로는 충분하지 않습니다. 하나님께서는 구멍에 밀어 넣을 많은 사람을 필요로 하지 않으십니다. 그분은 자격을 갖춘 사람을 찾으시며, 그런 자리에 오를 수 있었던 이는 소수입니다.

하나님께서 원하시는 것이 집회에 참석하거나 거리에서 공개적으로 신앙을 선포하는 것뿐이었다면, 의심할 여지 없이 그 선한 일을 하려는 사람은 많이 찾으실 수 있었을 것입니다. 그러나 하나님과 세상 사이의 틈에 서는 일은 그 자리에 설 자격이 있는 사람에게만 하나님께서 허락하십니다. 유용해지고 싶어 하기만 하면 실제로 쓰임받을 것이라고 믿게 만드는 것은 인간의 보편적인 교만입니다. 하나님의 집에는 귀히 쓰이는 그릇도 있고 천히 쓰이는 그릇도 있지만, 영예로운 자리를 받을 만한 자격을 갖추는 것은 그 자리를 바라는 것보다 훨씬 어렵습니다.

오늘날 “당신이 마땅히 받아야 할 인정을 받으세요”라는 문구가 적힌 우편물을 받는 일은 흔합니다. 많은 이들이 마땅히 받아야 할 인정이 전혀 없다는 사실은 비밀이 아닙니다. 그러나 누구나 인정을 받을 만하다는 은연중의 메시지는 우리 모두에게 영향을 미쳤습니다. 우리 사회는 부도덕하고 경솔하며 앞날을 내다보지 못하는 사람도 도덕적이고 근면한 사람과 똑같은 돌봄을 받아 마땅하다고 부추깁니다. 게으른 사람이 좋은 임금을 받아 마땅하고 낭비벽이 있는 사람이 재정적 안정을 누려 마땅하다면, 사도 바울은 교회로부터 지원을 받아야 할 과부에게 어떤 자격도 요구할 권리가 없습니다. 또한 감독의 직분을 바라는 진실한 영혼이 자격을 갖추지 못했다는 이유만으로 그를 거부할 권리도 없습니다. 그러나 하나님께서는 다음과 같은 몇몇 영혼을 눈여겨보셨습니다. …사데에 그 옷을 더럽히지 아니한 몇 사람이 있으니, 그들은 흰옷을 입고 나와 함께 다닐 것이니라. 그들은 합당한 자들이니라. –요한계시록 3:4

이들이 무너진 틈에 선 사람들입니다. 넘치는 열정이 있어서가 아니라 순결을 향한 비전이 있었기 때문입니다. 이는 우연이 아니었습니다. 하나님 앞에서 탁월한 지위에 이르고자 하는 사람은 다음과 같은 방식으로 해야 합니다…

…목적

믿음으로 모세는 장성하여 바로의 딸의 아들이라 불리기를 거절하고, 잠시 죄의 낙을 누리는 것보다 하나님의 백성과 함께 고난받기를 택하였으며, 그리스도를 위하여 받는 치욕을 이집트의 보화보다 더 큰 재물로 여겼으니, 이는 상 주심을 바라보았기 때문입니다. 믿음으로 그는 왕의 분노를 두려워하지 않고 이집트를 떠났습니다. 보이지 아니하시는 분을 보는 것처럼 하여 참았기 때문입니다. –히브리서 11:24-27

하나님의 일을 향한 참된 비전에는 대가가 따릅니다. 부자 청년 관원은 자기 영지의 통치자일 뿐 아니라 그리스도의 나라에서도 통치자가 되고 싶었겠지만, 두 가지를 모두 붙들 수는 없었습니다. 이 원칙은 그에게, 그리고 그처럼 고귀한 일을 바라는 모든 이에게 첫 번째 장애물이 되었습니다. 젊은 시절 모세는 결정을 내리고 자신의 충성을 바칠 대상을 택했습니다. 이집트에게 버림받을 각오는 되어 있었지만, 자기 백성에게 그토록 냉담하게 내쳐지리라고는 꿈에도 생각하지 못했습니다.

외로운 용광로에서 보낸 사십 년은 그의 교만을 씻어 내고 역량을 다듬었습니다. 그곳에서 그는 침묵의 신학교를 졸업하여, 땅 위에서 가장 온유한 사람으로 무너진 틈에 서도록 준비되고 갖추어졌습니다. 그는 사람들을 위해 하나님께 중보하는 자가 되었습니다. 사람과 하나님을 대변하는 자로서 설교하고 기도했으며, 걷고 울었고, 하나님과 형제자매를 사랑하며 살았습니다. 그 모든 시간 동안 그는 자신이 그 자리에 부적합하다고 여겼습니다. 이스라엘 자손은 그의 마음 한가운데 있었지만, 두려움과 시선은 끝내 하나님을 떠나지 않았습니다. 사람들에게 존경받으려 하면 우리의 목적은 흐려지고 무너진 틈에서 맡은 자리를 잃게 됩니다. 훌륭한 목회자와 부모와 순례자 가운데 많은 이들이 이런 실수를 저질렀고, 아내나 자녀, 친구, 교회가 써 준 각본을 받아들였습니다. 그것이 사랑과 배려를 보이고 가장 존중하는 일처럼 여겨질 수도 있습니다. 그러나 하나님께서는 절대적인 충성을 요구하시며 타협은 있을 수 없습니다. 사람이 “되고 싶어 하는 것”은 자신이 바라보는 목적에 이끌리지만, 사람이 “결국 어떤 사람이 되는가”는 그의…

…우선순위

이 말은 참됩니다. 누구든지 감독의 직분을 맡고자 하면 선한 일을 바라는 것입니다. 그러므로 감독은 책망받을 것이 없고, 한 아내의 남편이며, 절제하고 신중하며 단정하고 나그네를 잘 대접하며 가르치기를 잘해야 합니다. 술을 즐기지 않고, 폭력을 쓰지 않으며, 더러운 이익을 탐하지 않고, 온유하며, 다투지 않고, 돈을 사랑하지 않아야 합니다. 자기 집을 잘 다스리고, 자녀들을 온전히 복종하게 해야 합니다. –디모데전서 3:1-4. 우리의 목적은 도착지를 정하지만, 그곳에 이르는 길은 우리의 우선순위가 닦습니다.

안타깝게도 여론에 의해 사역자로 발탁되는 사람들도 있지만, 하나님께서는 우선순위와 영원한 자격을 근거로 자신의 사람들을 택하십니다. 소유물이나 정욕이나 지위에 지배받는 사람은 하나님의 목적을 위해 섬기는 데 쓸모가 없을 것입니다. 그들은 목사, 목사님, 신부님이라 불리기를 좋아합니다. 열심 있고 지식이 있으며 굳건하고 자비롭다고 존경받기를 좋아합니다. 내가 이제 사람들의 호의를 구하고 있습니까, 하나님의 호의를 구하고 있습니까? 내가 사람들을 기쁘게 하려 애쓰고 있습니까? 내가 여전히 사람들을 기쁘게 하고 있다면, 나는 그리스도의 종이 아닙니다. –갈라디아서 1:10 ASV

다행히 하나님은 사람을 외모로 취하지 않으시며, 담을 쌓기에 적합한 돌을 길에 버려두지 않으십니다. 나이 든 사람, 가난한 사람, 불구가 된 사람, 걷지 못하는 사람은 모두 틈을 메우는 자리에 설 유력한 후보입니다. 꿈이 깨지고 몸이 상하고 마음이 부서진 사람들도 노아, 아브라함, 요셉, 모세, 다니엘, 에스더, 룻과 셀 수 없이 많은 이들 곁에서 방해받지 않고 성벽의 틈에 설 수 있습니다. 이들은 모두 이 세상에 하나님을 훌륭히 드러내는 대표자들입니다. 그들은 모두 경박함과 명성, 익숙함과 부를 등지고 하늘의 영웅이 되었습니다. 그들은 성벽의 틈에서 어깨를 나란히 하고 “영원한 나라의 대사관”을 이룹니다. 남들이 미워할 때 그들은 사랑했습니다. 남들이 받을 때 그들은 모든 것을 내주었습니다. 그들은 조롱과 오해를 받고, 욕을 먹고 비웃음을 당했으며, 지치고 눈물 흘렸습니다.

우리는 구원받는 사람들 가운데서나 멸망하는 사람들 가운데서나 하나님께 그리스도의 향기입니다. 한쪽 사람들에게는 죽음에서 죽음에 이르는 냄새요, 다른 쪽 사람들에게는 생명에서 생명에 이르는 향기입니다. 누가 이런 일을 감당할 수 있겠습니까? –고린도후서 2:15-16. 오직 목적과 우선순위가 하나님께 다스림을 받는 사람들입니다.

It was 2:30 p.m., Tuesday afternoon.

“Señora!” a chorus of voices hollered from outside our property hedge. “Open the gate!”

“Just wait,” I called back. “It’s not three o’clock yet.”

Disgruntled murmurings sounded from the other side of the hedge. I turned to my wailing baby. Sinking into the rocker to feed her, I closed my eyes to relish each quiet moment before the coming tumult.

**************

We had scarcely settled onto the farm when the neighbor children found us. They appeared—uninvited and unannounced, any time of day—to stay as long as they wished. The first ones soon brought more friends along to join in their play with the foreigner’s children and toys. Play-Doh and table games entertained them but oh, what a commotion ten children could make in a concrete house.

After much exasperation, Ernest (my husband) and I finally came up with a plan…. They could come two afternoons a week, arriving no earlier than three o’clock in the afternoon. On Tuesdays they could stay for supper, but on Thursdays they must leave by 6 p.m.

We also had other rules…. Our children needed to stay within my eyesight and earshot when playing with neighbor children. And NO closed doors. Still, questions niggled my brain. Is this a good thing or a bad one? Will we live to regret it? What if they are a bad influence on our children? My questions formed a prayer, one which God had been hearing from me quite a bit these past months. Lord, give me wisdom and patience with these children today. And if they are a bad influence on our children, Lord, please reveal that to us before our children are harmed.

But what an opportunity! This was one way I could reach the world while being a stay-at-home mom… I read them Bible stories. I taught them the need to respect and obey grownups. I told them they needed to obey me, just as my children were expected to. Transgressors, I warned, would be sent home.

Zinnia did not believe me, until the day she disobeyed and was expelled. I grin now, remembering the little troublemaker perching on the neighbor’s wall, peering over into our farm where her cousins were happily playing. Once had taught her; after that Zinnia obeyed.

**************

“Señora!” Zinnia’s voice interrupted my reverie. “Is it three o’clock yet?”

I opened one eye to peek at the clock—2:47.

“Not quite!” I hollered out the window. Placing baby into the walker, I headed to the kitchen. What would I feed them tonight?

**************

“Zinnia, I need to look in your purse before you go home.”

It was Tuesday evening again, several months later. We had been missing various small things after Zinnia started bringing a purse along on her visits to our house. Tonight, we would see if our suspicions were correct.

Zinnia’s terror-filled eyes met mine. “Just a minute, Señora. I need to use the bathroom.”

“You can use the bathroom after we look in your purse.”

“No, Señora, I can’t wait…”, her voice trailed off as she rushed to the bathroom.

I sighed. Of course, her purse would be empty when she came back out. Searching the bathroom later that night revealed treasures hidden here and there.

“Let’s chat a little, Zinnia,” I invited the following week. Zinnia sat on the bed, twisting yarn knots on the comforter, her eyes defensive, fearful. My heart yearned for the dear girl. Her mom had left years ago to work in another country, leaving the girls with their Grandma.

“I don’t care about those things you stole, Zinnia,” I began. “But it’s a habit you don’t want to start. God cares about you….”

That was the last time Zinnia, her sister, and their cousins showed up at our place. “Our Grandma doesn’t let us come anymore,” they explained.

Maybe it was Grandma; I think it was God. We had prayed much that He would make it clear if their visits were harmful to our children and if they should stop coming. My heart was torn between love for the neighbor children and protection for our own. This was the way God chose to answer.

“Thank you, God,” I prayed. “We’ll take this as your answer, and not invite them back. Send them over if you want them to come again.”

**************

Several years passed. Now it was Jon, a neighbor boy, frequenting our home.

“Could he come to your house every day after school?” his parents had wondered. “We want him to learn good things, instead of playing with boys in our neighborhood.”

Hmm. So, we’re to raise the boy while both parents work?

“He can come Tuesday and Thursday afternoons,” Ernest decided. “Those are the days I’m more often at home.”

Jon showed up faithfully on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons. Problem was, Ernest couldn’t. Other responsibilities and obligations kept coming up, hindering him from being there like he wanted to.

I did not want to nag my husband… He really wished he could be at home, working with the boys. Should I say something, or not? It didn’t seem ideal to have an unconverted boy working for hours with our son, a new Christian.

I did mention my questions to Ernest, but mostly I made it a matter of prayer.

Jon stopped coming. I was amazed. I felt for Jon, yet once again I thanked God for His answer.

**************

“How can I reach out to my neighbor children without compromising my own?” a friend asked recently. Moving to a new area, she faces the challenge of neighbor children coming over.

There are no simple answers. I have discovered the urgency of prayer, and God’s faithfulness in answering when we cry out to Him for wisdom. His answer to others may well be different from what He worked out for us.

**************

Another sister granted me permission to share their experience in relating with neighbor children:

Alex and his mother live across the road from us and began attending church soon after we moved here. Alex came over almost every day and taught our boys Spanish in short order. The boys dreaded his visits at first, but they soon became great friends. After a while another neighbor boy, Nilton, started coming at times and we thought he seemed decent enough. Then one day a third boy, José, came along. I got a distinctly uncomfortable feeling. I gave them a time limit, but just couldn’t shake the uneasy feeling. So, though I thought I didn’t have time, I decided I would work outside the whole time while they were here. I worked close to them and kept an eye on things and thought everything was fine. They seemed to just be playing together nicely, so I was surprised when they went home before the time was up.

It wasn’t long before my boys came in crying; they felt so bad about what had happened. Alex had asked them to deliver a note to his girlfriend because his mom wouldn’t like it if he did. One of the other boys told them what he does out behind bushes at public school, so he doesn’t get caught. They tried to get my boys to promise not to tell me. They didn’t promise, and I was so thankful! But they were very torn up because they thought Alex would not be their friend anymore.

My husband and I talked with the boys and assured them that they had handled the situation correctly by not promising to keep secrets. Within the hour, Alex’s mom came over to visit and we told her about it. She was very alarmed that her son had tried to pass a note and later took care of the situation with her son. I was glad that the budding relationship he had with the neighbor girl was stopped before it went any farther. Alex’s friendship with our boys has continued but the other two boys discovered that our boys had told us about them and didn’t come over for years after that.

José recently asked our eight-year-old son if he could come over to his house and play. I said no. His grandma came over several days later, offended, and said that José was very sad about it. I explained that I feel I must always be with my boys if he would come over because one time, he had tried to get our son to play an electronic war game with him. The grandma understood and was sad that her grandson was a bad influence. She wanted the best for him. We have invited him to Sunday School, but he doesn’t want that. I just hope that we can always have the type of relationship with our children that they will feel free to come to us and not keep these situations to themselves and feel guilty.

**************

Wise parents seek to remove danger, but not difficulty, from their children’s path. I was recently amazed while reading Judges 3, to discover that God wanted some enemy nations to remain in the land of Canaan. Why? He wanted parents to teach their children war (v. 2). Instead, the children of Israel made friends with the enemy nations and began to intermarry. “It seems we live closer to the world here on the mission field,” one sister shared. Our children are growing up on the front lines, as it were. This can be positive. They have frequent opportunities to “speak with the enemy in the gates,” where they are asked what we believe, and why. But when parents are lax, or their children are rebellious, this closer association with the world can prove tragic.

As we connect with God in prayer for our children, we must also connect with them. No strict safety guidelines will substitute a close relationship with your child. The mother of a child who was abused shared, “The only way your child will tell you what is going on is if you have a close relationship.”

I stagger as I consider our enemy and my own inadequacy as a mother. Suddenly I am seized with urgency to pray for things which never entered my head when our children were still young. Abuse cases exist around us; at times in our very midst. I pray for our children’s protection from the evil which surrounds them and that which rises in their hearts. I pray they will never mar another’s purity. I pray for purity at the marriage altar, both for them and their future spouses.

I pray with urgency, yet with confidence. Because this I know: God loves our children—He cares about their purity and protection even more than we as parents do—He longs for us to partner with Him in raising them to be faithful servants of His—And He wants to show Himself strong on behalf of humble parents who cry out to Him as they train soldiers in enemy territory. For the eyes of the LORD run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to shew himself strong in the behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him… –2 Chronicles 16:9.

Eran las 2:30 p. m. del martes por la tarde.

—¡Señora! —gritó a coro un grupo de voces desde fuera de la cerca de nuestra propiedad—. ¡Abra la reja!

—Esperen un poco —respondí—. Todavía no son las tres.

Se oyeron murmullos de disgusto al otro lado de la cerca. Me volví hacia mi bebé, que lloraba. Me senté en la mecedora para darle de comer y cerré los ojos, disfrutando de cada momento de tranquilidad antes del alboroto que se avecinaba.

**************

Apenas nos habíamos instalado en la finca cuando los niños vecinos nos encontraron. Aparecían —sin invitación ni aviso, a cualquier hora del día— y se quedaban todo el tiempo que querían. Los primeros no tardaron en traer a más amigos para jugar con los hijos de la extranjera y sus juguetes. La plastilina Play-Doh y los juegos de mesa los entretenían, pero ¡qué alboroto podían armar diez niños en una casa de concreto!

Después de mucha frustración, Ernest (mi esposo) y yo finalmente ideamos un plan…. Podían venir dos tardes por semana, pero no antes de las tres de la tarde. Los martes podían quedarse a cenar, pero los jueves debían irse a las 6 p. m.

También teníamos otras reglas…. Nuestros hijos debían permanecer a la vista y al alcance del oído cuando jugaran con los niños vecinos. Y nada de puertas cerradas. Aun así, las preguntas me rondaban la cabeza. ¿Es algo bueno o malo? ¿Viviremos para arrepentirnos? ¿Y si son una mala influencia para nuestros hijos? Mis preguntas se convirtieron en una oración, una que Dios me había oído hacer muchas veces en los últimos meses. Señor, dame sabiduría y paciencia hoy con estos niños. Y si son una mala influencia para nuestros hijos, Señor, por favor, háznoslo saber antes de que nuestros hijos sufran daño.

¡Pero qué oportunidad! Era una manera de llegar al mundo sin dejar de ser una mamá que se queda en casa… Les leía historias bíblicas. Les enseñaba que debían respetar y obedecer a los adultos. Les decía que tenían que obedecerme, igual que se esperaba que lo hicieran mis hijos. Les advertía que quienes desobedecieran serían enviados a casa.

Zinnia no me creyó, hasta el día en que desobedeció y la expulsé. Ahora sonrío al recordar a la pequeña traviesa sentada en la pared del vecino, mirando por encima hacia nuestra finca, donde sus primos jugaban felices. Bastó una vez para enseñarle; después de eso, Zinnia obedeció.

**************

—¡Señora! —la voz de Zinnia interrumpió mis pensamientos—. ¿Ya son las tres?

Abrí un ojo para mirar el reloj: eran las 2:47.

—¡Todavía no! —grité por la ventana. Puse a la bebé en el andador y me dirigí a la cocina. ¿Qué les daría de comer esta noche?

**************

—Zinnia, necesito revisar tu bolso antes de que te vayas a casa.

Era martes por la noche otra vez, varios meses después. Desde que Zinnia había empezado a traer un bolso cuando venía a nuestra casa, nos faltaban varias cosas pequeñas. Esa noche comprobaríamos si nuestras sospechas eran correctas.

Sus ojos llenos de terror se encontraron con los míos. —Un momento, señora. Necesito ir al baño.

—Puedes ir al baño después de que revisemos tu bolso.

—No, señora, no puedo esperar… —su voz se apagó mientras corría al baño.

Suspiré. Por supuesto, cuando volviera, el bolso estaría vacío. Esa noche, más tarde, al revisar el baño, encontramos tesoros escondidos aquí y allá.

—Hablemos un poco, Zinnia —le propuse la semana siguiente. Zinnia se sentó en la cama, enrollando nudos de hilo sobre el edredón, con los ojos a la defensiva y asustados. Mi corazón anhelaba ayudar a aquella querida niña. Su mamá se había ido años atrás a trabajar a otro país, dejando a las niñas con su abuela.

—No me importan esas cosas que robaste, Zinnia —comencé—. Pero es un hábito que no quieres adquirir. A Dios sí le importas….

Esa fue la última vez que Zinnia, su hermana y sus primos aparecieron en nuestra casa. —Nuestra abuela ya no nos deja venir —explicaron.

Quizá fue la abuela; yo creo que fue Dios. Habíamos orado mucho para que Él nos mostrara claramente si sus visitas perjudicaban a nuestros hijos y si debían dejar de venir. Mi corazón estaba dividido entre el cariño por los niños vecinos y el deseo de proteger a los nuestros. Así fue como Dios decidió responder.

—Gracias, Dios —oré—. Tomaremos esto como tu respuesta y no los invitaremos a volver. Envíalos si quieres que vuelvan.

**************

Pasaron varios años. Ahora era Jon, un niño vecino, quien venía con frecuencia a nuestra casa.

—¿Podría venir a su casa todos los días después de la escuela? —nos habían preguntado sus padres—. Queremos que aprenda cosas buenas, en vez de jugar con los niños de nuestro vecindario.

Hmmm. ¿Así que nos toca criar al niño mientras sus dos padres trabajan?

—Puede venir los martes y jueves por la tarde —decidió Ernest—. Esos son los días que suelo estar más en casa.

Jon se presentó fielmente los martes y jueves por la tarde. El problema era que Ernest no podía estar. Seguían surgiendo otras responsabilidades y obligaciones que le impedían estar allí como quería.

No quería estar insistiendo a mi esposo… De verdad deseaba estar en casa trabajando con los niños. ¿Debía decir algo o no? No parecía lo ideal que un niño no convertido trabajara durante horas con nuestro hijo, que era un cristiano nuevo.

Sí le comenté mis inquietudes a Ernest, pero sobre todo las convertí en un asunto de oración.

Jon dejó de venir. Me sorprendió. Sentía pena por Jon, pero una vez más le di gracias a Dios por su respuesta.

**************

—¿Cómo puedo acercarme a los niños vecinos sin poner en riesgo a los míos? —me preguntó hace poco una amiga. Al mudarse a una zona nueva, se enfrenta al desafío de que los niños vecinos vayan a su casa.

No hay respuestas sencillas. He descubierto la urgencia de la oración y la fidelidad de Dios al responder cuando clamamos a Él por sabiduría. Es muy posible que su respuesta a otras personas sea distinta de lo que Él dispuso para nosotros.

**************

Otra hermana me dio permiso para compartir su experiencia al relacionarse con los niños vecinos:

Alex y su mamá viven al otro lado de la calle y empezaron a asistir a la iglesia poco después de que nos mudáramos aquí. Alex venía casi todos los días y enseguida les enseñó español a nuestros hijos. Al principio, ellos temían sus visitas, pero pronto se hicieron grandes amigos. Al cabo de un tiempo, otro niño vecino, Nilton, empezó a venir de vez en cuando y nos pareció bastante decente. Luego, un día, llegó un tercer niño, José. Tuve una sensación muy clara de incomodidad. Les puse un límite de tiempo, pero no pude quitarme de encima esa sensación de inquietud. Así que, aunque pensaba que no tenía tiempo, decidí trabajar afuera durante todo el tiempo que ellos estuvieran allí. Trabajé cerca de ellos y estuve pendiente de lo que pasaba; me pareció que todo iba bien. Parecía que simplemente jugaban juntos y se llevaban bien, así que me sorprendió que se fueran a casa antes de que se cumpliera el tiempo.

No pasó mucho tiempo antes de que mis hijos entraran llorando; se sentían muy mal por lo que había ocurrido. Alex les había pedido que le llevaran una nota a su novia porque a su mamá no le gustaría que lo hiciera. Uno de los otros niños les contó lo que hacía detrás de los arbustos en la escuela pública para que no lo descubrieran. Intentaron hacer que mis hijos prometieran no contármelo. No lo prometieron, ¡y se lo agradecí muchísimo! Pero estaban muy angustiados porque pensaban que Alex ya no sería su amigo.

Mi esposo y yo hablamos con los niños y les aseguramos que habían actuado correctamente al no prometer guardar secretos. En menos de una hora, la mamá de Alex vino a visitarnos y se lo contamos. Se alarmó mucho al enterarse de que su hijo había intentado hacer llegar una nota y luego se ocupó del asunto con él. Me alegré de que se detuviera la relación incipiente que él tenía con la niña vecina antes de que avanzara más. La amistad de Alex con nuestros hijos continuó, pero los otros dos niños se enteraron de que nuestros hijos nos habían hablado de ellos y no volvieron a venir durante años.

Hace poco, José le preguntó a nuestro hijo de ocho años si podía ir a su casa a jugar. Le dije que no. Varios días después, vino su abuela, ofendida, y dijo que José estaba muy triste por eso. Le expliqué que siento que siempre debo estar con mis hijos si él viene, porque una vez había intentado convencer a nuestro hijo de jugar con él a un videojuego electrónico de guerra. La abuela lo entendió y le entristeció que su nieto fuera una mala influencia. Quería lo mejor para él. Lo hemos invitado a la escuela dominical, pero no quiere ir. Solo espero que siempre podamos tener con nuestros hijos una relación tal que se sientan libres de acudir a nosotros y no guardarse estas situaciones para sí mismos ni sentirse culpables.

**************

Los padres sabios procuran quitar el peligro del camino de sus hijos, pero no las dificultades. Hace poco me asombró descubrir, al leer Jueces 3, que Dios quería que algunas naciones enemigas permanecieran en la tierra de Canaán. ¿Por qué? Quería que los padres enseñaran a sus hijos a combatir (v. 2). En cambio, los hijos de Israel se hicieron amigos de las naciones enemigas y comenzaron a casarse con ellas. —Parece que aquí, en el campo misionero, vivimos más cerca del mundo —comentó una hermana. Por así decirlo, nuestros hijos crecen en la primera línea de combate. Esto puede ser positivo. Tienen oportunidades frecuentes de «hablar con el enemigo en la puerta», donde les preguntan qué creemos y por qué. Pero cuando los padres son negligentes o sus hijos son rebeldes, esta mayor cercanía al mundo puede resultar trágica.

Al conectarnos con Dios en oración por nuestros hijos, también debemos conectarnos con ellos. Ninguna pauta estricta de seguridad puede sustituir una relación cercana con tu hijo. La madre de un niño que sufrió abuso dijo: «La única manera de que tu hijo te cuente lo que está pasando es que tengas una relación cercana con él».

Me estremezco al considerar a nuestro enemigo y mi propia insuficiencia como madre. De pronto me invade la urgencia de orar por cosas que ni se me pasaban por la cabeza cuando nuestros hijos aún eran pequeños. Hay casos de abuso a nuestro alrededor; a veces, en nuestro propio entorno. Oro para que nuestros hijos estén protegidos del mal que los rodea y del que surge en sus corazones. Oro para que nunca manchen la pureza de otra persona. Oro por la pureza en el altar matrimonial, tanto para ellos como para sus futuros cónyuges.

Oro con urgencia, pero también con confianza. Porque esto sé: Dios ama a nuestros hijos; a Él le importan su pureza y su protección aún más que a nosotros, sus padres; anhela que colaboremos con Él para criarlos como siervos suyos fieles; y quiere mostrarse poderoso en favor de los padres humildes que claman a Él mientras entrenan soldados en territorio enemigo. Porque los ojos del SEÑOR recorren toda la tierra para mostrarse fuerte a favor de aquellos cuyo corazón es íntegro para con él… –2 Crónicas 16:9.

I am Ted. I was born a male and I know I am a male. My skin color is white, and I know I am white. My parents are white, my grandparents were white, and I have no reason to suspect my other ancestors were anything other than white. These are foundational, irrefutable truths about myself. I do not think I am anything other than what I am. Nor do I desire to be anything other than what I am.

I am a Christian. In order to better define my faith—as there are many who profess Christianity—I am a “biblical” Christian. I believe that the Bible is the Word of God, that it is to be taken literally, and that it instructs a pattern and way of life that all believers should embrace. At the age of 24—after having lived a life of my own choosing and while searching for God who, if He was real, I wanted to know—I turned to Him and I was born again. My transformation as a new creation in Christ began immediately and it continues to this day. My faith in and relationship to Jesus Christ are as foundational and irrefutable as my gender and race.

I am writing in response to that which had been extensively covered by the secular media during the Spring and Summer of 2015: a man who reportedly, throughout his life, had considered himself a female and who had been “transitioning” into a woman; a white woman who had insisted that race is “fluid” and that she is black; and the redefinition of marriage by the Supreme Court of the United States of America affecting, as well, the definition of “family” for an entire nation. These are topics which simply cannot be minimized or otherwise ignored.

The white woman lacked much public support for her explanation of race. In fact, she was significantly ridiculed for her stance. This was not true, however, regarding gender identification or “gay” marriage and family issues, and one must wonder why. If a “genetically/physiologically-constructed” male can be accepted by others as a woman simply because that’s what he thinks he is, and if a man can “marry” a man and a woman can “marry” a woman and be accepted as a married couple by others under the premise of equal rights and because that’s what they want to do, why can’t a white woman be accepted as a black woman when she is convinced that she is black?

The question raised is one of reality. Even though I may think I am the greatest pianist and music composer of all times, the evidence simply does not support that conviction. Even though a white woman says she is black, the evidence likewise does not support that conviction. Also true is that of a man who says he is a woman. The genetic and physiological evidence does not support that conviction. Without the redefinition of marriage, two people of the same sex cannot be married. And regardless of definition, they cannot reproduce on their own, one of God’s primary purposes for marriage.

Without God, man does what is right in his own eyes. So-called “progressive thinking” is simply man’s attempt, given his rejection of God, at better understanding the world and better addressing and solving its problems. Essentially, “anything goes” based upon the latest of ideas.

A biblical Christian, however, believes that God has designed, has created, and is very much involved in the universe … even in the individual lives of people who live in it. There are absolutes. There is a distinction between right and wrong. There are moral values and—something that we frequently forget in these modern times—there is an eternity ahead. As a result of progressive thinking, Darwinism now replaces Creationism, within much of our education system, students as well as teachers who profess faith in the God of the Bible are ridiculed and are otherwise discriminated against, millions of pre-born babies (the politically correct prefer calling them “fetuses”) have been legally dismembered, burnt, crushed, suctioned and pharmacologically murdered (aborted), and no-fault divorce has ravaged the families of our nation. Just look at those things that used to be considered wrong or evil which are now a normal part of our “progressing” society.

And what about eternity? Doesn’t that matter anymore, either?

In response to the Supreme Court’s ruling on gay marriage, then-President Barack Obama, clearly one of our nation’s more powerful, progressive thinkers, indicated his desire that “religious people” respond accordingly by modifying their definition of marriage as well. Believing in the God of the Bible as the Creator of the universe and as the One who designed and ordained marriage as a life-long covenant between one man and one woman, I respectfully decline Mr. Obama’s request. As the world in its own fashion deviates from the design and will of God, a true believer in Christ is called to follow Him. Jesus said, Enter through the narrow gate. For wide is the gate and broad is the road that leads to destruction, and many enter through it. But small is the gate and narrow the road that leads to life, and only a few find it. –Mat 7:13-14 NIV

I am Ted. I am a white male. I am a Christian who desires not to belittle, mock, or otherwise mistreat those with whom I may disagree, but there will be disagreements. I am called to love God and to love my neighbor as myself, regardless of who my neighbor might be. My ultimate hope is not found in this world. It is found in eternity with Christ. And my prayer for others is that they, too, may come to know Him, receive forgiveness of their sins, be transformed into the people God so desires, and spend an eternity with Him. This is not a popular message found in today’s liberal media. But for those who are interested, for those who are seeking something much better than what this world has to offer, God has an answer: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. –Joh 3:16

나는 테드다. 나는 남성으로 태어났고 내가 남성임을 안다. 내 피부색은 백인이며, 내가 백인임을 안다. 부모님은 백인이셨고 조부모님도 백인이셨으며, 다른 조상들도 백인이 아니었을 것이라고 의심할 이유가 없다. 이것들은 나 자신에 관한 근본적이고 반박할 수 없는 진실이다. 나는 내가 아닌 다른 무엇이라고 생각하지 않는다. 또한 내가 아닌 다른 무엇이 되기를 바라지도 않는다.

나는 그리스도인이다. 기독교를 고백하는 이들이 많으므로 내 신앙을 더 분명히 말하자면, 나는 “성경적” 그리스도인이다. 나는 성경이 하나님의 말씀이며, 성경을 문자 그대로 받아들여야 하고, 모든 신자가 받아들여야 할 삶의 본보기와 방식을 가르친다고 믿는다. 스물네 살 때, 내가 선택한 대로 살아온 뒤, 하나님이 실재하신다면 그분을 알고 싶어 그분을 찾던 중 나는 그분께 돌아섰고 거듭났다. 그리스도 안에서 새로운 피조물로 변화되는 일은 즉시 시작되었고 오늘날까지 계속되고 있다. 예수 그리스도를 향한 나의 믿음과 그분과의 관계는 나의 성별과 인종만큼이나 근본적이고 반박할 수 없는 것이다.

나는 2015년 봄과 여름 동안 세속 언론에서 광범위하게 다루었던 일들에 대한 응답으로 글을 쓴다. 평생 자신을 여성으로 여겨 왔으며 여성으로 “전환”해 왔다고 보도된 한 남성, 인종은 “유동적”이라며 자신은 흑인이라고 주장한 백인 여성, 그리고 미국 대법원이 결혼을 재정의함으로써 한 나라 전체의 “가족”의 정의에도 영향을 미친 일이다. 이런 주제들은 결코 축소하거나 무시할 수 없다.

그 백인 여성의 인종에 관한 설명은 대중의 지지를 거의 얻지 못했다. 사실 그녀는 자신의 입장 때문에 상당한 조롱을 받았다. 그러나 성별 정체성이나 “동성” 결혼 및 가족 문제에 대해서는 그렇지 않았다. 그 이유가 무엇인지 의문을 품지 않을 수 없다. “유전적·생리적으로 구성된” 남성이 자신이 그렇다고 생각한다는 이유만으로 다른 이들에게 여성으로 받아들여질 수 있고, 평등한 권리라는 전제와 자신들이 그렇게 하기를 원한다는 이유로 남성이 남성과 “결혼”하고 여성이 여성과 “결혼”하여 다른 이들에게 부부로 받아들여질 수 있다면, 자신이 흑인이라고 확신하는 백인 여성은 왜 흑인 여성으로 받아들여질 수 없는가?

제기된 질문은 현실에 관한 것이다. 내가 역사상 가장 위대한 피아니스트이자 작곡가라고 생각할지라도, 증거는 그런 확신을 뒷받침하지 않는다. 백인 여성이 자신은 흑인이라고 말하더라도, 증거는 마찬가지로 그런 확신을 뒷받침하지 않는다. 자신은 여성이라고 말하는 남성의 경우도 마찬가지다. 유전적·생리적 증거는 그런 확신을 뒷받침하지 않는다. 결혼을 재정의하지 않는 한 동성인 두 사람은 결혼할 수 없다. 그리고 정의와 관계없이, 그들은 스스로 자녀를 낳을 수 없는데, 이는 결혼에 대한 하나님의 주요 목적 가운데 하나다.

하나님이 없으면 인간은 자기 눈에 옳은 대로 행한다. 이른바 “진보적 사고”란 하나님을 거부한 인간이 세상을 더 잘 이해하고 그 문제를 더 잘 다루고 해결하려는 시도에 불과하다. 본질적으로 최신 사상에 따라 “무엇이든 허용된다”는 것이다.

그러나 성경적 그리스도인은 하나님께서 우주를 설계하고 창조하셨으며, 그 안에 사는 사람들의 개별적인 삶에도 깊이 관여하신다고 믿는다. 절대적인 기준이 있다. 옳고 그름의 구분이 있다. 도덕적 가치가 있으며, 현대에 우리가 자주 잊는 것, 곧 앞으로 영원이 있다는 사실도 있다. 진보적 사고의 결과로, 이제 우리 교육 제도의 상당 부분에서 창조론 대신 다윈주의가 자리 잡았고, 성경의 하나님을 믿는다고 고백하는 학생과 교사는 조롱을 받거나 그 밖의 차별을 당하며, 수백만 명의 태어나지 않은 아기들(정치적으로 올바른 사람들은 그들을 “태아”라고 부르기를 선호한다)이 법적으로 절단되고, 불태워지고, 짓이겨지고, 흡입되고, 약물로 살해(낙태)되었으며, 무과실 이혼은 우리나라의 가정들을 황폐하게 만들었다. 한때 그릇되거나 악하다고 여겼지만 이제는 우리가 “진보하는” 사회의 일상적인 일부가 된 것들을 보라.

그렇다면 영원은 어떠한가? 그것은 이제 더는 중요하지 않은가?

동성 결혼에 관한 대법원 판결에 대한 응답으로, 당시 대통령 버락 오바마는 우리나라에서 가장 영향력 있는 진보적 사상가 중 한 사람임이 분명한데, “종교인들”도 그에 맞춰 결혼의 정의를 바꾸기를 바란다고 밝혔다. 성경의 하나님을 우주의 창조주이시며, 한 남자와 한 여자 사이의 평생 언약으로 결혼을 설계하고 제정하신 분으로 믿기에, 나는 오바마 씨의 요청을 정중히 거절한다. 세상이 나름의 방식으로 하나님의 설계와 뜻에서 벗어날 때, 그리스도를 참으로 믿는 이는 그분을 따르도록 부름받는다. 예수께서 말씀하셨다. 좁은 문으로 들어가라. 멸망으로 이끄는 문은 넓고 길이 널찍하여 그리로 들어가는 사람이 많다. 그러나 생명으로 이끄는 문은 작고 길이 좁아서 그것을 찾는 사람이 적다. –마태복음 7:13-14 NIV

나는 테드다. 나는 백인 남성이다. 나는 의견이 다를 수 있는 사람들을 깎아내리거나 조롱하거나 그 밖의 방식으로 함부로 대하지 않기를 바라는 그리스도인이지만, 의견 차이는 있을 것이다. 나는 내 이웃이 누구이든 상관없이 하나님을 사랑하고 내 이웃을 내 몸과 같이 사랑하도록 부름받았다. 나의 궁극적인 소망은 이 세상에서 찾을 수 없다. 그것은 그리스도와 함께하는 영원에서 찾을 수 있다. 다른 이들도 그분을 알고, 죄 사함을 받고, 하나님께서 바라시는 사람으로 변화되어 그분과 함께 영원히 지내기를 바라는 것이 나의 기도다. 오늘날의 진보적 언론에서 인기 있는 메시지는 아니다. 그러나 관심이 있는 이들, 이 세상이 줄 수 있는 것보다 훨씬 더 나은 것을 찾는 이들에게 하나님은 답을 주신다. 하나님께서 세상을 이처럼 사랑하셔서 독생자를 주셨으니, 이는 그를 믿는 사람마다 멸망하지 않고 영생을 얻게 하려는 것이다. –요한복음 3:16
