Muitas mulheres daqui do condado de Holmes, Ohio, me disseram que temos excelentes lojas beneficentes e lojas de artigos usados, como costuma acontecer onde vivem grandes grupos de pessoas simples. Pessoas de toda parte vieram nos visitar, reservando tempo extra para passar por essas lojas. Ao que parece, as pessoas daqui gostam de manter as coisas em ótimo estado; assim, ao primeiro sinal de desgaste, é “fora o velho e venha o novo”.

Da mesma forma, nenhum agricultor discordaria de que é uma sensação satisfatória ver todo o seu maquinário funcionar perfeitamente e todo o seu gado permanecer saudável. Desde o tempo de Adão, o Senhor sempre nos fez assim: …dominai sobre os peixes do mar, e sobre as aves dos céus, e sobre todo o animal que se move sobre a terra. –Gn 1:28

Uma atitude oposta deve ser evitada. Judas nos exorta a tomar cuidado com “certos homens” que, em nosso meio, “se introduziram com dissimulação”. Eles vivem segundo a carne e “desprezam a autoridade”. Dois mil anos depois, mesmo em nossa sociedade excessivamente descontraída, onde “está tudo bem” e precisamos “apenas relaxar”, o Senhor ainda espera que levemos a sério nosso chamado para exercer a responsabilidade, dada por Deus, de exercer domínio, usando princípios bíblicos em tudo o que fazemos.

Esse domínio também se estende ao nosso próprio corpo? Em 2 Crônicas, capítulo 34, podemos ler sobre o estado deplorável do Templo no início do reinado do rei Josias e sobre como ele o reconstruiu tanto fisicamente, com pedra e madeira — trabalhadas habilmente pelos artesãos — quanto espiritualmente, redescobrindo e assimilando a Palavra de Deus. Da mesma forma, devemos cuidar do nosso corpo, como o apóstolo Paulo nos instrui: Não sabeis vós que o vosso corpo é o templo do Espírito Santo, que habita em vós, proveniente de Deus, e que não sois de vós mesmos? Porque fostes comprados por preço; glorificai, pois, a Deus no vosso corpo e no vosso espírito, os quais pertencem a Deus. –1Co 6:19-20

É seguro dizer que, a julgar pela abundância de suplementos nutricionais, quiropráticos, médicos e outras pessoas e produtos de assistência suplementar à saúde, fazemos um bom esforço para manter nossos templos físicos bem cuidados e saudáveis. No entanto, como todos nascemos sob a maldição de Adão, ao contrário das peças de máquinas, que podem simplesmente ser substituídas, ou de uma máquina nova que se pode comprar quando a antiga chega ao fim de sua vida útil, temos de encarar a realidade de que as partes do nosso corpo também têm uma “vida útil” prática. Quanto mais envelhecemos, mais evidente fica que a vida é muito limitada. A Bíblia diz 70 a 80 anos (–ver Sl 90:10). (Na América, em 2018, a média era de 78,7 anos. Como pouca coisa mudou ao longo de mais de três milênios!)

Acho que todos podemos concordar que Deus se preocupa principalmente com o templo espiritual, ainda mais do que com o templo físico do nosso corpo. Não é preciso pensar muito para encontrar homens e mulheres piedosos de hoje e nossos antepassados espirituais de ontem que sacrificaram e suportaram a destruição do próprio corpo, glorificando a Deus, o que resultou na purificação de sua alma e na futura glorificação de seu corpo. Seu apelo era este: Cria em mim, ó Deus, um coração puro, e renova em mim um espírito reto. –Sl 51:10

O próprio Cristo suportou a destruição de seu corpo físico, dizendo: …Derribai este templo, e em três dias o levantarei. –Jo 2:19. Na ressurreição, seu corpo foi regenerado. Também lemos nas Escrituras sobre outra regeneração física, na qual a terra dará à luz os seus mortos, onde os que habitam no pó [despertarão] e cantarão de alegria! (–ver Is 26:19)

Apesar de tudo isso, quando nosso corpo se deteriora ou se desgasta, tentamos debilmente, com algum sucesso limitado, uma regeneração física por conta própria. Há todo um campo de estudo dedicado à Medicina Regenerativa. A palavra “regeneração” significa literalmente “refazer a gênese”, recriando um corpo novo — um objetivo bastante ambicioso, sem dúvida!

Há algo de errado em substituir peças quebradas (joelhos, quadris e cotovelos), remendar partes danificadas (ossos e pele) e manter a saúde em geral (por meio de boa alimentação e atividade física)? Certamente não — é assim que ganho a vida, aconselhando e tratando meus pacientes! No entanto, como acontece com a maioria das coisas, até a busca por “boa saúde” deve nos levar a parar para “calcular os custos” e agir com moderação — Seja a vossa moderação conhecida de todos os homens. Perto está o Senhor. –Fp 4:5. Pois, embora buscar a saúde física seja algo bom, buscá-la cegamente, sem considerar os custos espirituais (como descobrimos em nossa série sobre vacinas), pode nos desviar e afastar de Deus.

Há dois extremos nesse caminho rumo à saúde física, à saúde espiritual e ao nosso bem-estar geral. Num extremo, podemos ser imprudentes com a saúde, permitindo que nosso templo corporal se deteriore prematuramente. Jó disse a respeito do homem: Visto que os seus dias estão determinados, contigo está o número dos seus meses; e tu lhe puseste limites, e não passará além deles. –Jó 14:5. Portanto, se por negligência procuramos encurtar esses dias, não estamos desafiando a Deus — procurando frustrar sua vontade perfeita para nós? No outro extremo está a busca imprudente e inútil pela imortalidade — procurando a saúde física a qualquer custo. Ao fazer isso, não é também um ato de desafio? Paulo nos lembra: Portanto, como por um homem entrou o pecado no mundo, e pelo pecado a morte, assim também a morte passou a todos os homens, por isso que todos pecaram. –Rm 5:12. Em outras palavras, por causa do pecado, o plano de Deus para nós é que morramos fisicamente (para que possamos viver eternamente com Ele).

A esta altura, a maioria dos leitores concordaria que esses dois extremos têm algo em comum: ambos negligenciam a saúde espiritual de uma pessoa e ambos representam um estado de desafio a Deus. Então, aonde quero chegar com isso? A maioria dos cristãos que conheço não busca a saúde física a qualquer custo. Peço-lhes que me acompanhem, pois gostaria de dedicar o restante deste artigo (e o próximo) a apresentar a história da Medicina Regenerativa — essa “recriação da gênese”. Ela corresponde ao que promete? Há fraudes? Quais são os perigos? O que o futuro reserva? Mais importante: que impacto ela tem sobre nossa saúde espiritual e nosso relacionamento com o Senhor?

Primeiro, o que exatamente é a Medicina Regenerativa? Como mencionei anteriormente, significa literalmente os esforços humanos para “refazer” a gênese (origem, criação ou começo). O termo foi usado pela primeira vez há relativamente pouco tempo, na década de 1990, e é definido como o estudo e a prática da “substituição ou regeneração de células, tecidos ou órgãos humanos, para restaurar ou estabelecer o funcionamento normal”. Em sua breve história, foram usados todos os meios possíveis para isso.

Ela difere da Medicina de Transplantes, na qual órgãos inteiros são substituídos, mas continuam sendo considerados “estranhos” pelo corpo receptor. Por isso, são necessários medicamentos fortes contra a rejeição pelo resto da vida da pessoa. Também difere da Medicina Ortopédica, na qual materiais como parafusos e joelhos de titânio, por exemplo, fixam e substituem peças desgastadas. A Medicina Regenerativa se inspira na ocorrência natural em certos organismos, como estrelas-do-mar, lagartos e lagostas, que são capazes de “regenerar” membros e caudas perdidos. Em essência, o tecido regenerado é indistinguível do original, com poucas ou nenhuma complicação ou efeito colateral, pelo fato de estar totalmente integrado ao corpo hospedeiro daquela espécie específica. Parece bom, não é?

Esse conceito não é novo. Prometeu, na mitologia grega, era um “deus menor” punido pelo “deus supremo” Zeus (por “dar” o fogo aos homens), que fazia animais devorarem seu corpo, apenas para que ele se regenerasse no dia seguinte. Alguns milhares de anos depois, o romance Frankenstein, de Mary Shelley, recebeu o subtítulo “O moderno Prometeu”. Esse livro, escrito há quase exatamente 200 anos, contém um forte alerta sobre a ciência sem limites e a busca imprudente do homem pela regeneração carnal. Mesmo assim, é fácil ver que o homem tem um longo histórico de desejo de regenerar o próprio corpo, assim como um mecânico troca peças ou uma estrela-do-mar faz crescer um novo braço.

Os avanços na anestesia, na farmacologia (em particular, nos antibióticos e nos medicamentos contra a rejeição), na cirurgia e nas técnicas de esterilização levaram a marcos na medicina, como o primeiro transplante de rim, em 1954, e o primeiro transplante de medula óssea, em 1968. Mas os transplantes tinham limitações — alguns tecidos lesionados e danificados ou órgãos complexos, como o cérebro, não podiam simplesmente ser substituídos. Além disso, devido ao envelhecimento da população e à enorme demanda pelas grandes quantidades necessárias de alguns tecidos, como a pele para vítimas de queimaduras, juntamente com uma escassez crônica de doadores adequados, eram necessárias alternativas. Ademais, a sombra sombria da rejeição de tecidos estava sempre presente e precisava ser enfrentada.

Há muito se sabe que, embora o feto seja um ser humano único, é raro que a mãe rejeite o filho em desenvolvimento. Aprendemos que isso se deve ao fato de que, nos fetos em desenvolvimento, suas células não possuem muitos identificadores únicos. À medida que uma pessoa envelhece, suas células adquirem uma aparência e uma identificação cada vez mais únicas — algo como a mesma impressão digital na superfície de cada célula do corpo. O corpo de uma pessoa “sabe” como é a “impressão digital” de seus próprios tecidos e “sabe” que aquilo que não lhe é próprio é estranho e precisa ser atacado. Com o uso de tecido fetal, praticamente não haveria risco de rejeição nem necessidade de medicamentos perigosos contra a rejeição por toda a vida. Pensava-se que o novo tecido seria totalmente assimilado. Assim, tentativas de usar tecido fetal foram feitas para curar doenças como a doença de Addison (tecido adrenal), na década de 1920, e o diabetes (tecido pancreático), a partir da década de 1930. Embora tenham sido usados até 24 fetos por transplante, os procedimentos acabaram se mostrando malsucedidos.1

Na década de 1990, voltou a haver interesse no uso de tecido fetal. Não seria maravilhoso, pensaram alguns cientistas, se bastasse inserir algumas células pancreáticas fetais produtoras de insulina sob os antebraços para curar o diabetes? O mesmo valeria para transplantes de tireoide fetal e de glândulas adrenais — um simples procedimento ambulatorial, realizado em poucos minutos. E quanto a tecidos cerebrais para tratar a doença de Parkinson ou o Alzheimer? O potencial parecia ilimitado.

Se isso parece um tanto macabro, havia um aspecto ainda mais sinistro. Experimentos com ratos demonstraram que era possível transplantar com êxito tecido ovariano fetal.2 A ideia era transplantar tecido ovariano fetal em mulheres inférteis (por exemplo, sobreviventes de câncer infantil cuja quimioterapia as havia deixado inférteis). Isso eliminaria qualquer “necessidade” de tratamentos de fertilização in vitro. Imagine ser uma criança nascida de uma mãe genética que foi abortada!

Em meio às batalhas culturais em torno do aborto, houve uma intensa pressão para encontrar uma “cura”. Suponhamos que houvesse uma cura para o Alzheimer ou o diabetes. Quantas pessoas rejeitariam essa cura se ela viesse de tecido fetal? Se de fato recusassem o tratamento, quantas dessas pessoas manifestariam sua oposição ao aborto se um familiar escolhesse um tratamento curativo (embora antiético)? Se um pai ou uma mãe recusasse tratamento para um filho diabético, isso seria considerado negligência infantil, e o Estado teria motivos para tratar a criança à força ou removê-la de casa até que recebesse tratamento? Em última análise, um dos objetivos era que o aborto fosse justificado na opinião da população.

Mas algo aconteceu: os tratamentos não funcionaram como previsto para um número significativo de pacientes. Os tratamentos aplicados a um grande número de pacientes com Parkinson foram descritos pelos próprios médicos responsáveis como “catastróficos”, “absolutamente devastadores” e “um verdadeiro pesadelo”.3 Em vez da rigidez muscular clássica associada à doença de Parkinson, surgiram cabeças que sacudiam, braços que se agitavam e corpos que se contorciam. O tecido não “sabia” quando devia desligar-se, produzindo neuro-hormônios em excesso e chegando a formar tumores de pele, cabelo e cartilagem.4 Além disso, o tecido que “pegou” acabou morrendo pelo mesmo processo que causou a doença de Parkinson.5 Os tratamentos foram obviamente interrompidos.

Mas, por volta dessa época, no final da década de 1990, foram descobertas técnicas que permitiam aos pesquisadores isolar e cultivar em grande quantidade um certo tipo de célula, chamada “célula-tronco”, obtida de embriões humanos. Imagine essas células-tronco de rápido crescimento como o caule de uma planta. É delas que se originam os outros tipos de células (folhas, flores e frutos). Esses embriões, exclusivamente humanos, eram obtidos de tratamentos de fertilidade “sobressalentes”, nos quais a concepção era iniciada numa placa de Petri (de vidro) em laboratório e deixada crescer até formar um aglomerado de células. As células desejadas eram retiradas, e o restante, destruído. (Em essência, eram “micro” abortos.)

O tecido fetal não funcionou como esperado, em parte porque já era especializado demais e estava “pré-programado” demais, mas também era impuro demais, caro demais e exigia trabalho demais — era necessário colher tecido de numerosos bebês abortados usando microscópio e pinças. Alguns cientistas pensaram: por que não obter essas células-tronco, “programá-las” para se tornarem o tipo de célula desejado e cultivá-las até se obter a quantidade necessária?

Na próxima edição, vou contar em que ponto se encontra atualmente a pesquisa, onde houve sucessos e fracassos, e como os cristãos podem navegar eticamente pelas águas turbulentas destes tempos. É impressionante como o Senhor abre caminhos, usando as maravilhas da ciência, para criar alternativas éticas para aqueles que permanecem fiéis a Ele e aos seus caminhos. Será empolgante explicar como essas “alternativas” se tornaram o principal foco de pesquisa e tratamento tanto para crentes quanto para não crentes.

Mas, antes de me despedir, gostaria de mencionar que, ao longo dos anos, várias pessoas comentaram que esses bebês seriam abortados de qualquer maneira; então, por que não tirar algum proveito da tragédia? Isso não seria, de certa forma, redentor?

Aqui está minha (breve lista de) razões pelas quais seria antibíblico que os cristãos se beneficiassem de vacinas antiéticas — e agora de tratamentos com tecido fetal:

  1. O ato de redenção não pode ser separado da restituição e da reconciliação. O próprio ato de usar tecido fetal apenas incentiva uma exploração maior e ampliada — exatamente o oposto da restituição e da reconciliação (que exigem uma resolução de não repetir o pecado). A história demonstrou que há multiplicação do pecado, não redução. Onde antes havia uma linhagem celular, agora há dezenas. Os cientistas se sentem encorajados a realizar pesquisas ainda mais antiéticas, sobretudo se não houver objeções.

  2. A própria palavra “redimir” significa resgatar algo que originalmente era seu, mas que se perdeu. O corpo do nascituro nunca foi nosso, desde o início; nunca nos coube entregá-lo, nem lucrar com ele.

  3. A redenção sempre envolve um sacrifício — de si mesmo. Como alguém pode sacrificar a si mesmo oferecendo o corpo de outra pessoa? (Hb 9:12) João 15:13 diz: Ninguém tem maior amor do que este: de dar alguém a sua vida pelos seus amigos. Alguns cristãos gostam de usar esse versículo para justificar ir à guerra. Embora haja, sem dúvida, autossacrifício em ir à guerra, o objetivo é fazer com que o inimigo entregue a SUA vida. O uso utilitário de tecido fetal segue a mesma linha de raciocínio, exceto que NÃO há autossacrifício algum na exploração do corpo de um bebê abortado.

  4. Embora a redenção da humanidade realizada por Jesus tenha transformado algo horrível e repugnante em algo que glorifica a Deus, ela foi um ato de santificação por meio da santidade e da justiça. Quanto a essa questão, não consigo pensar em ato mais distante da santificação, da santidade e da justiça — trata-se apenas de oportunismo. –ver Sl 111:9 e 1 Co 1:30

  5. Não podemos esperar que Deus nos livre do mal participando dele e nos beneficiando dele. Nossos pecados nos são perdoados somente quando perdoamos, não quando conspiramos juntos; somente quando retribuímos o mal com o bem. –ver Mt 5 e 6

  6. Deus considera abominável o derramamento de sangue inocente (Ele odeia isso!). –ver Pv 6:17. Só podemos agradar a Deus e receber expiação se nos purificarmos de qualquer associação com essa culpa — não participando dela. –ver Dt 21:8, 9. Alguém consegue imaginar usar produtos como sabão e cúpulas de abajur feitos com restos de vítimas do Holocausto que “morreriam de qualquer maneira”?

  7. Quando Saul destruiu os amalequitas, guardou o melhor do saque — supostamente como oferta a Deus (pelo menos foi o que disse quando Samuel o questionou). –ver 1Sm 15. Por que Deus rejeitou completamente seu rei ungido por causa disso? Será que não queria que seus escolhidos lucrassem ou se beneficiassem do mal — mesmo ao destruir esse mal? Será que, ao levar o despojo dos ímpios para o meio de seu povo escolhido, o povo corria o risco de ficar insensível àquela mesma perversidade e, assim, corromper-se? Samuel chorou e lamentou por Saul, clamando ao Senhor. Se não formos nós, então quem chorará por nós e por uma geração caída?

  8. O mesmo poderia ser dito sobre o julgamento do tesouro que Acã escondeu após a derrota em Ai. Em resumo, se houver algum benefício pessoal a obter após uma tragédia ou o julgamento de outra pessoa, a melhor maneira de saber se é legítimo é verificar se os detalhes não estão encobertos em segredo. (Porque o fruto do Espírito está em toda a bondade, justiça e verdade;) Aprovando o que é agradável ao Senhor. E não comuniqueis com as obras infrutuosas das trevas, mas antes condenai-as. –Ef 5:9-11

  9. Há alternativas — por que dar justificativa a práticas antiéticas? Quanto à busca de vacinas alternativas, é um processo difícil, mas não impossível. Seguir a Cristo muitas vezes significa trilhar um caminho mais árduo, em vez do caminho de menor resistência. O exemplo de nossos antepassados fiéis comprova isso.

Pocos entendían por qué vivía así.
«Renunciar a todo es una locura», decían.
No podían haber visto la paz que había dentro,
una paz que yo pensaba que nadie podría ocultar.
No deseaba vivir huyendo,
pero querían mi cuerpo para arrojarlo al fuego.
De cueva en cueva, llamaba hogar a cada una,
sabiendo que un día ya no vagaría más.
Al mirar atrás, no cambiaría nada.
Ha sido un gran honor servir a mi rey.
Pero ahora debo irme, el humo es demasiado espeso.
Mi cuerpo se convierte en cenizas mientras las llamas lo lamen.
Hay algo que necesito preguntar:
¿Moriré en vano, o asumirás la tarea?
Jesús busca hoy a un pueblo
que resista la prueba y no se desvíe.
Dar la vida es parte del precio.
¿Tomarás esa decisión antes de que se agote el tiempo?
La iglesia está en apuros; el mundo ha entrado.
Mataron a nuestro Jesús y aman su pecado.
No cedamos; hay demasiado en juego.
¡Más bien luchemos! ¡Hay un reino que conquistar!

–Barry Grant

I am Ted. I was born a male and I know I am a male. My skin color is white, and I know I am white. My parents are white, my grandparents were white, and I have no reason to suspect my other ancestors were anything other than white. These are foundational, irrefutable truths about myself. I do not think I am anything other than what I am. Nor do I desire to be anything other than what I am.

I am a Christian. In order to better define my faith—as there are many who profess Christianity—I am a “biblical” Christian. I believe that the Bible is the Word of God, that it is to be taken literally, and that it instructs a pattern and way of life that all believers should embrace. At the age of 24—after having lived a life of my own choosing and while searching for God who, if He was real, I wanted to know—I turned to Him and I was born again. My transformation as a new creation in Christ began immediately and it continues to this day. My faith in and relationship to Jesus Christ are as foundational and irrefutable as my gender and race.

I am writing in response to that which had been extensively covered by the secular media during the Spring and Summer of 2015: a man who reportedly, throughout his life, had considered himself a female and who had been “transitioning” into a woman; a white woman who had insisted that race is “fluid” and that she is black; and the redefinition of marriage by the Supreme Court of the United States of America affecting, as well, the definition of “family” for an entire nation. These are topics which simply cannot be minimized or otherwise ignored.

The white woman lacked much public support for her explanation of race. In fact, she was significantly ridiculed for her stance. This was not true, however, regarding gender identification or “gay” marriage and family issues, and one must wonder why. If a “genetically/physiologically-constructed” male can be accepted by others as a woman simply because that’s what he thinks he is, and if a man can “marry” a man and a woman can “marry” a woman and be accepted as a married couple by others under the premise of equal rights and because that’s what they want to do, why can’t a white woman be accepted as a black woman when she is convinced that she is black?

The question raised is one of reality. Even though I may think I am the greatest pianist and music composer of all times, the evidence simply does not support that conviction. Even though a white woman says she is black, the evidence likewise does not support that conviction. Also true is that of a man who says he is a woman. The genetic and physiological evidence does not support that conviction. Without the redefinition of marriage, two people of the same sex cannot be married. And regardless of definition, they cannot reproduce on their own, one of God’s primary purposes for marriage.

Without God, man does what is right in his own eyes. So-called “progressive thinking” is simply man’s attempt, given his rejection of God, at better understanding the world and better addressing and solving its problems. Essentially, “anything goes” based upon the latest of ideas.

A biblical Christian, however, believes that God has designed, has created, and is very much involved in the universe … even in the individual lives of people who live in it. There are absolutes. There is a distinction between right and wrong. There are moral values and—something that we frequently forget in these modern times—there is an eternity ahead. As a result of progressive thinking, Darwinism now replaces Creationism, within much of our education system, students as well as teachers who profess faith in the God of the Bible are ridiculed and are otherwise discriminated against, millions of pre-born babies (the politically correct prefer calling them “fetuses”) have been legally dismembered, burnt, crushed, suctioned and pharmacologically murdered (aborted), and no-fault divorce has ravaged the families of our nation. Just look at those things that used to be considered wrong or evil which are now a normal part of our “progressing” society.

And what about eternity? Doesn’t that matter anymore, either?

In response to the Supreme Court’s ruling on gay marriage, then-President Barack Obama, clearly one of our nation’s more powerful, progressive thinkers, indicated his desire that “religious people” respond accordingly by modifying their definition of marriage as well. Believing in the God of the Bible as the Creator of the universe and as the One who designed and ordained marriage as a life-long covenant between one man and one woman, I respectfully decline Mr. Obama’s request. As the world in its own fashion deviates from the design and will of God, a true believer in Christ is called to follow Him. Jesus said, Enter through the narrow gate. For wide is the gate and broad is the road that leads to destruction, and many enter through it. But small is the gate and narrow the road that leads to life, and only a few find it. –Mat 7:13-14 NIV

I am Ted. I am a white male. I am a Christian who desires not to belittle, mock, or otherwise mistreat those with whom I may disagree, but there will be disagreements. I am called to love God and to love my neighbor as myself, regardless of who my neighbor might be. My ultimate hope is not found in this world. It is found in eternity with Christ. And my prayer for others is that they, too, may come to know Him, receive forgiveness of their sins, be transformed into the people God so desires, and spend an eternity with Him. Mimi ni Ted. Nilizaliwa wa kiume, na ninajua kwamba mimi ni wa kiume. Rangi ya ngozi yangu ni nyeupe, na ninajua kwamba mimi ni mweupe. Wazazi wangu ni weupe, babu na nyanya zangu walikuwa weupe, na sina sababu ya kushuku kwamba mababu zangu wengine walikuwa wa rangi nyingine isipokuwa nyeupe. Haya ni ukweli wa msingi na usioweza kukanushwa kunihusu. Sidhani kwamba mimi ni kitu kingine isipokuwa kile nilicho. Wala sitamani kuwa kitu kingine isipokuwa kile nilicho.

Mimi ni Mkristo. Ili kufafanua zaidi imani yangu—kwa kuwa kuna wengi wanaodai kuwa Wakristo—mimi ni Mkristo wa “kibiblia.” Ninaamini kwamba Biblia ni Neno la Mungu, kwamba inapaswa kuchukuliwa kihalisi, na kwamba inafundisha mtindo na namna ya maisha ambayo waumini wote wanapaswa kuukumbatia. Nikiwa na umri wa miaka 24—baada ya kuishi maisha niliyochagua mwenyewe na nilipokuwa nikimtafuta Mungu ambaye, kama alikuwa halisi, nilitaka kumjua—nilimgeukia, nami nilizaliwa mara ya pili. Mabadiliko yangu kuwa kiumbe kipya katika Kristo yalianza mara moja na yanaendelea hadi leo. Imani yangu na uhusiano wangu na Yesu Kristo ni wa msingi na usioweza kukanushwa sawa na jinsia yangu na rangi yangu.

Ninaandika nikijibu yale yaliyokuwa yameripotiwa kwa kina na vyombo vya habari vya kilimwengu katika Majira ya Kuchipua na Majira ya Kiangazi ya mwaka 2015: mwanamume ambaye, kama ilivyoripotiwa, katika maisha yake yote alikuwa amejiona kuwa mwanamke na alikuwa “akibadili” kuwa mwanamke; mwanamke mweupe aliyesisitiza kwamba rangi ya kabila ni “inayobadilika” na kwamba yeye ni mweusi; na Mahakama Kuu ya Marekani kufafanua upya ndoa, jambo lililoathiri pia ufafanuzi wa “familia” kwa taifa zima. Haya ni mada ambazo haziwezi kupuuzwa au kupunguzwa umuhimu kwa namna yoyote.

Mwanamke huyo mweupe hakupata uungwaji mkono mkubwa kutoka kwa umma kwa maelezo yake kuhusu rangi ya kabila. Kwa kweli, alidhihakiwa sana kwa msimamo wake. Hata hivyo, haikuwa hivyo kuhusu utambulisho wa kijinsia au masuala ya ndoa ya “mashoga” na familia, na mtu lazima ajiulize kwa nini. Ikiwa mwanamume “aliyeumbwa kijenetiki/kifiziolojia” anaweza kukubaliwa na wengine kuwa mwanamke kwa sababu tu anafikiri hivyo ndivyo alivyo, na ikiwa mwanamume anaweza “kuoa” mwanamume na mwanamke anaweza “kuoa” mwanamke na wakakubaliwa na wengine kuwa wanandoa kwa msingi wa haki sawa na kwa sababu wanataka kufanya hivyo, kwa nini mwanamke mweupe hawezi kukubaliwa kuwa mwanamke mweusi anapokuwa na hakika kwamba yeye ni mweusi?

Swali linaloulizwa linahusu uhalisia. Hata kama ningeweza kufikiri kwamba mimi ndiye mpiga piano na mtunzi wa muziki mkuu kuliko wote, ushahidi hauungi mkono imani hiyo. Hata kama mwanamke mweupe anasema yeye ni mweusi, vivyo hivyo ushahidi hauungi mkono imani hiyo. Ndivyo ilivyo pia kwa mwanamume anayesema yeye ni mwanamke. Ushahidi wa kijenetiki na kifiziolojia hauungi mkono imani hiyo. Bila kufafanua upya ndoa, watu wawili wa jinsia moja hawawezi kuoana. Na bila kujali ufafanuzi, hawawezi kuzaa wenyewe, mojawapo ya makusudi makuu ya Mungu kwa ndoa.

Bila Mungu, mwanadamu hufanya yaliyo sawa machoni pake mwenyewe. “Mawazo ya kimaendeleo” yanayoitwa hivyo ni jaribio tu la mwanadamu, kutokana na kumkataa kwake Mungu, la kuelewa ulimwengu vizuri zaidi na kushughulikia na kutatua matatizo yake vizuri zaidi. Kimsingi, “chochote kinawezekana” kwa kutegemea mawazo mapya zaidi.

Hata hivyo, Mkristo wa kibiblia anaamini kwamba Mungu ameuunda na kuuleta ulimwengu kuwapo, na anahusika sana nao … hata katika maisha ya kibinafsi ya watu wanaoishi ndani yake. Kuna mambo ya hakika yasiyobadilika. Kuna tofauti kati ya mema na mabaya. Kuna maadili na—jambo ambalo mara nyingi tunalisahau katika nyakati hizi za kisasa—kuna umilele unaotungoja. Kutokana na mawazo ya kimaendeleo, sasa Darwinismu inachukua nafasi ya imani ya Uumbaji; katika sehemu kubwa ya mfumo wetu wa elimu, wanafunzi na walimu wanaokiri imani katika Mungu wa Biblia hudhihakiwa na kubaguliwa kwa njia nyingine; mamilioni ya watoto ambao bado hawajazaliwa (watu wanaopendelea lugha sahihi kisiasa hupendelea kuwaita “vijusi”) wamekatwa viungo, kuchomwa moto, kusagwa, kuvutwa kwa mashine na kuuawa kwa dawa (kutoa mimba) kisheria; na talaka isiyo na ulazima wa kuthibitisha kosa imeharibu familia za taifa letu. Tazameni tu mambo yale yaliyokuwa yakichukuliwa kuwa mabaya au maovu ambayo sasa ni sehemu ya kawaida ya jamii yetu “inayoendelea.”

Na vipi kuhusu umilele? Je, hilo pia halina umuhimu tena?

Kujibu uamuzi wa Mahakama Kuu kuhusu ndoa za mashoga, Rais wa wakati huo Barack Obama, ambaye kwa hakika alikuwa mmoja wa wanafikra wetu wenye nguvu zaidi na wanaoendeleza mawazo ya kimaendeleo, alionyesha nia yake kwamba “watu wa dini” nao wajibu ipasavyo kwa kurekebisha ufafanuzi wao wa ndoa. Kwa kuwa ninaamini katika Mungu wa Biblia kama Muumba wa ulimwengu na kama Yule aliyebuni na kuagiza ndoa iwe agano la maisha yote kati ya mwanamume mmoja na mwanamke mmoja, ninakataa kwa heshima ombi la Bw. Obama. Ulimwengu unapopotoka kwa namna yake mwenyewe kutoka kwa mpango na mapenzi ya Mungu, mwamini wa kweli katika Kristo ameitwa kumfuata. Yesu alisema, Ingieni kupitia lango jembamba. Kwa maana lango ni pana na njia ni kubwa iendayo kwenye uharibifu, nao ni wengi waingiao kwa hiyo. Lakini lango ni jembamba na njia ni nyembamba iendayo uzimani, nao ni wachache waionao. –Mt 7:13-14 NIV

Mimi ni Ted. Mimi ni mwanamume mweupe. Mimi ni Mkristo ambaye hatamani kuwadharau, kuwadhihaki, au kuwatendea vibaya kwa namna nyingine wale ambao huenda sikubaliani nao, lakini kutakuwa na kutokubaliana. Nimeitwa kumpenda Mungu na kumpenda jirani yangu kama nafsi yangu, bila kujali jirani yangu ni nani. Tumaini langu kuu halipatikani katika ulimwengu huu. Linapatikana katika umilele pamoja na Kristo. Nami ninawaombea wengine kwamba wao pia wapate kumjua, wapokee msamaha wa dhambi zao, wabadilishwe wawe watu ambao Mungu anatamani sana wawe, na watumie umilele pamoja naye. Huu si ujumbe maarufu unaopatikana katika vyombo vya habari vya kiliberali vya leo. Lakini kwa wale wanaopendezwa, kwa wale wanaotafuta kitu kilicho bora zaidi kuliko kile ambacho ulimwengu huu unaweza kutoa, Mungu ana jibu: Kwa maana jinsi hii Mungu aliupenda ulimwengu, hata akamtoa Mwanawe wa pekee, ili kila mtu amwaminiye asipotee, bali awe na uzima wa milele. –Yn 3:16

As a man was dying, his thoughts went back.
Will I leave a good mark, that none can attack?
I forsook all, on the alter I went
Keeping nothing back, not even a cent.
I wanted to do, all that was right.
I sometimes prayed, all through the night.
It was easy? I cannot say.
But rather a battle, I fought everyday.
Few understood why I lived this way.
Giving up everything was foolish they’d say.
They couldn’t have seen the peace inside.
A peace that I thought, no one could hide.
A life on the run, was not my desire.
But they wanted my body, to put in the fire.
From cave to cave, I would call home
Knowing one day, I’d never more roam.
As I look back, I wouldn’t change a thing.
It has been a great honor serving my king.
But I must go now, the smoke is too thick.
My body to ashes, as the flames lick.
There is one thing, I need to ask.
Will I die in vain, or will you take up the task?
Jesus is looking for A people today
That will stand the test, and not go astray.
Giving our life is part of the cost.
Will you make that decision, before time is lost?
The church is struggling, the world has come in.
They killed our Jesus, and love their sin.
Let’s not give in, there’s too much at stake.
But rather let’s fight! There’s a kingdom to take!

–Barry Grant

Als ein Mann im Sterben lag, gingen seine Gedanken zurück.
Werde ich eine gute Spur hinterlassen, die keiner angreifen kann?
Ich entsagte allem und trat an den Altar,
hielt nichts zurück, nicht einmal einen Cent.
Ich wollte alles tun, was recht war.
Manchmal betete ich die ganze Nacht.
War es leicht? Das kann ich nicht sagen.
Vielmehr war es ein Kampf, den ich täglich focht.
Nur wenige verstanden, warum ich so lebte.
Alles aufzugeben, sei töricht, sagten sie.
Sie konnten den Frieden in mir nicht sehen.
Einen Frieden, von dem ich dachte, niemand könne ihn verbergen.
Ein Leben auf der Flucht war nicht mein Wunsch.
Doch sie wollten meinen Körper ins Feuer werfen.
Von Höhle zu Höhle nannte ich mein Zuhause,
im Wissen, dass ich eines Tages nie wieder umherziehen würde.

Es war eine große Ehre, meinem König zu dienen.
Doch jetzt muss ich gehen, der Rauch ist zu dicht.
Mein Körper wird zu Asche, während die Flammen daran lecken.
Eines muss ich noch fragen:
Werde ich vergeblich sterben, oder übernehmt ihr die Aufgabe?
Jesus sucht heute ein Volk,
das die Prüfung besteht und nicht vom Weg abkommt.
Unser Leben hinzugeben, gehört zu dem Preis, den wir zahlen.
Wirst du diese Entscheidung treffen, bevor die Zeit abläuft?
Die Kirche kämpft, die Welt ist eingedrungen.
Sie haben unseren Jesus getötet und lieben ihre Sünde.
Geben wir nicht nach, zu viel steht auf dem Spiel.
Kämpfen wir lieber! Ein Königreich ist zu erobern!

–Barry Grant

When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said, It is finished: and he bowed his head, and gave up the ghost. –Joh 19:30

As we have been developing this article over the last year, we have become increasingly aware of a growing interest in this subject. Various papers and booklets have been, or are being, written about it. Some writings debate specific theories of the atonement, while others reason about various terms or Bible verses. What ideas and statements concerning the atonement are found in the clear teachings of Scripture, and which are misunderstandings or wrong interpretations?

I. The Atonement

The term atonement is usually understood to explain all or part of what happened spiritually (for the believer) when Christ went through His suffering, death, and resurrection. Sometimes the term atonement is used to define that which brings men and women to a place of “at-one-ment” (to be at one) with God. How does that event in history still affect us today, some 2,000 years later?

In these discussions, there is the tendency to forget that the finished work of Christ includes multiple aspects, with each one contributing to a different effect for the believer today. These different aspects include Christ’s Suffering, His Blood, His Death, His Burial, His Resurrection, and His Ascension.

a. His Suffering

His suffering covers the physical, emotional, and mental anguish He endured that culminated with His death on the cross. Here we see that …it behoved Christ to suffer, and to rise from the dead the third day … that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name… –Luk 24:46-47. The suffering servant, as portrayed in the whole of Isaiah chapter 53, gives a vivid picture of this aspect of the atonement. Isaiah describes Him as being …wounded for our transgressions, [and] …bruised for our iniquities: –Isa 53:5. Here we also have the reality that with his stripes we are healed. –Isa 53:5. Finally, we see that He was oppressed, and he was afflicted… –Isa 53:7, and that he endured … travail of his soul… –Isa 53:11

Let’s note a few more of the many passages that speak of His suffering: For Christ also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God… –1Pe 3:18; Though he were a Son, yet learned he obedience by the things which he suffered –Heb 5:8; For it became him, for whom are all things, and by whom are all things, in bringing many sons unto glory, to make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings –Heb 2:10.

A sometimes forgotten purpose of Jesus’ suffering is that, as believers, we are to identify with His suffering as given in the following passages: For as the sufferings of Christ abound in us, so our consolation also aboundeth by Christ –2Co 1:5; …if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together –Rom 8:17; That I may know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, being made conformable unto his death –Php 3:10.

b. His Blood that was Shed

The blood of Christ being shed for the atonement of sinful man needs some careful consideration as a specific vital aspect of the whole. Of course, it is included in points a. and c., but the Scriptures also give much attention to this particular part. It would perhaps require a whole book to expound on this aspect, but we should note one thing on this point. It is with the shedding of the blood of Jesus that we have God’s specific solution for the remission of our sins given here in Jesus’ own words, For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins –Mat 26:28.

In Hebrews chapters 9 and 10, we have very detailed explanation showing how the “blood sacrifices” of the Old Testament were not perfect in themselves, rather they were a “type” that pointed forward to the perfect sacrifice—Jesus, the Lamb of God. It is in this context that we have this—that …almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission. –Heb 9:22. This is particularly important to remember when we consider that some people claim that God could just simply forgive sin without death or the shedding of blood if He so chose. These people use the story found in Matthew 18:23-35 as their proof text. It would do us well to consider that this story is revealing the “why” (compassion) of the outcome, not the “how” of the details. We cannot take this story out of context of Scripture and build a doctrine that undermines all the rest of Scripture. Thus, we conclude that in God’s economy He has ordained that sin must be washed away with the blood of Christ—And from Jesus Christ, who … washed us from our sins in his own blood, –Rev 1:5.

For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God; Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus: Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God –Rom 3:23-25. Here we see that for anyone of us that has sinned (ALL of us), we have our propitiation made possible through faith in His (Jesus’) blood.

c. His Death

Jesus said, …I lay down my life for the sheep –Joh 10:15, and again He said, …I lay down my life, that I might take it again. No man taketh it from me, but I lay it down of myself. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it again… –Joh 10:17-18.

But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour; that he by the grace of God should taste death for every man. For it became him, for whom are all things, and by whom are all things, in bringing many sons unto glory, to make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings. –Heb 2:9-10. When you partake of communion …ye do shew the Lord’s death till he come –1Co 11:26.

Know ye not, that so many of us as were baptized into Jesus Christ were baptized into his death? Therefore we are buried with him by baptism into death: that like as Christ was raised up from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life. –Rom 6:3-4

It is during this period of Jesus’ time on earth that the earthly, mortal part of Him separated from that which was heavenly, eternal, and immortal.

d. His Burial

We note again, as referenced above, the truth that Therefore we are buried with him by baptism into death… –Rom. 6:4. While all these aspects are a part of the whole, the burial represents …a corn of wheat fall into the ground and die… –Joh 12:24. First is the ending of life (pouring out of the blood), then death, then burial, then resurrection. The burial part is the confirmation that death has occurred. It brings finality, closure, and an end to the former. It is the necessary interval between death and resurrection.

It is also the time of Jesus’ entrance into Hades, the place of departed souls, of which we are given only glimpses through several passages of Scripture.

e. His Resurrection

In His resurrection we are raised with Him in newness of life. (Romans 6:4) …wherein also ye are risen with him through the faith of the operation of God, who hath raised him from the dead –Col 2:12. So, in His resurrection we are raised up with Him from death (if we were dead prior) and are provided the power to walk in newness of life (the power to have victory over sin).

f. His Ascension

In His ascension we understand that …he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight. –Act 1:9. It is due to His leaving this earth that we have many key aspects for the believer’s life today. There is the provision of the Holy Spirit made possible once Jesus left this earth. We have the promise of His going to prepare a better home for us to someday join Him in everlasting joy. We have Jesus sitting at the right hand of the throne of God interceding for us. We have Jesus acting in the role of our sympathetic High Priest, one that knows and understands our every need and struggle, since He has the experience of living on the sinful earth inside a mortal body.

Herein, we start to see how each part of the Atonement achieves a different result for the believer and that each part is only that—A PART. A part of the whole. A part of the finished work of Christ. These lists could each go on and fill page after page of all the blessings and benefits each one enables for the believer. For the sake of space, we will stop on this part for now and continue with the rest of the article, but hopefully this will stimulate each of us to further meditation in God’s Word on these matters.

II. Common statements that are not Biblically correct

There are some popular statements which we may hear concerning the atonement that do not accurately describe what the Scriptures teach. But because they are popular in our conversations, or perhaps they’re even the words of a familiar song, they may skew our understanding of the finished work of Christ. For some examples, let’s look at the following statements:

a. “Christ took my place on Calvary.”

This may seem like a logical conclusion, because He died for us, …the just for the unjust… –1Pe 3:18. and He died that we might live. There is no question that it was for us, but the preposition, for, can be understood several different ways. It can mean in my place, or it can mean on my behalf. Most of Scripture clearly emphasizes that He died on my behalf, but less clear is the idea of a direct substitution. Emphasizing substitution leads us to the following concept: He died in my place, so I don’t need to. If this becomes the primary way of thinking about the atonement, we may miss what is equally important—that since He died, so I must also die with Him. See Rom 6:1-11

b. “The guilt of my sin was placed on Christ.”

There are passages that speak of Christ bearing our sins. So Christ was once offered to bear the sins of many… –Heb 9:28 and, Who his own self bare our sins in his own body on the tree… –1Pe 2:24. But what is the proper understanding of what it means to ‘bear (carry) our sins’? We do NOT find Scripture which supports the idea that the guilt of my sin was transferred to Christ. Christ offered Himself to be the sacrifice for sin (Heb 10:10-12), the propitiation for our sins (1Jo 2:1), to put away sin, even to be the forgiveness of sin. This great work of dealing with sin was accomplished without Him ever losing His condition as the Lamb without blemish.

There is one passage we should note on this topic, For he [God] hath made him [Jesus] to be sin for us, who [Jesus] knew no sin… –2Co 5:21. When we look at the Greek word in this verse translated as “sin” and compare this passage with all the other Scriptures, it seems the intended meaning for this phrase to be sin is more clearly defined as to be a sin offering. Christ’s soul was not blackened with the guilt of our sin, else He could not have retained His position … as of a lamb without blemish and without spot –1Pe 1:19. A proper understanding of the sense in which He took our sins is that He assumed the settlement for them.

c. “He took the wrath of God upon Himself.”

Concerning God’s wrath, we know that …he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him –Joh 3:36; …the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness –Rom 1:18; …and were by nature the children of wrath, even as others –Eph 2:3.

However, atonement was made, and then, in Romans, Much more then, being now justified by his blood, we shall be saved from wrath through him –Rom 5:9. So, it is clear that the wrath of God toward us on account of sin is now averted when we are justified by His blood. However, the Scriptures do not say that Christ suffered the wrath of God. It may seem like a logical conclusion that if wrath was averted, and atonement was being made, then God›s wrath for sin must have fallen upon Christ, but that is not so stated in the scriptures. If we look at the picture of Abraham offering up his son Isaac, there was no wrath on Abraham’s part. Finally, God was “in Christ, reconciling the world unto Himself” and here what is emphasized is that Christ’s sacrifice to put away sin demonstrates to us the great love that the Father has toward us.

d. “God no longer looks at me; all He sees is Christ.”

The atonement should not be viewed, as perhaps many do, as a cloak for sin (to cover it). It is also sometimes stated this way: “Since Christ died on the cross for my sin, and I believe in Him, now Christ’s righteousness is all that God sees. When God looks at me, He no longer sees my sin; all He sees is Christ’s righteousness.” There is a great deal of error in this view, and the fruit of it is that many become complacent and tolerant of sin in their own lives. Through the atonement in Christ, God has made available to us everything needed for cleansing and to be made holy, but no, God does not credit Christ’s righteousness to our account. God’s purpose in the atonement was to make us righteous by purging our sin. We are to reckon ourselves dead unto sin, alive unto God. This does not mean that we have attained to a state of perfection, but we allow the atonement to be continually effective in our life.

For now, in section III, we are making summary statements, and in sections IV and V we are simply putting subheadings in place. Lord willing, we can take more time to flesh each one out in a future article. Until then, we encourage each one to do your own Bible study to more fully understand the whole of Scriptures’ teaching on the subject. Finally, it is our sincere desire that each of us would take heed that we are not deceived by the many voices from without and from within that Satan wishes to use to turn the church of Jesus Christ away from …the faith which was once delivered unto the saints. –Jud 1:3

III. What the Atonement does NOT do

a. Does NOT transfer guilt from one to another

As we stated above, our guilt did not blacken the soul of Christ. He provided atonement that our sins might be forgiven. He made, or was made, an offering for sin, and He was wounded for our transgressions, and by this act our sin is purged, and our guilt is taken away, without Him becoming guilty in our place.

b. Does NOT transfer righteousness from one to another—from Christ to us

Through Jesus our Lord we receive, given unto us, all things that pertain to life and godliness. We can say that our righteousness is only in Him, but we don’t say that His righteousness is somehow credited to our account when we are deficient. See also below on the issue of walking in the Light.

c. Does NOT protect us from harm/Does not build a hedge of protection around us

Our Sovereign Father provides our protection according to His will. Our protection does not come from the atonement, rather it comes out of our relationship with God as we walk by faith in obedience and draw near to Him. God protects, according to His will, those who are His. There is no guarantee that bad things will not happen, rather God promises that He will be with His children through whatever He allows them to go through.

d. Does not keep Satan away from us

Our Father does that according to His will (see Job 1 and 2, also 1 Cor 10:13). We do not need to “plead the blood for our protection” as though the blood of Christ was a means to ward off evil powers. We have the armor of God, shield of faith, and the sword of the Spirit, with all prayer, to overcome the powers of darkness.

IV. What the Atonement DOES do

  1. It reconciles
  2. It prepares a sacrifice for sin
  3. It provides a sin offering
  4. It redeems
  5. It ransoms
  6. It provides forgiveness of sins
  7. It provides remission of sins
  8. It cleanses us
  9. It enables God to see us as blameless
  10. It makes us righteous in God’s sight
  11. It causes believers to become a part of God’s family
  12. It causes believers to become brothers and sisters

V. What ALL was finished

  1. His suffering
  2. His temptations
  3. His labors on earth—His preaching and teaching
  4. The sacrificial system—sacrifices, which can never take away sins –Heb 10:11
  5. The law—was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ… –Gal 3:24
  6. Limited access to God—And the veil of the temple was rent in twain… –Mar 15:38

Als Jesus nun den Essig genommen hatte, sprach er: Es ist vollbracht: Und er neigte das Haupt und verschied. –Joh 19:30

Während wir diesen Artikel im Laufe des vergangenen Jahres ausgearbeitet haben, ist uns ein wachsendes Interesse an diesem Thema immer stärker bewusst geworden. Verschiedene Abhandlungen und Broschüren wurden darüber geschrieben oder werden gerade verfasst. Einige Schriften erörtern bestimmte Theorien über die Versöhnung, während andere über verschiedene Begriffe oder Bibelverse nachdenken. Welche Vorstellungen und Aussagen über die Versöhnung finden sich in der klaren Lehre der Schrift, und welche sind Missverständnisse oder falsche Auslegungen?

I. Die Versöhnung

Der Begriff Versöhnung wird gewöhnlich so verstanden, dass er alles oder einen Teil dessen erklärt, was geistlich (für den Gläubigen) geschah, als Christus sein Leiden, seinen Tod und seine Auferstehung durchlebte. Manchmal wird der Begriff Versöhnung dazu verwendet, den Vorgang zu beschreiben, durch den Männer und Frauen in einen Zustand des Einsseins mit Gott kommen. Wie wirkt sich dieses Ereignis der Geschichte, rund 2.000 Jahre später, noch heute auf uns aus?

Bei diesen Gesprächen vergisst man leicht, dass das vollbrachte Werk Christi mehrere Aspekte umfasst, von denen jeder für den Gläubigen heute eine andere Wirkung hat. Zu diesen verschiedenen Aspekten gehören Christi Leiden, sein Blut, sein Tod, sein Begräbnis, seine Auferstehung und seine Himmelfahrt.

a. Sein Leiden

Sein Leiden umfasst die körperliche, seelische und geistige Qual, die er ertrug und die schließlich mit seinem Tod am Kreuz ihren Höhepunkt erreichte. Hier sehen wir: …Christus musste leiden und am dritten Tag von den Toten auferstehen … und in seinem Namen sollte Umkehr zur Vergebung der Sünden verkündigt werden… –Luk 24:46-47. Der leidende Knecht, wie er im gesamten Kapitel 53 des Jesajabuches dargestellt wird, vermittelt ein eindrückliches Bild dieses Aspekts der Versöhnung. Jesaja beschreibt ihn als den, der …um unserer Übertretungen willen verwundet [und] …um unserer Missetaten willen zerschlagen wurde: –Jes 53:5. Hier finden wir auch die Wirklichkeit, dass durch seine Striemen sind wir geheilt. –Jes 53:5. Schließlich sehen wir: Er wurde bedrängt und misshandelt… –Jes 53:7, und er ertrug …die Mühsal seiner Seele… –Jes 53:11

Beachten wir noch einige der vielen weiteren Stellen, die von seinem Leiden sprechen: Denn auch Christus hat einmal für die Sünden gelitten, der Gerechte für die Ungerechten, damit er uns zu Gott führe… –1Pe 3:18; Obwohl er Sohn war, lernte er an dem, was er litt, den Gehorsam –Heb 5:8; Denn es entsprach ihm, um dessentwillen alles ist und durch den alles ist, viele Söhne zur Herrlichkeit zu führen und den Urheber ihrer Errettung durch Leiden vollkommen zu machen –Heb 2:10.

Ein manchmal vergessener Zweck des Leidens Jesu ist, dass wir als Gläubige uns mit seinem Leiden identifizieren sollen, wie die folgenden Stellen zeigen: Wie die Leiden Christi in uns überreich sind, so ist auch unser Trost durch Christus überreich –2Co 1:5; …wenn wir tatsächlich mit ihm leiden, damit wir auch mit ihm verherrlicht werden –Rom 8:17; damit ich ihn erkenne und die Kraft seiner Auferstehung und die Gemeinschaft seiner Leiden, indem ich seinem Tod gleichgestaltet werde –Php 3:10.

b. Sein vergossenes Blut

Dass das Blut Christi zur Versöhnung des sündigen Menschen vergossen wurde, muss als ein wesentlicher Einzelaspekt des Ganzen sorgfältig bedacht werden. Natürlich ist dies in den Punkten a. und c. eingeschlossen, doch die Schrift widmet diesem besonderen Aspekt ebenfalls viel Aufmerksamkeit. Es würde vielleicht ein ganzes Buch erfordern, diesen Aspekt ausführlich zu behandeln, doch eines sollten wir dazu festhalten. Mit dem Vergießen des Blutes Jesu haben wir Gottes konkrete Lösung für die Vergebung unserer Sünden, die Jesus selbst mit diesen Worten nennt: Denn dies ist mein Blut des neuen Bundes, das für viele vergossen wird zur Vergebung der Sünden –Mat 26:28.

In den Kapiteln 9 und 10 des Hebräerbriefs wird sehr ausführlich erklärt, dass die „Blutopfer“ des Alten Testaments nicht an sich vollkommen waren, sondern ein „Vorbild“ darstellten, das auf das vollkommene Opfer hinwies – Jesus, das Lamm Gottes. In diesem Zusammenhang heißt es: …fast alles wird nach dem Gesetz mit Blut gereinigt, und ohne Blutvergießen gibt es keine Vergebung. –Heb 9:22. Das ist besonders wichtig, wenn wir bedenken, dass manche behaupten, Gott könne Sünde einfach ohne Tod oder Blutvergießen vergeben, wenn er es so wollte. Diese Menschen führen die Geschichte in Matthäus 18:23-35 als Belegstelle an. Wir sollten bedenken, dass diese Geschichte das „Warum“ (Mitgefühl) des Ergebnisses offenbart, nicht das „Wie“ der Einzelheiten. Wir dürfen diese Geschichte nicht aus dem Zusammenhang der Schrift lösen und eine Lehre aufstellen, die den übrigen Aussagen der Schrift widerspricht. Daher schließen wir, dass Gott in seiner Heilsordnung bestimmt hat, dass die Sünde durch das Blut Christi abgewaschen werden muss –und von Jesus Christus, der … uns mit seinem eigenen Blut von unseren Sünden gewaschen hat, –Off 1:5.

Alle haben gesündigt und ermangeln der Herrlichkeit Gottes; sie werden ohne Verdienst gerechtfertigt durch seine Gnade aufgrund der Erlösung, die in Christus Jesus ist. Ihn hat Gott durch den Glauben an sein Blut als Sühnemittel hingestellt, um seine Gerechtigkeit zu erweisen zur Vergebung der zuvor begangenen Sünden in der Geduld Gottes –Rom 3:23-25. Hier sehen wir: Für jeden von uns, der gesündigt hat (also für uns ALLE), ist durch den Glauben an sein (Jesu) Blut Sühnung möglich geworden.

c. Sein Tod

Jesus sagte: …ich lasse mein Leben für die Schafe –Joh 10:15, und noch einmal sagte er: …ich lasse mein Leben, damit ich es wieder nehme. Niemand nimmt es von mir, sondern ich lasse es von mir aus. Ich habe Vollmacht, es zu lassen, und habe Vollmacht, es wieder zu nehmen… –Joh 10:17-18.

Wir sehen aber Jesus, der ein wenig niedriger gemacht war als die Engel, wegen des Leidens des Todes mit Herrlichkeit und Ehre gekrönt, damit er durch Gottes Gnade für jeden den Tod schmecke. Denn es entsprach ihm, um dessentwillen alles ist und durch den alles ist, viele Söhne zur Herrlichkeit zu führen und den Urheber ihrer Errettung durch Leiden vollkommen zu machen. –Heb 2:9-10. Wenn ihr am Abendmahl teilnehmt, …verkündigt ihr den Tod des Herrn, bis er kommt –1Co 11:26.

Wisst ihr nicht, dass wir alle, die wir auf Christus Jesus getauft sind, auf seinen Tod getauft sind? So sind wir nun mit ihm begraben durch die Taufe in den Tod, damit, wie Christus durch die Herrlichkeit des Vaters von den Toten auferweckt worden ist, auch wir in einem neuen Leben wandeln. –Rom 6:3-4

In dieser Zeit von Jesu Leben auf Erden trennte sich sein irdischer, sterblicher Teil von dem, was himmlisch, ewig und unsterblich war.

d. Sein Begräbnis

Wir halten nochmals die oben angeführte Wahrheit fest: So sind wir nun mit ihm begraben durch die Taufe in den Tod… –Rom 6:4. Alle diese Aspekte gehören zwar zum Ganzen, doch das Begräbnis stellt …ein Weizenkorn dar, das in die Erde fällt und stirbt… –Joh 12:24. Zuerst kommt das Ende des Lebens (das Vergießen des Blutes), dann der Tod, dann das Begräbnis und danach die Auferstehung. Das Begräbnis bestätigt, dass der Tod eingetreten ist. Es bringt Endgültigkeit, Abschluss und das Ende des Vorherigen. Es ist die notwendige Zeitspanne zwischen Tod und Auferstehung.

Es ist auch die Zeit, in der Jesus in den Hades eintrat, den Ort der abgeschiedenen Seelen, von dem uns in mehreren Schriftstellen nur einzelne Einblicke gewährt werden.

e. Seine Auferstehung

Durch seine Auferstehung werden auch wir mit ihm zu einem neuen Leben auferweckt. (Römer 6:4) …in der ihr auch mit ihm auferweckt worden seid durch den Glauben an die wirksame Kraft Gottes, der ihn von den Toten auferweckt hat –Kol 2:12. In seiner Auferstehung werden also auch wir mit ihm vom Tod auferweckt (sofern wir zuvor tot waren) und erhalten die Kraft, in einem neuen Leben zu wandeln (die Kraft, über die Sünde zu siegen).

f. Seine Himmelfahrt

Bei seiner Himmelfahrt erkennen wir: …er wurde emporgehoben, und eine Wolke nahm ihn vor ihren Augen auf. –Apg 1:9. Weil er diese Erde verlassen hat, stehen dem Gläubigen heute viele wichtige Dinge zur Verfügung. Die Gabe des Heiligen Geistes wurde möglich, nachdem Jesus diese Erde verlassen hatte. Wir haben die Verheißung, dass er hingeht, um uns eine bessere Heimat zu bereiten, damit wir eines Tages zu ihm kommen und uns in ewiger Freude mit ihm vereinen können. Jesus sitzt zur Rechten des Thrones Gottes und tritt für uns ein. Jesus nimmt die Rolle unseres mitfühlenden Hohenpriesters ein, der alle unsere Bedürfnisse und Kämpfe kennt und versteht, weil er selbst auf der sündigen Erde in einem sterblichen Leib gelebt hat.

Hier beginnen wir zu erkennen, wie jeder Teil der Versöhnung für den Gläubigen ein anderes Ergebnis bewirkt und dass jeder Teil genau das ist – EIN TEIL. Ein Teil des Ganzen. Ein Teil des vollbrachten Werkes Christi. Diese Aufzählungen könnten jeweils noch Seite um Seite mit all den Segnungen und Vorzügen gefüllt werden, die jeder einzelne Teil dem Gläubigen ermöglicht. Der Kürze halber machen wir an dieser Stelle zunächst Schluss und setzen den restlichen Artikel fort. Hoffentlich regt dies jeden von uns dazu an, über diese Dinge im Wort Gottes weiter nachzusinnen.

II. Verbreitete Aussagen, die nicht mit der Bibel übereinstimmen

Es gibt einige verbreitete Aussagen über die Versöhnung, die wir vielleicht hören und die nicht genau wiedergeben, was die Schrift lehrt. Doch weil sie in unseren Gesprächen geläufig sind oder vielleicht sogar in einem bekannten Lied vorkommen, können sie unser Verständnis vom vollbrachten Werk Christi verzerren. Betrachten wir einige Beispiele:

a. „Christus nahm meinen Platz auf Golgatha ein.“

Das mag wie eine logische Schlussfolgerung erscheinen, denn er starb für uns, …der Gerechte für die Ungerechten… –1Pe 3:18. und er starb, damit wir leben könnten. Es steht außer Frage, dass er es für uns tat, doch die Präposition für kann auf verschiedene Weise verstanden werden. Sie kann an meiner Stelle oder zu meinen Gunsten bedeuten. Die Schrift betont eindeutig, dass er zu meinen Gunsten starb; weniger eindeutig ist die Vorstellung eines direkten Stellvertreters. Wenn wir die Stellvertretung betonen, gelangen wir zu folgendem Gedanken: Er starb an meiner Stelle, also muss ich nicht sterben. Wird dies zur vorherrschenden Sichtweise der Versöhnung, übersehen wir vielleicht, was ebenso wichtig ist: Weil er starb, muss auch ich mit ihm sterben. Siehe Röm 6:1-11

b. „Die Schuld meiner Sünde wurde Christus auferlegt.“

Es gibt Stellen, die davon sprechen, dass Christus unsere Sünden trug. So ist auch Christus einmal geopfert worden, um die Sünden vieler zu tragen… –Heb 9:28 und: Er hat unsere Sünden selbst an seinem Leib auf dem Holz getragen… –1Pe 2:24. Doch wie ist es richtig zu verstehen, was es bedeutet, unsere Sünden zu „tragen“? Wir finden in der Schrift KEINE Grundlage für die Vorstellung, dass die Schuld meiner Sünde auf Christus übertragen wurde. Christus gab sich selbst als Opfer für die Sünde hin (Heb 10:10-12), als Sühnemittel für unsere Sünden (1Jo 2:1), um die Sünde wegzuschaffen und sogar die Vergebung der Sünde zu sein. Dieses große Werk zur Bewältigung der Sünde wurde vollbracht, ohne dass er je seinen Zustand als makelloses Lamm verlor.

Zu diesem Thema sollten wir eine Stelle beachten: Den [Gott] hat er [Jesus], der von keiner Sünde wusste, für uns zur Sünde gemacht… –2Co 5:21. Wenn wir das griechische Wort betrachten, das in diesem Vers mit „Sünde“ übersetzt wird, und diese Stelle mit allen anderen Schriftstellen vergleichen, scheint die beabsichtigte Bedeutung der Wendung zur Sünde gemacht zu werden genauer zu einem Sündopfer gemacht zu werden zu sein. Die Seele Christi wurde nicht von der Schuld unserer Sünde befleckt, sonst hätte er seine Stellung …als eines Lammes ohne Fehler und ohne Flecken –1Pe 1:19. nicht bewahren können. Richtig verstanden, nahm er unsere Sünden in dem Sinne auf sich, dass er ihre Begleichung übernahm.

c. „Er nahm den Zorn Gottes auf sich.“

Über Gottes Zorn wissen wir: …wer dem Sohn nicht glaubt, wird das Leben nicht sehen, sondern der Zorn Gottes bleibt auf ihm –Joh 3:36; …der Zorn Gottes wird vom Himmel her offenbart gegen alle Gottlosigkeit und Ungerechtigkeit der Menschen, die die Wahrheit durch Ungerechtigkeit niederhalten –Rom 1:18; …und waren von Natur aus Kinder des Zorns wie auch die anderen –Eph 2:3.

Die Versöhnung wurde jedoch vollbracht, und dann heißt es im Römerbrief: Umso mehr werden wir, nachdem wir jetzt durch sein Blut gerechtfertigt sind, durch ihn vor dem Zorn gerettet werden –Rom 5:9. Es ist also klar, dass Gottes Zorn über uns wegen der Sünde abgewendet ist, wenn wir durch sein Blut gerechtfertigt sind. Die Schrift sagt jedoch nicht, dass Christus den Zorn Gottes erlitt. Es mag wie eine logische Schlussfolgerung erscheinen, dass Gottes Zorn über die Sünde auf Christus gefallen sein müsse, wenn der Zorn abgewendet und die Versöhnung vollbracht wurde; doch das wird in der Schrift nicht gesagt. Betrachten wir das Bild von Abraham, der seinen Sohn Isaak darbrachte: Abraham war nicht zornig. Schließlich war Gott „in Christus und versöhnte die Welt mit sich“, und hier wird betont, dass Christi Opfer, durch das die Sünde beseitigt wird, uns die große Liebe zeigt, die der Vater zu uns hat.

d. „Gott sieht nicht mehr mich; er sieht nur noch Christus.“

Die Versöhnung sollte nicht, wie es vielleicht viele tun, als Tarnung für die Sünde (um sie zu bedecken) betrachtet werden. Manchmal wird es auch so ausgedrückt: „Da Christus für meine Sünde am Kreuz gestorben ist und ich an ihn glaube, sieht Gott jetzt nur noch Christi Gerechtigkeit. Wenn Gott mich ansieht, sieht er meine Sünde nicht mehr; er sieht nur noch Christi Gerechtigkeit.“ Diese Auffassung enthält viele Irrtümer, und ihre Folge ist, dass viele in ihrem eigenen Leben gegenüber der Sünde gleichgültig und nachsichtig werden. Durch die Versöhnung in Christus hat Gott uns alles zugänglich gemacht, was zur Reinigung und Heiligung nötig ist. Aber nein: Gott rechnet uns Christi Gerechtigkeit nicht an. Gottes Ziel mit der Versöhnung war, uns gerecht zu machen, indem er unsere Sünde tilgt. Wir sollen uns der Sünde für tot halten, Gott aber lebendig. Das bedeutet nicht, dass wir einen Zustand der Vollkommenheit erreicht hätten; vielmehr lassen wir die Versöhnung in unserem Leben fortwährend wirksam sein.

In Abschnitt III geben wir vorerst zusammenfassende Aussagen, und in den Abschnitten IV und V setzen wir lediglich Zwischenüberschriften. So der Herr will, können wir jede davon in einem zukünftigen Artikel ausführlicher behandeln. Bis dahin ermutigen wir jeden von euch, selbst die Bibel zu studieren, um die gesamte Lehre der Schrift zu diesem Thema besser zu verstehen. Schließlich ist es unser aufrichtiger Wunsch, dass jeder von uns darauf achte, sich nicht von den vielen Stimmen von außen und innen täuschen zu lassen, die Satan dazu benutzen möchte, die Gemeinde Jesu Christi von …dem Glauben abzubringen, der den Heiligen ein für alle Mal überliefert worden ist. –Jud 1:3

III. Was die Versöhnung NICHT bewirkt

a. Sie überträgt NICHT die Schuld von einem auf einen anderen

Wie oben gesagt, befleckte unsere Schuld die Seele Christi nicht. Er bewirkte die Versöhnung, damit unsere Sünden vergeben werden könnten. Er brachte ein Opfer für die Sünde dar oder wurde selbst zu einem solchen Opfer, und er wurde um unserer Übertretungen willen verwundet. Durch diese Tat wird unsere Sünde getilgt und unsere Schuld weggenommen, ohne dass er an unserer Stelle schuldig wird.

b. Sie überträgt NICHT Gerechtigkeit von einem auf einen anderen – von Christus auf uns

Durch Jesus, unseren Herrn, empfangen wir alles, was zum Leben und zur Gottseligkeit gehört. Wir können sagen, dass unsere Gerechtigkeit allein in ihm liegt; wir sagen aber nicht, dass seine Gerechtigkeit uns irgendwie angerechnet wird, wenn es uns daran mangelt. Siehe weiter unten auch den Abschnitt über das Wandeln im Licht.

c. Sie bewahrt uns NICHT vor Schaden / errichtet keinen Schutzwall um uns

Unser souveräner Vater beschützt uns nach seinem Willen. Unser Schutz kommt nicht durch die Versöhnung, sondern aus unserer Beziehung zu Gott, während wir im Glauben gehorsam wandeln und uns ihm nahen. Gott beschützt nach seinem Willen die, die ihm gehören. Es gibt keine Garantie, dass keine schlimmen Dinge geschehen werden; vielmehr verspricht Gott, dass er bei seinen Kindern sein wird, in allem, was er ihnen durchzumachen erlaubt.

d. Sie hält Satan nicht von uns fern

Unser Vater tut das nach seinem Willen (siehe Hiob 1 und 2 sowie 1 Kor 10:13). Wir müssen nicht „das Blut zu unserem Schutz anrufen“, als wäre das Blut Christi ein Mittel, um böse Mächte abzuwehren. Wir haben die Waffenrüstung Gottes, den Schild des Glaubens und das Schwert des Geistes sowie alles Gebet, um die Mächte der Finsternis zu überwinden.

IV. Was die Versöhnung bewirkt

  1. Sie versöhnt
  2. Sie stellt ein Opfer für die Sünde bereit
  3. Sie stellt ein Sündopfer bereit
  4. Sie erlöst
  5. Sie kauft los
  6. Sie ermöglicht die Vergebung der Sünden
  7. Sie ermöglicht den Erlass der Sünden
  8. Sie reinigt uns
  9. Sie ermöglicht es Gott, uns als untadelig zu sehen
  10. Sie macht uns in Gottes Augen gerecht
  11. Sie bewirkt, dass Gläubige Teil der Familie Gottes werden
  12. Sie bewirkt, dass Gläubige Brüder und Schwestern werden

V. Was ALLES vollbracht war

  1. Sein Leiden
  2. Seine Versuchungen
  3. Sein Wirken auf Erden – sein Predigen und Lehren
  4. Das Opfersystem – Opfer, die niemals Sünden wegnehmen können –Heb 10:11
  5. Das Gesetz – war unser Erzieher, der uns zu Christus führen sollte… –Gal 3:24
  6. Der eingeschränkte Zugang zu Gott – Und der Vorhang des Tempels zerriss in zwei Stücke… –Mar 15:38

Mile after mile sped by as Carol drove the old Chevy along the busy interstate highway toward home. Between intervals of silence and conversation, Carol and her two sisters, Elaine and Gloria, lifted their voices in song, giving thanks and praise to their Creator. How thankful they were for the opportunity to spend the evening with their friends at Pine Creek Church and to receive another inspiring message from God’s Word.

Suddenly their smooth travel was interrupted by signs of trouble. “Now what can be wrong with this car?” Carol worried out loud as she guided the stalled car to the side of the road. “Oh, no, girls, we’re out of gas! I was in such a hurry this evening that I forgot to check the gauge. I thought the tank was almost full when we left home, and… Oh no!” wailed Carol again. “Dad put the cell phone on the counter for me to take along, and I forgot that also!”

“Whatever are we going to do now?” exclaimed Elaine. “Here we are, stranded in the dark, no gas, no phone, and seven more miles to our exit! And another thing, people just don’t stop very quickly these days and offer help. They know that most everyone carries a phone. This seems almost impossible to me!” she mournfully uttered from the back seat.

As the girls lapsed into silence, the old Chevy seemed to shake in protest as a long row of trucks whizzed by. “You know,” said Gloria, “I was just remembering Brother Lester’s message this evening. How can we forget so quickly! Maybe God has allowed this to happen to us so our faith might be increased as we place our trust in Him. Let’s take this to the Lord in prayer. Let’s look for a miracle from God’s hand.”

Together the girls bowed their heads and pled for the Lord’s protection and help.

“You know, I feel better already,” smiled Elaine. “I was so worried and fearful, but since we prayed and committed everything to God, I have confidence that He will watch over us. I’m so glad we have a God who hears all of our cries. What would we do without His comforting Holy Spirit? Let’s sing again.”

“Joys are flowing like a river,
Since the Comforter has come;
He abides with us forever,
Makes the trusting heart His home.
Blessed quietness, holy quietness,
Blest assurance in my soul!
On the stormy sea Jesus speaks to me,
And the billows cease to roll!”

-Manie P. Ferguson, 19th century

As the girls sang song after song, their hearts were deeply stirred. How quiet and peaceful they felt, even though they were stranded on a dark highway thirteen miles from home. Car after car, and truck after truck sped by without stopping. Then they noticed a pickup truck, with two dirt bikes on the back, slowing down. It pulled off the road several hundred feet ahead of them, and slowly began to back up. The girls’ voices were stilled in silence as they desperately cried out to God from the bottom of their hearts. When the truck came to a halt, two husky, long-haired men jumped out. Carol rolled her window down as a man wearing a red-checked flannel jacket approached.

“What’s the trouble here, girls?” he asked, glancing over the car.

“We’re out of gas,” Carol quickly replied.

“Well, I’d say we’re pretty lucky. We have a can of gas with us. How far do you need to go yet?”

“About thirteen miles.”

“Good. We’ll just pour some of our gas into your tank and you can be on your way again. No payment necessary.”

“O thank you so much,” responded Carol. “We were praying that God would send us help, and He did more than we could ever have thought! Thanks so much.”

“Yes, yes”, replied the man gruffly, “You’re pretty lucky we came along. We’re just glad to help you out.”

Several minutes later, the girls were on their way again. “You know,” said Carol, “when I saw that truck pull over, I was scared and glad at the same time. I began to scold myself again for not having that cell phone with me. But then I asked God to help me completely trust in Him and not be afraid. After all, isn’t He much more dependable than any cell phone? This has been such a faith booster for me. How different this may have turned out, if we had depended solely on our cell phones or “good luck” as those men called it. It must grieve our Father’s heart tremendously when we do not place our trust in Him.”

“It’s just as Brother Lester preached this evening”, added Gloria. “Remember some of those verses? I waited patiently for the LORD; and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry … And he hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God… Blessed is that man that maketh the LORD his trust, and respecteth not the proud, nor such as turn aside to lies. –Psa 40:1-4. This makes me so happy I just want to keep singing and thanking the Lord!”

Again, the girls raised their voices in song:

“His eye is always watching,
His ear is keen to hear;
His love is all-sufficient
To calm the gravest fear.
Then trust Him in shine and shade;
Trust Him, be not afraid:
He’s walking close beside thee;
His hand will safely guide thee;
His wings securely hide thee;
Then trust! Be not afraid.”

-Charles H. Gabriel, 1856-1932

اور موجوں کا اٹھنا تھم جاتا ہے!“

-مینی پی فرگوسن، انیسویں صدی

لڑکیاں یکے بعد دیگرے گیت گاتی رہیں اور ان کے دل گہرائی تک چھو گئے۔ وہ کتنی پرسکون اور مطمئن محسوس کر رہی تھیں، حالاں کہ وہ گھر سے تیرہ میل دور ایک تاریک شاہراہ پر پھنسی ہوئی تھیں۔ ایک کے بعد ایک کار اور ٹرک بغیر رکے تیزی سے گزر گئے۔ پھر انہوں نے دیکھا کہ ایک پک اَپ ٹرک، جس کے پچھلے حصے پر دو ڈرٹ بائیکیں تھیں، رفتار کم کر رہا ہے۔ وہ ان سے کئی سو فٹ آگے سڑک سے ہٹ کر رکا اور آہستہ آہستہ پیچھے آنے لگا۔ لڑکیوں کی آوازیں خاموش ہو گئیں اور وہ اپنے دل کی گہرائیوں سے شدت کے ساتھ خدا کو پکارنے لگیں۔ ٹرک رکا تو دو مضبوط جسامت کے لمبے بالوں والے آدمی باہر کودے۔ سرخ چیک والی فلالین جیکٹ پہنے ایک آدمی قریب آیا تو کیرول نے اپنی کھڑکی نیچے کر دی۔

”لڑکیو، یہاں کیا مسئلہ ہے؟“ اس نے گاڑی پر نظر ڈالتے ہوئے پوچھا۔

”ہمارا پٹرول ختم ہو گیا ہے،“ کیرول نے فوراً جواب دیا۔

”خیر، میں تو کہوں گا کہ ہماری قسمت اچھی ہے۔ ہمارے پاس پٹرول کا ایک کین ہے۔ تمہیں ابھی کتنی دور جانا ہے؟“

”تقریباً تیرہ میل۔“

”اچھا۔ ہم اپنے پٹرول میں سے کچھ تمہارے ٹینک میں ڈال دیتے ہیں، پھر تم دوبارہ روانہ ہو سکتی ہو۔ کوئی پیسے دینے کی ضرورت نہیں۔“

”اوہ، آپ کا بہت بہت شکریہ،“ کیرول نے جواب دیا۔ ”ہم دعا کر رہے تھے کہ خدا ہماری مدد کے لیے کسی کو بھیجے، اور اُس نے ہماری سوچ سے بھی بڑھ کر کیا! بہت شکریہ۔“

”ہاں، ہاں،“ آدمی نے کھردری آواز میں جواب دیا، ”تم خوش قسمت ہو کہ ہم ادھر سے گزرے۔ ہمیں تمہاری مدد کرکے خوشی ہوئی۔“

چند منٹ بعد لڑکیاں پھر سے سفر پر روانہ ہو گئیں۔ ”تمہیں معلوم ہے،“ کیرول نے کہا، ”جب میں نے اُس ٹرک کو سڑک کے کنارے رکتے دیکھا تو میں ایک ہی وقت میں ڈر بھی گئی اور خوش بھی ہوئی۔ میں نے پھر خود کو ڈانٹنا شروع کر دیا کہ موبائل فون ساتھ نہیں لائی۔ لیکن پھر میں نے خدا سے کہا کہ وہ میری مدد کرے تاکہ میں اُس پر پورا بھروسا کروں اور خوف زدہ نہ ہوں۔ آخر، کیا وہ کسی بھی موبائل فون سے کہیں زیادہ قابلِ بھروسا نہیں؟ اس تجربے نے میرے ایمان کو بہت تقویت دی ہے۔ اگر ہم صرف اپنے موبائل فون یا ’اچھی قسمت‘ پر بھروسا کرتے، جیسا کہ ان آدمیوں نے اسے کہا، تو نتیجہ کتنا مختلف ہو سکتا تھا۔ جب ہم اُس پر بھروسا نہیں کرتے تو یقیناً ہمارے باپ کا دل بہت رنجیدہ ہوتا ہوگا۔“

”یہ بالکل ویسا ہی ہے جیسا بھائی لیسٹر نے آج شام وعظ میں کہا تھا،“ گلوریا نے مزید کہا۔ ”کیا تمہیں ان آیات میں سے کچھ یاد ہیں؟ میں نے صبر سے خداوند کا انتظار کیا؛ اور اُس نے میری طرف جھک کر میری فریاد سنی۔۔۔ اُس نے میرے منہ میں ایک نیا گیت، ہمارے خدا کی حمد، ڈال دیا۔۔۔ مبارک ہے وہ آدمی جو خداوند پر بھروسا رکھتا ہے، اور جو مغروروں اور جھوٹ کی طرف پھرنے والوں کی طرف مائل نہیں ہوتا۔ –زبور 40:1-4۔ یہ بات مجھے اتنی خوش کرتی ہے کہ میرا دل چاہتا ہے کہ گاتی اور خداوند کا شکر کرتی رہوں!“

لڑکیوں نے پھر گیت گانا شروع کیا:

”اُس کی آنکھ ہمیشہ نگہبان ہے،
اُس کا کان سننے کے لیے تیز ہے؛
اُس کی محبت ہر خوف کو
دور کرنے کے لیے کافی ہے۔
پس دھوپ ہو یا چھاؤں، اُس پر بھروسا رکھ؛
اُس پر بھروسا رکھ، خوف نہ کر:
وہ تیرے بالکل ساتھ ساتھ چلتا ہے؛
اُس کا ہاتھ تجھے محفوظ راہ دکھائے گا؛
اُس کے پَر تجھے محفوظ چھپائیں گے؛
پس بھروسا رکھ! خوف نہ کر۔“

-چارلس ایچ گیبریل، 1856-1932

As a man was dying, his thoughts went back.
Will I leave a good mark, that none can attack?
I forsook all, on the alter I went
Keeping nothing back, not even a cent.
I wanted to do, all that was right.
I sometimes prayed, all through the night.
It was easy? I cannot say.
But rather a battle, I fought everyday.
Few understood why I lived this way.
Giving up everything was foolish they’d say.
They couldn’t have seen the peace inside.
A peace that I thought, no one could hide.
A life on the run, was not my desire.
But they wanted my body, to put in the fire.
From cave to cave, I would call home
Knowing one day, I’d never more roam.
As I look back, I wouldn’t change a thing.
It has been a great honor serving my king.
But I must go now, the smoke is too thick.
My body to ashes, as the flames lick.
There is one thing, I need to ask.
Will I die in vain, or will you take up the task?
Jesus is looking for A people today
That will stand the test, and not go astray.
Giving our life is part of the cost.
Will you make that decision, before time is lost?
The church is struggling, the world has come in.
They killed our Jesus, and love their sin.
Let’s not give in, there’s too much at stake.
But rather let’s fight! There’s a kingdom to take!

–Barry Grant

ثمة أمر واحد أحتاج إلى أن أسأل عنه.

بذل حياتنا جزء من الثمن.

الكنيسة تكافح، والعالم قد دخل إليها.
