Molte donne qui nella contea di Holmes, in Ohio, mi hanno detto che abbiamo ottimi negozi di beneficenza e di articoli di seconda mano, come spesso accade nei luoghi in cui vivono numerosi gruppi di persone semplici. Sono venute persone da ogni parte per visitarci, dedicando del tempo in più a passare da questi negozi. A quanto pare, qui la gente ama tenere le cose in ottimo stato, così, al primo segno di usura, si dice: «Via il vecchio, dentro il nuovo».

Allo stesso modo, nessun agricoltore contesterebbe che vedere tutti i propri macchinari funzionare alla perfezione e tutto il bestiame rimanere sano sia una sensazione appagante. Fin dai tempi di Adamo, il Signore ci ha sempre fatti così: …abbiate dominio sui pesci del mare, sugli uccelli del cielo e su ogni essere vivente che si muove sulla terra. –Gen 1:28

Un atteggiamento opposto va evitato. Giuda ci esorta a guardarci da «certi uomini» che, in mezzo a noi, «si sono insinuati di nascosto». Vivono secondo la carne e «disprezzano l’autorità». Duemila anni dopo, persino nella nostra società eccessivamente disinvolta, dove «va tutto bene» e dobbiamo «rilassarci e basta», il Signore si aspetta ancora che prendiamo sul serio la nostra chiamata a esercitare la responsabilità del dominio affidataci da Dio, usando i principi biblici in tutto ciò che facciamo.

Questo dominio si estende anche ai nostri corpi? Nel Secondo libro delle Cronache, capitolo 34, leggiamo delle condizioni deplorevoli in cui si trovava il Tempio all’inizio del regno del re Giosia e di come egli lo ricostruì sia materialmente, con pietre e legname lavorati con maestria dagli artigiani, sia spiritualmente, riscoprendo e assimilando la Parola di Dio. Allo stesso modo dovremmo prenderci cura dei nostri corpi, come ci insegna l’apostolo Paolo: Che? Non sapete che il vostro corpo è il tempio dello Spirito Santo che è in voi, il quale avete ricevuto da Dio, e che non appartenete a voi stessi? Poiché siete stati comprati a caro prezzo: glorificate dunque Dio nel vostro corpo e nel vostro spirito, che appartengono a Dio. –1Co 6:19-20

Si può affermare con sicurezza che, a giudicare dalla moltitudine di integratori alimentari, chiropratici, medici e altre figure e prodotti di assistenza sanitaria complementare (supplementare), ci impegniamo molto per mantenere i nostri templi fisici ben curati e in salute. Tuttavia, poiché siamo tutti nati sotto la maledizione di Adamo, a differenza dei componenti di una macchina, che si possono semplicemente sostituire, o di una macchina nuova che si può acquistare quando quella vecchia ha concluso il suo ciclo di vita, dobbiamo fare i conti con la realtà che anche le parti del nostro corpo hanno una «durata di conservazione» pratica. Più invecchiamo, più è evidente che la vita è molto limitata. La Bibbia parla di 70-80 anni (–vedi Sal 90:10). (In America, nel 2018, la media era di 78,7 anni. Ben poco è cambiato in oltre tre millenni!)

Credo che tutti possiamo convenire che Dio si preoccupa soprattutto del tempio spirituale, ancora più del tempio fisico costituito dai nostri corpi. Non occorre riflettere a lungo per trovare uomini e donne pii dei nostri giorni e i nostri padri spirituali di un tempo che hanno sacrificato e sopportato la distruzione dei propri corpi, glorificando Dio e ottenendo così la purificazione delle loro anime e la futura glorificazione dei loro corpi. La loro supplica era questa: Crea in me, o Dio, un cuore puro, e rinnova dentro di me uno spirito saldo. –Sal 51:10

Cristo stesso sopportò la distruzione del Suo corpo fisico, dicendo: …Distruggete questo tempio e in tre giorni lo farò risorgere. –Gv 2:19. Nella risurrezione, il suo corpo fu rigenerato. Nelle Scritture leggiamo anche di un’altra rigenerazione fisica, in cui la terra darà alla luce i suoi morti e quanti dimorano nella polvere [si] sveglieranno e grideranno di gioia! (–vedi Is 26:19)

Eppure, nonostante tutto questo, quando i nostri corpi cedono o si logorano, tentiamo debolmente, con un successo limitato, una rigenerazione fisica per conto nostro. Esiste un intero campo di studi incentrato sulla Medicina rigenerativa. La parola «rigenerazione» significa letteralmente «rifare la genesi», ricreando un corpo nuovo: un obiettivo davvero ambizioso!

C’è qualcosa di sbagliato nel sostituire le parti rotte (ginocchia, anche e gomiti), riparare le parti lesionate (ossa e pelle) e mantenersi generalmente in salute (con una buona alimentazione e l’attività fisica)? Certamente no: è così che mi guadagno da vivere, consigliando e curando i miei pazienti! Eppure, come per la maggior parte delle cose, anche il perseguimento della «buona salute» dovrebbe indurci a fermarci a «calcolare il costo» e a esercitare moderazione: La vostra moderazione sia nota a tutti gli uomini. Il Signore è vicino. –Fl 4:5. Perché, se perseguire la salute fisica è una cosa buona, farlo ciecamente e senza considerare i costi spirituali (come abbiamo scoperto nella nostra serie sui vaccini) può portarci fuori strada e lontano da Dio.

Su questa strada verso la salute fisica, la salute spirituale e il benessere complessivo, ci sono due fossati. Da una parte, nel fossato, possiamo essere irresponsabili riguardo alla nostra salute, lasciando che il tempio del nostro corpo si deteriori prematuramente. Giobbe disse dell’uomo: Giacché i suoi giorni sono stabiliti, il numero dei suoi mesi è presso di te; tu gli hai fissato un limite che non può oltrepassare; –Gb 14:5. Se dunque, per negligenza, cerchiamo di accorciare quei giorni, non siamo in sfida a Dio, cercando di vanificare la Sua perfetta volontà per noi? Nell’altro fossato c’è la ricerca irresponsabile e vana dell’immortalità, perseguendo la salute fisica a qualunque costo. Così facendo, non è forse anche questo un atto di sfida? Paolo ci ricorda: Perciò, come per mezzo di un solo uomo il peccato è entrato nel mondo, e per mezzo del peccato la morte, e così la morte è passata su tutti gli uomini, perché tutti hanno peccato: –Ro 5:12. In altre parole, a causa del peccato, il piano di Dio per noi è che moriamo fisicamente (affinché possiamo vivere eternamente con Lui).

A questo punto, la maggior parte dei lettori sarebbe d’accordo che i due estremi hanno questo in comune: trascurano entrambi la salute spirituale di una persona e sono entrambi in uno stato di sfida a Dio. Dove voglio arrivare? La maggior parte dei cristiani che conosco non persegue la salute fisica a qualunque costo. Abbiate pazienza, dunque, mentre vorrei dedicare il resto di questo articolo (e il prossimo) a raccontarvi la storia della Medicina rigenerativa, questo «rifare la genesi». È all’altezza delle sue promesse? Ci sono truffe? Quali sono le insidie? Che cosa riserva il futuro? E, soprattutto, che impatto ha sulla nostra salute spirituale e sul nostro rapporto con il Signore?

Per prima cosa, che cos’è esattamente la Medicina rigenerativa? Come ho accennato prima, significa letteralmente gli sforzi dell’uomo per «rifare» la genesi (l’origine, la creazione o l’inizio). Il termine è stato usato per la prima volta solo negli anni Novanta ed è definito come lo studio e la pratica della «sostituzione o rigenerazione di cellule, tessuti o organi umani, al fine di ripristinare o stabilire una funzione normale». Nella sua breve storia, per riuscirci sono stati impiegati tutti i mezzi possibili.

È diversa dalla Medicina dei trapianti, in cui vengono sostituiti organi interi, ma il corpo che li riceve continua a considerarli «estranei». Per questo sono necessari potenti farmaci antirigetto per il resto della vita della persona. È diversa anche dalla Medicina ortopedica, in cui dispositivi, come viti e ginocchia di titanio, per esempio, fissano e sostituiscono parti usurate. La Medicina rigenerativa si ispira al fenomeno naturale osservabile in alcuni organismi, come stelle marine, lucertole e aragoste, capaci di «rigenerare» arti e code mancanti. In sostanza, il tessuto rigenerato è indistinguibile da quello originale e presenta poche o nessuna complicazione o effetto collaterale, poiché si integra completamente nell’organismo ospite di quella specifica specie. Sembra una buona cosa, vero?

Non è un concetto nuovo. Nella mitologia greca, Prometeo era un «dio minore», punito dal «dio supremo» Zeus (per aver «dato» il fuoco agli uomini): gli animali si nutrivano del suo corpo, che però si rigenerava il giorno dopo. Un paio di migliaia di anni più tardi, il romanzo di Mary Shelley, Frankenstein, fu sottotitolato «Il moderno Prometeo». Questo libro, scritto quasi esattamente 200 anni fa, contiene un forte monito contro la scienza senza freni e l’irresponsabile ricerca dell’uomo di rigenerare la carne. È facile vedere, nondimeno, che da lungo tempo l’uomo desidera rigenerare il proprio corpo, proprio come un meccanico sostituisce dei pezzi o una stella marina fa ricrescere un braccio.

I progressi dell’anestesia, della farmacologia (in particolare degli antibiotici e dei farmaci antirigetto), della chirurgia e delle tecniche di sterilizzazione portarono a importanti traguardi medici, come il primo trapianto di rene nel 1954 e il primo trapianto di midollo osseo nel 1968. Ma i trapianti avevano dei limiti: alcuni tessuti lesi e danneggiati o organi complessi, come il cervello, non potevano essere semplicemente sostituiti. Inoltre, a causa dell’invecchiamento della popolazione e dell’enorme quantità richiesta di alcuni tessuti, come la pelle per le vittime di ustioni, nonché della cronica carenza di donatori idonei, erano necessarie delle alternative. Era inoltre sempre presente l’oscura minaccia del rigetto dei tessuti, che andava affrontata.

Da tempo si sa che, benché il nascituro sia un essere umano unico, è raro che la madre rifiuti tali figli in via di sviluppo. Abbiamo appreso che ciò dipende dal fatto che le cellule dei feti in sviluppo non presentano molti identificatori univoci. Più una persona cresce, più le sue cellule assumono un aspetto e un’identificazione peculiari: è un po’ come se sulla superficie di ogni singola cellula del corpo di una persona ci fosse la stessa impronta digitale. Il corpo di una persona «sa» che aspetto ha l’«impronta» dei propri tessuti e «sa» che ciò che non gli è proprio è estraneo e va attaccato. Usando tessuto fetale, la probabilità di rigetto sarebbe stata pressoché nulla e non ci sarebbe stato bisogno di pericolosi farmaci antirigetto per tutta la vita. Si pensava che il nuovo tessuto sarebbe stato assimilato del tutto. Si tentò quindi di usare tessuto fetale per curare malattie come il morbo di Addison (tessuto surrenale) negli anni Venti e il diabete (tessuto pancreatico) a partire dagli anni Trenta. Benché per ogni trapianto venissero usati fino a 24 feti, alla fine si rivelarono tentativi fallimentari.1

Negli anni Novanta si rinnovò l’interesse per l’uso del tessuto fetale. Non sarebbe meraviglioso, pensavano alcuni scienziati, se si potesse curare il diabete semplicemente inserendo sotto gli avambracci cellule pancreatiche fetali che producono insulina? Lo stesso valeva per i trapianti di tiroide e di surrene fetali: una semplice procedura ambulatoriale, da eseguire in pochi minuti. E che dire di tessuto cerebrale per il morbo di Parkinson o l’Alzheimer? Il potenziale sembrava illimitato.

Se ciò sembra alquanto macabro, c’era un aspetto ancora più inquietante. Sperimentazioni sui topi avevano dimostrato che era possibile trapiantare con successo tessuto ovarico fetale.2 L’idea era trapiantare tessuto ovarico fetale in donne infertili (per esempio, sopravvissute a un tumore infantile, le cui cure chemioterapiche le avevano rese sterili). In questo modo si sarebbe eliminata ogni «necessità» di ricorrere alla fecondazione in vitro. Immaginate di essere un bambino nato da una madre genetica che è stata abortita!

Nel contesto delle battaglie culturali sull’aborto, ci fu una forte spinta a trovare una «cura». E se esistesse una cura per l’Alzheimer o il diabete? Quante persone rifiuterebbero quella cura se provenisse da tessuto fetale? Se rifiutassero davvero il trattamento, quante di loro si opporrebbero all’aborto se un familiare scegliesse una cura (seppure non etica)? Se un genitore di un bambino diabetico rifiutasse il trattamento, sarebbe considerato un caso di negligenza nei confronti del minore? E lo Stato avrebbe motivo di imporre il trattamento al bambino o di allontanarlo dalla famiglia finché non fosse stato curato? In definitiva, uno degli obiettivi era giustificare l’aborto nella mente della popolazione.

Ma accadde qualcosa: i trattamenti non funzionarono come previsto in un numero significativo di pazienti. I medici che li somministravano descrissero effettivamente i trattamenti praticati a un gran numero di pazienti affetti dal morbo di Parkinson come «catastrofici», «assolutamente devastanti» e «un vero incubo».3 Alla classica rigidità muscolare associata al morbo di Parkinson subentrarono teste che scattavano, braccia che si agitavano e corpi che si contorcevano. Il tessuto non «sapeva» quando smettere, produceva neuroormoni in eccesso e arrivava persino a formare tumori di pelle, capelli e cartilagine.4 Inoltre, il tessuto che «attecchiva» alla fine moriva per lo stesso processo che aveva causato il morbo di Parkinson.5 I trattamenti furono ovviamente interrotti.

Ma proprio in quel periodo, alla fine degli anni Novanta, furono scoperte tecniche che permisero ai ricercatori di isolare e coltivare in grandi quantità un particolare tipo di cellula, detta «cellula staminale», da embrioni umani. Immaginate queste cellule staminali a rapida crescita come il fusto di una pianta. Da esse derivano gli altri tipi di cellule (foglie, fiori e frutti). Questi embrioni, unicamente umani, provenivano da trattamenti per la fertilità in cui la fecondazione era stata avviata in laboratorio in una piastra di Petri (di vetro) e lasciata crescere fino a raggiungere le dimensioni di un ammasso cellulare. Si prelevavano le cellule desiderate e si distruggeva il resto. (In sostanza, erano «micro» aborti.)

Il tessuto fetale non funzionò come previsto, in parte perché era già troppo specializzato e «preprogrammato», ma anche troppo impuro, costoso e laborioso da ottenere: occorreva prelevare tessuto da numerosi bambini abortiti, usando un microscopio e delle pinzette. Alcuni scienziati pensarono: perché non ottenere queste cellule staminali, «programmarle» affinché diventino il tipo di cellula desiderato e coltivarne quante ne occorrono?

Nel prossimo numero vi dirò a che punto è attualmente la ricerca, dove ci sono stati successi e fallimenti e come i cristiani possono orientarsi eticamente nelle acque turbolente di questi tempi. È sorprendente come il Signore apra delle porte e si serva delle meraviglie della scienza per creare alternative etiche per coloro che gli rimangono fedeli e seguono le Sue vie. Sarà emozionante spiegarvi come queste «alternative» siano diventate il principale fulcro della ricerca e dei trattamenti sia per i credenti sia per i non credenti.

Ma prima di lasciarvi, vorrei menzionare che nel corso degli anni diverse persone mi hanno detto che tanto questi bambini vengono abortiti comunque, quindi perché non ricavare qualche beneficio da questa tragedia? Non sarebbe, in un certo senso, un modo per redimerla?

Ecco il mio (breve elenco di) motivi per cui sarebbe contrario alla Bibbia che i cristiani traessero beneficio da vaccini non etici e, ora, da trattamenti basati su tessuto fetale:

  1. L’atto della redenzione non può essere separato dalla restituzione e dalla riconciliazione. L’atto stesso di usare tessuto fetale incoraggia soltanto uno sfruttamento ulteriore e più esteso: l’esatto contrario della restituzione e della riconciliazione (che richiedono una risoluzione a non ripetere più il peccato). La storia ha dimostrato che il peccato si moltiplica, non si riduce. Un tempo c’era una sola linea cellulare; ora ce ne sono decine. Gli scienziati sono incoraggiati a condurre ricerche sempre più non etiche, soprattutto se non ci si oppone.

  2. La parola stessa «redimere» significa ricomprare qualcosa che originariamente era tuo, ma che poi è andato perduto. Il corpo del nascituro non è mai stato nostro, non è mai stato nostro da offrire e non è mai stato nostro da cui trarre profitto.

  3. La redenzione comporta sempre un sacrificio di sé. Come si può sacrificare se stessi offrendo il corpo di un altro? (Eb 9:12) Giovanni 15:13 dice: Nessuno ha amore più grande di questo: dare la propria vita per i propri amici. Alcuni cristiani sono pronti a usare questo versetto per giustificare l’andare in guerra. In guerra c’è senz’altro sacrificio di sé, ma lo scopo è far sì che siano i nemici a dare la LORO vita. L’uso utilitaristico del tessuto fetale segue lo stesso ragionamento, salvo che nello sfruttare il corpo di un bambino abortito NON c’è alcun sacrificio di sé.

  4. La redenzione dell’umanità compiuta da Gesù trasformò qualcosa di orribile e ripugnante in qualcosa che glorifica Dio, ma fu un atto di santificazione mediante la santità e la giustizia. Riguardo a questa questione, non riesco a pensare a un atto più lontano dalla santificazione, dalla santità e dalla giustizia: soltanto opportunismo. –vedi Sal 111:9 e 1 Co 1:30

  5. Non possiamo sperare di essere liberati dal male da Dio partecipando al male e traendone beneficio. Ci vengono perdonate le nostre trasgressioni soltanto perdonando, non cospirando insieme, e soltanto rendendo il bene per il male. –vedi Mt 5 e 6

  6. Dio considera abominevole lo spargimento di sangue innocente (lo odia!). –vedi Pr 6:17. Possiamo piacere a Dio e ricevere espiazione soltanto purificandoci da ogni associazione con questa colpa, non partecipandovi. –vedi De 21:8, 9. Riuscite a immaginare di usare prodotti come sapone e paralumi fabbricati con le vittime dell’Olocausto, che «sarebbero morte comunque»?

  7. Quando Saul distrusse gli Amaleciti, tenne per sé il meglio del bottino, ostensibilmente come offerta a Dio (almeno così disse quando Samuele lo rimproverò). –vedi 1 Sam 15. Perché Dio respinse completamente il suo re unto per questo? Potrebbe essere perché non voleva che i Suoi eletti traessero profitto o beneficio dal male, neppure dalla distruzione del male stesso? Potrebbe essere che, portando il bottino dei malvagi in mezzo al Suo popolo eletto, il Suo popolo rischiasse di diventare insensibile proprio a quella stessa malvagità e così di corrompersi? Samuele pianse e si addolorò per Saul, gridando al Signore. Se non siamo noi, chi piangerà per noi e per una generazione decaduta?

  8. Lo stesso si potrebbe dire del giudizio sul tesoro che Acan aveva nascosto dopo la sconfitta di Ai. In sintesi, se dopo una tragedia o il giudizio su un altro c’è un beneficio personale da ricavare, il modo migliore per capire se è legittimo è verificare che i dettagli non siano avvolti nel segreto. (Il frutto dello Spirito consiste in ogni bontà, giustizia e verità;) esaminando ciò che è gradito al Signore. E non partecipate alle opere infruttuose delle tenebre, ma piuttosto denunciatele. –Ef 5:9-11

  9. Esistono alternative: perché giustificare pratiche non etiche? Per quanto riguarda la ricerca di vaccini alternativi, è un processo difficile, ma non impossibile. Seguire Cristo spesso significa percorrere la strada più ardua, anziché quella di minor resistenza. Lo dimostra l’esempio dei nostri fedeli padri spirituali.

As a man was dying, his thoughts went back.
Will I leave a good mark, that none can attack?
I forsook all, on the alter I went
Keeping nothing back, not even a cent.
I wanted to do, all that was right.
I sometimes prayed, all through the night.
It was easy? I cannot say.
But rather a battle, I fought everyday.
Few understood why I lived this way.
Giving up everything was foolish they’d say.
They couldn’t have seen the peace inside.
A peace that I thought, no one could hide.
A life on the run, was not my desire.
But they wanted my body, to put in the fire.
From cave to cave, I would call home
Knowing one day, I’d never more roam.
As I look back, I wouldn’t change a thing.
It has been a great honor serving my king.
But I must go now, the smoke is too thick.
My body to ashes, as the flames lick.
There is one thing, I need to ask.
Will I die in vain, or will you take up the task?
Jesus is looking for A people today
That will stand the test, and not go astray.
Giving our life is part of the cost.
Will you make that decision, before time is lost?
The church is struggling, the world has come in.
They killed our Jesus, and love their sin.
Let’s not give in, there’s too much at stake.
But rather let’s fight! There’s a kingdom to take!

–Barry Grant

The cold, grey days of winter are being transformed into the warm, sunny days of spring. The first flowers of the year are persistently pushing their way up out of the cold earth towards the warmth of the sun. It never seems to get old—this exciting feeling in the springtime air. There’s the warmth and light of sunny days. There’s the cheery, lilting music of the song birds as they once more take up housekeeping with seemingly boundless energy. And we are again blessed with another season to plant seeds with the expectation of another crop of food to enjoy.

This year I will turn 48 years of age. My how that sounds old to me. I remember that as a youth I thought that folks who were 50 were old. Now I am almost there. For me, this is a clear reminder that we all are getting older and that we will not live forever. Next, comes a number of sobering thoughts: “What have I done for the furtherance of God’s Kingdom? Am I remaining faithful to Him in all that I do? Lord, what wilt thou have me to do—this year?” Let’s, each one, prayerfully seek the Lord about His present and future will for our lives. Let’s encourage and exhort each other to remain faithful in relationship with, and in service for, our Master.

In this issue we have an excellent article on marriage, which we felt can take the place of an article on Discipleship this time. We feel that this marriage article is quite thorough in its evaluation of building and maintaining a Biblical foundation. Lord willing, we plan to have ongoing articles relating to this subject.

ימי החורף הקרים והאפורים הופכים לימי האביב החמים והשמשיים. הפרחים הראשונים של השנה מפלסים בעקשנות את דרכם מעלה מתוך האדמה הקרה, לעבר חמימות השמש. נדמה שהתחושה המרגשת באוויר האביבי לעולם אינה נמאסת. יש בהם את החמימות ואת האור של הימים השמשיים. יש בהם את מנגינתם העליזה והקלילה של ציפורי השיר, ששבות להקים את קיניהן במרץ שנדמה שאין לו גבול. ושוב זכינו לעונה נוספת שבה נוכל לזרוע זרעים, בתקווה ליבול נוסף של מזון שנוכל ליהנות ממנו.

השנה אהיה בן 48. כמה זקן זה נשמע לי. אני זוכר שכשהייתי צעיר חשבתי שאנשים בני 50 הם זקנים. עכשיו אני כמעט שם. מבחינתי, זוהי תזכורת ברורה לכך שכולנו מזדקנים ושלא נחיה לנצח. ואז עולות כמה מחשבות רציניות: „מה עשיתי לקידום מלכות האלוהים? האם אני נשאר נאמן לו בכל מעשיי? אדון, מה תרצה שאעשה השנה?” הבה נבקש כולנו, כל אחד ואחת, בתפילה את הדרכתו של האדון בנוגע לרצונו בהווה ובעתיד לחיינו. הבה נעודד ונדרבן זה את זה להישאר נאמנים בקשר עם אדוננו ובשירות למענו.

בגיליון הזה יש לנו מאמר מצוין על נישואים, שלדעתנו יכול להחליף הפעם מאמר על תלמידוּת. כשאנחנו נפגשים עם זוגות שהתמודדו במשך שנים עם בעיות נישואים קשות, אנחנו בדרך כלל מגלים שמשהו אינו מתנהל על פי דרך האלוהים ברובד היסודי. לדעתנו, מאמר זה על נישואים מקיף למדי בהערכתו כיצד לבנות ולשמר יסוד מקראי. אם ירצה האדון, אנו מתכננים לפרסם מאמרים נוספים בנושא זה.

אנו מתוכננים לקיים סדרת מפגשים במחוז לבנון שבפנסילבניה ביולי הקרוב. כמה כנסיות באזור פועלות יחד כדי לאפשר את האירוע, והזמינו את מרכז האירועים פיירוויו. אנא התפללו למען המפגשים, ובקשו: שרצון האלוהים ייעשה; שאלוהים ינחה את הדוברים בעת הכנתם; ושאלוהים יחזק את הכנסייה באמצעות המאמץ הזה. אנא העבירו את המידע הזה לאחרים שעשויים להתעניין. כמו כן, סמנו ביומן ושמרו את התאריך.

אם תרצו לקבל מידע מעודכן לאחר שכל הפרטים ייקבעו, אנא צרו קשר עם „The Berean Voice” בטלפון (330) 439-9547 או בדוא״ל subscribe@bereanvoice.org. מכיוון שיוגשו ארוחות ומספר המקומות מוגבל, ההרשמה לאירוע תהיה חובה. להלן הכותרות הזמניות של הסדרה וההרצאות, אך הן עדיין עשויות להשתנות.

„מבט מקראי על סוגיות של התעללות נפשית, רגשית, זוגית ומינית”

  1. הבנת הלב — שורש כל הבעיות
  2. הבשורה — תשובת האלוהים לכל סוגיות הרוח והנפש (פסיכה) של האדם
  3. כיצד הפסיכולוגיה והפילוסופיות החילוניות משפיעות עלינו כיום
  4. תלמידוּת מעשית — עזרה יעילה לאנשים להשתנות
  5. מבט מקראי על הפרעות נפשיות
  6. בחינה מקראית של סוגיות אימוץ ואומנה
  7. הבנת אפקט הפלצבו ושימוש בטוח בתרופות לנפש
  8. הבנה מקראית של כישלון מוסרי, פורנוגרפיה והתעללות מינית (למבוגרים בלבד)
  9. טוהר — מהעריסה ועד לחזרה בתשובה, ומשם לנישואים או לחיי רווקות (להורים בלבד)
  10. מניעת בעיות והתמודדות עמן באמצעות בתים יראי אלוהים
  11. מניעה וסיוע בהתמודדות עם כל מאבקי החיים במסגרת הכנסייה המקומית

26–28 ביולי 2019

מיקום: מרכז האירועים פיירוויו | 141 Jackson Rd | Lebanon, PA 17042

And I sought for a man among them, that should make up the hedge, and stand in the gap before me for the land, that I should not destroy it: but I found none. –Ezekiel 22:30

The account of the little Dutch boy who heroically stuck his finger in the hole in the dike comes to mind as we consider such a verse. He couldn’t leave the spot for fear of erosion, so he waited the long night through until someone came along in the morning to rescue him from his plight. Many men have performed astounding feats on impulse when the moment so required. Lives were rescued, towns were saved, and enemies defeated because someone filled a role that was needed. Books are written, and monuments erected in honor of those whose benefaction has touched us. These are considered the heroes of history and they are remembered for their staunch bravery and steadfast faithfulness.

But the gaps in life are not always so obvious and the results not always measurable. Solomon informs us of the account of …a little city, and few men within it; and there came a great king against it, and besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it: Now there was found in it a poor wise man, and he by his wisdom delivered the city; yet no man remembered that same poor man. –Ecc 9:14-15. Though we have many thorough descriptions in the Bible of pious men who stood in the gap for God, there are, no doubt, hordes of others who overcame tremendous odds on a spiritual level yet received no recognition in this life.

The problem lies not so much in that, standing in the gap is beyond our capabilities or finances, but in the reality that often the job bears no title, ordination, or recognition. It is to be filled by volunteers with enough vision and care to sacrifice their own agenda for the sole cause of filling the hole in the hedge. It often does not lie within the realm of the physical, but within the borders of the spiritual. While the poor we have with us always and spiritual nobility will stoop to help them, we must consider that God probably has more in mind here than needing someone to organize bread lines and soup kitchens. He is looking for a man clad in a robe of “purple principles” that won’t be shed when the temperatures get hot.

King Darius signed the fateful degree that was designed to escort Daniel to a luncheon with the lions. Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime. –Dan 6:10. What a slight thing it would have been for Daniel to close the shutters before he prayed. But Daniel was not filling the gap by his presence in the high governmental position that he held. The gap lay in the dearth of godly witnesses in Babylon. Thus, the hole between heaven and earth was to be fulfilled by prayer at the open window while sacrificing his “seat in the senate.”

The underlying reason that so many gaps exist and there are so few men to fill them is because we often get our personal, earthly vision of circumstances confused with the eternal purposes of God. We are busily occupied with good things and feeling quite useful. Martha was zealously active in filling what she perceived as the imminent gap in the household, while Mary was sitting in the eternal one. It is incredibly easy to get caught up in the activity trap of a busy life. We may give intensive care to efficiently climb to the top of the ladder, only to discover that it is leaning against the wrong wall. Many people are very busy, but not very effective. Many have labored industriously for years in the Lord’s work, only to arrive at the finish line and realize that the things, which mattered most, had eluded them. Some, while giving their lives to serve others, allowed their marriage to suffer, or their children to disrespect them. Others have given “Corban” to their church while neglecting their relationship with their own parents.

The man in the gap must be wise, and wisdom must understand wherein the true gap lies. In this we must be driven by a purposed, biblical vision. Life will afford many opportunities to abandon our course. If we actively seek to live the expectations handed to us by our family, friends, associates, church agendas, and life’s circumstances, we will be driven by people rather than biblical principles. While this may seem legitimate on the surface, we may reap the bitter disappointment of finding ourselves dangling at the end of the wrong rope.

So, what does the gap of God’s concern look like? Some would say that this gap consists where any need arises. The poor we have with us always and certainly herein is an opportunity to do good. But the better part chosen by Mary had nothing to do with helping the poor or feeding the hungry. Likewise, the woman with the precious alabaster box of ointment of spikenard could have sold it and supplied the poor for quite a while with the sum of its value. But the real gap could not be filled by caressing the cripple, but by crowning the Christ. In the Garden of Eden there was no gap, for man walked in perfect harmony with his Creator. It was sin that created the gap and rankled the relationship. Also, there will be no breach at the end of time when the Lamb receives His bride. Until then, we have a large gap that exists because this earth refuses to glorify its Creator. To stand in that gap must be the chief purpose of all who aspire to bear His name.

This calls for a complete transformation in relationship to our God. The atonement of Christ’s blood makes it judicially possible. The comfort of the Holy Spirit makes it emotionally satisfying, but it is in the realm of our surrender and glorification of God that animates the scene. The Prodigal Son is a prime example of a soul who had brought a world of trouble upon himself by forsaking the position that he held as a son of his father. At the bottom of his restoration was nothing more than a re-establishing of the father-son relationship which had existed from his birth.

It appears to me that God is not so much looking for souls with their hands waving in the air shouting, “Here am I send me!” Rather His eyes search for the humble souls who bow their wills before the Almighty and recognize Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created. –Revelation 4:11. There is no lack for Sons of Sceva who imagine they are filling an important role in their willingness to broadcast the “Jesus” that they have heard of. In 1997, some 800,000 men arrived at a Promise Keepers rally in Washington D.C in response to the theme of “Standing in the Gap.” These men may have had good intentions of representing God to a nation in swift departure from spiritual underpinnings, but it takes more than just a willing heart. God doesn’t need of a large mass of bodies to stuff into a hole. He is looking for qualified men, and few have been promoted to such a position.

If all God wanted was men to show up at a rally or publicly proclaim their faith on the streets, He, no doubt, could have found many desiring such a good work. But to stand in the gap between God and the world will only be sanctioned by God for those who deserve to be there. It is the universal pride of man that drives man to believe that he must only desire to be useful and then he will be used. In God’s house there are some vessels to honor and some to dishonor, yet to deserve an honorable place is much more difficult than to desire one.

It is very common in our day to receive mail bearing the message, “Get the credit you deserve.” It is no secret that the credit that many deserve is zero credit. But we have all been impacted by the subliminal message that everybody deserves credit. Our society is promoting that all immoral, imprudent, and improvident people deserve the same care as the moral and industrious. If the slothful individual deserves a good wage and the spendthrift deserves financial security, then the Apostle Paul certainly has no right to lay any qualifications upon the widows who should receive support from the church. Neither has he any right to reject any sincere soul who desires the office of a Bishop, just because he does not meet the qualifications. But God noticed a few souls …in Sardis which have not defiled their garments; and they shall walk with me in white: for they are worthy. –Rev 3:4

These are men in the gap. Not because they had energy to burn, but because they had a vision for purity. This was no mere accident, for men who wish to attain to preeminence with God must do it by…

…Purpose

By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter; Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season; Esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt: for he had respect unto the recompence of the reward. By faith he forsook Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king: for he endured, as seeing him who is invisible. –Heb 11:24-27

A true vision for the work of God will come with a price tag. The rich young ruler would have loved to be a ruler in the kingdom of Christ as well as on his estate, but he couldn’t hold both. This principle provided the first hurdle for him and for everyone else who would desire such a noble work. As a young man, Moses made his decision and chose his loyalties. He was prepared to be rejected by Egypt, but he never dreamed he would also be so flippantly discarded by his own people.

It was forty years in the lonely furnace that purged his pride and pruned his prowess. There he graduated from the seminary of silence, equipped and prepared to stand in the gap as the meekest man on the face of the earth. He became an intercessor for men to God. As an advocate of men and of God, he preached and prayed, he walked and wept, he lived and loved his God and his brethren. All this while, he deemed himself inadequate for the position. While the children of Israel were at the very core of his heart, his fear and focus never left his God. When we seek to be respected by men, our purpose is clouded over and our position in the gap forfeited. Many good pastors, parents, and pilgrims have made this mistake and received their script from their wife, their children, their friends, or their church. Perhaps it seems like the loving, caring, and most respectful thing to do. But God requires absolute fidelity and there can be no compromise. What a man “wants to be” is driven by his visionary purpose, but what he “turns out to be” rests upon his…

…Priorities

This is a true saying, If a man desire the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work. A bishop then must be blameless, the husband of one wife, vigilant, sober, of good behaviour, given to hospitality, apt to teach; Not given to wine, no striker, not greedy of filthy lucre; but patient, not a brawler, not covetous; One that ruleth well his own house, having his children in subjection with all gravity; –1Ti 3:1-4. Our purpose forms our destination, but our priorities pave the road to get us there.

Unfortunately, some men are promoted to the ministry by popular opinion, but God chooses his men based upon their priorities and eternal qualifications. Men who are governed by their possessions, passions, or position will be useless to serve for God’s purpose. They love to be called Pastor, Reverend, or Father. They love to be esteemed as zealous, knowledgeable, steadfast, or compassionate. For am I now seeking the favor of men, or of God? Or am I striving to please men? If I were still pleasing men, I should not be a servant of Christ. –Gal 1:10 ASV

Fortunately, God is not a respecter of persons, and a stone fit for the wall will not be left in the way. The aged, the poor, the maimed, and the halt are all prime candidates for the position of filling the gap. Those with broken dreams, broken bodies, and broken hearts can stand unhindered in the hedge beside Noah, Abraham, Joseph, Moses, Daniel, Esther, Ruth and a countless battalion of others. These are all stellar representatives of God to this world. They all have turned their back on frivolity, fame, familiarity, and fortune and have become the heroes of heaven. They stand shoulder to shoulder in the hedge and form the “Embassy of the Eternal.” They loved, while others hated. They gave all, while others received. They were mocked and misunderstood, reviled and ridiculed, weary and weeping.

For we are unto God a sweet savour of Christ, in them that are saved, and in them that perish: To the one we are the savour of death unto death; and to the other the savour of life unto life. And who is sufficient for these things? –2 Co 2:15-16. Those whose sole purpose and priorities are governed by God.

Ik zocht onder hen iemand die de muur zou kunnen herstellen en voor Mij in de bres zou staan voor het land, zodat Ik het niet hoefde te vernietigen, maar Ik vond niemand. –Ezechiël 22:30

Wanneer we zo’n vers overdenken, denken we aan het verhaal van het kleine Nederlandse jongetje dat heldhaftig zijn vinger in het gat in de dijk stak. Uit angst voor erosie kon hij niet van zijn plek weggaan, dus wachtte hij de lange nacht door totdat er ’s morgens iemand langskwam om hem uit zijn benarde situatie te redden. Veel mannen hebben op het moment dat het nodig was impulsief verbazingwekkende prestaties geleverd. Levens werden gered, steden werden behouden en vijanden verslagen omdat iemand een noodzakelijke rol vervulde. Er worden boeken geschreven en monumenten opgericht ter ere van hen wier verdiensten ons hebben geraakt. Zij worden beschouwd als de helden van de geschiedenis en herinnerd om hun standvastige moed en onwankelbare trouw.

Maar de gaten in het leven zijn niet altijd zo duidelijk en de resultaten zijn niet altijd meetbaar. Salomo vertelt ons het verhaal van …een kleine stad met weinig inwoners; er kwam een groot koning op haar af, omsingelde haar en bouwde grote belegeringswerken tegen haar. Nu bevond zich in die stad een arme, wijze man, en die redde de stad door zijn wijsheid; toch herinnerde niemand zich die arme man. –Pred 9:14-15. Hoewel de Bijbel ons veel uitvoerige beschrijvingen geeft van godvruchtige mannen die voor God in de bres stonden, zijn er ongetwijfeld talloze anderen die op geestelijk vlak enorme hindernissen overwonnen, maar in dit leven geen erkenning kregen.

Het probleem is niet zozeer dat in de bres staan onze mogelijkheden of middelen te boven gaat, maar dat het werk vaak geen titel, wijding of erkenning met zich meebrengt. Het moet worden gedaan door vrijwilligers met voldoende inzicht en toewijding om hun eigen agenda op te offeren voor het enige doel: het gat in de omheining te vullen. Vaak gaat het niet om het fysieke, maar om het geestelijke. Hoewel wij de armen altijd bij ons hebben en geestelijke edelen zich zullen bukken om hen te helpen, moeten we bedenken dat God hier waarschijnlijk meer op het oog heeft dan iemand die voedseluitdelingen en gaarkeukens organiseert. Hij zoekt een man gehuld in een gewaad van ‘paarse principes’ dat niet wordt afgelegd wanneer de temperaturen oplopen.

Koning Darius ondertekende het noodlottige decreet dat Daniël naar een lunch met de leeuwen zou sturen. Toen Daniël wist dat het geschrift ondertekend was, ging hij naar zijn huis. In zijn bovenkamer waren de vensters open in de richting van Jeruzalem. Hij knielde drie keer per dag op zijn knieën, bad en dankte zijn God, zoals hij vroeger ook deed. –Dan 6:10. Wat een kleinigheid zou het voor Daniël zijn geweest om de luiken te sluiten voordat hij bad. Maar Daniël vulde de bres niet door zijn aanwezigheid in de hoge regeringsfunctie die hij bekleedde. De bres bestond uit het gebrek aan godvruchtige getuigen in Babylon. Zo moest het gat tussen hemel en aarde worden gevuld door bij het open raam te bidden, terwijl hij zijn ‘zetel in de senaat’ op het spel zette.

De onderliggende reden dat er zoveel bressen zijn en zo weinig mannen om ze te vullen, is dat we ons persoonlijke, aardse beeld van de omstandigheden vaak verwarren met Gods eeuwige bedoelingen. We zijn druk bezig met goede dingen en voelen ons heel nuttig. Martha was ijverig bezig de dreigende leemte in het huishouden te vullen zoals zij die zag, terwijl Maria plaatsnam in de eeuwige. Het is verbazingwekkend gemakkelijk om verstrikt te raken in de activiteitenval van een druk leven. We kunnen ons intensief inspannen om efficiënt de top van de ladder te bereiken, om vervolgens te ontdekken dat die tegen de verkeerde muur staat. Veel mensen zijn erg druk, maar niet erg doeltreffend. Velen hebben jarenlang ijverig in het werk van de Heer gezwoegd, om bij de finish te ontdekken dat ze de dingen die er het meest toe deden uit het oog waren verloren. Sommigen lieten, terwijl ze hun leven gaven om anderen te dienen, hun huwelijk lijden of stonden toe dat hun kinderen hen niet respecteerden. Anderen hebben ‘Korban’ aan hun kerk gegeven, terwijl ze hun relatie met hun eigen ouders verwaarloosden.

De man in de bres moet wijs zijn, en wijsheid moet begrijpen waar de werkelijke bres ligt. Daarbij moeten we ons laten leiden door een doelgerichte, bijbelse visie. Het leven biedt veel kansen om onze koers te verlaten. Als we actief proberen te voldoen aan de verwachtingen die onze familie, vrienden, kennissen, kerkelijke agenda’s en levensomstandigheden ons opleggen, zullen we ons door mensen laten leiden in plaats van door bijbelse beginselen. Hoewel dat aan de oppervlakte redelijk kan lijken, kunnen we de bittere teleurstelling oogsten dat we aan het verkeerde touw bungelen.

Hoe ziet de bres eruit waarover God zich zorgen maakt? Sommigen zeggen dat deze bres ontstaat wanneer er maar enige nood is. De armen hebben we altijd bij ons en daar ligt beslist een gelegenheid om goed te doen. Maar het betere deel dat Maria koos, had niets te maken met de armen helpen of de hongerigen voeden. Evenzo had de vrouw met de kostbare albasten kruik met nardusolie die kunnen verkopen en de armen met de opbrengst geruime tijd kunnen onderhouden. Maar de werkelijke bres kon niet worden gevuld door de verlamde liefdevol te omhelzen, maar door Christus te kronen. In de hof van Eden was er geen bres, want de mens wandelde in volmaakte harmonie met zijn Schepper. De zonde schiep de bres en verstoorde de relatie. Ook zal er aan het einde der tijden geen breuk zijn wanneer het Lam Zijn bruid ontvangt. Tot die tijd bestaat er een grote bres, omdat deze aarde weigert haar Schepper te verheerlijken. In die bres staan moet het voornaamste doel zijn van allen die ernaar streven Zijn naam te dragen.

Dit vraagt om een volledige verandering in onze relatie met God. De verzoening door het bloed van Christus maakt dit juridisch mogelijk. De troost van de Heilige Geest maakt het emotioneel bevredigend, maar het is het terrein van onze overgave en verheerlijking van God dat de scène tot leven brengt. De verloren zoon is een treffend voorbeeld van iemand die zichzelf een wereld aan ellende had bezorgd door de positie te verzaken die hij als zoon van zijn vader innam. De kern van zijn herstel was niets anders dan het opnieuw tot stand brengen van de vader-zoonrelatie die vanaf zijn geboorte had bestaan.

Het lijkt mij dat God niet zozeer zoekt naar mensen die met hun handen in de lucht zwaaien en roepen: ‘Hier ben ik, zend mij!’ Zijn ogen zoeken veeleer de nederige mensen die hun wil buigen voor de Almachtige en erkennen: U bent waardig, o Heer, om de heerlijkheid, de eer en de kracht te ontvangen, want U hebt alle dingen geschapen en door Uw wil bestaan zij en zijn zij geschapen. –Openbaring 4:11. Er is geen gebrek aan zonen van Sceva die denken dat ze een belangrijke rol vervullen door bereidwillig de ‘Jezus’ rond te bazuinen over wie ze hebben gehoord. In 1997 kwamen ongeveer 800.000 mannen bijeen bij een Promise Keepers-rally in Washington D.C. als reactie op het thema ‘In de bres staan’. Deze mannen hadden misschien goede bedoelingen: God vertegenwoordigen tegenover een natie die zich snel van haar geestelijke fundamenten verwijderde. Maar meer dan alleen een bereidwillig hart is nodig. God heeft geen grote massa lichamen nodig om een gat op te vullen. Hij zoekt geschikte mannen, en slechts weinigen zijn tot zo’n positie bevorderd.

Als God alleen maar wilde dat mannen naar een bijeenkomst kwamen of in het openbaar op straat hun geloof verkondigden, had Hij ongetwijfeld velen kunnen vinden die zo’n goed werk wilden doen. Maar God zal alleen degenen toestaan in de bres tussen Hem en de wereld te staan die het verdienen daar te zijn. Het is de universele trots van de mens die hem ertoe brengt te geloven dat hij alleen maar nuttig hoeft te willen zijn, waarna hij ook gebruikt zal worden. In Gods huis zijn er vaten tot eer en vaten tot oneer, maar een eervolle plaats verdienen is veel moeilijker dan er een te verlangen.

In onze tijd ontvangen we heel vaak post met de boodschap: ‘Krijg de erkenning die u verdient.’ Het is geen geheim dat de erkenning die velen verdienen nul is. Maar we zijn allemaal beïnvloed door de subliminale boodschap dat iedereen erkenning verdient. Onze samenleving propageert dat alle immorele, onbezonnen en onverstandige mensen dezelfde zorg verdienen als de morele en ijverige mensen. Als de luie persoon een goed loon verdient en de verkwister financiële zekerheid verdient, heeft de apostel Paulus beslist niet het recht om voorwaarden te stellen aan de weduwen die steun van de kerk behoren te ontvangen. Evenmin heeft hij het recht om een oprechte persoon die het ambt van opziener verlangt af te wijzen, alleen omdat die niet aan de vereisten voldoet. Maar God zag enkele mensen …in Sardis die hun kleren niet bevlekt hebben; zij zullen met Mij in het wit wandelen, want zij zijn het waard. –Openb 3:4.

Dit zijn mannen in de bres. Niet omdat ze over energie beschikten om te verbranden, maar omdat ze een visie op reinheid hadden. Dat was geen toeval, want mannen die bij God aanzien willen verwerven, moeten dat doen door middel van…

…Doel

Door het geloof weigerde Mozes, toen hij volwassen geworden was, een zoon van de dochter van Farao genoemd te worden. Hij verkoos liever met het volk van God slecht behandeld te worden dan tijdelijk van de zonde te genieten. Hij beschouwde de smaad van Christus als grotere rijkdom dan de schatten in Egypte, want hij had het oog gericht op de beloning. Door het geloof verliet hij Egypte zonder bevreesd te zijn voor de woede van de koning, want hij hield stand als zag hij de Onzichtbare. –Heb 11:24-27.

Een ware visie op Gods werk heeft een prijskaartje. De rijke jongeling had graag zowel heerser in het koninkrijk van Christus als heer op zijn landgoed willen zijn, maar hij kon niet beide zijn. Dit beginsel vormde de eerste hindernis voor hem en voor iedereen die zo’n edel werk zou willen doen. Als jonge man nam Mozes zijn besluit en koos hij partij. Hij was erop voorbereid door Egypte verworpen te worden, maar had nooit gedacht dat ook zijn eigen volk hem zo lichtvaardig zou afwijzen.

Veertig jaar in de eenzame smeltoven zuiverden zijn trots en snoeiden zijn kracht. Daar studeerde hij af aan het seminarie van de stilte, toegerust en voorbereid om als de zachtmoedigste man op aarde in de bres te staan. Hij werd een voorspreker voor mensen bij God. Als pleitbezorger voor mensen en voor God predikte en bad hij, wandelde en weende hij, leefde hij en had hij zijn God en zijn broeders lief. Dit alles terwijl hij zichzelf ongeschikt achtte voor de positie. Hoewel de kinderen van Israël hem na aan het hart lagen, verloren zijn vrees voor God en zijn aandacht voor Hem nooit hun plaats. Wanneer we door mensen gerespecteerd willen worden, raakt ons doel vertroebeld en geven we onze positie in de bres op. Veel goede predikanten, ouders en pelgrims hebben deze fout gemaakt en hun richtsnoer gekregen van hun vrouw, hun kinderen, hun vrienden of hun kerk. Misschien lijkt het liefdevol, zorgzaam en het meest respectvol om dat te doen. Maar God vereist absolute trouw en er kan geen compromis zijn. Wat een man ‘wil zijn’ wordt bepaald door zijn doelgerichte visie, maar wat hij ‘blijkt te zijn’ hangt af van zijn…

…Prioriteiten

Dit is een betrouwbaar woord: als iemand verlangen heeft naar het ambt van opziener, begeert hij een voortreffelijk werk. Een opziener moet dan onberispelijk zijn, de man van één vrouw, waakzaam, bezonnen, eerbaar, gastvrij, bekwaam om te onderwijzen; niet verslaafd aan wijn, niet opvliegend, niet uit op schandelijke winst, maar inschikkelijk, niet twistziek, niet geldzuchtig; iemand die zijn eigen huis goed bestuurt en zijn kinderen met alle waardigheid onderdanig houdt; –1 Tim 3:1-4. Ons doel bepaalt onze bestemming, maar onze prioriteiten banen de weg ernaartoe.

Helaas worden sommige mannen door de publieke opinie tot de bediening bevorderd, maar God kiest Zijn mannen op grond van hun prioriteiten en eeuwige vereisten. Mannen die door hun bezit, hartstochten of positie worden beheerst, zijn nutteloos voor Gods doel. Ze willen graag dominee, eerwaarde of vader worden genoemd. Ze willen graag worden beschouwd als ijverig, kundig, standvastig of meelevend. Zoek ik nu de gunst van mensen of die van God? Of probeer ik mensen te behagen? Als ik nog steeds mensen behaagde, zou ik geen dienaar van Christus zijn. –Gal 1:10 NBG.

Gelukkig is God geen aannemer des persoons, en een steen die geschikt is voor de muur zal niet aan de kant worden gelegd. Ouderen, armen, verminkten en kreupelen zijn allemaal uitstekende kandidaten om de bres te vullen. Mensen met gebroken dromen, gebroken lichamen en gebroken harten kunnen ongehinderd in de omheining naast Noach, Abraham, Jozef, Mozes, Daniël, Esther, Ruth en een ontelbaar legioen anderen staan. Zij zijn allemaal voortreffelijke vertegenwoordigers van God in deze wereld. Ze hebben allemaal de rug toegekeerd aan lichtzinnigheid, roem, vertrouwelijkheid en rijkdom, en zijn helden van de hemel geworden. Ze staan schouder aan schouder in de omheining en vormen de ‘Ambassade van de Eeuwige’. Zij hadden lief, terwijl anderen haatten. Zij gaven alles, terwijl anderen ontvingen. Er werd met hen gespot en ze werden verkeerd begrepen, beschimpt en bespot, vermoeid en huilend.

Want wij zijn voor God een aangename geur van Christus, onder hen die behouden worden en onder hen die verloren gaan. Voor de een zijn wij een geur van de dood die tot de dood leidt, voor de ander een geur van het leven die tot het leven leidt. En wie is tot deze dingen bekwaam? –2 Kor 2:15-16. Dat zijn zij wier enige doel en prioriteiten door God worden bepaald.

When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said, It is finished: and he bowed his head, and gave up the ghost. –Joh 19:30

As we have been developing this article over the last year, we have become increasingly aware of a growing interest in this subject. Various papers and booklets have been, or are being, written about it. Some writings debate specific theories of the atonement, while others reason about various terms or Bible verses. What ideas and statements concerning the atonement are found in the clear teachings of Scripture, and which are misunderstandings or wrong interpretations?

I. The Atonement

The term atonement is usually understood to explain all or part of what happened spiritually (for the believer) when Christ went through His suffering, death, and resurrection. Sometimes the term atonement is used to define that which brings men and women to a place of “at-one-ment” (to be at one) with God. How does that event in history still affect us today, some 2,000 years later?

In these discussions, there is the tendency to forget that the finished work of Christ includes multiple aspects, with each one contributing to a different effect for the believer today. These different aspects include Christ’s Suffering, His Blood, His Death, His Burial, His Resurrection, and His Ascension.

a. His Suffering

His suffering covers the physical, emotional, and mental anguish He endured that culminated with His death on the cross. Here we see that …it behoved Christ to suffer, and to rise from the dead the third day … that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name… –Luk 24:46-47. The suffering servant, as portrayed in the whole of Isaiah chapter 53, gives a vivid picture of this aspect of the atonement. Isaiah describes Him as being …wounded for our transgressions, [and] …bruised for our iniquities: –Isa 53:5. Here we also have the reality that with his stripes we are healed. –Isa 53:5. Finally, we see that He was oppressed, and he was afflicted… –Isa 53:7, and that he endured … travail of his soul… –Isa 53:11

Let’s note a few more of the many passages that speak of His suffering: For Christ also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God… –1Pe 3:18; Though he were a Son, yet learned he obedience by the things which he suffered –Heb 5:8; For it became him, for whom are all things, and by whom are all things, in bringing many sons unto glory, to make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings –Heb 2:10.

A sometimes forgotten purpose of Jesus’ suffering is that, as believers, we are to identify with His suffering as given in the following passages: For as the sufferings of Christ abound in us, so our consolation also aboundeth by Christ –2Co 1:5; …if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together –Rom 8:17; That I may know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, being made conformable unto his death –Php 3:10.

b. His Blood that was Shed

The blood of Christ being shed for the atonement of sinful man needs some careful consideration as a specific vital aspect of the whole. Of course, it is included in points a. and c., but the Scriptures also give much attention to this particular part. It would perhaps require a whole book to expound on this aspect, but we should note one thing on this point. It is with the shedding of the blood of Jesus that we have God’s specific solution for the remission of our sins given here in Jesus’ own words, For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins –Mat 26:28.

In Hebrews chapters 9 and 10, we have very detailed explanation showing how the “blood sacrifices” of the Old Testament were not perfect in themselves, rather they were a “type” that pointed forward to the perfect sacrifice—Jesus, the Lamb of God. It is in this context that we have this—that …almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission. –Heb 9:22. This is particularly important to remember when we consider that some people claim that God could just simply forgive sin without death or the shedding of blood if He so chose. These people use the story found in Matthew 18:23-35 as their proof text. It would do us well to consider that this story is revealing the “why” (compassion) of the outcome, not the “how” of the details. We cannot take this story out of context of Scripture and build a doctrine that undermines all the rest of Scripture. Thus, we conclude that in God’s economy He has ordained that sin must be washed away with the blood of Christ—And from Jesus Christ, who … washed us from our sins in his own blood, –Rev 1:5.

For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God; Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus: Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God –Rom 3:23-25. Here we see that for anyone of us that has sinned (ALL of us), we have our propitiation made possible through faith in His (Jesus’) blood.

c. His Death

Jesus said, …I lay down my life for the sheep –Joh 10:15, and again He said, …I lay down my life, that I might take it again. No man taketh it from me, but I lay it down of myself. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it again… –Joh 10:17-18.

But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour; that he by the grace of God should taste death for every man. For it became him, for whom are all things, and by whom are all things, in bringing many sons unto glory, to make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings. –Heb 2:9-10. When you partake of communion …ye do shew the Lord’s death till he come –1Co 11:26.

Know ye not, that so many of us as were baptized into Jesus Christ were baptized into his death? Therefore we are buried with him by baptism into death: that like as Christ was raised up from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life. –Rom 6:3-4

It is during this period of Jesus’ time on earth that the earthly, mortal part of Him separated from that which was heavenly, eternal, and immortal.

d. His Burial

We note again, as referenced above, the truth that Therefore we are buried with him by baptism into death… –Rom. 6:4. While all these aspects are a part of the whole, the burial represents …a corn of wheat fall into the ground and die… –Joh 12:24. First is the ending of life (pouring out of the blood), then death, then burial, then resurrection. The burial part is the confirmation that death has occurred. It brings finality, closure, and an end to the former. It is the necessary interval between death and resurrection.

It is also the time of Jesus’ entrance into Hades, the place of departed souls, of which we are given only glimpses through several passages of Scripture.

e. His Resurrection

In His resurrection we are raised with Him in newness of life. (Romans 6:4) …wherein also ye are risen with him through the faith of the operation of God, who hath raised him from the dead –Col 2:12. So, in His resurrection we are raised up with Him from death (if we were dead prior) and are provided the power to walk in newness of life (the power to have victory over sin).

f. His Ascension

In His ascension we understand that …he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight. –Act 1:9. It is due to His leaving this earth that we have many key aspects for the believer’s life today. There is the provision of the Holy Spirit made possible once Jesus left this earth. We have the promise of His going to prepare a better home for us to someday join Him in everlasting joy. We have Jesus sitting at the right hand of the throne of God interceding for us. We have Jesus acting in the role of our sympathetic High Priest, one that knows and understands our every need and struggle, since He has the experience of living on the sinful earth inside a mortal body.

Herein, we start to see how each part of the Atonement achieves a different result for the believer and that each part is only that—A PART. A part of the whole. A part of the finished work of Christ. These lists could each go on and fill page after page of all the blessings and benefits each one enables for the believer. For the sake of space, we will stop on this part for now and continue with the rest of the article, but hopefully this will stimulate each of us to further meditation in God’s Word on these matters.

II. Common statements that are not Biblically correct

There are some popular statements which we may hear concerning the atonement that do not accurately describe what the Scriptures teach. But because they are popular in our conversations, or perhaps they’re even the words of a familiar song, they may skew our understanding of the finished work of Christ. For some examples, let’s look at the following statements:

a. “Christ took my place on Calvary.”

This may seem like a logical conclusion, because He died for us, …the just for the unjust… –1Pe 3:18. and He died that we might live. There is no question that it was for us, but the preposition, for, can be understood several different ways. It can mean in my place, or it can mean on my behalf. Most of Scripture clearly emphasizes that He died on my behalf, but less clear is the idea of a direct substitution. Emphasizing substitution leads us to the following concept: He died in my place, so I don’t need to. If this becomes the primary way of thinking about the atonement, we may miss what is equally important—that since He died, so I must also die with Him. See Rom 6:1-11

b. “The guilt of my sin was placed on Christ.”

There are passages that speak of Christ bearing our sins. So Christ was once offered to bear the sins of many… –Heb 9:28 and, Who his own self bare our sins in his own body on the tree… –1Pe 2:24. But what is the proper understanding of what it means to ‘bear (carry) our sins’? We do NOT find Scripture which supports the idea that the guilt of my sin was transferred to Christ. Christ offered Himself to be the sacrifice for sin (Heb 10:10-12), the propitiation for our sins (1Jo 2:1), to put away sin, even to be the forgiveness of sin. This great work of dealing with sin was accomplished without Him ever losing His condition as the Lamb without blemish.

There is one passage we should note on this topic, For he [God] hath made him [Jesus] to be sin for us, who [Jesus] knew no sin… –2Co 5:21. When we look at the Greek word in this verse translated as “sin” and compare this passage with all the other Scriptures, it seems the intended meaning for this phrase to be sin is more clearly defined as to be a sin offering. Christ’s soul was not blackened with the guilt of our sin, else He could not have retained His position … as of a lamb without blemish and without spot –1Pe 1:19. A proper understanding of the sense in which He took our sins is that He assumed the settlement for them.

c. “He took the wrath of God upon Himself.”

Concerning God’s wrath, we know that …he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him –Joh 3:36; …the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness –Rom 1:18; …and were by nature the children of wrath, even as others –Eph 2:3.

However, atonement was made, and then, in Romans, Much more then, being now justified by his blood, we shall be saved from wrath through him –Rom 5:9. So, it is clear that the wrath of God toward us on account of sin is now averted when we are justified by His blood. However, the Scriptures do not say that Christ suffered the wrath of God. It may seem like a logical conclusion that if wrath was averted, and atonement was being made, then God›s wrath for sin must have fallen upon Christ, but that is not so stated in the scriptures. If we look at the picture of Abraham offering up his son Isaac, there was no wrath on Abraham’s part. Finally, God was “in Christ, reconciling the world unto Himself” and here what is emphasized is that Christ’s sacrifice to put away sin demonstrates to us the great love that the Father has toward us.

d. “God no longer looks at me; all He sees is Christ.”

The atonement should not be viewed, as perhaps many do, as a cloak for sin (to cover it). It is also sometimes stated this way: “Since Christ died on the cross for my sin, and I believe in Him, now Christ’s righteousness is all that God sees. When God looks at me, He no longer sees my sin; all He sees is Christ’s righteousness.” There is a great deal of error in this view, and the fruit of it is that many become complacent and tolerant of sin in their own lives. Through the atonement in Christ, God has made available to us everything needed for cleansing and to be made holy, but no, God does not credit Christ’s righteousness to our account. God’s purpose in the atonement was to make us righteous by purging our sin. We are to reckon ourselves dead unto sin, alive unto God. This does not mean that we have attained to a state of perfection, but we allow the atonement to be continually effective in our life.

For now, in section III, we are making summary statements, and in sections IV and V we are simply putting subheadings in place. Lord willing, we can take more time to flesh each one out in a future article. Until then, we encourage each one to do your own Bible study to more fully understand the whole of Scriptures’ teaching on the subject. Finally, it is our sincere desire that each of us would take heed that we are not deceived by the many voices from without and from within that Satan wishes to use to turn the church of Jesus Christ away from …the faith which was once delivered unto the saints. –Jud 1:3

III. What the Atonement does NOT do

a. Does NOT transfer guilt from one to another

As we stated above, our guilt did not blacken the soul of Christ. He provided atonement that our sins might be forgiven. He made, or was made, an offering for sin, and He was wounded for our transgressions, and by this act our sin is purged, and our guilt is taken away, without Him becoming guilty in our place.

b. Does NOT transfer righteousness from one to another—from Christ to us

Through Jesus our Lord we receive, given unto us, all things that pertain to life and godliness. We can say that our righteousness is only in Him, but we don’t say that His righteousness is somehow credited to our account when we are deficient. See also below on the issue of walking in the Light.

c. Does NOT protect us from harm/Does not build a hedge of protection around us

Our Sovereign Father provides our protection according to His will. Our protection does not come from the atonement, rather it comes out of our relationship with God as we walk by faith in obedience and draw near to Him. God protects, according to His will, those who are His. There is no guarantee that bad things will not happen, rather God promises that He will be with His children through whatever He allows them to go through.

d. Does not keep Satan away from us

Our Father does that according to His will (see Job 1 and 2, also 1 Cor 10:13). We do not need to “plead the blood for our protection” as though the blood of Christ was a means to ward off evil powers. We have the armor of God, shield of faith, and the sword of the Spirit, with all prayer, to overcome the powers of darkness.

IV. What the Atonement DOES do

  1. It reconciles
  2. It prepares a sacrifice for sin
  3. It provides a sin offering
  4. It redeems
  5. It ransoms
  6. It provides forgiveness of sins
  7. It provides remission of sins
  8. It cleanses us
  9. It enables God to see us as blameless
  10. It makes us righteous in God’s sight
  11. It causes believers to become a part of God’s family
  12. It causes believers to become brothers and sisters

V. What ALL was finished

  1. His suffering
  2. His temptations
  3. His labors on earth—His preaching and teaching
  4. The sacrificial system—sacrifices, which can never take away sins –Heb 10:11
  5. The law—was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ… –Gal 3:24
  6. Limited access to God—And the veil of the temple was rent in twain… –Mar 15:38
