“Nami nikatafuta mtu miongoni mwao, atakayelitengeneza ukuta na kusimama mahali palipobomoka mbele zangu kwa ajili ya nchi, nisije nikaiharibu; lakini sikumwona mtu.” –Ezekieli 22:30

Hadithi ya mvulana mdogo Mholanzi, aliyechomeka kidole chake kishujaa kwenye tundu la kingo ya bwawa, inakuja akilini tunapotafakari mstari kama huu. Hangeweza kuondoka pale kwa kuhofia mmomonyoko, hivyo alingoja usiku wote hadi mtu alipofika asubuhi kumwokoa kutoka katika hali yake ngumu. Wanaume wengi wamefanya mambo ya ajabu kwa msukumo wa ghafla wakati hali ilipohitaji hivyo. Watu waliokolewa, miji iliokolewa, na maadui wakashindwa kwa sababu mtu fulani alitimiza jukumu lililohitajika. Vitabu huandikwa, na minara ya ukumbusho hujengwa kwa heshima ya wale ambao wema wao umetugusa. Hawa huonwa kuwa mashujaa wa historia, nao hukumbukwa kwa ujasiri wao thabiti na uaminifu wao usioyumba.

Lakini mapengo maishani hayaonekani wazi kila wakati, wala matokeo yake hayawezi kupimika kila wakati. Sulemani anatueleza habari za …mji mdogo, na watu wachache ndani yake; mfalme mkuu akaja kuushambulia, akauzingira, akajenga maboma makubwa dhidi yake. Basi ndani yake akapatikana mtu maskini mwenye hekima, naye kwa hekima yake akauokoa mji; lakini hakuna mtu aliyemkumbuka yule maskini. –Mhubiri 9:14-15. Ingawa Biblia ina maelezo mengi ya kina kuhusu watu wacha Mungu waliosimama mahali palipobomoka kwa ajili ya Mungu, bila shaka, kuna makundi mengi ya wengine walioshinda vikwazo vikubwa katika ulimwengu wa kiroho lakini hawakutambuliwa katika maisha haya.

Tatizo si sana kwamba kusimama mahali palipobomoka ni zaidi ya uwezo au fedha zetu, bali ukweli ni kwamba mara nyingi jukumu hilo halina cheo, kuwekwa wakfu, wala kutambuliwa. Linapaswa kutimizwa na wajitolea wenye maono na kujali vya kutosha kuacha ajenda zao wenyewe kwa ajili ya lengo pekee la kuziba pengo katika ukuta. Mara nyingi halihusu mambo ya kimwili, bali mambo ya kiroho. Ingawa maskini tutakuwa nao daima, na watu waungwana kiroho watainama kuwasaidia, ni lazima tufikirie kwamba huenda Mungu analenga jambo kubwa zaidi hapa kuliko kuhitaji mtu wa kupanga foleni za kugawa mkate na jikoni za supu. Anatafuta mtu aliyevaa joho la “kanuni za zambarau” ambalo hataachilia halijoto inapopanda.

Mfalme Dario alitia saini amri ya maangamizi iliyokusudiwa kumpeleka Danieli kwenye chakula cha mchana pamoja na simba. Basi Danieli alipofahamu kwamba ile hati imetiwa saini, akaingia nyumbani mwake; na madirisha ya chumba chake yakiwa wazi kuelekea Yerusalemu, akapiga magoti mara tatu kwa siku, akaomba na kumshukuru Mungu wake, kama alivyokuwa akifanya hapo awali. –Danieli 6:10. Jambo dogo tu lingekuwa kwa Danieli kufunga vifuniko vya madirisha kabla ya kuomba. Lakini Danieli hakuziba pengo kwa kuwapo kwake katika cheo cha juu cha serikali alichokuwa nacho. Pengo lilikuwa ukosefu wa mashahidi wacha Mungu katika Babeli. Hivyo, pengo kati ya mbingu na dunia lingezibwa kwa kuomba kwenye dirisha lililo wazi huku akitoa dhabihu ya “kiti chake bungeni.”

Sababu ya msingi ya kuwapo kwa mapengo mengi na wanaume wachache wa kuyaziba ni kwamba mara nyingi tunachanganya maono yetu binafsi, ya kidunia kuhusu hali na makusudi ya milele ya Mungu. Tunajishughulisha sana na mambo mema na kujiona kuwa wenye manufaa kabisa. Martha alikuwa akihangaika kwa bidii kuziba kile alichodhani kuwa pengo lililokuwa karibu kutokea nyumbani, huku Maria akiwa ameketi katika lile la milele. Ni rahisi sana kunaswa katika mtego wa shughuli nyingi za maisha. Tunaweza kujitahidi sana kupanda kwa ufanisi hadi juu ya ngazi, na kugundua tu kwamba imeegemezwa kwenye ukuta usiofaa. Watu wengi wana shughuli nyingi sana, lakini hawana matokeo mengi. Wengi wamefanya kazi kwa bidii kwa miaka mingi katika kazi ya Bwana, na kufika tu kwenye mstari wa mwisho na kutambua kwamba mambo yaliyokuwa muhimu zaidi yaliwapita. Baadhi yao, walipotoa maisha yao kuwahudumia wengine, waliruhusu ndoa zao ziteseke au watoto wao wasiwaheshimu. Wengine wametoa “Korban” kwa kanisa lao huku wakipuuza uhusiano wao na wazazi wao wenyewe.

Mtu aliye mahali palipobomoka lazima awe na hekima, na hekima lazima itambue pengo halisi lilipo. Katika jambo hili, ni lazima tuongozwe na maono yenye kusudi, ya kibiblia. Maisha yatatupa fursa nyingi za kuacha njia yetu. Tukitafuta kikamilifu kuishi kulingana na matarajio tuliyopewa na familia zetu, marafiki, washirika, ajenda za kanisa na hali za maisha, tutaongozwa na watu badala ya kanuni za Biblia. Ingawa hili linaweza kuonekana kuwa halali kwa juu juu, huenda tukavuna masikitiko makali ya kujikuta tunaning’inia mwisho wa kamba isiyo sahihi.

Kwa hiyo, pengo ambalo Mungu analijali linaonekanaje? Wengine wangesema pengo hili linapatikana kila hitaji linapotokea. Maskini tutakuwa nao daima, na bila shaka hapa pana fursa ya kutenda mema. Lakini sehemu iliyo bora zaidi aliyoichagua Maria haikuhusu kuwasaidia maskini wala kuwalisha wenye njaa. Vivyo hivyo, yule mwanamke aliyekuwa na chupa ya alabasta yenye marhamu ya nardo angeweza kuiuza na kuwapatia maskini mahitaji kwa muda mrefu kutokana na thamani yake. Lakini pengo halisi lisingezibwa kwa kumbembeleza kilema, bali kwa kumvika taji Kristo. Katika Bustani ya Edeni hakukuwa na pengo, kwa maana mwanadamu aliishi kwa upatano mkamilifu na Muumba wake. Dhambi ndiyo iliyotokeza pengo na kuvuruga uhusiano. Pia, hakutakuwa na ufa mwishoni mwa wakati Mwana-Kondoo atakapompokea bibi-arusi wake. Hadi wakati huo, kuna pengo kubwa kwa sababu dunia hii inakataa kumtukuza Muumba wake. Kusimama katika pengo hilo lazima kuwe kusudi kuu la wote wanaotamani kulibeba jina lake.

Hili linahitaji mabadiliko kamili katika uhusiano wetu na Mungu. Upatanisho wa damu ya Kristo unalifanya liwezekane kisheria. Faraja ya Roho Mtakatifu hulifanya liridhishe kihisia, lakini ni kujisalimisha kwetu na kumtukuza Mungu kunakolihuisha tukio hili. Mwana Mpotevu ni mfano mkuu wa nafsi iliyojiletea matatizo mengi kwa kuacha nafasi yake ya kuwa mwana wa baba yake. Msingi wa kurejeshwa kwake haukuwa jambo jingine bali kurejeshwa kwa uhusiano wa baba na mwana uliokuwapo tangu kuzaliwa kwake.

Inaonekana kwangu kwamba Mungu hatafuti sana nafsi zinazopunga mikono hewani huku zikisema, “Mimi hapa, nitume!” Badala yake, macho yake huwatafuta wanyenyekevu wanaoinamisha mapenzi yao mbele za Mwenyezi na kutambua “Umestahili, Ee Bwana, kuupokea utukufu na heshima na uweza; kwa kuwa wewe ndiwe uliyeviumba vitu vyote, na kwa sababu ya mapenzi yako vilikuwako, navyo vikaumbwa.” –Ufunuo 4:11. Hawakosekani wana wa Skewa wanaodhani wanatimiza jukumu muhimu kwa kuwa tayari kutangaza “Yesu” ambaye wamesikia habari zake. Mwaka wa 1997, wanaume wapatao 800,000 walifika kwenye mkutano wa Promise Keepers huko Washington D.C. kufuatia kaulimbiu ya “Kusimama Mahali Palipobomoka.” Huenda wanaume hawa walikuwa na nia njema ya kumwakilisha Mungu kwa taifa lililokuwa likiachana kwa kasi na misingi ya kiroho, lakini moyo wa kujitolea pekee hautoshi. Mungu hahitaji umati mkubwa wa watu wa kuziba tundu. Anatafuta wanaume wanaostahili, na ni wachache waliopandishwa kwenye nafasi hiyo.

Kama Mungu alichotaka ni wanaume waonekane kwenye mkutano au watangaze hadharani imani yao mitaani, bila shaka angeweza kupata wengi wanaotamani kufanya kazi hiyo njema. Lakini kusimama katika pengo kati ya Mungu na ulimwengu kutakubaliwa na Mungu kwa wale tu wanaostahili kuwapo hapo. Ni kiburi cha jumla cha mwanadamu kinachomfanya aamini kwamba anahitaji tu kutamani kuwa na manufaa ndipo atakapotumiwa. Katika nyumba ya Mungu kuna vyombo vingine vya heshima na vingine vya kuvunjiwa heshima, lakini kustahili nafasi ya heshima ni kugumu zaidi kuliko kutamani nafasi hiyo.

Katika siku zetu ni jambo la kawaida sana kupokea barua yenye ujumbe, “Pata sifa unazostahili.” Si siri kwamba sifa ambazo wengi wanastahili ni sifuri. Lakini sote tumeathiriwa na ujumbe fiche kwamba kila mtu anastahili sifa. Jamii yetu inahimiza kwamba watu wote wasio na maadili, wasio na busara na wasiojali wajibu wanastahili kutunzwa sawa na watu wenye maadili na bidii. Ikiwa mzembe anastahili mshahara mzuri na mtu mpotevu anastahili usalama wa kifedha, basi kwa hakika Mtume Paulo hana haki ya kuweka masharti yoyote kwa wajane wanaopaswa kusaidiwa na kanisa. Wala hana haki ya kumkataa nafsi yoyote ya kweli inayotamani ofisi ya askofu, kwa sababu tu haikidhi sifa zinazohitajika. Lakini Mungu aliona nafsi chache …katika Sardisi ambao hawakuzitia unajisi nguo zao; nao watatembea pamoja nami wakiwa wamevaa mavazi meupe, kwa maana wanastahili. –Ufunuo 3:4

Hawa ndio wanaume walio mahali palipobomoka. Si kwa sababu walikuwa na nguvu nyingi za kutumia, bali kwa sababu walikuwa na maono ya usafi. Hili halikutokea kwa bahati tu, kwa maana wanaume wanaotaka kufikia ukuu mbele za Mungu lazima wafanye hivyo kwa…

…Kusudi

Kwa imani Musa alipokuwa mtu mzima, alikataa kuitwa mwana wa binti Farao; akachagua afadhali kuteswa pamoja na watu wa Mungu kuliko kujifurahisha katika dhambi kwa muda; akihesabu kushutumiwa kwa ajili ya Kristo kuwa ni utajiri mkuu kuliko hazina za Misri; kwa maana alitazamia kupata thawabu. Kwa imani aliiacha Misri, asiogope ghadhabu ya mfalme; maana alistahimili kana kwamba anamwona yeye asiyeonekana. –Waebrania 11:24-27

Maono ya kweli kuhusu kazi ya Mungu yatakuwa na gharama. Yule mtawala kijana tajiri angependa kuwa mtawala katika ufalme wa Kristo na pia katika mali yake, lakini hangeweza kushikilia vyote viwili. Kanuni hii ilikuwa kikwazo cha kwanza kwake na kwa kila mtu mwingine ambaye angetamani kazi hiyo adhimu. Akiwa kijana, Musa alifanya uamuzi wake na kuchagua uaminifu wake. Alikuwa tayari kukataliwa na Misri, lakini hakuwahi kufikiria kwamba watu wake mwenyewe wangemfukuza kwa urahisi hivyo.

Miaka arobaini katika tanuru la upweke ilisafisha kiburi chake na kupogoa uwezo wake. Huko alihitimu kutoka seminari ya ukimya, akiwa amejitayarisha na kuwezeshwa kusimama mahali palipobomoka akiwa mtu mpole kuliko wote duniani. Akawa mwombezi wa watu mbele za Mungu. Akiwa mtetezi wa watu na wa Mungu, alihubiri na kuomba, alitembea na kulia, aliishi na kumpenda Mungu wake na ndugu zake. Wakati wote huo, alijiona kuwa hafai kwa nafasi hiyo. Ingawa wana wa Israeli walikuwa kiini cha moyo wake, hofu na fikira zake hazikumwacha Mungu wake kamwe. Tunapotafuta kuheshimiwa na watu, kusudi letu hufunikwa na nafasi yetu katika pengo hupotea. Wachungaji wengi wazuri, wazazi na wasafiri wamefanya kosa hili na kupokea mwongozo wao kutoka kwa mke, watoto, marafiki au kanisa lao. Huenda likaonekana kuwa jambo la upendo, kujali na heshima zaidi. Lakini Mungu anahitaji uaminifu kamili na hakuna nafasi ya kulegeza msimamo. Kile mtu “anachotaka kuwa” huongozwa na kusudi lake lenye maono, lakini kile “atakachokuwa hatimaye” hutegemea…

…Vipaumbele

Ni neno la kuaminiwa: mtu akitaka kazi ya askofu, atamani kazi njema. Basi imempasa askofu awe mtu asiyelaumika, mume wa mke mmoja, mwenye kiasi, mwenye busara, mwenye mwenendo mzuri, mkaribishaji, ajuaye kufundisha; asiwe mlevi wa divai, asiwe mpiga watu, asiwe mwenye kupenda fedha chafu; bali awe mpole, asiwe mgomvi, asiwe mwenye tamaa; mtu anayeisimamia vema nyumba yake mwenyewe, akiwa na watoto wanaotii kwa heshima yote; –1 Timotheo 3:1-4. Kusudi letu hutengeneza tunakoelekea, lakini vipaumbele vyetu huweka njia ya kutufikisha huko.

Kwa bahati mbaya, baadhi ya wanaume hupandishwa kwenye huduma ya kanisa kwa maoni ya umma, lakini Mungu huchagua watu wake kulingana na vipaumbele vyao na sifa za milele. Wanaume wanaotawaliwa na mali zao, tamaa zao au vyeo vyao hawatakuwa na manufaa katika kutumikia kusudi la Mungu. Wanapenda kuitwa Mchungaji, Mchungaji Mkuu au Baba. Wanapenda kuonwa kuwa wenye bidii, maarifa, uthabiti au huruma. Je, sasa natafuta kibali cha wanadamu au cha Mungu? Au najitahidi kuwapendeza wanadamu? Kama ningekuwa bado nawapendeza wanadamu, singekuwa mtumishi wa Kristo. –Wagalatia 1:10 ASV

Kwa bahati nzuri, Mungu hana upendeleo kwa watu, na jiwe linalofaa kwa ukuta halitaachwa njiani. Wazee, maskini, vilema na viwete wote wanafaa kabisa kwa nafasi ya kuziba pengo. Wale walio na ndoto zilizovunjika, miili iliyovunjika na mioyo iliyovunjika wanaweza kusimama bila kizuizi katika ukuta pamoja na Nuhu, Ibrahimu, Yusufu, Musa, Danieli, Esta, Ruthu na kikosi kisichohesabika cha wengine. Hawa wote ni wawakilishi bora wa Mungu kwa ulimwengu huu. Wameipa kisogo anasa zisizo na maana, umaarufu, mazoea na utajiri, na wamekuwa mashujaa wa mbinguni. Wanasimama bega kwa bega kwenye ukuta na kuunda “Ubalozi wa Milele.” Walipenda huku wengine wakichukia. Walitoa vyote huku wengine wakipokea. Walidhihakiwa na kutoeleweka, walitukanwa na kufanyiwa dhihaka, walichoka na kulia.

Kwa maana sisi tu harufu nzuri ya Kristo kwa Mungu, miongoni mwa wale wanaookolewa na miongoni mwa wale wanaopotea: kwa hawa harufu ya mauti iletayo mauti; na kwa wale harufu ya uzima iletayo uzima. Na ni nani anayestahili mambo haya? –2 Wakorintho 2:15-16. Ni wale ambao makusudi na vipaumbele vyao pekee huongozwa na Mungu.

The cold, grey days of winter are being transformed into the warm, sunny days of spring. The first flowers of the year are persistently pushing their way up out of the cold earth towards the warmth of the sun. It never seems to get old—this exciting feeling in the springtime air. There’s the warmth and light of sunny days. There’s the cheery, lilting music of the song birds as they once more take up housekeeping with seemingly boundless energy. And we are again blessed with another season to plant seeds with the expectation of another crop of food to enjoy.

This year I will turn 48 years of age. My how that sounds old to me. I remember that as a youth I thought that folks who were 50 were old. Now I am almost there. For me, this is a clear reminder that we all are getting older and that we will not live forever. Next, comes a number of sobering thoughts: “What have I done for the furtherance of God’s Kingdom? Am I remaining faithful to Him in all that I do? Lord, what wilt thou have me to do—this year?” Let’s, each one, prayerfully seek the Lord about His present and future will for our lives. Let’s encourage and exhort each other to remain faithful in relationship with, and in service for, our Master.

We feel that this marriage article is quite thorough in its evaluation of building and maintaining a Biblical foundation. Lord willing, we plan to have ongoing articles relating to this subject.

Die koue, grys winterdae verander in die warm, sonnige lentedae. Die eerste blomme van die jaar dring aanhoudend deur die koue grond op, na die warmte van die son. Dit lyk asof hierdie opwindende gevoel in die lentelug nooit oud word nie. Daar is die warmte en lig van sonnige dae. Daar is die vrolike, wiegende musiek van die sangvoëls wanneer hulle weer met skynbaar onuitputlike energie nes maak. En ons is weer geseën met nog ’n seisoen waarin ons saad kan plant, met die verwagting van nog ’n oes kos om te geniet.

Ek word vanjaar 48 jaar oud. Sjoe, dit klink vir my oud. Ek onthou dat ek as jongmens gedink het mense van 50 is oud. Nou is ek amper daar. Vir my is dit ’n duidelike herinnering dat ons almal ouer word en nie vir ewig sal lewe nie. Daarna volg ’n aantal ernstige gedagtes: “Wat het ek gedoen om die uitbreiding van God se koninkryk te bevorder? Bly ek getrou aan Hom in alles wat ek doen? Here, wat wil U hê moet ek hierdie jaar doen?” Laat ons elkeen biddend die Here soek oor sy wil vir ons lewens, nou en in die toekoms. Laat ons mekaar aanmoedig en vermaan om getrou te bly in ons verhouding met ons Meester en in ons diens aan Hom.

In hierdie uitgawe is daar ’n uitstekende artikel oor die huwelik, wat ons gevoel het hierdie keer die plek van ’n artikel oor Dissipelskap kan inneem. Wanneer ons paartjies ontmoet wat al jare lank met ernstige huweliksprobleme worstel, vind ons gewoonlik dat iets op ’n grondliggende vlak nie op ’n godvrugtige manier funksioneer nie. Ons meen dat hierdie huweliksartikel ’n deeglike beoordeling bied van hoe om ’n Bybelse grondslag te bou en te handhaaf. As die Here wil, beplan ons om voortaan artikels oor hierdie onderwerp te plaas.

Ons sal na verwagting hierdie Julie ’n reeks byeenkomste in Lebanon County, Pennsylvania, aanbied. Verskeie kerke in daardie omgewing werk saam om hierdie geleentheid moontlik te maak en het die Fairview Reception Center bespreek. Bid asseblief vir hierdie byeenkomste, met die volgende in gedagte: dat God se wil volbring sal word; dat God die sprekers sal lei terwyl hulle voorberei; en dat God die kerk deur hierdie poging sal versterk. Gee hierdie inligting asseblief aan ander deur wat dalk belangstel. Merk ook die datum op jou kalender.

As jy opgedateerde inligting wil ontvang sodra al die besonderhede afgehandel is, kontak asseblief “The Berean Voice” telefonies by (330) 439-9547 of per e-pos by subscribe@bereanvoice.org. Omdat etes voorsien sal word en daar beperkte sitplek is, sal registrasie vir hierdie geleentheid verpligtend wees. Hieronder is die voorlopige titels vir die reeks en die boodskappe, maar dit kan steeds verander.

“’n Bybelse beskouing van kwessies rondom geestelike, emosionele, huweliks- en seksuele mishandeling”

  1. Om die hart te verstaan—die wortel van ALLE probleme
  2. Die Evangelie—God se antwoord op ALLE kwessies van die mens se gees en siel (psige)
  3. Hoe sielkunde en wêreldse filosofieë ons vandag beïnvloed
  4. Praktiese dissipelskap—om mense doeltreffend te help verander
  5. ’n Bybelse beskouing van geestesversteurings
  6. ’n Bybelse beoordeling van kwessies rondom aanneming en pleegsorg
  7. Om die placebo-effek te verstaan en psigiese medikasie veilig te gebruik
  8. ’n Bybelse begrip van morele mislukking, pornografie en seksuele mishandeling (slegs volwassenes)
  9. Suiwerheid—van die wieg tot bekering, en daarna tot die huwelik of ongetroude lewe (slegs ouers)
  10. Om probleme deur godvrugtige gesinne te voorkom en aan te pak
  11. Om ALLE lewensprobleme binne die plaaslike kerk te voorkom en mense daarmee te help

26–28 Julie 2019

Plek: Fairview Reception Center | 141 Jackson Rd | Lebanon, PA 17042

Kontak Rudy Yoder om te registreer: (717) 450-8640 of e-pos: theyoders@yoderhome.net

The cold, grey days of winter are being transformed into the warm, sunny days of spring. The first flowers of the year are persistently pushing their way up out of the cold earth towards the warmth of the sun. It never seems to get old—this exciting feeling in the springtime air. There’s the warmth and light of sunny days. There’s the cheery, lilting music of the song birds as they once more take up housekeeping with seemingly boundless energy. And we are again blessed with another season to plant seeds with the expectation of another crop of food to enjoy.

This year I will turn 48 years of age. My how that sounds old to me. I remember that as a youth I thought that folks who were 50 were old. Now I am almost there. For me, this is a clear reminder that we all are getting older and that we will not live forever. Next, comes a number of sobering thoughts: “What have I done for the furtherance of God’s Kingdom? Am I remaining faithful to Him in all that I do? Lord, what wilt thou have me to do—this year?” Let’s, each one, prayerfully seek the Lord about His present and future will for our lives. Let’s encourage and exhort each other to remain faithful in relationship with, and in service for, our Master.

In this issue we have an excellent article on marriage, which we felt can take the place of an article on Discipleship this time. When we meet with couples who have struggled with extreme marriage problems for years, we usually find that something is not working in a godly way at a foundational level. We feel that this marriage article is quite thorough in its evaluation of building and maintaining a Biblical foundation. Lord willing, we plan to have ongoing articles relating to this subject.

We are scheduled to share a series of meetings in Lebanon County, Pennsylvania, this coming July. Several churches in that area are working together to facilitate this event and have reserved the Fairview Reception Center. Please pray for these meetings for the following: that God’s will would be accomplished; that God would guide the speakers as they prepare; and that God would strengthen the church through this effort. Please pass this on to others who may be interested. Also, mark your calendar to save the date.

If you wish to receive updated information once all details are finalized, please contact “The Berean Voice” by phone at (330) 439-9547 or by email at subscribe@bereanvoice.org. Due to providing meals and due to seating limitations, registration will be required for this event. Below are the tentative titles for the series and the messages, but they are still subject to change.

“A Biblical View of Mental, Emotional, Marriage, and Sexual Abuse Issues”

  1. Understanding the Heart—The Root of ALL Problems
  2. The Gospel—God’s Answer for ALL Issues of the Spirit & Soul (psyche) of Man
  3. How Psychology & Worldly Philosophies Affect Us Today
  4. Practical Discipleship—Effectively Helping People Change
  5. A Biblical View of Mental Disorders
  6. Biblically Evaluating Adoption & Fostering Issues
  7. Understanding Placebo Effect & A Safe Use of Psyche Meds
  8. A Biblical Understanding of Moral Failure, Pornography, and Sexual Abuse (Adults only)
  9. Purity—From the Cradle to Conversion, then on to Marriage or Singlehood (Parents only)
  10. Preventing & Addressing Problems Through Godly Homes
  11. Preventing and Helping ALL of Life’s Struggles Within the Local Church

July 26–28, 2019

Location: Fairview Reception Center | 141 Jackson Rd | Lebanon, PA 17042

To Register contact Rudy Yoder: (717) 450-8640 or email: theyoders@yoderhome.net

冬日寒冷灰暗的日子正转变为春日温暖明媚的日子。一年中最早绽放的花朵，执着地从寒冷的泥土中破土而出，朝着温暖的阳光生长。春日空气中那种令人振奋的感觉，似乎永远不会令人厌倦：有阳光明媚日子的温暖与光亮，有鸣禽重新开始筑巢、精力仿佛无穷无尽时那欢快轻扬的歌声。我们也再次蒙福，迎来又一个播种的季节，期待收获另一季可享用的食物。

今年我将年满48岁。哎，这听起来对我来说真是老了。我记得年轻时觉得50岁的人都老了。如今我也快到那个年纪了。对我而言，这清楚地提醒我们，人人都会渐渐老去，我们不会永远活着。接下来，便浮现出一些令人警醒的思绪：“我为拓展上帝的国度做了什么？我在所做的一切事上仍忠于祂吗？主啊，今年你要我做什么？”让我们每个人都以祷告的心寻求主对我们生命现今和将来的旨意。让我们彼此鼓励、彼此劝勉，在与主的关系中以及服事我们的主时持守忠心。

本期有一篇关于婚姻的优秀文章，我们认为这次可以用它取代一篇有关门徒训练的文章。我们与多年来一直受严重婚姻问题困扰的夫妻交谈时，通常会发现，在根基层面上，有些事情并未按照敬虔的方式运作。我们认为，这篇婚姻文章对如何建立并维持合乎圣经的根基，作了相当全面的评估。若主许可，我们计划持续刊登与这一主题有关的文章。

我们计划今年七月在宾夕法尼亚州黎巴嫩县举办一系列聚会。该地区有几间教会正携手筹办这项活动，并已预订费尔维尤接待中心。请为这些聚会祷告，求上帝成就祂的旨意；求上帝在讲员预备信息时引导他们；并求上帝借着这项努力坚固教会。请将这消息转告其他可能感兴趣的人，也请在日历上标记日期，预留时间。

如果您希望在所有细节确定后收到最新消息，请通过电话（330）439-9547或电子邮件 subscribe@bereanvoice.org 联系《庇哩亚之声》。由于需要提供餐食且座位有限，参加这项活动必须注册。以下是系列活动和各场信息的暂定题目，但仍可能变更。

“从圣经看心理、情绪、婚姻及性虐待问题”

  1. 认识人心——一切问题的根源
  2. 福音——上帝对人灵与魂（心理）的所有问题的答案
  3. 心理学与世俗哲学今天如何影响我们
  4. 实际的门徒训练——有效地帮助人改变
  5. 从圣经看心理障碍
  6. 从圣经评估收养与寄养问题
  7. 认识安慰剂效应与安全使用精神类药物
  8. 从圣经认识道德失范、色情内容与性虐待（仅限成年人）
  9. 纯洁——从摇篮到归信，然后迈向婚姻或独身（仅限家长）
  10. 借着敬虔的家庭预防并处理问题
  11. 在地方教会中预防并帮助应对人生中的一切挣扎

2019年7月26日至28日

地点：费尔维尤接待中心 | 141 Jackson Rd | Lebanon, PA 17042

报名请联系鲁迪·约德：（717）450-8640，或发送电子邮件至：theyoders@yoderhome.net

As a man was dying, his thoughts went back.
Will I leave a good mark, that none can attack?
I forsook all, on the alter I went
Keeping nothing back, not even a cent.
I wanted to do, all that was right.
I sometimes prayed, all through the night.
It was easy? I cannot say.
But rather a battle, I fought everyday.
Few understood why I lived this way.
Giving up everything was foolish they’d say.
They couldn’t have seen the peace inside.
A peace that I thought, no one could hide.
A life on the run, was not my desire.
But they wanted my body, to put in the fire.
From cave to cave, I would call home
Knowing one day, I’d never more roam.
As I look back, I wouldn’t change a thing.
It has been a great honor serving my king.
But I must go now, the smoke is too thick.
My body to ashes, as the flames lick.
There is one thing, I need to ask.
Will I die in vain, or will you take up the task?
Jesus is looking for A people today
That will stand the test, and not go astray.
Giving our life is part of the cost.
Will you make that decision, before time is lost?
The church is struggling, the world has come in.
They killed our Jesus, and love their sin.
Let’s not give in, there’s too much at stake.
But rather let’s fight! There’s a kingdom to take!

–Barry Grant

Оставлю ли добрый след, которому никто не сможет повредить?
Я от всего отказался, к алтарю пришёл,
Ничего не утаил, ни единого цента.
Я хотел поступать во всём правильно.
Порой я молился всю ночь напролёт.
Легко ли было? Не могу сказать.
Но это была борьба, и я сражался каждый день.
Немногие понимали, почему я так жил.
Они говорили: глупо отказываться от всего.
Они не могли увидеть мир в моей душе.
Мир, который, как я думал, никто не мог скрыть.
Жизнь в бегах была не по мне.
Но они хотели бросить моё тело в огонь.
От одной пещеры к другой я перебирался,
Зная, что однажды больше не буду скитаться.
Оглядываясь назад, я бы ничего не изменил.
Для меня было великой честью служить моему Царю.
Но теперь мне пора: дым слишком густой.
Пламя лижет моё тело, превращая его в пепел.
Есть одна вещь, о которой я хочу спросить.
Умру ли я напрасно или ты возьмёшься за это дело?
Сегодня Иисус ищет людей,

Отдать свою жизнь — часть цены.
Примешь ли ты это решение, пока не стало слишком поздно?
Церковь переживает трудности, мир проник в неё.
Они убили нашего Иисуса и любят свой грех.
Не будем сдаваться: на кону слишком многое.
Лучше будем сражаться! Ведь нам предстоит завоевать Царство!

–Барри Грант

I am Ted. I was born a male and I know I am a male. My skin color is white, and I know I am white. My parents are white, my grandparents were white, and I have no reason to suspect my other ancestors were anything other than white. These are foundational, irrefutable truths about myself. I do not think I am anything other than what I am. Nor do I desire to be anything other than what I am.

I am a Christian. In order to better define my faith—as there are many who profess Christianity—I am a “biblical” Christian. I believe that the Bible is the Word of God, that it is to be taken literally, and that it instructs a pattern and way of life that all believers should embrace. At the age of 24—after having lived a life of my own choosing and while searching for God who, if He was real, I wanted to know—I turned to Him and I was born again. My transformation as a new creation in Christ began immediately and it continues to this day. My faith in and relationship to Jesus Christ are as foundational and irrefutable as my gender and race.

I am writing in response to that which had been extensively covered by the secular media during the Spring and Summer of 2015: a man who reportedly, throughout his life, had considered himself a female and who had been “transitioning” into a woman; a white woman who had insisted that race is “fluid” and that she is black; and the redefinition of marriage by the Supreme Court of the United States of America affecting, as well, the definition of “family” for an entire nation. These are topics which simply cannot be minimized or otherwise ignored.

The white woman lacked much public support for her explanation of race. In fact, she was significantly ridiculed for her stance. This was not true, however, regarding gender identification or “gay” marriage and family issues, and one must wonder why. If a “genetically/physiologically-constructed” male can be accepted by others as a woman simply because that’s what he thinks he is, and if a man can “marry” a man and a woman can “marry” a woman and be accepted as a married couple by others under the premise of equal rights and because that’s what they want to do, why can’t a white woman be accepted as a black woman when she is convinced that she is black?

The question raised is one of reality. Even though I may think I am the greatest pianist and music composer of all times, the evidence simply does not support that conviction. Even though a white woman says she is black, the evidence likewise does not support that conviction. Also true is that of a man who says he is a woman. The genetic and physiological evidence does not support that conviction. Without the redefinition of marriage, two people of the same sex cannot be married. And regardless of definition, they cannot reproduce on their own, one of God’s primary purposes for marriage.

Without God, man does what is right in his own eyes. So-called “progressive thinking” is simply man’s attempt, given his rejection of God, at better understanding the world and better addressing and solving its problems. Essentially, “anything goes” based upon the latest of ideas.

A biblical Christian, however, believes that God has designed, has created, and is very much involved in the universe … even in the individual lives of people who live in it. There are absolutes. There is a distinction between right and wrong. There are moral values and—something that we frequently forget in these modern times—there is an eternity ahead. As a result of progressive thinking, Darwinism now replaces Creationism, within much of our education system, students as well as teachers who profess faith in the God of the Bible are ridiculed and are otherwise discriminated against, millions of pre-born babies (the politically correct prefer calling them “fetuses”) have been legally dismembered, burnt, crushed, suctioned and pharmacologically murdered (aborted), and no-fault divorce has ravaged the families of our nation. Just look at those things that used to be considered wrong or evil which are now a normal part of our “progressing” society.

And what about eternity? Doesn’t that matter anymore, either?

In response to the Supreme Court’s ruling on gay marriage, then-President Barack Obama, clearly one of our nation’s more powerful, progressive thinkers, indicated his desire that “religious people” respond accordingly by modifying their definition of marriage as well. Believing in the God of the Bible as the Creator of the universe and as the One who designed and ordained marriage as a life-long covenant between one man and one woman, I respectfully decline Mr. Obama’s request. As the world in its own fashion deviates from the design and will of God, a true believer in Christ is called to follow Him. Jesus said, Enter through the narrow gate. For wide is the gate and broad is the road that leads to destruction, and many enter through it. But small is the gate and narrow the road that leads to life, and only a few find it. –Mat 7:13-14 NIV

I am Ted. I am a white male. I am a Christian who desires not to belittle, mock, or otherwise mistreat those with whom I may disagree, but there will be disagreements. I am called to love God and to love my neighbor as myself, regardless of who my neighbor might be. My ultimate hope is not found in this world. It is found in eternity with Christ. And my prayer for others is that they, too, may come to know Him, receive forgiveness of their sins, be transformed into the people God so desires, and spend an eternity with Him. This is not a popular message found in today’s liberal media. But for those who are interested, for those who are seeking something much better than what this world has to offer, God has an answer: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. –Joh 3:16

Soy Ted. Nací varón y sé que soy varón. Mi piel es blanca y sé que soy blanco. Mis padres son blancos, mis abuelos eran blancos y no tengo motivos para sospechar que mis otros antepasados fueran otra cosa que blancos. Estas son verdades fundamentales e irrefutables sobre mí. No creo ser otra cosa que lo que soy. Tampoco deseo ser otra cosa que lo que soy.

Soy cristiano. Para definir mejor mi fe —ya que son muchos los que profesan el cristianismo—, soy un cristiano «bíblico». Creo que la Biblia es la Palabra de Dios, que debe tomarse literalmente y que enseña un modelo y una forma de vida que todos los creyentes deberían adoptar. A los 24 años —después de haber vivido a mi manera y mientras buscaba a Dios, a quien quería conocer si realmente existía—, me volví a Él y nací de nuevo. Mi transformación en una nueva creación en Cristo comenzó de inmediato y continúa hasta el día de hoy. Mi fe en Jesucristo y mi relación con Él son tan fundamentales e irrefutables como mi género y mi raza.

Escribo en respuesta a aquello que los medios de comunicación laicos cubrieron ampliamente durante la primavera y el verano de 2015: un hombre que, según se informó, a lo largo de su vida se había considerado mujer y que estaba «transicionando» para convertirse en mujer; una mujer blanca que insistía en que la raza es «fluida» y que ella es negra; y la redefinición del matrimonio por parte de la Corte Suprema de los Estados Unidos de América, que también afecta la definición de «familia» para toda una nación. Son temas que sencillamente no se pueden minimizar ni ignorar de ningún otro modo.

La mujer blanca no recibió mucho apoyo público para su explicación de la raza. De hecho, su postura fue objeto de considerables burlas. Sin embargo, esto no ocurrió con respecto a la identificación de género ni a los asuntos del matrimonio «gay» y la familia, y uno no puede dejar de preguntarse por qué. Si los demás pueden aceptar como mujer a un hombre «de constitución genética/fisiológica» masculina simplemente porque él cree serlo, y si un hombre puede «casarse» con un hombre y una mujer puede «casarse» con una mujer, y los demás pueden aceptarlos como una pareja casada con el argumento de la igualdad de derechos y porque eso es lo que quieren hacer, ¿por qué no se puede aceptar a una mujer blanca como mujer negra cuando está convencida de que es negra?

La pregunta que se plantea es la de la realidad. Aunque yo crea que soy el mejor pianista y compositor musical de todos los tiempos, las pruebas sencillamente no respaldan esa convicción. Aunque una mujer blanca diga que es negra, las pruebas tampoco respaldan esa convicción. Lo mismo ocurre con un hombre que dice ser mujer. Las pruebas genéticas y fisiológicas no respaldan esa convicción. Sin la redefinición del matrimonio, dos personas del mismo sexo no pueden estar casadas. Y, independientemente de la definición, no pueden reproducirse por sí mismas, uno de los propósitos principales que Dios tiene para el matrimonio.

Sin Dios, el hombre hace lo que le parece correcto. El llamado «pensamiento progresista» no es más que el intento del hombre, dado que rechaza a Dios, de comprender mejor el mundo y de abordar y resolver mejor sus problemas. En esencia, «todo vale», según las ideas más recientes.

Sin embargo, un cristiano bíblico cree que Dios diseñó y creó el universo, y que está muy involucrado en él… incluso en la vida individual de las personas que viven en él. Hay absolutos. Hay una distinción entre el bien y el mal. Hay valores morales y —algo que con frecuencia olvidamos en estos tiempos modernos— nos espera una eternidad. Como resultado del pensamiento progresista, el darwinismo ha reemplazado al creacionismo en gran parte de nuestro sistema educativo; estudiantes y docentes que profesan fe en el Dios de la Biblia son ridiculizados y también discriminados; millones de bebés no nacidos (los políticamente correctos prefieren llamarlos «fetos») han sido desmembrados, quemados, aplastados, succionados y asesinados farmacológicamente (abortados) de manera legal; y el divorcio sin expresión de causa ha devastado las familias de nuestra nación. Basta con mirar esas cosas que antes se consideraban incorrectas o malvadas y que ahora son una parte normal de nuestra sociedad «progresista».

¿Y qué hay de la eternidad? ¿Ya no importa tampoco?

En respuesta al fallo de la Corte Suprema sobre el matrimonio entre personas del mismo sexo, el entonces presidente Barack Obama, sin duda uno de los pensadores progresistas más influyentes de nuestra nación, expresó su deseo de que las «personas religiosas» respondieran en consecuencia modificando también su definición del matrimonio. Como creo en el Dios de la Biblia, Creador del universo y quien diseñó y ordenó el matrimonio como un pacto para toda la vida entre un hombre y una mujer, declino respetuosamente la petición del señor Obama. A medida que el mundo, a su manera, se aparta del diseño y la voluntad de Dios, el verdadero creyente en Cristo está llamado a seguirlo. Jesús dijo: Entren por la puerta estrecha. Porque ancha es la puerta y espacioso el camino que lleva a la destrucción, y muchos entran por él. Pero estrecha es la puerta y angosto el camino que lleva a la vida, y pocos lo encuentran. –Mat 7:13-14 NIV

Soy Ted. Soy un hombre blanco. Soy un cristiano que no desea menospreciar, burlarse ni tratar mal de ninguna otra manera a quienes puedan pensar distinto de mí, pero habrá desacuerdos. Estoy llamado a amar a Dios y a amar a mi prójimo como a mí mismo, sin importar quién sea mi prójimo. Mi esperanza última no se encuentra en este mundo. Se encuentra en la eternidad con Cristo. Y mi oración por los demás es que ellos también lleguen a conocerlo, reciban el perdón de sus pecados, sean transformados en las personas que Dios tanto desea que sean y pasen la eternidad con Él. Este no es un mensaje popular en los medios liberales de hoy. Pero para quienes estén interesados, para quienes busquen algo mucho mejor que lo que este mundo ofrece, Dios tiene una respuesta: Porque tanto amó Dios al mundo, que dio a su Hijo unigénito, para que todo el que cree en él no perezca, sino que tenga vida eterna. –Joh 3:16

Many of us, in our youth, have fantasized about the ideal marriage. We have envisioned being married to someone who loves us unconditionally and who cheerfully accommodates our every peculiarity. In Ephesians 5:22-33 we find just such a marriage. Here the Apostle Paul compares the husband and wife relationship with that of the intimate relationship between Jesus Christ and His bride, the Church. He transitions so easily from the relationship between husband and wife to that of Christ and His bride that we are left wondering which one his primary focus was. In verse 22, he instructs wives to …submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord. Then in verse 25, he instructs husbands to …love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church….

Paul summarizes this passage by stating that This is a great mystery: but I speak concerning Christ and the church. –Eph 5:32. This striking parallelism leads us to believe that marriage is intended to fully reflect the intense, self-sacrificing relationship that Christ demonstrated in securing a bride for himself. This imagery is so powerful that we can only believe that from the time of creation, God designed marriage to reflect his passionate love for us.

Paul wrote, Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it; –Eph 5:25. As we observe the life of Jesus during his brief stay here on earth, we see nothing but self-sacrifice for the benefit of others. We find not a hint of self-serving. It is this selfless laying down of His life that makes the Gospel so powerfully attractive to so many.

In 2 Cor 5:14, Paul wrote, For the love of Christ constraineth us…. This is the nature of the Gospel. We are compelled by Christ’s great love for us to love him in return. This reciprocal love results in a life of devoted service that we sometimes call obedience. If you as a husband desire to have a wife that delights in devoted service to you, learn to love like Christ loved.

I. Christ loved with a “sacrificial love”

Philippians chapter two is sometimes referred to as the “great kenosis” of Christ. The Greek word kenoo found in verse seven (But made himself of no reputation), means “to pour out”. In coming to earth, Jesus laid aside his position with the Father and entered life on planet earth through a questionable conception (humanly speaking) as the son of a humble, virgin, peasant girl. That is the reputation that he adopted. He chose to identify with fallen humanity although he had every right to claim equality with God.

In the Garden of Gethsemane, Jesus demonstrated “sacrificial love” when he …prayed, saying, O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt. –Mat 26:39. Through His life and sacrificial death, he showed us that intimacy in relationship can only be found by losing ourselves in that relationship. The great bane of our day is self-love and self-absorption. Paul wrote to Timothy …that in the last days perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves… –2Ti 3:1-2

We see this prophecy being fulfilled with the advent of social networking. While it claims to be a platform where individuals can connect, it actually is a platform for the promotion of self. This obsession with self is “perilous” because it militates against intimacy in relationship and can be fatal in a marriage relationship. Intimacy in marriage is contingent upon two individuals being willing to relinquish their personal identity and assume a new joint identity.

II. Christ loved with a “faithful love”

Now before the feast of the passover, when Jesus knew that his hour was come that he should depart out of this world unto the Father, having loved his own which were in the world, he loved them unto the end. –Joh 13:1. Christ demonstrated faithful love, even in the face of rejection. John wrote that He came unto his own, and his own received him not. –Joh 1:11

Matthew wrote, But all this was done, that the scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled. Then all the disciples forsook him, and fled. –Mat 26:56. It is one thing to love those who love us in return. Jesus said that even the publicans do that much. Jesus demonstrated love to those who hated him, to those who betrayed him, to those who denied him, and he even prayed for those who crucified him. His love was sustained by a covenant commitment. He was …the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world. –Rev 13:8. He allowed nothing to deter him from his eternal purpose.

Our society has lost an understanding of covenant; hence we have so many broken marriages. Even many churches that embrace “covenant theology” in regard to salvation fail to apply those same covenant principles to marriage. Malachi clearly states that marriage is a covenant—…yet is she thy companion, and the wife of thy covenant. –Mal 2:14. Biblical covenant love is a love that is enduring whether or not it is reciprocated.

The most dramatic disclosure of covenant love is found in the Prophets. The message of the prophets is primarily that of a passionate lover “God” calling out to his unfaithful wife “Israel” to return to him—…turn ye, turn ye from your evil ways; for why will ye die, O house of Israel? –Eze 33:11. Isaiah wrote: Seek ye the LORD while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near: Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts: and let him return unto the LORD, and he will have mercy upon him; and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon. –Isa 55:6-7

Although Israel rebelled against the Lord again and again, yet we see God’s love to her as constant and unaltered. God was faithful to his covenant promise even though His bride bowed the knee to pagan altars. It is this quality of faithful covenant love that brought about the coming of a Redeemer. God made a promise in the Garden of Eden—And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel. –Gen 3:15. This promise was fulfilled in Christ some four thousand years later.

On our wedding day we promise to love “till death do us part”. This is a promise made in faith. No one can know on their wedding day what that promise may cost in the span of a lifetime. The cost is irrelevant to the commitment if there is an abiding, enduring love, rooted in the eternal faithfulness of God as our witness.

III. Christ’s love embraced suffering

One characteristic of our self-focused generation is the idea that I should not need to suffer in a relationship. This is a product of our hedonistic, pleasure-seeking society. It finds its way into our Anabaptist culture as we become increasingly affluent and as the lines of separation between us and the world become increasingly obscure. The product of this mind-set is that we have young people going into marriage thinking that “my partner will serve me, and I will be able to live like a prince or a princess.”

Our Anabaptist faith and heritage has been preserved to our day by men and women who understood that a relationship with Christ involves cross-bearing. Stories abound of families who abandoned their homeland and all that they had for the sake of the Gospel.

The concept of embracing suffering in relationship is clearly taught in Peter’s epistle. Peter was writing to a church that was enduring the raging fire of persecution. He was encouraging them to consider Christ’s example of suffering for a cause outside of themselves. Forasmuch then as Christ hath suffered for us in the flesh, arm yourselves likewise with the same mind… –1Pe 4:1. In chapter two, Peter writes: For this is thankworthy, if a man for conscience toward God endure grief, suffering wrongfully. –1Pe 2:19. Several verses later he states: For even hereunto were ye called: because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps: –1Pe 2:21.

After calling us to be willing to emulate Christ’s example of suffering in chapter two, Peter moves into chapter three by saying, Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives; While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear. –1Pe 3:1-2. This suffering for well-doing has been regarded as a high honor with Christians of all ages. Only in recent years has suffering for well-doing been regarded as “abuse”. There are at least three forces are shaping our understanding of suffering in a negative way.

1. A Selfish, Pleasure-Seeking Society

One has already been described above, which is the hedonistic (devotion to pleasure as a way of life) society in which we live.

2. The Health, Wealth, and Prosperity Gospel

A second one is the health, wealth, and prosperity gospel of many evangelical churches. The implication is that if we choose to follow Christ our lives will be overflowing with physical well-being and material abundance. This understanding is based on the promises to ancient Israel in the Old Testament of a land flowing with milk and honey. We believe this promise is fulfilled in the church age with a life that is overflowing with the fruit of the Spirit of love, joy, peace, etc. It is possible for these fruit can to abound in the midst of suffering. In fact, when others observe fruit amid another individual’s suffering, that is when it is the most noticeable and the most appreciated.

3. The Feminist Movement

The third influence that today shapes our perspective on suffering comes from the feminist movement that boldly declares that no woman should suffer or experience privation of any kind in a marriage relationship. Hence, we have a society of women with their own careers, drawing their own salary, and maintaining their own bank account. How very different from the testimony of women of faith like Sarah who …obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement. –1Pe 3:6

Suffering for the benefit of relationship has been initiated by Christ and emulated by thousands of faithful Christians throughout the church age. We are challenged by the words of the Apostle Peter and by the witness of faithful Christians to embrace suffering as a badge of the authenticity of our faith.

IV. Christ loved with a sanctifying love

God’s plan in creating us was that we would be holy as he is holy so we can experience intimate fellowship with him. But mankind rebelled against God, so he promised a redeemer. In the interim he introduced a contingency plan that was intended to prevent mankind from destroying themselves, and that was “the Law”.

However, it was never God’s intent that our relationship with him should be governed by law. He desires a love relationship with us, so he sent his Son to us and overwhelmed us with his love. We now reciprocate his love, not through fear of judgment, but as a love response to his compelling love. This concept is most clearly stated in Romans For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh [limited to what could be accomplished in the flesh], God sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh [satisfied the righteous demands of the law]: That the righteousness of the law [the full and complete fulfillment of the law] might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit. –Rom 8:3-4

Jesus accomplished through love what could never be accomplished through the strict demands of a penal code. He raised the bar on righteousness. For I say unto you, That except your righteousness shall exceed the righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees, ye shall in no case enter into the kingdom of heaven. –Mat 5:20. He showed us how to live and how to love. His sacrificial death satisfied the penal demands of the law. Through his resurrection, ascension, and the outpouring of the Holy Spirit he has empowered believers to live and to love as he did.

Paul admonishes us to relate in marriage in this same way: Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it; That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word, That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish. –Eph 5:27. Jesus came to earth to secure a bride for himself. She was not a beautiful, radiant bride that was eagerly awaiting his arrival. She was defaced by sin and living in rebellion against him—He came unto his own, and his own received him not. –Joh 1:11. Through his patient, persistent love he transformed his bride into a glorious radiant bride that stands in awe of him and joyfully worships and adores him.

Does your wife have spots and wrinkles? Are there some attitudes that you wish were different? Or are there fears and insecurities that hinder her freedom and joy? You could demand that she change and berate her for not living up to your expectations. This approach would be comparable to that of the law. It would serve to amplify her limitations and increase her anxieties. Or you could love her in spite of her spots and wrinkles. With words of compassion and encouragement you could motivate her to rise above her fears, just like Christ sanctifies his bride by his word. Jesus demonstrated that love can accomplish what harsh demands never can. Paul taught that this is a fundamental principle of marriage. It is intended to be a relationship in which the compelling force is love.

V. The great mystery

Paul concluded his treatise on marriage by saying: This is a great mystery: but I speak concerning Christ and the church. –Eph 5:32. A mystery in Biblical language in not something that cannot be comprehended, but rather something that can only be understood by those who by faith receive and embrace the Truth. It is revealed to sincere Christians; it is veiled to others.

As believers in Jesus we are privileged to understand a perspective of marriage that many cannot begin to comprehend: that sacrificial love opens the door to intimacy, that covenant love is the key to life-long fulfillment, that our willingness to suffer for the relationship proves the authenticity of our love, and finally, that the most effective way to expedite change in our spouse is unconditional love.

These principles are time-proven and Biblically-based. They are foundational to the Gospel and are a fundamental part of our Anabaptist kingdom-based theology. Where faithfully applied they will transform any marriage.

Muitos de nós, na juventude, fantasiamos sobre o casamento ideal. Imaginamos ser casados com alguém que nos ame incondicionalmente e que se acomode alegremente a cada uma de nossas peculiaridades. Em Efésios 5:22-33 encontramos um casamento assim. Aqui, o apóstolo Paulo compara a relação entre marido e mulher com a relação íntima entre Jesus Cristo e sua noiva, a Igreja. Ele passa com tanta facilidade da relação entre marido e mulher para a relação entre Cristo e sua noiva que ficamos sem saber qual delas era seu foco principal. No versículo 22, ele instrui as esposas a …sujeitai-vos a vosso próprio marido, como ao Senhor. Depois, no versículo 25, instrui os maridos a …amai vossas mulheres, como também Cristo amou a igreja….

Paulo resume esta passagem afirmando que Grande é este mistério: digo-o, porém, a respeito de Cristo e da igreja. –Ef 5:32. Esse notável paralelismo nos leva a crer que o casamento se destina a refletir plenamente a relação intensa e abnegada que Cristo demonstrou ao assegurar para si uma noiva. Essa imagem é tão poderosa que só podemos crer que, desde o tempo da criação, Deus planejou o casamento para refletir seu amor apaixonado por nós.

Paulo escreveu: Maridos, amai vossas mulheres, como também Cristo amou a igreja e a si mesmo se entregou por ela; –Ef 5:25. Ao observarmos a vida de Jesus durante sua breve permanência aqui na terra, vemos apenas abnegação em benefício dos outros. Não encontramos nem sinal de egoísmo. É essa entrega altruísta de sua vida que torna o Evangelho tão poderosamente atraente para tantos.

Em 2Co 5:14, Paulo escreveu: Porque o amor de Cristo nos constrange…. Essa é a natureza do Evangelho. O grande amor de Cristo por nós nos impele a amá-lo em retribuição. Esse amor recíproco resulta numa vida de serviço dedicado, que às vezes chamamos de obediência. Se você, como marido, deseja ter uma esposa que se alegre em servi-lo com dedicação, aprenda a amar como Cristo amou.

I. Cristo amou com “amor sacrificial”

O capítulo dois de Filipenses às vezes é chamado de “grande kenosis” de Cristo. A palavra grega kenoo, encontrada no versículo sete (Mas esvaziou-se a si mesmo), significa “derramar”. Ao vir à terra, Jesus deixou de lado sua posição junto ao Pai e entrou na vida no planeta Terra por meio de uma concepção questionável (do ponto de vista humano), como filho de uma humilde jovem camponesa e virgem. Essa foi a reputação que adotou. Escolheu identificar-se com a humanidade caída, embora tivesse todo o direito de reivindicar igualdade com Deus.

No Jardim do Getsêmani, Jesus demonstrou “amor sacrificial” quando …orou, dizendo: Meu Pai, se é possível, passe de mim este cálice; todavia, não seja como eu quero, mas como tu queres. –Mt 26:39. Por meio de sua vida e morte sacrificial, ele nos mostrou que a intimidade numa relação só pode ser encontrada quando nos perdemos nessa relação. O grande flagelo de nossos dias é o amor-próprio e a absorção em si mesmo. Paulo escreveu a Timóteo: …que nos últimos dias sobrevirão tempos trabalhosos. Porque os homens serão amantes de si mesmos… –2Tm 3:1-2

Vemos essa profecia se cumprir com o advento das redes sociais. Embora afirmem ser uma plataforma na qual as pessoas podem se conectar, na realidade são uma plataforma para a promoção de si mesmo. Essa obsessão consigo mesmo é “perigosa” porque se opõe à intimidade nas relações e pode ser fatal numa relação conjugal. A intimidade no casamento depende de duas pessoas estarem dispostas a renunciar à sua identidade pessoal e assumir uma nova identidade conjunta.

II. Cristo amou com “amor fiel”

Ora, antes da festa da Páscoa, sabendo Jesus que era chegada a sua hora de passar deste mundo para o Pai, havendo amado os seus que estavam no mundo, amou-os até ao fim. –Jo 13:1. Cristo demonstrou amor fiel, mesmo diante da rejeição. João escreveu que Veio para o que era seu, e os seus não o receberam. –Jo 1:11

Mateus escreveu: Tudo isso aconteceu para que se cumprissem as Escrituras dos profetas. Então, todos os discípulos o abandonaram e fugiram. –Mt 26:56. Uma coisa é amar aqueles que nos amam em retribuição. Jesus disse que até os publicanos fazem isso. Jesus demonstrou amor aos que o odiavam, aos que o traíram, aos que o negaram e até orou pelos que o crucificaram. Seu amor era sustentado por um compromisso de aliança. Ele era …o Cordeiro que foi morto desde a fundação do mundo. –Ap 13:8. Nada permitiu que o desviasse de seu propósito eterno.

Nossa sociedade perdeu a compreensão da aliança; por isso temos tantos casamentos desfeitos. Até mesmo muitas igrejas que abraçam a “teologia da aliança” em relação à salvação deixam de aplicar esses mesmos princípios da aliança ao casamento. Malaquias afirma claramente que o casamento é uma aliança—…ela é tua companheira e a mulher da tua aliança. –Ml 2:14. O amor bíblico da aliança é um amor duradouro, seja ou não correspondido.

A revelação mais dramática do amor da aliança encontra-se nos Profetas. A mensagem dos profetas é, sobretudo, a de um amante apaixonado, “Deus”, que chama sua esposa infiel, “Israel”, para que volte a ele—…convertei-vos, convertei-vos dos vossos maus caminhos; pois por que morreríeis, ó casa de Israel? –Ez 33:11. Isaías escreveu: Buscai ao SENHOR enquanto se pode achar, invocai-o enquanto está perto. Deixe o ímpio o seu caminho, e o homem maligno os seus pensamentos; volte-se ao SENHOR, que se compadecerá dele; e para o nosso Deus, porque grandioso é em perdoar. –Is 55:6-7

Embora Israel se rebelasse contra o Senhor repetidas vezes, vemos que o amor de Deus por ela permaneceu constante e inalterado. Deus foi fiel à sua promessa de aliança, embora sua noiva se ajoelhasse diante de altares pagãos. Foi essa qualidade de amor fiel à aliança que trouxe a vinda de um Redentor. Deus fez uma promessa no Jardim do Éden—E porei inimizade entre ti e a mulher, e entre a tua semente e a sua semente; esta te ferirá a cabeça, e tu lhe ferirás o calcanhar. –Gn 3:15. Essa promessa foi cumprida em Cristo cerca de quatro mil anos depois.

No dia do nosso casamento, prometemos amar “até que a morte nos separe”. Essa é uma promessa feita pela fé. Ninguém pode saber, no dia do casamento, quanto essa promessa poderá custar ao longo de uma vida. O custo é irrelevante para o compromisso se houver um amor constante e duradouro, arraigado na fidelidade eterna de Deus, que é nossa testemunha.

III. O amor de Cristo abraçou o sofrimento

Uma característica de nossa geração centrada em si mesma é a ideia de que eu não deveria precisar sofrer numa relação. Isso é produto de nossa sociedade hedonista e voltada à busca do prazer. Essa mentalidade também se introduz em nossa cultura anabatista, à medida que nos tornamos cada vez mais afluentes e as linhas de separação entre nós e o mundo ficam cada vez mais indistintas. O resultado dessa mentalidade é que temos jovens entrando no casamento pensando: “meu cônjuge me servirá, e poderei viver como um príncipe ou uma princesa”.

Nossa fé e herança anabatistas foram preservadas até os nossos dias por homens e mulheres que compreenderam que uma relação com Cristo envolve carregar a cruz. São inúmeras as histórias de famílias que abandonaram sua terra natal e tudo o que possuíam por causa do Evangelho.

O conceito de abraçar o sofrimento numa relação é claramente ensinado na epístola de Pedro. Pedro escrevia a uma igreja que suportava o fogo ardente da perseguição. Ele os incentivava a considerar o exemplo de Cristo, que sofreu por uma causa que não dizia respeito a si mesmo. Ora, pois, já que Cristo padeceu por nós na carne, armai-vos também vós com este mesmo pensamento… –1Pe 4:1. No capítulo dois, Pedro escreve: Porque coisa louvável é que alguém, por causa da consciência para com Deus, suporte tristezas, padecendo injustamente. –1Pe 2:19. Alguns versículos depois, afirma: Porque para isto sois chamados; pois também Cristo padeceu por nós, deixando-nos o exemplo, para que sigais as suas pisadas. –1Pe 2:21.

Depois de nos chamar, no capítulo dois, a estarmos dispostos a imitar o exemplo de sofrimento de Cristo, Pedro passa ao capítulo três dizendo: Semelhantemente, vós, mulheres, sede submissas a vosso próprio marido; para que também, se alguns não obedecem à palavra, pelo procedimento de suas mulheres sejam ganhos sem palavra; considerando a vossa vida casta, em temor. –1Pe 3:1-2. Os cristãos de todas as épocas consideraram uma grande honra sofrer por fazer o bem. Somente nos últimos anos o sofrimento por fazer o bem passou a ser considerado “abuso”. Há pelo menos três forças que estão moldando de forma negativa nossa compreensão do sofrimento.

1. Uma sociedade egoísta e voltada à busca do prazer

Uma delas já foi descrita acima: a sociedade hedonista (dedicada ao prazer como modo de vida) em que vivemos.

2. O evangelho da saúde, da riqueza e da prosperidade

Outra é o evangelho da saúde, da riqueza e da prosperidade pregado por muitas igrejas evangélicas. A implicação é que, se escolhermos seguir a Cristo, nossa vida transbordará de bem-estar físico e abundância material. Essa compreensão se baseia nas promessas feitas à antiga Israel, no Antigo Testamento, de uma terra que mana leite e mel. Cremos que essa promessa se cumpre na era da igreja por meio de uma vida que transborda do fruto do Espírito: amor, alegria, paz etc. É possível que esses frutos abundem em meio ao sofrimento. Na verdade, quando outros observam frutos em meio ao sofrimento de outra pessoa, é então que eles são mais evidentes e mais apreciados.

3. O movimento feminista

A terceira influência que hoje molda nossa perspectiva sobre o sofrimento vem do movimento feminista, que declara ousadamente que nenhuma mulher deveria sofrer ou passar por qualquer tipo de privação numa relação conjugal. Por isso, temos uma sociedade de mulheres com carreiras próprias, que recebem seus próprios salários e mantêm suas próprias contas bancárias. Como é diferente o testemunho de mulheres de fé como Sara, que …obedecia a Abraão, chamando-lhe senhor; da qual vós sois filhas, fazendo o bem e não temendo nenhum espanto. –1Pe 3:6

O sofrimento em benefício da relação foi iniciado por Cristo e imitado por milhares de cristãos fiéis ao longo da era da igreja. Somos desafiados pelas palavras do apóstolo Pedro e pelo testemunho de cristãos fiéis a abraçar o sofrimento como sinal da autenticidade de nossa fé.

IV. Cristo amou com amor santificador

O plano de Deus ao nos criar era que fôssemos santos como ele é santo, para que pudéssemos desfrutar de comunhão íntima com ele. Mas a humanidade se rebelou contra Deus, por isso ele prometeu um redentor. Nesse ínterim, introduziu um plano contingencial destinado a impedir que a humanidade se destruísse, e esse plano era “a Lei”.

No entanto, nunca foi intenção de Deus que nossa relação com ele fosse regida pela lei. Ele deseja ter uma relação de amor conosco, por isso enviou seu Filho a nós e nos inundou com seu amor. Agora correspondemos ao seu amor, não por medo do juízo, mas como resposta amorosa ao seu amor irresistível. Esse conceito é expresso com maior clareza em Romanos: Porquanto, o que era impossível à lei, visto como estava enferma pela carne [limitada ao que podia ser realizado na carne], Deus, enviando o seu próprio Filho em semelhança da carne do pecado, pelo pecado condenou o pecado na carne [satisfez as justas exigências da lei]; para que a justiça da lei [o cumprimento pleno e completo da lei] se cumprisse em nós, que não andamos segundo a carne, mas segundo o Espírito. –Rm 8:3-4

Jesus realizou por meio do amor aquilo que jamais poderia ser realizado pelas exigências rigorosas de um código penal. Ele elevou o padrão da justiça. Porque vos digo que, se a vossa justiça não exceder a dos escribas e fariseus, de modo nenhum entrareis no reino dos céus. –Mt 5:20. Ele nos mostrou como viver e como amar. Sua morte sacrificial satisfez as exigências penais da lei. Por meio de sua ressurreição, ascensão e do derramamento do Espírito Santo, ele capacitou os crentes a viver e amar como ele viveu e amou.

Paulo nos exorta a nos relacionarmos no casamento da mesma maneira: Maridos, amai vossas mulheres, como também Cristo amou a igreja e a si mesmo se entregou por ela, para a santificar, purificando-a com a lavagem da água, pela palavra, para a apresentar a si mesmo igreja gloriosa, sem mácula, nem ruga, nem coisa semelhante, mas santa e irrepreensível. –Ef 5:27. Jesus veio à terra para assegurar para si uma noiva. Ela não era uma noiva bela e radiante, que aguardasse ansiosamente sua chegada. Estava desfigurada pelo pecado e vivia em rebelião contra ele—Veio para o que era seu, e os seus não o receberam. –Jo 1:11. Com seu amor paciente e persistente, ele transformou sua noiva numa noiva gloriosa e radiante, que o contempla com reverência e o adora e louva com alegria.

Sua esposa tem manchas e rugas? Há atitudes que você gostaria que fossem diferentes? Ou há medos e inseguranças que limitam a liberdade e a alegria dela? Você poderia exigir que ela mudasse e repreendê-la por não corresponder às suas expectativas. Essa abordagem seria comparável à da lei. Serviria para realçar suas limitações e aumentar suas ansiedades. Ou você poderia amá-la apesar de suas manchas e rugas. Com palavras compassivas e encorajadoras, poderia motivá-la a superar seus medos, assim como Cristo santifica sua noiva por meio de sua palavra. Jesus demonstrou que o amor pode realizar aquilo que exigências severas jamais conseguem. Paulo ensinou que esse é um princípio fundamental do casamento. Ele deve ser uma relação em que o amor é a força que impele.

V. O grande mistério

Paulo concluiu seu tratado sobre o casamento dizendo: Grande é este mistério: digo-o, porém, a respeito de Cristo e da igreja. –Ef 5:32. Na linguagem bíblica, um mistério não é algo que não possa ser compreendido, mas algo que só pode ser entendido por aqueles que, pela fé, recebem e abraçam a Verdade. Ele é revelado aos cristãos sinceros e permanece velado para os outros.

Como crentes em Jesus, temos o privilégio de compreender uma perspectiva do casamento que muitos mal conseguem entender: que o amor sacrificial abre a porta para a intimidade, que o amor da aliança é a chave para a realização ao longo de toda a vida, que nossa disposição para sofrer pela relação comprova a autenticidade de nosso amor e, por fim, que a maneira mais eficaz de acelerar a mudança em nosso cônjuge é o amor incondicional.

Esses princípios foram comprovados pelo tempo e se baseiam na Bíblia. São fundamentais para o Evangelho e constituem parte essencial de nossa teologia anabatista, centrada no reino. Quando aplicados com fidelidade, transformarão qualquer casamento.

I am Ted. I was born a male and I know I am a male. My skin color is white, and I know I am white. My parents are white, my grandparents were white, and I have no reason to suspect my other ancestors were anything other than white. These are foundational, irrefutable truths about myself. I do not think I am anything other than what I am. Nor do I desire to be anything other than what I am.

I am a Christian. In order to better define my faith—as there are many who profess Christianity—I am a “biblical” Christian. I believe that the Bible is the Word of God, that it is to be taken literally, and that it instructs a pattern and way of life that all believers should embrace. At the age of 24—after having lived a life of my own choosing and while searching for God who, if He was real, I wanted to know—I turned to Him and I was born again. My transformation as a new creation in Christ began immediately and it continues to this day. My faith in and relationship to Jesus Christ are as foundational and irrefutable as my gender and race.

I am writing in response to that which had been extensively covered by the secular media during the Spring and Summer of 2015: a man who reportedly, throughout his life, had considered himself a female and who had been “transitioning” into a woman; a white woman who had insisted that race is “fluid” and that she is black; and the redefinition of marriage by the Supreme Court of the United States of America affecting, as well, the definition of “family” for an entire nation. These are topics which simply cannot be minimized or otherwise ignored.

The white woman lacked much public support for her explanation of race. In fact, she was significantly ridiculed for her stance. This was not true, however, regarding gender identification or “gay” marriage and family issues, and one must wonder why. If a “genetically/physiologically-constructed” male can be accepted by others as a woman simply because that’s what he thinks he is, and if a man can “marry” a man and a woman can “marry” a woman and be accepted as a married couple by others under the premise of equal rights and because that’s what they want to do, why can’t a white woman be accepted as a black woman when she is convinced that she is black?

The question raised is one of reality. Even though I may think I am the greatest pianist and music composer of all times, the evidence simply does not support that conviction. Even though a white woman says she is black, the evidence likewise does not support that conviction. Also true is that of a man who says he is a woman. The genetic and physiological evidence does not support that conviction. Without the redefinition of marriage, two people of the same sex cannot be married. And regardless of definition, they cannot reproduce on their own, one of God’s primary purposes for marriage.

Without God, man does what is right in his own eyes. So-called “progressive thinking” is simply man’s attempt, given his rejection of God, at better understanding the world and better addressing and solving its problems. Essentially, “anything goes” based upon the latest of ideas.

A biblical Christian, however, believes that God has designed, has created, and is very much involved in the universe … even in the individual lives of people who live in it. There are absolutes. There is a distinction between right and wrong. There are moral values and—something that we frequently forget in these modern times—there is an eternity ahead. As a result of progressive thinking, Darwinism now replaces Creationism, within much of our education system, students as well as teachers who profess faith in the God of the Bible are ridiculed and are otherwise discriminated against, millions of pre-born babies (the politically correct prefer calling them “fetuses”) have been legally dismembered, burnt, crushed, suctioned and pharmacologically murdered (aborted), and no-fault divorce has ravaged the families of our nation. Just look at those things that used to be considered wrong or evil which are now a normal part of our “progressing” society.

And what about eternity? Doesn’t that matter anymore, either?

In response to the Supreme Court’s ruling on gay marriage, then-President Barack Obama, clearly one of our nation’s more powerful, progressive thinkers, indicated his desire that “religious people” respond accordingly by modifying their definition of marriage as well. Believing in the God of the Bible as the Creator of the universe and as the One who designed and ordained marriage as a life-long covenant between one man and one woman, I respectfully decline Mr. Obama’s request. As the world in its own fashion deviates from the design and will of God, a true believer in Christ is called to follow Him. Jesus said, Enter through the narrow gate. For wide is the gate and broad is the road that leads to destruction, and many enter through it. But small is the gate and narrow the road that leads to life, and only a few find it. –Mat 7:13-14 NIV

I am Ted. I am a white male. I am a Christian who desires not to belittle, mock, or otherwise mistreat those with whom I may disagree, but there will be disagreements. I am called to love God and to love my neighbor as myself, regardless of who my neighbor might be. My ultimate hope is not found in this world. It is found in eternity with Christ. And my prayer for others is that they, too, may come to know Him, receive forgiveness of their sins, be transformed into the people God so desires, and spend an eternity with Him. This is not a popular message found in today’s liberal media. But for those who are interested, for those who are seeking something much better than what this world has to offer, God has an answer: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. –Joh 3:16

Ik ben Ted. Ik ben geboren als man en ik weet dat ik een man ben. Mijn huidskleur is wit en ik weet dat ik wit ben. Mijn ouders zijn wit, mijn grootouders waren wit, en ik heb geen reden om te vermoeden dat mijn andere voorouders iets anders dan wit waren. Dit zijn fundamentele, onweerlegbare waarheden over mezelf. Ik denk niet dat ik iets anders ben dan wat ik ben. Ook verlang ik er niet naar iets anders te zijn dan wat ik ben.

Ik ben christen. Om mijn geloof beter te omschrijven — aangezien velen belijden christen te zijn — ben ik een ‘bijbelse’ christen. Ik geloof dat de Bijbel het Woord van God is, dat hij letterlijk moet worden opgevat en dat hij een levenspatroon en levenswijze voorschrijft die alle gelovigen zouden moeten omarmen. Op 24-jarige leeftijd — nadat ik mijn leven had geleid zoals ik zelf wilde en terwijl ik op zoek was naar God, die ik, als Hij echt bestond, wilde leren kennen — wendde ik mij tot Hem en werd ik wedergeboren. Mijn verandering tot een nieuwe schepping in Christus begon onmiddellijk en gaat tot op de dag van vandaag door. Mijn geloof in Jezus Christus en mijn relatie met Hem zijn even fundamenteel en onweerlegbaar als mijn geslacht en ras.

Ik schrijf als reactie op datgene waarover de seculiere media in het voorjaar en de zomer van 2015 uitgebreid berichtten: een man die naar verluidt zichzelf zijn hele leven als vrouw had beschouwd en die bezig was ‘over te gaan’ naar een vrouw; een witte vrouw die had volgehouden dat ras ‘vloeibaar’ is en dat zij zwart is; en de herdefiniëring van het huwelijk door het Hooggerechtshof van de Verenigde Staten van Amerika, die ook gevolgen had voor de definitie van ‘gezin’ voor een hele natie. Dit zijn onderwerpen die eenvoudigweg niet kunnen worden gebagatelliseerd of anderszins genegeerd.

De witte vrouw kreeg weinig publieke steun voor haar uitleg van ras. Sterker nog, ze werd vanwege haar standpunt behoorlijk belachelijk gemaakt. Dat gold echter niet voor kwesties rond genderidentiteit of ‘homohuwelijk’ en gezin, en men moet zich afvragen waarom. Als anderen een ‘genetisch/fysiologisch bepaalde’ man als vrouw kunnen aanvaarden, simpelweg omdat hij denkt dat hij dat is, en als een man met een man kan ‘trouwen’ en een vrouw met een vrouw en zij door anderen als getrouwd stel kunnen worden aanvaard op grond van gelijke rechten en omdat ze dat willen, waarom kan een witte vrouw dan niet als zwarte vrouw worden aanvaard wanneer ze ervan overtuigd is dat ze zwart is?

De vraag die wordt opgeworpen, gaat over de werkelijkheid. Ook al denk ik misschien dat ik de grootste pianist en muziekcomponist aller tijden ben, het bewijs ondersteunt die overtuiging eenvoudigweg niet. Ook al zegt een witte vrouw dat ze zwart is, het bewijs ondersteunt die overtuiging evenmin. Hetzelfde geldt voor een man die zegt dat hij een vrouw is. Het genetische en fysiologische bewijs ondersteunt die overtuiging niet. Zonder herdefiniëring van het huwelijk kunnen twee mensen van hetzelfde geslacht niet getrouwd zijn. En ongeacht de definitie kunnen ze niet zelf kinderen voortbrengen, een van Gods belangrijkste bedoelingen met het huwelijk.

Zonder God doet de mens wat juist is in zijn eigen ogen. Het zogenaamde ‘progressieve denken’ is eenvoudigweg de poging van de mens om, vanwege zijn afwijzing van God, de wereld beter te begrijpen en haar problemen beter aan te pakken en op te lossen. In wezen komt het neer op: ‘alles kan’, gebaseerd op de nieuwste ideeën.

Een bijbelse christen gelooft echter dat God het universum heeft ontworpen, heeft geschapen en er nauw bij betrokken is … zelfs bij het individuele leven van de mensen die erin leven. Er zijn absolute waarheden. Er is een onderscheid tussen goed en kwaad. Er zijn morele waarden en — iets wat we in deze moderne tijd vaak vergeten — er ligt een eeuwigheid in het verschiet. Als gevolg van progressief denken heeft het darwinisme het creationisme vervangen; in een groot deel van ons onderwijssysteem worden leerlingen en leraren die hun geloof in de God van de Bijbel belijden belachelijk gemaakt en anderszins gediscrimineerd; miljoenen ongeboren baby’s (politiek correct noemt men hen liever ‘foetussen’) zijn legaal uiteengereten, verbrand, verpletterd, weggezogen en farmacologisch vermoord (geaborteerd); en echtscheidingen zonder schuldvraag hebben de gezinnen van onze natie verwoest. Kijk maar eens naar de dingen die vroeger als verkeerd of kwaad werden beschouwd en die nu een normaal onderdeel zijn van onze ‘vooruitstrevende’ samenleving.

En hoe zit het met de eeuwigheid? Doet die er ook niet meer toe?

In reactie op de uitspraak van het Hooggerechtshof over het homohuwelijk gaf toenmalig president Barack Obama, duidelijk een van de invloedrijkste progressieve denkers van ons land, aan dat hij wilde dat ‘religieuze mensen’ daarop zouden reageren door ook hun definitie van het huwelijk aan te passen. Omdat ik geloof in de God van de Bijbel als de Schepper van het universum en als Degene die het huwelijk heeft ontworpen en ingesteld als een levenslang verbond tussen één man en één vrouw, wijs ik het verzoek van de heer Obama respectvol af. Wanneer de wereld op haar eigen manier afwijkt van Gods ontwerp en wil, wordt een ware gelovige in Christus geroepen Hem te volgen. Jezus zei: Ga binnen door de nauwe poort. Want wijd is de poort en breed de weg die naar de ondergang leidt, en velen gaan daardoor naar binnen. Maar nauw is de poort en smal de weg die naar het leven leidt, en slechts weinigen vinden die. –Mat 7:13-14 NIV

Ik ben Ted. Ik ben een witte man. Ik ben een christen die niemand wil kleineren, bespotten of anderszins slecht behandelen met wie ik het misschien oneens ben, maar meningsverschillen zullen er zijn. Ik ben geroepen God lief te hebben en mijn naaste lief te hebben als mezelf, ongeacht wie mijn naaste is. Mijn uiteindelijke hoop ligt niet in deze wereld. Ze ligt in de eeuwigheid met Christus. En mijn gebed voor anderen is dat ook zij Hem mogen leren kennen, vergeving voor hun zonden ontvangen, veranderd worden in de mensen die God zo graag wil dat zij zijn, en de eeuwigheid met Hem mogen doorbrengen. Dit is geen populaire boodschap in de liberale media van vandaag. Maar voor wie geïnteresseerd is, voor wie op zoek is naar iets dat veel beter is dan wat deze wereld te bieden heeft, heeft God een antwoord: Want God had de wereld zo lief dat Hij zijn eniggeboren Zoon heeft gegeven, opdat ieder die in Hem gelooft niet verloren gaat, maar eeuwig leven heeft. –Joh 3:16
