Mile after mile sped by as Carol drove the old Chevy along the busy interstate highway toward home. Between intervals of silence and conversation, Carol and her two sisters, Elaine and Gloria, lifted their voices in song, giving thanks and praise to their Creator. How thankful they were for the opportunity to spend the evening with their friends at Pine Creek Church and to receive another inspiring message from God’s Word.

Suddenly their smooth travel was interrupted by signs of trouble. “Now what can be wrong with this car?” Carol worried out loud as she guided the stalled car to the side of the road. “Oh, no, girls, we’re out of gas! I was in such a hurry this evening that I forgot to check the gauge. I thought the tank was almost full when we left home, and… Oh no!” wailed Carol again. “Dad put the cell phone on the counter for me to take along, and I forgot that also!”

“Whatever are we going to do now?” exclaimed Elaine. “Here we are, stranded in the dark, no gas, no phone, and seven more miles to our exit! And another thing, people just don’t stop very quickly these days and offer help. They know that most everyone carries a phone. This seems almost impossible to me!” she mournfully uttered from the back seat.

As the girls lapsed into silence, the old Chevy seemed to shake in protest as a long row of trucks whizzed by. “You know,” said Gloria, “I was just remembering Brother Lester’s message this evening. How can we forget so quickly! Maybe God has allowed this to happen to us so our faith might be increased as we place our trust in Him. Let’s take this to the Lord in prayer. Let’s look for a miracle from God’s hand.”

Together the girls bowed their heads and pled for the Lord’s protection and help.

“You know, I feel better already,” smiled Elaine. “I was so worried and fearful, but since we prayed and committed everything to God, I have confidence that He will watch over us. I’m so glad we have a God who hears all of our cries. What would we do without His comforting Holy Spirit? Let’s sing again.”

“Joys are flowing like a river,
Since the Comforter has come;
He abides with us forever,
Makes the trusting heart His home.
Blessed quietness, holy quietness,
Blest assurance in my soul!
On the stormy sea Jesus speaks to me,
And the billows cease to roll!”

-Manie P. Ferguson, 19th century

As the girls sang song after song, their hearts were deeply stirred. How quiet and peaceful they felt, even though they were stranded on a dark highway thirteen miles from home. Car after car, and truck after truck sped by without stopping. Then they noticed a pickup truck, with two dirt bikes on the back, slowing down. It pulled off the road several hundred feet ahead of them, and slowly began to back up. The girls’ voices were stilled in silence as they desperately cried out to God from the bottom of their hearts. When the truck came to a halt, two husky, long-haired men jumped out. Carol rolled her window down as a man wearing a red-checked flannel jacket approached.

“What’s the trouble here, girls?” he asked, glancing over the car.

“We’re out of gas,” Carol quickly replied.

“Well, I’d say we’re pretty lucky. We have a can of gas with us. How far do you need to go yet?”

“About thirteen miles.”

“Good. We’ll just pour some of our gas into your tank and you can be on your way again. No payment necessary.”

“O thank you so much,” responded Carol. “We were praying that God would send us help, and He did more than we could ever have thought! Thanks so much.”

“Yes, yes”, replied the man gruffly, “You’re pretty lucky we came along. We’re just glad to help you out.”

Several minutes later, the girls were on their way again. “You know,” said Carol, “when I saw that truck pull over, I was scared and glad at the same time. I began to scold myself again for not having that cell phone with me. But then I asked God to help me completely trust in Him and not be afraid. After all, isn’t He much more dependable than any cell phone? This has been such a faith booster for me. How different this may have turned out, if we had depended solely on our cell phones or “good luck” as those men called it. It must grieve our Father’s heart tremendously when we do not place our trust in Him.”

“It’s just as Brother Lester preached this evening”, added Gloria. “Remember some of those verses? I waited patiently for the LORD; and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry … And he hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God… Blessed is that man that maketh the LORD his trust, and respecteth not the proud, nor such as turn aside to lies. –Psa 40:1-4. This makes me so happy I just want to keep singing and thanking the Lord!”

Again, the girls raised their voices in song:

“His eye is always watching,
His ear is keen to hear;
His love is all-sufficient
To calm the gravest fear.
Then trust Him in shine and shade;
Trust Him, be not afraid:
He’s walking close beside thee;
His hand will safely guide thee;
His wings securely hide thee;
Then trust! Be not afraid.”

-Charles H. Gabriel, 1856-1932

Les kilomètres défilaient tandis que Carol conduisait la vieille Chevy sur l’autoroute très fréquentée en direction de la maison. Entre des moments de silence et de conversation, Carol et ses deux sœurs, Elaine et Gloria, élevaient la voix pour chanter, rendant grâce et louange à leur Créateur. Comme elles étaient reconnaissantes d’avoir pu passer la soirée avec leurs amis à l’église de Pine Creek et recevoir un nouveau message inspirant tiré de la Parole de Dieu !

Soudain, leur trajet sans encombre fut interrompu par des signes de problème. « Qu’est-ce qui peut bien arriver à cette voiture ? » s’inquiéta Carol à voix haute en guidant la voiture en panne sur le bas-côté. « Oh non, les filles, nous sommes à court d’essence ! J’étais tellement pressée ce soir que j’ai oublié de vérifier la jauge. Je pensais que le réservoir était presque plein quand nous sommes parties de la maison, et… Oh non ! » s’écria de nouveau Carol. « Papa avait posé le téléphone portable sur le comptoir pour que je l’emporte, et je l’ai aussi oublié ! »

« Mais qu’allons-nous faire maintenant ? » s’exclama Elaine. « Nous voilà bloquées dans le noir, sans essence, sans téléphone, et à sept miles de notre sortie ! Et puis, les gens ne s’arrêtent plus si facilement de nos jours pour proposer leur aide. Ils savent que presque tout le monde a un téléphone. Cela me semble presque impossible ! » dit-elle tristement depuis la banquette arrière.

Alors que les filles se taisaient, la vieille Chevy semblait trembler de protestation tandis qu’une longue file de camions passait en trombe. « Vous savez, dit Gloria, je repensais justement au message de frère Lester ce soir. Comment pouvons-nous l’oublier si vite ! Peut-être que Dieu a permis que cela nous arrive afin que notre foi grandisse tandis que nous mettons notre confiance en Lui. Confions cela au Seigneur dans la prière. Attendons-nous à un miracle de la part de Dieu. »

Ensemble, les filles inclinèrent la tête et implorèrent le Seigneur de les protéger et de les aider.

« Vous savez, je me sens déjà mieux, dit Elaine en souriant. J’étais si inquiète et effrayée, mais depuis que nous avons prié et tout confié à Dieu, j’ai confiance qu’Il veillera sur nous. Je suis tellement heureuse que nous ayons un Dieu qui entend tous nos cris. Que ferions-nous sans son Saint-Esprit consolateur ? Chantons encore. »

« Les joies coulent comme un fleuve,
Depuis que le Consolateur est venu ;
Il demeure avec nous à jamais,
Et fait du cœur confiant sa demeure.
Bienheureuse quiétude, sainte quiétude,
Bienheureuse assurance dans mon âme !
Sur la mer agitée, Jésus me parle,
Et les vagues cessent de déferler ! »

-Manie P. Ferguson, XIXe siècle

À mesure que les filles enchaînaient les chants, leurs cœurs étaient profondément touchés. Elles se sentaient si calmes et paisibles, bien qu’elles fussent immobilisées sur une route sombre, à treize miles de chez elles. Voiture après voiture, camion après camion, tous passaient sans s’arrêter. Puis elles remarquèrent un pick-up, avec deux motos tout-terrain à l’arrière, qui ralentissait. Il quitta la route quelques centaines de pieds devant elles et commença lentement à reculer. Les voix des filles se turent tandis qu’elles criaient désespérément vers Dieu du fond du cœur. Quand le camion s’arrêta, deux hommes robustes aux cheveux longs en descendirent. Carol baissa sa vitre tandis qu’un homme vêtu d’une veste en flanelle à carreaux rouges s’approchait.

« Qu’est-ce qui se passe, les filles ? » demanda-t-il en jetant un coup d’œil à la voiture.

« Nous sommes à court d’essence », répondit rapidement Carol.

« Eh bien, je dirais que nous avons de la chance. Nous avons un bidon d’essence avec nous. Combien de chemin vous reste-t-il à faire ? »

« Environ treize miles. »

« Parfait. Nous allons simplement verser un peu de notre essence dans votre réservoir, et vous pourrez reprendre la route. Rien à payer. »

« Oh, merci beaucoup, répondit Carol. Nous priions pour que Dieu nous envoie de l’aide, et Il a fait bien plus que nous n’aurions jamais pu l’imaginer ! Merci infiniment. »

« Oui, oui, répondit l’homme d’un ton bourru. Vous avez de la chance que nous soyons passés par là. Nous sommes simplement heureux de pouvoir vous aider. »

Quelques minutes plus tard, les filles reprirent la route. « Vous savez, dit Carol, quand j’ai vu ce camion s’arrêter, j’ai eu peur et j’étais soulagée en même temps. J’ai recommencé à me reprocher de ne pas avoir pris mon téléphone portable. Mais ensuite, j’ai demandé à Dieu de m’aider à Lui faire entièrement confiance et à ne pas avoir peur. Après tout, n’est-Il pas bien plus fiable que n’importe quel téléphone portable ? Cette expérience a vraiment fortifié ma foi. La situation aurait pu prendre une tournure bien différente si nous avions compté uniquement sur nos téléphones portables ou sur la “chance”, comme l’ont appelé ces hommes. Notre Père doit avoir le cœur profondément attristé lorsque nous ne mettons pas notre confiance en Lui. »

« C’est exactement ce que frère Lester a prêché ce soir, ajouta Gloria. Vous vous souvenez de certains de ces versets ? J’ai patiemment attendu l’Éternel ; il s’est incliné vers moi et a entendu mon cri… Il a mis dans ma bouche un cantique nouveau, une louange à notre Dieu… Heureux l’homme qui place sa confiance en l’Éternel et ne se tourne pas vers les orgueilleux ni vers ceux qui se détournent pour suivre le mensonge. –Ps 40:1-4. Cela me rend si heureuse que j’ai envie de continuer à chanter et à remercier le Seigneur ! »

De nouveau, les filles élevèrent la voix pour chanter :

« Son œil veille sans cesse,
Son oreille entend avec acuité ;
Son amour suffit pleinement
À apaiser la plus grande peur.
Alors, fais-Lui confiance dans le soleil et dans l’ombre ;
Fais-Lui confiance, n’aie pas peur :
Il marche tout près de toi ;
Sa main te guidera en sûreté ;
Ses ailes te garderont à l’abri ;
Alors, fais confiance ! N’aie pas peur. »

-Charles H. Gabriel, 1856-1932

It was 2:30 p.m., Tuesday afternoon.

“Señora!” a chorus of voices hollered from outside our property hedge. “Open the gate!”

“Just wait,” I called back. “It’s not three o’clock yet.”

Disgruntled murmurings sounded from the other side of the hedge. I turned to my wailing baby. Sinking into the rocker to feed her, I closed my eyes to relish each quiet moment before the coming tumult.

**************

We had scarcely settled onto the farm when the neighbor children found us. They appeared—uninvited and unannounced, any time of day—to stay as long as they wished. The first ones soon brought more friends along to join in their play with the foreigner’s children and toys. Play-Doh and table games entertained them but oh, what a commotion ten children could make in a concrete house.

After much exasperation, Ernest (my husband) and I finally came up with a plan…. They could come two afternoons a week, arriving no earlier than three o’clock in the afternoon. On Tuesdays they could stay for supper, but on Thursdays they must leave by 6 p.m.

We also had other rules…. Our children needed to stay within my eyesight and earshot when playing with neighbor children. And NO closed doors. Still, questions niggled my brain. Is this a good thing or a bad one? Will we live to regret it? What if they are a bad influence on our children? My questions formed a prayer, one which God had been hearing from me quite a bit these past months. Lord, give me wisdom and patience with these children today. And if they are a bad influence on our children, Lord, please reveal that to us before our children are harmed.

But what an opportunity! This was one way I could reach the world while being a stay-at-home mom… I read them Bible stories. I taught them the need to respect and obey grownups. I told them they needed to obey me, just as my children were expected to. Transgressors, I warned, would be sent home.

Zinnia did not believe me, until the day she disobeyed and was expelled. I grin now, remembering the little troublemaker perching on the neighbor’s wall, peering over into our farm where her cousins were happily playing. Once had taught her; after that Zinnia obeyed.

**************

“Señora!” Zinnia’s voice interrupted my reverie. “Is it three o’clock yet?”

I opened one eye to peek at the clock—2:47.

“Not quite!” I hollered out the window. Placing baby into the walker, I headed to the kitchen. What would I feed them tonight?

**************

“Zinnia, I need to look in your purse before you go home.”

It was Tuesday evening again, several months later. We had been missing various small things after Zinnia started bringing a purse along on her visits to our house. Tonight, we would see if our suspicions were correct.

Zinnia’s terror-filled eyes met mine. “Just a minute, Señora. I need to use the bathroom.”

“You can use the bathroom after we look in your purse.”

“No, Señora, I can’t wait…”, her voice trailed off as she rushed to the bathroom.

I sighed. Of course, her purse would be empty when she came back out. Searching the bathroom later that night revealed treasures hidden here and there.

“Let’s chat a little, Zinnia,” I invited the following week. Zinnia sat on the bed, twisting yarn knots on the comforter, her eyes defensive, fearful. My heart yearned for the dear girl. Her mom had left years ago to work in another country, leaving the girls with their Grandma.

“I don’t care about those things you stole, Zinnia,” I began. “But it’s a habit you don’t want to start. God cares about you….”

That was the last time Zinnia, her sister, and their cousins showed up at our place. “Our Grandma doesn’t let us come anymore,” they explained.

Maybe it was Grandma; I think it was God. We had prayed much that He would make it clear if their visits were harmful to our children and if they should stop coming. My heart was torn between love for the neighbor children and protection for our own. This was the way God chose to answer.

“Thank you, God,” I prayed. “We’ll take this as your answer, and not invite them back. Send them over if you want them to come again.”

**************

Several years passed. Now it was Jon, a neighbor boy, frequenting our home.

“Could he come to your house every day after school?” his parents had wondered. “We want him to learn good things, instead of playing with boys in our neighborhood.”

Hmm. So, we’re to raise the boy while both parents work?

“He can come Tuesday and Thursday afternoons,” Ernest decided. “Those are the days I’m more often at home.”

Jon showed up faithfully on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons. Problem was, Ernest couldn’t. Other responsibilities and obligations kept coming up, hindering him from being there like he wanted to.

I did not want to nag my husband… He really wished he could be at home, working with the boys. Should I say something, or not? It didn’t seem ideal to have an unconverted boy working for hours with our son, a new Christian.

I did mention my questions to Ernest, but mostly I made it a matter of prayer.

Jon stopped coming. I was amazed. I felt for Jon, yet once again I thanked God for His answer.

**************

“How can I reach out to my neighbor children without compromising my own?” a friend asked recently. Moving to a new area, she faces the challenge of neighbor children coming over.

There are no simple answers. I have discovered the urgency of prayer, and God’s faithfulness in answering when we cry out to Him for wisdom. His answer to others may well be different from what He worked out for us.

**************

Another sister granted me permission to share their experience in relating with neighbor children:

Alex and his mother live across the road from us and began attending church soon after we moved here. Alex came over almost every day and taught our boys Spanish in short order. The boys dreaded his visits at first, but they soon became great friends. After a while another neighbor boy, Nilton, started coming at times and we thought he seemed decent enough. Then one day a third boy, José, came along. I got a distinctly uncomfortable feeling. I gave them a time limit, but just couldn’t shake the uneasy feeling. So, though I thought I didn’t have time, I decided I would work outside the whole time while they were here. I worked close to them and kept an eye on things and thought everything was fine. They seemed to just be playing together nicely, so I was surprised when they went home before the time was up.

It wasn’t long before my boys came in crying; they felt so bad about what had happened. Alex had asked them to deliver a note to his girlfriend because his mom wouldn’t like it if he did. One of the other boys told them what he does out behind bushes at public school, so he doesn’t get caught. They tried to get my boys to promise not to tell me. They didn’t promise, and I was so thankful! But they were very torn up because they thought Alex would not be their friend anymore.

My husband and I talked with the boys and assured them that they had handled the situation correctly by not promising to keep secrets. Within the hour, Alex’s mom came over to visit and we told her about it. She was very alarmed that her son had tried to pass a note and later took care of the situation with her son. I was glad that the budding relationship he had with the neighbor girl was stopped before it went any farther. Alex’s friendship with our boys has continued but the other two boys discovered that our boys had told us about them and didn’t come over for years after that.

José recently asked our eight-year-old son if he could come over to his house and play. I said no. His grandma came over several days later, offended, and said that José was very sad about it. I explained that I feel I must always be with my boys if he would come over because one time, he had tried to get our son to play an electronic war game with him. The grandma understood and was sad that her grandson was a bad influence. She wanted the best for him. We have invited him to Sunday School, but he doesn’t want that. I just hope that we can always have the type of relationship with our children that they will feel free to come to us and not keep these situations to themselves and feel guilty.

**************

Wise parents seek to remove danger, but not difficulty, from their children’s path. I was recently amazed while reading Judges 3, to discover that God wanted some enemy nations to remain in the land of Canaan. Why? He wanted parents to teach their children war (v. 2). Instead, the children of Israel made friends with the enemy nations and began to intermarry. “It seems we live closer to the world here on the mission field,” one sister shared. Our children are growing up on the front lines, as it were. This can be positive. They have frequent opportunities to “speak with the enemy in the gates,” where they are asked what we believe, and why. But when parents are lax, or their children are rebellious, this closer association with the world can prove tragic.

As we connect with God in prayer for our children, we must also connect with them. No strict safety guidelines will substitute a close relationship with your child. The mother of a child who was abused shared, “The only way your child will tell you what is going on is if you have a close relationship.”

I stagger as I consider our enemy and my own inadequacy as a mother. Suddenly I am seized with urgency to pray for things which never entered my head when our children were still young. Abuse cases exist around us; at times in our very midst. I pray for our children’s protection from the evil which surrounds them and that which rises in their hearts. I pray they will never mar another’s purity. I pray for purity at the marriage altar, both for them and their future spouses.

I pray with urgency, yet with confidence. Because this I know: God loves our children—He cares about their purity and protection even more than we as parents do—He longs for us to partner with Him in raising them to be faithful servants of His—And He wants to show Himself strong on behalf of humble parents who cry out to Him as they train soldiers in enemy territory. For the eyes of the LORD run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to shew himself strong in the behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him… –2 Chronicles 16:9.

Было 14:30 во вторник.

«Сеньора!» — хором закричали голоса снаружи, за живой изгородью вокруг нашего участка. «Откройте ворота!»

«Подождите, — крикнула я в ответ. — Ещё нет трёх часов».

По ту сторону изгороди послышалось недовольное ворчание. Я повернулась к плачущему младенцу. Опустившись в кресло-качалку, чтобы покормить её, я закрыла глаза, наслаждаясь каждой минутой тишины перед надвигающимся шумом.

**************

Мы едва успели обосноваться на ферме, как нас нашли соседские дети. Они приходили — без приглашения и предупреждения, в любое время дня — и оставались, сколько хотели. Вскоре первые привели с собой ещё друзей, чтобы играть с детьми и игрушками иностранки. Пластилин Play-Doh и настольные игры занимали их, но, о, какой шум могли поднять десять детей в бетонном доме!

После немалого раздражения мы с Эрнестом, моим мужем, наконец придумали план… Они могли приходить два раза в неделю во второй половине дня, не раньше трёх часов. По вторникам они могли оставаться на ужин, а по четвергам должны были уходить к шести вечера.

У нас были и другие правила… Когда наши дети играли с соседскими, они должны были оставаться у меня на виду и в пределах слышимости. И никаких закрытых дверей. И всё же меня не отпускали вопросы. Хорошо ли это или плохо? Не пожалеем ли мы об этом? А вдруг они дурно повлияют на наших детей? Мои вопросы складывались в молитву — такую, которую Бог часто слышал от меня в последние месяцы. Господи, дай мне сегодня мудрость и терпение с этими детьми. И если они дурно влияют на наших детей, Господи, прошу, открой нам это, прежде чем нашим детям будет причинён вред.

Но какая возможность! Так я могла достичь мира, оставаясь мамой, которая сидит дома… Я читала им библейские истории. Учила их необходимости уважать взрослых и слушаться их. Говорила, что они должны слушаться меня так же, как этого ожидалось от моих детей. Я предупредила: нарушителей отправят домой.

Зинния мне не поверила, пока однажды не ослушалась и её не выгнали. Теперь я улыбаюсь, вспоминая, как эта маленькая проказница сидела на стене соседского дома и заглядывала на нашу ферму, где её двоюродные братья и сёстры весело играли. Однажды я её научила; после этого Зинния слушалась.

**************

«Сеньора!» — голос Зиннии прервал мои размышления. «Уже три часа?»

Я приоткрыла один глаз и взглянула на часы — 2:47.

«Ещё нет!» — крикнула я в окно. Посадив малышку в ходунки, я направилась на кухню. Чем же я накормлю их сегодня вечером?

**************

«Зинния, мне нужно осмотреть твою сумочку, прежде чем ты пойдёшь домой».

Снова был вечер вторника, несколько месяцев спустя. С тех пор как Зинния стала приносить к нам сумочку, у нас пропадали разные мелочи. Сегодня мы узнаем, верны ли наши подозрения.

Её полные ужаса глаза встретились с моими. «Только минутку, сеньора. Мне нужно в туалет».

«Ты можешь сходить в туалет после того, как мы посмотрим в твою сумочку».

«Нет, сеньора, я не могу ждать…» — её голос затих, когда она поспешила в туалет.

Я вздохнула. Конечно, когда она выйдет, сумочка будет пустой. Позже той ночью, обыскав туалет, я обнаружила спрятанные здесь и там сокровища.

«Давай немного поговорим, Зинния», — предложила я на следующей неделе. Зинния сидела на кровати и накручивала узелки пряжи на покрывале; её взгляд был настороженным и испуганным. Моё сердце тянулось к этой милой девочке. Её мама уехала много лет назад работать в другую страну, оставив девочек с бабушкой.

«Мне не важны те вещи, которые ты украла, Зинния, — начала я. — Но это привычка, которую не стоит заводить. Богу небезразлична ты…»

В тот раз Зинния, её сестра и их двоюродные братья и сёстры пришли к нам в последний раз. «Бабушка больше не разрешает нам приходить», — объяснили они.

Может быть, это была бабушка; мне кажется, это был Бог. Мы много молились, чтобы Он ясно показал нам, вредят ли их визиты нашим детям и следует ли им перестать приходить. Моё сердце разрывалось между любовью к соседским детям и желанием защитить своих. Именно так Бог решил ответить.

«Спасибо Тебе, Боже, — молилась я. — Мы примем это как Твой ответ и не будем приглашать их снова. Если Ты захочешь, чтобы они пришли опять, пошли их к нам».

**************

Прошло несколько лет. Теперь к нам часто приходил Джон, мальчик из соседей.

«Может ли он каждый день после школы приходить к вам домой? — спросили его родители. — Мы хотим, чтобы он учился хорошему, а не играл с мальчиками из нашего района».

Хм. Значит, нам растить этого мальчика, пока оба родителя работают?

«Пусть приходит во вторник и четверг после обеда, — решил Эрнест. — В эти дни я чаще бываю дома».

Джон исправно приходил по вторникам и четвергам после обеда. Проблема была в том, что Эрнест не мог быть дома. То и дело возникали другие обязанности и дела, мешавшие ему быть рядом, как ему хотелось.

Мне не хотелось пилить мужа… Он очень хотел быть дома и заниматься мальчиками. Стоит ли мне что-то сказать или нет? Не казалось разумным оставлять неуверовавшего мальчика на несколько часов с нашим сыном, недавно ставшим христианином.

Я всё же поделилась с Эрнестом своими сомнениями, но главным образом молилась об этом.

Джон перестал приходить. Я удивилась. Мне было жаль Джона, но я снова поблагодарила Бога за Его ответ.

**************

«Как мне общаться с соседскими детьми, не подвергая опасности собственных?» — недавно спросила подруга. Переехав в новый район, она столкнулась с тем, что соседские дети приходят к ним домой.

Простых ответов нет. Я поняла, насколько необходима молитва и насколько верен Бог, отвечая, когда мы взываем к Нему о мудрости. Другим Он вполне может ответить иначе, чем ответил нам.

**************

Другая сестра разрешила мне поделиться их опытом общения с соседскими детьми:

Алекс и его мама живут через дорогу от нас и начали ходить в церковь вскоре после нашего переезда сюда. Алекс почти каждый день приходил к нам и быстро научил наших мальчиков испанскому. Сначала мальчики боялись его визитов, но вскоре они стали большими друзьями. Через некоторое время стал иногда приходить другой соседский мальчик, Нильтон, и нам казалось, что он вполне приличный. А однажды пришёл и третий мальчик, Хосе. У меня возникло отчётливое неприятное чувство. Я ограничила время их визита, но тревога не проходила. И хотя мне казалось, что у меня нет времени, я решила всё время, пока они будут у нас, работать во дворе. Я работала рядом с ними, следила за происходящим и думала, что всё в порядке. Казалось, они просто мирно играют вместе, поэтому я удивилась, когда они ушли раньше условленного времени.

Вскоре мои мальчики вошли в дом в слезах; им было очень плохо из-за случившегося. Алекс попросил их передать записку своей подружке, потому что его мама не одобрила бы, если бы он сделал это сам. Один из других мальчиков рассказал им, чем занимается за кустами в государственной школе, чтобы его не поймали. Они пытались взять с моих мальчиков обещание никому не рассказывать. Те не обещали, и я была так благодарна! Но они очень переживали, потому что думали, что Алекс больше не будет с ними дружить.

Мы с мужем поговорили с мальчиками и заверили их, что они поступили правильно, не обещав хранить секреты. Не прошло и часа, как мама Алекса пришла к нам в гости, и мы рассказали ей о случившемся. Она была очень встревожена тем, что сын пытался передать записку, и позже разобралась с ним. Я была рада, что зарождавшиеся отношения Алекса с соседской девочкой прекратились, пока не зашли дальше. Дружба Алекса с нашими мальчиками продолжилась, но два других мальчика узнали, что наши сыновья рассказали нам о них, и после этого годами к нам не приходили.

Недавно Хосе спросил нашего восьмилетнего сына, может ли тот прийти к нему домой поиграть. Я отказала. Через несколько дней пришла его бабушка, обиженная, и сказала, что Хосе очень расстроен. Я объяснила, что считаю необходимым всегда быть рядом с мальчиками, если он придёт к нам, потому что однажды он пытался уговорить нашего сына поиграть с ним в электронную военную игру. Бабушка поняла и огорчилась, что её внук дурно влияет на других. Она хотела для него самого лучшего. Мы приглашали его в воскресную школу, но он не хочет туда идти. Я лишь надеюсь, что у нас всегда будут такие отношения с детьми, чтобы они свободно приходили к нам, не утаивали подобные ситуации и не мучились чувством вины.

**************

Мудрые родители стараются убрать с пути своих детей опасности, но не трудности. Недавно я была поражена, читая Судей 3, и обнаружила, что Бог хотел, чтобы некоторые вражеские народы остались в земле Ханаанской. Почему? Он хотел, чтобы родители учили детей войне (ст. 2). Вместо этого израильтяне подружились с вражескими народами и стали вступать с ними в браки. «Кажется, здесь, на миссионерском поле, мы живём ближе к миру», — поделилась одна сестра. Наши дети, так сказать, растут на передовой. Это может быть полезно. У них часто появляется возможность «говорить с врагом у ворот», когда их спрашивают, во что мы верим и почему. Но когда родители беспечны или дети непокорны, такое тесное соприкосновение с миром может обернуться трагедией.

Молясь Богу о наших детях, мы должны также поддерживать связь с ними. Никакие строгие правила безопасности не заменят близких отношений с ребёнком. Мать ребёнка, подвергшегося насилию, сказала: «Единственный способ, чтобы ваш ребёнок рассказал вам о происходящем, — это близкие отношения».

Я содрогаюсь, думая о нашем враге и о собственной несостоятельности как матери. Внезапно меня охватывает настоятельная потребность молиться о том, что даже не приходило мне в голову, пока дети были маленькими. Вокруг нас происходят случаи насилия; порой — прямо среди нас. Я молюсь о защите наших детей от зла, которое окружает их и поднимается в их сердцах. Я молюсь, чтобы они никогда не запятнали чистоту другого человека. Я молюсь о чистоте у брачного алтаря — и для них, и для их будущих супругов.

Я молюсь настойчиво, но с уверенностью. Ведь одно я знаю: Бог любит наших детей — Он заботится об их чистоте и защите даже больше, чем мы, родители; Он желает, чтобы мы были Его соработниками в воспитании их верными служителями; и Он хочет явить Свою силу ради смиренных родителей, которые взывают к Нему, воспитывая воинов на вражеской территории. Ибо очи Господа обозревают всю землю, чтобы поддерживать тех, чьё сердце всецело предано Ему… — 2 Паралипоменон 16:9.

It was 2:30 p.m., Tuesday afternoon.

“Señora!” a chorus of voices hollered from outside our property hedge. “Open the gate!”

“Just wait,” I called back. “It’s not three o’clock yet.”

Disgruntled murmurings sounded from the other side of the hedge. I turned to my wailing baby. Sinking into the rocker to feed her, I closed my eyes to relish each quiet moment before the coming tumult.

**************

We had scarcely settled onto the farm when the neighbor children found us. They appeared—uninvited and unannounced, any time of day—to stay as long as they wished. The first ones soon brought more friends along to join in their play with the foreigner’s children and toys. Play-Doh and table games entertained them but oh, what a commotion ten children could make in a concrete house.

After much exasperation, Ernest (my husband) and I finally came up with a plan…. They could come two afternoons a week, arriving no earlier than three o’clock in the afternoon. On Tuesdays they could stay for supper, but on Thursdays they must leave by 6 p.m.

We also had other rules…. Our children needed to stay within my eyesight and earshot when playing with neighbor children. And NO closed doors. Still, questions niggled my brain. Is this a good thing or a bad one? Will we live to regret it? What if they are a bad influence on our children? My questions formed a prayer, one which God had been hearing from me quite a bit these past months. Lord, give me wisdom and patience with these children today. And if they are a bad influence on our children, Lord, please reveal that to us before our children are harmed.

But what an opportunity! This was one way I could reach the world while being a stay-at-home mom… I read them Bible stories. I taught them the need to respect and obey grownups. I told them they needed to obey me, just as my children were expected to. Transgressors, I warned, would be sent home.

Zinnia did not believe me, until the day she disobeyed and was expelled. I grin now, remembering the little troublemaker perching on the neighbor’s wall, peering over into our farm where her cousins were happily playing. Once had taught her; after that Zinnia obeyed.

**************

“Señora!” Zinnia’s voice interrupted my reverie. “Is it three o’clock yet?”

I opened one eye to peek at the clock—2:47.

“Not quite!” I hollered out the window. Placing baby into the walker, I headed to the kitchen. What would I feed them tonight?

**************

“Zinnia, I need to look in your purse before you go home.”

It was Tuesday evening again, several months later. We had been missing various small things after Zinnia started bringing a purse along on her visits to our house. Tonight, we would see if our suspicions were correct.

Zinnia’s terror-filled eyes met mine. “Just a minute, Señora. I need to use the bathroom.”

“You can use the bathroom after we look in your purse.”

“No, Señora, I can’t wait…”, her voice trailed off as she rushed to the bathroom.

I sighed. Of course, her purse would be empty when she came back out. Searching the bathroom later that night revealed treasures hidden here and there.

“Let’s chat a little, Zinnia,” I invited the following week. Zinnia sat on the bed, twisting yarn knots on the comforter, her eyes defensive, fearful. My heart yearned for the dear girl. Her mom had left years ago to work in another country, leaving the girls with their Grandma.

“I don’t care about those things you stole, Zinnia,” I began. “But it’s a habit you don’t want to start. God cares about you….”

That was the last time Zinnia, her sister, and their cousins showed up at our place. “Our Grandma doesn’t let us come anymore,” they explained.

Maybe it was Grandma; I think it was God. We had prayed much that He would make it clear if their visits were harmful to our children and if they should stop coming. My heart was torn between love for the neighbor children and protection for our own. This was the way God chose to answer.

“Thank you, God,” I prayed. “We’ll take this as your answer, and not invite them back. Send them over if you want them to come again.”

**************

Several years passed. Now it was Jon, a neighbor boy, frequenting our home.

“Could he come to your house every day after school?” his parents had wondered. “We want him to learn good things, instead of playing with boys in our neighborhood.”

Hmm. So, we’re to raise the boy while both parents work?

“He can come Tuesday and Thursday afternoons,” Ernest decided. “Those are the days I’m more often at home.”

Jon showed up faithfully on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons. Problem was, Ernest couldn’t. Other responsibilities and obligations kept coming up, hindering him from being there like he wanted to.

I did not want to nag my husband… He really wished he could be at home, working with the boys. Should I say something, or not? It didn’t seem ideal to have an unconverted boy working for hours with our son, a new Christian.

I did mention my questions to Ernest, but mostly I made it a matter of prayer.

Jon stopped coming. I was amazed. I felt for Jon, yet once again I thanked God for His answer.

**************

“How can I reach out to my neighbor children without compromising my own?” a friend asked recently. Moving to a new area, she faces the challenge of neighbor children coming over.

There are no simple answers. I have discovered the urgency of prayer, and God’s faithfulness in answering when we cry out to Him for wisdom. His answer to others may well be different from what He worked out for us.

**************

Another sister granted me permission to share their experience in relating with neighbor children:

Alex and his mother live across the road from us and began attending church soon after we moved here. Alex came over almost every day and taught our boys Spanish in short order. The boys dreaded his visits at first, but they soon became great friends. After a while another neighbor boy, Nilton, started coming at times and we thought he seemed decent enough. Then one day a third boy, José, came along. I got a distinctly uncomfortable feeling. I gave them a time limit, but just couldn’t shake the uneasy feeling. So, though I thought I didn’t have time, I decided I would work outside the whole time while they were here. I worked close to them and kept an eye on things and thought everything was fine. They seemed to just be playing together nicely, so I was surprised when they went home before the time was up.

It wasn’t long before my boys came in crying; they felt so bad about what had happened. Alex had asked them to deliver a note to his girlfriend because his mom wouldn’t like it if he did. One of the other boys told them what he does out behind bushes at public school, so he doesn’t get caught. They tried to get my boys to promise not to tell me. They didn’t promise, and I was so thankful! But they were very torn up because they thought Alex would not be their friend anymore.

My husband and I talked with the boys and assured them that they had handled the situation correctly by not promising to keep secrets. Within the hour, Alex’s mom came over to visit and we told her about it. She was very alarmed that her son had tried to pass a note and later took care of the situation with her son. I was glad that the budding relationship he had with the neighbor girl was stopped before it went any farther. Alex’s friendship with our boys has continued but the other two boys discovered that our boys had told us about them and didn’t come over for years after that.

José recently asked our eight-year-old son if he could come over to his house and play. I said no. His grandma came over several days later, offended, and said that José was very sad about it. I explained that I feel I must always be with my boys if he would come over because one time, he had tried to get our son to play an electronic war game with him. The grandma understood and was sad that her grandson was a bad influence. She wanted the best for him. We have invited him to Sunday School, but he doesn’t want that. I just hope that we can always have the type of relationship with our children that they will feel free to come to us and not keep these situations to themselves and feel guilty.

**************

Wise parents seek to remove danger, but not difficulty, from their children’s path. I was recently amazed while reading Judges 3, to discover that God wanted some enemy nations to remain in the land of Canaan. Why? He wanted parents to teach their children war (v. 2). Instead, the children of Israel made friends with the enemy nations and began to intermarry. “It seems we live closer to the world here on the mission field,” one sister shared. Our children are growing up on the front lines, as it were. This can be positive. They have frequent opportunities to “speak with the enemy in the gates,” where they are asked what we believe, and why. But when parents are lax, or their children are rebellious, this closer association with the world can prove tragic.

As we connect with God in prayer for our children, we must also connect with them. No strict safety guidelines will substitute a close relationship with your child. The mother of a child who was abused shared, “The only way your child will tell you what is going on is if you have a close relationship.”

I stagger as I consider our enemy and my own inadequacy as a mother. Suddenly I am seized with urgency to pray for things which never entered my head when our children were still young. Abuse cases exist around us; at times in our very midst. I pray for our children’s protection from the evil which surrounds them and that which rises in their hearts. I pray they will never mar another’s purity. I pray for purity at the marriage altar, both for them and their future spouses.

I pray with urgency, yet with confidence. Because this I know: God loves our children—He cares about their purity and protection even more than we as parents do—He longs for us to partner with Him in raising them to be faithful servants of His—And He wants to show Himself strong on behalf of humble parents who cry out to Him as they train soldiers in enemy territory. For the eyes of the LORD run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to shew himself strong in the behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him… –2 Chronicles 16:9.

Klockan var 2:30 på eftermiddagen, en tisdag.

”Señora!” ropade en kör av röster utanför häcken runt vår tomt. ”Öppna grinden!”

”Vänta lite”, ropade jag tillbaka. ”Klockan är inte tre än.”

Missnöjda mummel hördes från andra sidan häcken. Jag vände mig till min gråtande baby. Jag sjönk ner i gungstolen för att mata henne och slöt ögonen för att njuta av varje lugn stund innan tumultet bröt ut.

**************

Vi hade knappt hunnit komma till ro på gården innan grannbarnen hittade oss. De dök upp — utan inbjudan och utan förvarning, när som helst på dagen — och stannade så länge de ville. De första tog snart med sig fler vänner som ville leka med utlänningens barn och leksaker. Play-Doh och sällskapsspel roade dem, men oj, vilket oväsen tio barn kunde ställa till med i ett hus med betongväggar.

Efter mycket frustration kom Ernest (min man) och jag till slut på en plan…. De fick komma två eftermiddagar i veckan, tidigast klockan tre på eftermiddagen. På tisdagar fick de stanna och äta kvällsmat, men på torsdagar måste de gå senast klockan 6.

Vi hade också andra regler…. Våra barn behövde hålla sig inom syn- och hörhåll för mig när de lekte med grannbarnen. Och inga stängda dörrar. Ändå gnagde frågor i mitt huvud. Är det här något bra eller något dåligt? Kommer vi att ångra det? Tänk om de har dåligt inflytande på våra barn? Mina frågor blev till en bön, en bön som Gud hade hört mig be ganska ofta under de senaste månaderna. Herre, ge mig vishet och tålamod med de här barnen i dag. Och om de har dåligt inflytande på våra barn, Herre, låt oss få veta det innan våra barn kommer till skada.

Men vilken möjlighet! Det här var ett sätt för mig att nå ut till världen medan jag var hemmamamma… Jag läste bibelberättelser för dem. Jag lärde dem att de behövde respektera och lyda vuxna. Jag sa att de behövde lyda mig, precis som mina barn förväntades göra. Jag varnade dem för att den som inte lydde skulle skickas hem.

Zinnia trodde mig inte förrän den dag då hon inte lydde och blev hemskickad. Nu ler jag när jag minns den lilla busungen som satt uppe på grannens mur och kikade in på vår gård, där hennes kusiner glatt lekte. En gång hade jag lärt henne en läxa; efter det lydde Zinnia.

**************

”Señora!” Zinnias röst avbröt mina tankar. ”Är klockan tre än?”

Jag öppnade ena ögat och tittade på klockan — 2:47.

”Inte riktigt!” ropade jag ut genom fönstret. Jag satte bebisen i gåstolen och gick mot köket. Vad skulle jag bjuda dem på till kvällsmat?

**************

”Zinnia, jag behöver titta i din handväska innan du går hem.”

Det var tisdag kväll igen, flera månader senare. Olika småsaker hade försvunnit sedan Zinnia börjat ta med sig en handväska när hon kom hem till oss. I kväll skulle vi få se om våra misstankar stämde.

Zinnia mötte min blick med skräck i ögonen. ”Vänta lite, Señora. Jag behöver gå på toaletten.”

”Du kan gå på toaletten efter att vi har tittat i din handväska.”

”Nej, Señora, jag kan inte vänta…”, sa hon och lät rösten dö bort medan hon skyndade till toaletten.

Jag suckade. Hennes handväska skulle förstås vara tom när hon kom ut igen. När jag senare samma kväll letade igenom badrummet hittade jag skatter som låg gömda här och där.

”Ska vi prata lite, Zinnia?” föreslog jag veckan därpå. Zinnia satt på sängen och snurrade garnknutar på överkastet, med en avvaktande och rädd blick. Mitt hjärta ömmade för den kära flickan. Hennes mamma hade åkt till ett annat land för att arbeta flera år tidigare och lämnat flickorna hos deras mormor.

”Jag bryr mig inte om de där sakerna du stal, Zinnia”, började jag. ”Men det är en vana du inte vill börja med. Gud bryr sig om dig….”

Det var sista gången Zinnia, hennes syster och deras kusiner kom hem till oss. ”Vår mormor låter oss inte komma längre”, förklarade de.

Det kanske var mormor; jag tror att det var Gud. Vi hade bett mycket om att han skulle göra det tydligt om deras besök var skadliga för våra barn och om de skulle sluta komma. Mitt hjärta slets mellan kärleken till grannbarnen och viljan att skydda våra egna. Det var så Gud valde att svara.

”Tack, Gud”, bad jag. ”Vi tar det här som ditt svar och bjuder inte tillbaka dem. Skicka dem hit om du vill att de ska komma igen.”

**************

Flera år gick. Nu var det Jon, en grannpojke, som ofta kom hem till oss.

”Skulle han kunna komma hem till er varje dag efter skolan?” hade hans föräldrar undrat. ”Vi vill att han ska lära sig bra saker i stället för att leka med pojkarna i vårt område.”

Hmm. Så vi ska uppfostra pojken medan båda föräldrarna arbetar?

”Han kan komma på tisdagar och torsdagar eftermiddag”, bestämde Ernest. ”Det är oftare de dagarna jag är hemma.”

Jon kom troget på tisdagar och torsdagar eftermiddag. Problemet var att Ernest inte kunde vara hemma. Andra ansvarsuppgifter och åtaganden dök ständigt upp och hindrade honom från att vara där som han ville.

Jag ville inte tjata på min man… Han önskade verkligen att han kunde vara hemma och arbeta med pojkarna. Skulle jag säga något eller inte? Det kändes inte idealiskt att en pojke som inte var kristen arbetade i timmar tillsammans med vår son, som nyligen blivit kristen.

Jag tog upp mina frågor med Ernest, men framför allt gjorde jag det till en bönefråga.

Jon slutade komma. Jag blev förvånad. Jag kände med Jon, men än en gång tackade jag Gud för hans svar.

**************

”Hur kan jag nå ut till grannbarnen utan att äventyra mina egna barns väl?” frågade en vän nyligen. Hon har flyttat till ett nytt område och står inför utmaningen att grannbarnen kommer hem till henne.

Det finns inga enkla svar. Jag har upptäckt hur angeläget det är att be och hur trofast Gud är när han svarar när vi ropar till honom om vishet. Hans svar till andra kan mycket väl vara annorlunda än det han gjorde för oss.

**************

En annan syster gav mig tillåtelse att dela deras erfarenhet av umgänge med grannbarn:

Alex och hans mamma bor på andra sidan vägen och började gå i kyrkan kort efter att vi flyttat hit. Alex kom hem till oss nästan varje dag och lärde snabbt våra pojkar spanska. Till en början fasade pojkarna för hans besök, men snart blev de goda vänner. Efter ett tag började en annan grannpojke, Nilton, komma ibland, och vi tyckte att han verkade tillräckligt hygglig. Sedan kom en dag en tredje pojke, José, med. Jag fick en tydlig olustkänsla. Jag satte en tidsgräns, men kunde ändå inte skaka av mig den obehagliga känslan. Så även om jag tyckte att jag inte hade tid bestämde jag mig för att arbeta utomhus hela tiden medan de var här. Jag arbetade nära dem och höll uppsikt, och tyckte att allt verkade bra. De verkade bara leka fint tillsammans, så jag blev förvånad när de gick hem innan tiden var ute.

Det dröjde inte länge förrän mina pojkar kom in gråtande; de mådde så dåligt över det som hade hänt. Alex hade bett dem lämna en lapp till hans flickvän, eftersom hans mamma inte skulle tycka om att han gjorde det själv. En av de andra pojkarna berättade för dem vad han gör bakom buskarna på den kommunala skolan för att inte bli upptäckt. De försökte få mina pojkar att lova att inte berätta det för mig. De lovade inte, och jag var så tacksam! Men de var mycket upprörda eftersom de trodde att Alex inte skulle vara deras vän längre.

Min man och jag pratade med pojkarna och försäkrade dem om att de hade hanterat situationen rätt genom att inte lova att hålla hemligheter. Inom en timme kom Alex mamma på besök, och vi berättade för henne om det. Hon blev mycket upprörd över att hennes son hade försökt få en lapp överlämnad och tog senare hand om situationen med sin son. Jag var glad att den spirande relationen han hade med grannflickan stoppades innan den gick längre. Alex vänskap med våra pojkar har fortsatt, men de två andra pojkarna fick reda på att våra pojkar hade berättat om dem för oss och kom inte hem till oss på flera år efter det.

José frågade nyligen vår åttaårige son om han fick komma hem till honom och leka. Jag sa nej. Hans mormor kom över flera dagar senare, tog illa upp och sa att José var mycket ledsen över det. Jag förklarade att jag känner att jag alltid måste vara med mina pojkar om han kommer hit, eftersom han en gång hade försökt få vår son att spela ett elektroniskt krigsspel med honom. Mormodern förstod och var ledsen över att hennes barnbarn hade dåligt inflytande. Hon ville honom väl. Vi har bjudit med honom till söndagsskolan, men det vill han inte. Jag hoppas bara att vi alltid kan ha en sådan relation med våra barn att de känner sig fria att komma till oss och inte håller sådana här situationer för sig själva och känner skuld.

**************

Visa föräldrar försöker undanröja faror, men inte svårigheter, ur sina barns väg. Jag blev nyligen förvånad när jag läste Domarboken 3 och upptäckte att Gud ville att några fiendefolk skulle bli kvar i Kanaans land. Varför? Han ville att föräldrarna skulle lära sina barn krig (v. 2). I stället blev Israels barn vänner med fiendefolken och började gifta in sig i dem. ”Det verkar som om vi här på missionsfältet lever närmare världen”, berättade en syster. Våra barn växer så att säga upp vid frontlinjen. Det kan vara positivt. De får ofta tillfälle att ”tala med fienden i porten”, där de får frågor om vad vi tror och varför. Men när föräldrar är försumliga eller deras barn är upproriska kan den närmare kontakten med världen få tragiska följder.

När vi söker gemenskap med Gud i bön för våra barn måste vi också ha en nära relation till dem. Inga strikta säkerhetsregler kan ersätta en nära relation till ditt barn. En mamma vars barn hade utsatts för övergrepp berättade: ”Det enda sättet för ditt barn att berätta för dig vad som händer är om ni har en nära relation.”

Jag bävar när jag tänker på vår fiende och på hur otillräcklig jag själv är som mamma. Plötsligt grips jag av en stark brådska att be om sådant som aldrig föll mig in när våra barn fortfarande var små. Det finns fall av övergrepp omkring oss, ibland mitt ibland oss. Jag ber om att våra barn ska skyddas från det onda som omger dem och det som växer i deras hjärtan. Jag ber att de aldrig ska skada någon annans renhet. Jag ber om renhet vid vigselaltaret, både för dem och för deras framtida makar.

Jag ber med stor iver, men också med tillförsikt. För detta vet jag: Gud älskar våra barn — han bryr sig om deras renhet och beskydd ännu mer än vi föräldrar gör — han längtar efter att vi ska samarbeta med honom i att uppfostra dem till trogna tjänare åt honom — och han vill visa sin styrka till förmån för ödmjuka föräldrar som ropar till honom medan de tränar soldater på fiendens territorium. Ty HERRENS ögon far över hela jorden för att kraftfullt hjälpa dem som med odelat hjärta håller sig till honom… –2 Krönikeboken 16:9.

It was 2:30 p.m., Tuesday afternoon.

“Señora!” a chorus of voices hollered from outside our property hedge. “Open the gate!”

“Just wait,” I called back. “It’s not three o’clock yet.”

Disgruntled murmurings sounded from the other side of the hedge. I turned to my wailing baby. Sinking into the rocker to feed her, I closed my eyes to relish each quiet moment before the coming tumult.

**************

We had scarcely settled onto the farm when the neighbor children found us. They appeared—uninvited and unannounced, any time of day—to stay as long as they wished. The first ones soon brought more friends along to join in their play with the foreigner’s children and toys. Play-Doh and table games entertained them but oh, what a commotion ten children could make in a concrete house.

After much exasperation, Ernest (my husband) and I finally came up with a plan…. They could come two afternoons a week, arriving no earlier than three o’clock in the afternoon. On Tuesdays they could stay for supper, but on Thursdays they must leave by 6 p.m.

We also had other rules…. Our children needed to stay within my eyesight and earshot when playing with neighbor children. And NO closed doors. Still, questions niggled my brain. Is this a good thing or a bad one? Will we live to regret it? What if they are a bad influence on our children? My questions formed a prayer, one which God had been hearing from me quite a bit these past months. Lord, give me wisdom and patience with these children today. And if they are a bad influence on our children, Lord, please reveal that to us before our children are harmed.

But what an opportunity! This was one way I could reach the world while being a stay-at-home mom… I read them Bible stories. I taught them the need to respect and obey grownups. I told them they needed to obey me, just as my children were expected to. Transgressors, I warned, would be sent home.

Zinnia did not believe me, until the day she disobeyed and was expelled. I grin now, remembering the little troublemaker perching on the neighbor’s wall, peering over into our farm where her cousins were happily playing. Once had taught her; after that Zinnia obeyed.

**************

“Señora!” Zinnia’s voice interrupted my reverie. “Is it three o’clock yet?”

I opened one eye to peek at the clock—2:47.

“Not quite!” I hollered out the window. Placing baby into the walker, I headed to the kitchen. What would I feed them tonight?

**************

“Zinnia, I need to look in your purse before you go home.”

It was Tuesday evening again, several months later. We had been missing various small things after Zinnia started bringing a purse along on her visits to our house. Tonight, we would see if our suspicions were correct.

Zinnia’s terror-filled eyes met mine. “Just a minute, Señora. I need to use the bathroom.”

“You can use the bathroom after we look in your purse.”

“No, Señora, I can’t wait…”, her voice trailed off as she rushed to the bathroom.

I sighed. Of course, her purse would be empty when she came back out. Searching the bathroom later that night revealed treasures hidden here and there.

“Let’s chat a little, Zinnia,” I invited the following week. Zinnia sat on the bed, twisting yarn knots on the comforter, her eyes defensive, fearful. My heart yearned for the dear girl. Her mom had left years ago to work in another country, leaving the girls with their Grandma.

“I don’t care about those things you stole, Zinnia,” I began. “But it’s a habit you don’t want to start. God cares about you….”

That was the last time Zinnia, her sister, and their cousins showed up at our place. “Our Grandma doesn’t let us come anymore,” they explained.

Maybe it was Grandma; I think it was God. We had prayed much that He would make it clear if their visits were harmful to our children and if they should stop coming. My heart was torn between love for the neighbor children and protection for our own. This was the way God chose to answer.

“Thank you, God,” I prayed. “We’ll take this as your answer, and not invite them back. Send them over if you want them to come again.”

**************

Several years passed. Now it was Jon, a neighbor boy, frequenting our home.

“Could he come to your house every day after school?” his parents had wondered. “We want him to learn good things, instead of playing with boys in our neighborhood.”

Hmm. So, we’re to raise the boy while both parents work?

“He can come Tuesday and Thursday afternoons,” Ernest decided. “Those are the days I’m more often at home.”

Jon showed up faithfully on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons. Problem was, Ernest couldn’t. Other responsibilities and obligations kept coming up, hindering him from being there like he wanted to.

I did not want to nag my husband… He really wished he could be at home, working with the boys. Should I say something, or not? It didn’t seem ideal to have an unconverted boy working for hours with our son, a new Christian.

I did mention my questions to Ernest, but mostly I made it a matter of prayer.

Jon stopped coming. I was amazed. I felt for Jon, yet once again I thanked God for His answer.

**************

“How can I reach out to my neighbor children without compromising my own?” a friend asked recently. Moving to a new area, she faces the challenge of neighbor children coming over.

There are no simple answers. I have discovered the urgency of prayer, and God’s faithfulness in answering when we cry out to Him for wisdom. His answer to others may well be different from what He worked out for us.

**************

Another sister granted me permission to share their experience in relating with neighbor children:

Alex and his mother live across the road from us and began attending church soon after we moved here. Alex came over almost every day and taught our boys Spanish in short order. The boys dreaded his visits at first, but they soon became great friends. After a while another neighbor boy, Nilton, started coming at times and we thought he seemed decent enough. Then one day a third boy, José, came along. I got a distinctly uncomfortable feeling. I gave them a time limit, but just couldn’t shake the uneasy feeling. So, though I thought I didn’t have time, I decided I would work outside the whole time while they were here. I worked close to them and kept an eye on things and thought everything was fine. They seemed to just be playing together nicely, so I was surprised when they went home before the time was up.

It wasn’t long before my boys came in crying; they felt so bad about what had happened. Alex had asked them to deliver a note to his girlfriend because his mom wouldn’t like it if he did. One of the other boys told them what he does out behind bushes at public school, so he doesn’t get caught. They tried to get my boys to promise not to tell me. They didn’t promise, and I was so thankful! But they were very torn up because they thought Alex would not be their friend anymore.

My husband and I talked with the boys and assured them that they had handled the situation correctly by not promising to keep secrets. Within the hour, Alex’s mom came over to visit and we told her about it. She was very alarmed that her son had tried to pass a note and later took care of the situation with her son. I was glad that the budding relationship he had with the neighbor girl was stopped before it went any farther. Alex’s friendship with our boys has continued but the other two boys discovered that our boys had told us about them and didn’t come over for years after that.

José recently asked our eight-year-old son if he could come over to his house and play. I said no. His grandma came over several days later, offended, and said that José was very sad about it. I explained that I feel I must always be with my boys if he would come over because one time, he had tried to get our son to play an electronic war game with him. The grandma understood and was sad that her grandson was a bad influence. She wanted the best for him. We have invited him to Sunday School, but he doesn’t want that. I just hope that we can always have the type of relationship with our children that they will feel free to come to us and not keep these situations to themselves and feel guilty.

**************

Wise parents seek to remove danger, but not difficulty, from their children’s path. I was recently amazed while reading Judges 3, to discover that God wanted some enemy nations to remain in the land of Canaan. Why? He wanted parents to teach their children war (v. 2). Instead, the children of Israel made friends with the enemy nations and began to intermarry. “It seems we live closer to the world here on the mission field,” one sister shared. Our children are growing up on the front lines, as it were. This can be positive. They have frequent opportunities to “speak with the enemy in the gates,” where they are asked what we believe, and why. But when parents are lax, or their children are rebellious, this closer association with the world can prove tragic.

As we connect with God in prayer for our children, we must also connect with them. No strict safety guidelines will substitute a close relationship with your child. The mother of a child who was abused shared, “The only way your child will tell you what is going on is if you have a close relationship.”

I stagger as I consider our enemy and my own inadequacy as a mother. Suddenly I am seized with urgency to pray for things which never entered my head when our children were still young. Abuse cases exist around us; at times in our very midst. I pray for our children’s protection from the evil which surrounds them and that which rises in their hearts. I pray they will never mar another’s purity. I pray for purity at the marriage altar, both for them and their future spouses.

I pray with urgency, yet with confidence. Because this I know: God loves our children—He cares about their purity and protection even more than we as parents do—He longs for us to partner with Him in raising them to be faithful servants of His—And He wants to show Himself strong on behalf of humble parents who cry out to Him as they train soldiers in enemy territory. For the eyes of the LORD run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to shew himself strong in the behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him… –2 Chronicles 16:9.

화요일 오후, 오후 2시 30분이었다.

“세뇨라!” 우리 집 경계의 생울타리 너머에서 여러 목소리가 합창하듯 외쳤다. “대문을 열어 주세요!”

“기다려!” 내가 대답했다. “아직 세 시가 안 됐어.”

울타리 너머에서 불만스러운 웅성거림이 들려왔다. 나는 울고 있는 아기에게로 돌아섰다. 아기에게 젖을 먹이려고 흔들의자에 몸을 기대고는, 곧 닥칠 소란에 앞서 잠깐의 고요를 만끽하려 눈을 감았다.

**************

농장에 막 정착했을 때 이웃 아이들이 우리를 찾아냈다. 아이들은 초대도 예고도 없이 하루 중 아무 때나 나타나, 원하는 만큼 머물렀다. 처음 온 아이들은 이내 친구들을 더 데려와 외국인 아이들과 장난감을 가지고 함께 놀았다. 플레이도와 보드게임이 아이들을 즐겁게 해 주었지만, 콘크리트 집에서 아이 열 명이 얼마나 큰 소란을 피울 수 있는지!

한참 애를 먹은 끝에 남편 어니스트와 나는 마침내 계획을 세웠다…. 아이들은 일주일에 두 번 오후에 올 수 있었고, 오후 세 시보다 일찍 오면 안 되었다. 화요일에는 저녁 식사까지 함께할 수 있었지만, 목요일에는 오후 6시까지 집에 가야 했다.

다른 규칙도 있었다…. 우리 아이들이 이웃 아이들과 놀 때는 내가 보고 들을 수 있는 곳에 있어야 했다. 그리고 문을 닫아 두는 것은 절대 안 되었다. 그래도 마음속에 질문이 맴돌았다. 이게 좋은 일일까, 나쁜 일일까? 우리가 후회하게 될까? 아이들이 우리 아이들에게 나쁜 영향을 주면 어쩌지? 내 질문은 기도가 되었다. 지난 몇 달 동안 하나님께 자주 드리던 기도였다. 주님, 오늘 이 아이들을 대할 지혜와 인내를 제게 주세요. 이 아이들이 우리 아이들에게 나쁜 영향을 준다면, 우리 아이들이 해를 입기 전에 저희에게 알려 주세요.

하지만 얼마나 좋은 기회인가! 전업주부로 지내면서도 세상에 다가갈 수 있는 한 가지 방법이었다… 나는 아이들에게 성경 이야기를 읽어 주었다. 어른들을 존중하고 순종해야 한다고 가르쳤다. 우리 아이들에게 기대하는 것처럼 나에게도 순종해야 한다고 말했다. 규칙을 어기는 아이들은 집으로 돌려보내겠다고 경고했다.

지니아는 내가 정말 그렇게 할 거라고 믿지 않았다. 그러다 불순종한 어느 날 쫓겨났다. 이제 그 말썽꾸러기가 이웃집 담장에 걸터앉아, 사촌들이 우리 농장에서 신나게 노는 모습을 들여다보던 일이 떠올라 나는 미소 짓는다. 한 번 그렇게 하자, 그 뒤로 지니아는 순종했다.

**************

“세뇨라!” 지니아의 목소리가 내 생각을 끊었다. “세 시 됐어요?”

나는 한쪽 눈을 떠 시계를 힐끗 보았다. 2시 47분이었다.

“아직이야!” 창문 밖으로 외쳤다. 아기를 보행기에 앉히고 부엌으로 향했다. 오늘 저녁엔 아이들에게 뭘 먹일까?

**************

“지니아, 집에 가기 전에 네 지갑을 살펴봐야겠다.”

몇 달이 지난 또 다른 화요일 저녁이었다. 지니아가 우리 집에 올 때마다 지갑을 들고 다니기 시작한 뒤로 작은 물건들이 여러 번 사라졌다. 오늘 밤에는 우리의 의심이 맞는지 확인해 볼 참이었다.

공포에 질린 지니아의 눈이 내 눈과 마주쳤다. “잠깐만요, 세뇨라. 화장실에 다녀와야 해요.”

“지갑을 살펴본 다음에 화장실에 가도 돼.”

“안 돼요, 세뇨라. 못 참겠어요….” 지니아는 말을 흐리며 화장실로 달려갔다.

나는 한숨을 쉬었다. 물론 돌아오면 지갑은 비어 있을 것이다. 그날 밤 나중에 화장실을 뒤져 보니 여기저기에 숨겨 둔 물건들이 나왔다.

“지니아, 잠깐 이야기하자.” 다음 주에 내가 말했다. 지니아는 침대에 앉아 이불 위의 실뭉치를 꼬고 있었고, 눈에는 경계심과 두려움이 어려 있었다. 그 아이가 참 안쓰러웠다. 지니아의 엄마는 몇 년 전에 다른 나라로 일하러 떠나면서, 딸들을 할머니에게 맡겼다.

“네가 훔친 물건들은 신경 쓰지 않아, 지니아.” 내가 말을 꺼냈다. “하지만 그런 습관은 들이고 싶지 않을 거야. 하나님은 너를 아끼셔….”

그 뒤로 지니아와 그 여동생, 그리고 사촌들은 우리 집에 오지 않았다. “할머니가 이제 못 오게 하세요.” 아이들이 설명했다.

할머니의 뜻이었을 수도 있다. 하지만 나는 하나님이 하신 일이라고 생각한다. 그 아이들의 방문이 우리 아이들에게 해로운지, 이제 그만 오게 해야 할지 분명히 알려 달라고 우리는 많이 기도했다. 이웃 아이들을 사랑하는 마음과 우리 아이들을 보호하려는 마음 사이에서 갈등했다. 하나님은 이런 방식으로 기도에 응답하셨다.

“하나님, 감사합니다.” 나는 기도했다. “이것을 하나님의 응답으로 받아들이고, 아이들을 다시 부르지 않겠습니다. 다시 오기를 원하시면 아이들을 보내 주세요.”

**************

몇 년이 흘렀다. 이제는 이웃집 소년 존이 우리 집에 자주 왔다.

“존이 매일 방과 후에 댁에 가도 될까요?” 부모가 물었다. “동네 아이들과 어울려 노는 대신 좋은 것을 배우게 하고 싶어서요.”

음. 부모가 둘 다 일하는 동안 우리가 그 아이를 키우라는 건가?

“화요일과 목요일 오후에는 올 수 있어요.” 어니스트가 결정했다. “그날은 내가 집에 있는 경우가 더 많으니까요.”

존은 화요일과 목요일 오후마다 빠짐없이 왔다. 문제는 어니스트가 집에 없을 때가 많았다는 것이다. 다른 책임과 의무가 계속 생겨, 원했던 대로 그 자리에 함께하지 못했다.

남편에게 잔소리하고 싶지는 않았다… 어니스트도 집에서 아이들과 함께 시간을 보내며 지도하기를 정말 바랐다. 내가 말해야 할까, 말아야 할까? 아직 회심하지 않은 소년이 새 신자인 우리 아들과 몇 시간씩 함께 있는 건 바람직해 보이지 않았다.

내가 가진 의문을 어니스트에게 말하기는 했지만, 대부분은 기도의 문제로 맡겼다.

존은 더는 오지 않았다. 나는 놀랐다. 존이 안쓰러웠지만, 또다시 하나님의 응답에 감사했다.

**************

“내 아이들을 위험에 빠뜨리지 않으면서 이웃 아이들에게 어떻게 다가갈 수 있을까요?” 최근 한 친구가 물었다. 새 지역으로 이사한 그 친구는 이웃 아이들이 집에 찾아오는 문제에 맞닥뜨리고 있다.

간단한 답은 없다. 나는 기도가 얼마나 절실한지, 그리고 지혜를 구하며 부르짖을 때 하나님께서 신실하게 응답하신다는 것을 깨달았다. 다른 사람들에게 주시는 하나님의 응답은 우리에게 이루신 일과 다를 수도 있다.

**************

또 다른 자매가 이웃 아이들과 교류한 경험을 나누도록 허락해 주었다.

알렉스와 그의 어머니는 길 건너편에 살며 우리가 이곳에 이사 온 지 얼마 지나지 않아 교회에 다니기 시작했다. 알렉스는 거의 매일 놀러 왔고, 얼마 지나지 않아 우리 아들들에게 스페인어를 가르쳤다. 처음에는 아들들이 알렉스가 오는 걸 싫어했지만, 이내 아주 친한 친구가 되었다. 한동안 지나 다른 이웃 소년 닐턴도 가끔 오기 시작했는데, 우리 생각에는 꽤 괜찮은 아이 같았다. 그러다 어느 날 세 번째 소년 호세가 함께 왔다. 나는 뚜렷하게 불편한 느낌을 받았다. 머물 시간을 정해 주었지만, 불안한 마음을 떨칠 수가 없었다. 그래서 시간이 없다고 생각하면서도, 아이들이 있는 내내 밖에서 일하기로 했다. 가까이서 일하며 상황을 지켜보니 모든 것이 괜찮아 보였다. 아이들은 그저 사이좋게 노는 것 같았다. 그래서 약속한 시간이 되기도 전에 아이들이 돌아갔을 때 놀랐다.

얼마 지나지 않아 아들들이 울면서 들어왔다. 있었던 일 때문에 마음이 너무 괴로웠던 것이다. 알렉스는 엄마가 알면 싫어할 테니 여자 친구에게 쪽지를 전해 달라고 부탁했다. 다른 소년 하나는 공립학교에서 들키지 않으려고 학교 뒤 수풀 속에서 자기가 하는 일을 우리 아들들에게 말했다. 아이들은 우리 아들들에게 이 일을 내게 말하지 않겠다고 약속하라고 했다. 아들들은 약속하지 않았다. 정말 고마웠다! 하지만 알렉스가 더는 친구가 되어 주지 않을까 봐 몹시 괴로워했다.

남편과 나는 아이들과 이야기하며, 비밀을 지키겠다고 약속하지 않은 것이 옳은 대처였다고 안심시켜 주었다. 한 시간도 지나지 않아 알렉스의 엄마가 놀러 왔고, 우리는 그 일에 대해 이야기했다. 아들이 쪽지를 전하려 했다는 사실에 크게 놀란 알렉스의 엄마는 나중에 아들과 이 문제를 해결했다. 이웃집 여자아이와 막 시작되던 관계가 더 진전되기 전에 멈춰서 다행이었다. 알렉스는 지금도 우리 아들들과 친구로 지내지만, 다른 두 소년은 우리 아들들이 자기들에 대해 우리에게 말했다는 걸 알고는 그 뒤로 여러 해 동안 놀러 오지 않았다.

최근 호세가 여덟 살인 우리 아들에게 자기 집에 놀러 올 수 있냐고 물었다. 나는 안 된다고 했다. 며칠 뒤 호세의 할머니가 기분이 상해 우리 집에 와서, 호세가 그 일로 무척 슬퍼한다고 말했다. 나는 호세가 예전에 우리 아들에게 전자 전쟁 게임을 같이 하자고 한 적이 있어서, 그가 우리 집에 오면 늘 아들들과 함께 있어야 한다고 생각한다고 설명했다. 할머니는 이해했고, 손자가 나쁜 영향을 끼치는 아이라는 사실에 슬퍼했다. 할머니는 손자에게 가장 좋은 것을 바라셨다. 우리는 호세를 주일학교에 초대했지만, 그는 가고 싶어 하지 않는다. 우리 아이들이 이런 일을 혼자 간직하며 죄책감을 느끼지 않고 우리에게 털어놓을 수 있도록, 언제나 아이들과 그런 관계를 맺을 수 있기를 바랄 뿐이다.

지혜로운 부모는 자녀의 앞길에서 위험을 없애려 하지만, 어려움까지 없애려 하지는 않는다. 최근 사사기 3장을 읽다가 하나님께서 가나안 땅에 일부 적대 민족들을 남겨 두기를 원하셨다는 사실을 알고 깜짝 놀랐다. 왜였을까? 부모들이 자녀에게 전쟁을 가르치게 하시려는 것이었다(2절). 그러나 이스라엘 자손은 적대 민족들과 친구가 되어 그들과 통혼하기 시작했다. “선교지에서는 우리가 세상과 더 가까이 사는 것 같아요.” 한 자매가 말했다. 말하자면 우리 아이들은 최전선에서 자라고 있다. 여기에는 긍정적인 면도 있다. 아이들은 자주 “성문에서 원수와 말할” 기회를 얻고, 우리가 무엇을 믿는지, 왜 믿는지 질문을 받는다. 그러나 부모가 방심하거나 자녀들이 반항적이면, 세상과 더 가까이 지내는 일이 비극으로 이어질 수 있다.

기도로 하나님과 연결되는 동시에, 자녀들과도 연결되어야 한다. 아무리 엄격한 안전 지침도 자녀와의 친밀한 관계를 대신할 수 없다. 학대당한 아이의 어머니는 이렇게 말했다. “자녀가 무슨 일이 있는지 당신에게 말하는 유일한 길은, 당신과 친밀한 관계를 맺는 것입니다.”

우리의 원수와 어머니로서의 내 부족함을 생각하면 아찔하다. 아이들이 아직 어렸을 때는 한 번도 생각지 못한 일들을 위해 기도해야 한다는 절박함이 갑자기 나를 사로잡는다. 우리 주변에는 학대 사건이 있다. 때로는 바로 우리 가운데에도 있다. 아이들이 주변을 둘러싼 악과 아이들의 마음에서 일어나는 악으로부터 보호받도록 기도한다. 아이들이 다른 사람의 순결을 훼손하지 않기를 기도한다. 아이들과 장차 그들의 배우자들이 혼인 제단에 설 때까지 순결을 지키기를 기도한다.

절박한 마음으로 기도하지만, 확신을 가지고 기도한다. 이것을 알기 때문이다. 하나님은 우리 아이들을 사랑하신다. 하나님은 부모인 우리보다도 아이들의 순결과 보호를 더 염려하신다. 하나님은 우리가 그분과 함께 아이들을 신실한 종으로 기르기를 간절히 바라신다. 그리고 적진에서 병사들을 훈련시키며 겸손히 하나님께 부르짖는 부모들을 위해 능력을 나타내 보이고자 하신다. “여호와의 눈은 온 땅을 두루 살피시며, 전심으로 자기에게 향하는 자들을 위하여 능력을 베푸시나니….” –역대하 16:9.
