Many of us, in our youth, have fantasized about the ideal marriage. We have envisioned being married to someone who loves us unconditionally and who cheerfully accommodates our every peculiarity. In Ephesians 5:22-33 we find just such a marriage. Here the Apostle Paul compares the husband and wife relationship with that of the intimate relationship between Jesus Christ and His bride, the Church. He transitions so easily from the relationship between husband and wife to that of Christ and His bride that we are left wondering which one his primary focus was. In verse 22, he instructs wives to …submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord. Then in verse 25, he instructs husbands to …love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church….

Paul summarizes this passage by stating that This is a great mystery: but I speak concerning Christ and the church. –Eph 5:32. This striking parallelism leads us to believe that marriage is intended to fully reflect the intense, self-sacrificing relationship that Christ demonstrated in securing a bride for himself. This imagery is so powerful that we can only believe that from the time of creation, God designed marriage to reflect his passionate love for us.

Paul wrote, Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it; –Eph 5:25. As we observe the life of Jesus during his brief stay here on earth, we see nothing but self-sacrifice for the benefit of others. We find not a hint of self-serving. It is this selfless laying down of His life that makes the Gospel so powerfully attractive to so many.

In 2 Cor 5:14, Paul wrote, For the love of Christ constraineth us…. This is the nature of the Gospel. We are compelled by Christ’s great love for us to love him in return. This reciprocal love results in a life of devoted service that we sometimes call obedience. If you as a husband desire to have a wife that delights in devoted service to you, learn to love like Christ loved.

I. Christ loved with a “sacrificial love”

Philippians chapter two is sometimes referred to as the “great kenosis” of Christ. The Greek word kenoo found in verse seven (But made himself of no reputation), means “to pour out”. In coming to earth, Jesus laid aside his position with the Father and entered life on planet earth through a questionable conception (humanly speaking) as the son of a humble, virgin, peasant girl. That is the reputation that he adopted. He chose to identify with fallen humanity although he had every right to claim equality with God.

In the Garden of Gethsemane, Jesus demonstrated “sacrificial love” when he …prayed, saying, O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt. –Mat 26:39. Through His life and sacrificial death, he showed us that intimacy in relationship can only be found by losing ourselves in that relationship. The great bane of our day is self-love and self-absorption. Paul wrote to Timothy …that in the last days perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves… –2Ti 3:1-2

We see this prophecy being fulfilled with the advent of social networking. While it claims to be a platform where individuals can connect, it actually is a platform for the promotion of self. This obsession with self is “perilous” because it militates against intimacy in relationship and can be fatal in a marriage relationship. Intimacy in marriage is contingent upon two individuals being willing to relinquish their personal identity and assume a new joint identity.

II. Christ loved with a “faithful love”

Now before the feast of the passover, when Jesus knew that his hour was come that he should depart out of this world unto the Father, having loved his own which were in the world, he loved them unto the end. –Joh 13:1. Christ demonstrated faithful love, even in the face of rejection. John wrote that He came unto his own, and his own received him not. –Joh 1:11

Matthew wrote, But all this was done, that the scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled. Then all the disciples forsook him, and fled. –Mat 26:56. It is one thing to love those who love us in return. Jesus said that even the publicans do that much. Jesus demonstrated love to those who hated him, to those who betrayed him, to those who denied him, and he even prayed for those who crucified him. His love was sustained by a covenant commitment. He was …the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world. –Rev 13:8. He allowed nothing to deter him from his eternal purpose.

Our society has lost an understanding of covenant; hence we have so many broken marriages. Even many churches that embrace “covenant theology” in regard to salvation fail to apply those same covenant principles to marriage. Malachi clearly states that marriage is a covenant—…yet is she thy companion, and the wife of thy covenant. –Mal 2:14. Biblical covenant love is a love that is enduring whether or not it is reciprocated.

The most dramatic disclosure of covenant love is found in the Prophets. The message of the prophets is primarily that of a passionate lover “God” calling out to his unfaithful wife “Israel” to return to him—…turn ye, turn ye from your evil ways; for why will ye die, O house of Israel? –Eze 33:11. Isaiah wrote: Seek ye the LORD while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near: Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts: and let him return unto the LORD, and he will have mercy upon him; and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon. –Isa 55:6-7

Although Israel rebelled against the Lord again and again, yet we see God’s love to her as constant and unaltered. God was faithful to his covenant promise even though His bride bowed the knee to pagan altars. It is this quality of faithful covenant love that brought about the coming of a Redeemer. God made a promise in the Garden of Eden—And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel. –Gen 3:15. This promise was fulfilled in Christ some four thousand years later.

On our wedding day we promise to love “till death do us part”. This is a promise made in faith. No one can know on their wedding day what that promise may cost in the span of a lifetime. The cost is irrelevant to the commitment if there is an abiding, enduring love, rooted in the eternal faithfulness of God as our witness.

III. Christ’s love embraced suffering

One characteristic of our self-focused generation is the idea that I should not need to suffer in a relationship. This is a product of our hedonistic, pleasure-seeking society. It finds its way into our Anabaptist culture as we become increasingly affluent and as the lines of separation between us and the world become increasingly obscure. The product of this mind-set is that we have young people going into marriage thinking that “my partner will serve me, and I will be able to live like a prince or a princess.”

Our Anabaptist faith and heritage has been preserved to our day by men and women who understood that a relationship with Christ involves cross-bearing. Stories abound of families who abandoned their homeland and all that they had for the sake of the Gospel.

The concept of embracing suffering in relationship is clearly taught in Peter’s epistle. Peter was writing to a church that was enduring the raging fire of persecution. He was encouraging them to consider Christ’s example of suffering for a cause outside of themselves. Forasmuch then as Christ hath suffered for us in the flesh, arm yourselves likewise with the same mind… –1Pe 4:1. In chapter two, Peter writes: For this is thankworthy, if a man for conscience toward God endure grief, suffering wrongfully. –1Pe 2:19. Several verses later he states: For even hereunto were ye called: because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps: –1Pe 2:21.

After calling us to be willing to emulate Christ’s example of suffering in chapter two, Peter moves into chapter three by saying, Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives; While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear. –1Pe 3:1-2. This suffering for well-doing has been regarded as a high honor with Christians of all ages. Only in recent years has suffering for well-doing been regarded as “abuse”. There are at least three forces are shaping our understanding of suffering in a negative way.

1. A Selfish, Pleasure-Seeking Society

One has already been described above, which is the hedonistic (devotion to pleasure as a way of life) society in which we live.

2. The Health, Wealth, and Prosperity Gospel

A second one is the health, wealth, and prosperity gospel of many evangelical churches. The implication is that if we choose to follow Christ our lives will be overflowing with physical well-being and material abundance. This understanding is based on the promises to ancient Israel in the Old Testament of a land flowing with milk and honey. We believe this promise is fulfilled in the church age with a life that is overflowing with the fruit of the Spirit of love, joy, peace, etc. It is possible for these fruit can to abound in the midst of suffering. In fact, when others observe fruit amid another individual’s suffering, that is when it is the most noticeable and the most appreciated.

3. The Feminist Movement

The third influence that today shapes our perspective on suffering comes from the feminist movement that boldly declares that no woman should suffer or experience privation of any kind in a marriage relationship. Hence, we have a society of women with their own careers, drawing their own salary, and maintaining their own bank account. How very different from the testimony of women of faith like Sarah who …obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement. –1Pe 3:6

Suffering for the benefit of relationship has been initiated by Christ and emulated by thousands of faithful Christians throughout the church age. We are challenged by the words of the Apostle Peter and by the witness of faithful Christians to embrace suffering as a badge of the authenticity of our faith.

IV. Christ loved with a sanctifying love

God’s plan in creating us was that we would be holy as he is holy so we can experience intimate fellowship with him. But mankind rebelled against God, so he promised a redeemer. In the interim he introduced a contingency plan that was intended to prevent mankind from destroying themselves, and that was “the Law”.

However, it was never God’s intent that our relationship with him should be governed by law. He desires a love relationship with us, so he sent his Son to us and overwhelmed us with his love. We now reciprocate his love, not through fear of judgment, but as a love response to his compelling love. This concept is most clearly stated in Romans For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh [limited to what could be accomplished in the flesh], God sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh [satisfied the righteous demands of the law]: That the righteousness of the law [the full and complete fulfillment of the law] might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit. –Rom 8:3-4

Jesus accomplished through love what could never be accomplished through the strict demands of a penal code. He raised the bar on righteousness. For I say unto you, That except your righteousness shall exceed the righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees, ye shall in no case enter into the kingdom of heaven. –Mat 5:20. He showed us how to live and how to love. His sacrificial death satisfied the penal demands of the law. Through his resurrection, ascension, and the outpouring of the Holy Spirit he has empowered believers to live and to love as he did.

Paul admonishes us to relate in marriage in this same way: Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it; That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word, That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish. –Eph 5:27. Jesus came to earth to secure a bride for himself. She was not a beautiful, radiant bride that was eagerly awaiting his arrival. She was defaced by sin and living in rebellion against him—He came unto his own, and his own received him not. –Joh 1:11. Through his patient, persistent love he transformed his bride into a glorious radiant bride that stands in awe of him and joyfully worships and adores him.

Does your wife have spots and wrinkles? Are there some attitudes that you wish were different? Or are there fears and insecurities that hinder her freedom and joy? You could demand that she change and berate her for not living up to your expectations. This approach would be comparable to that of the law. It would serve to amplify her limitations and increase her anxieties. Or you could love her in spite of her spots and wrinkles. With words of compassion and encouragement you could motivate her to rise above her fears, just like Christ sanctifies his bride by his word. Jesus demonstrated that love can accomplish what harsh demands never can. Paul taught that this is a fundamental principle of marriage. It is intended to be a relationship in which the compelling force is love.

V. The great mystery

Paul concluded his treatise on marriage by saying: This is a great mystery: but I speak concerning Christ and the church. –Eph 5:32. A mystery in Biblical language in not something that cannot be comprehended, but rather something that can only be understood by those who by faith receive and embrace the Truth. It is revealed to sincere Christians; it is veiled to others.

As believers in Jesus we are privileged to understand a perspective of marriage that many cannot begin to comprehend: that sacrificial love opens the door to intimacy, that covenant love is the key to life-long fulfillment, that our willingness to suffer for the relationship proves the authenticity of our love, and finally, that the most effective way to expedite change in our spouse is unconditional love.

These principles are time-proven and Biblically-based. They are foundational to the Gospel and are a fundamental part of our Anabaptist kingdom-based theology. Where faithfully applied they will transform any marriage.

Baie van ons het in ons jeug oor die ideale huwelik gefantaseer. Ons het ons voorgestel dat ons getroud is met iemand wat ons onvoorwaardelik liefhet en elkeen van ons eienaardighede met blymoedigheid aanvaar. In Efesiërs 5:22-33 vind ons juis so ’n huwelik. Hier vergelyk die apostel Paulus die verhouding tussen man en vrou met die intieme verhouding tussen Jesus Christus en sy bruid, die Kerk. Hy beweeg so moeiteloos van die verhouding tussen man en vrou na dié van Christus en sy bruid dat ons wonder op watter een hy hoofsaaklik fokus. In vers 22 vermaan hy vroue: …wees aan julle eie mans onderdanig, soos aan die Here. Dan vermaan hy in vers 25 mans: …julle moet jul vroue liefhê, soos Christus ook die gemeente liefgehad het….

Paulus som hierdie gedeelte op deur te sê: Hierdie verborgenheid is groot; maar ek sê dit met die oog op Christus en die gemeente. –Ef 5:32. Hierdie treffende parallel lei ons tot die gevolgtrekking dat die huwelik bedoel is om die intense, selfopofferende verhouding wat Christus getoon het toe Hy vir Homself ’n bruid verwerf het, ten volle te weerspieël. Hierdie beeldspraak is so kragtig dat ons net kan glo dat God die huwelik van die skepping af ontwerp het om sy vurige liefde vir ons te weerspieël.

Paulus het geskryf: Manne, julle moet jul eie vroue liefhê, soos Christus ook die gemeente liefgehad en Homself daarvoor oorgegee het; –Ef 5:25. Wanneer ons Jesus se lewe tydens sy kort verblyf hier op aarde waarneem, sien ons niks anders nie as selfopoffering tot voordeel van ander. Ons vind nie die geringste teken van selfsug nie. Dit is hierdie onselfsugtige oorgawe van sy lewe wat die Evangelie vir so baie so kragtig aantreklik maak.

In 2 Kor 5:14 het Paulus geskryf: Want die liefde van Christus dring ons…. Dit is die aard van die Evangelie. Christus se groot liefde vir ons dwing ons om Hom op ons beurt lief te hê. Hierdie wedersydse liefde lei tot ’n lewe van toegewyde diens, wat ons soms gehoorsaamheid noem. As jy as man ’n vrou wil hê wat dit geniet om jou toegewyd te dien, leer om lief te hê soos Christus liefgehad het.

I. Christus het met ’n “opofferende liefde” liefgehad

Filippense hoofstuk twee word soms die “groot kenosis” van Christus genoem. Die Griekse woord kenoo wat in vers sewe voorkom (maar het Homself ontledig), beteken “uitgiet”. Toe Jesus na die aarde gekom het, het Hy sy posisie by die Vader opsygesit en die lewe op planeet Aarde betree deur ’n bedenklike ontvangenis (menslik gesproke), as die seun van ’n nederige, maagdelike boeremeisie. Dit was die reputasie wat Hy aangeneem het. Hy het gekies om Hom met die gevalle mensdom te vereenselwig, hoewel Hy alle reg gehad het om gelykheid met God op te eis.

In die tuin van Getsemane het Jesus “opofferende liefde” getoon toe Hy …gebid en gesê het: My Vader, as dit moontlik is, laat hierdie beker by My verbygaan; nogtans nie soos Ek wil nie, maar soos U wil. –Matt 26:39. Deur sy lewe en selfopofferende dood het Hy ons gewys dat intimiteit in ’n verhouding slegs gevind kan word wanneer ons onsself in daardie verhouding verloor. Die groot euwel van ons tyd is selfliefde en selfbeheptheid. Paulus het aan Timoteus geskryf: …dat daar in die laaste dae swaar tye sal kom. Want die mense sal liefhebbers van hulleself wees… –2 Tim 3:1-2

Ons sien hierdie profesie vervul word met die koms van sosiale netwerke. Hoewel dit voorgee dat dit ’n platform is waar mense met mekaar kan skakel, is dit in werklikheid ’n platform vir die bevordering van die self. Hierdie beheptheid met die self is “gevaarlik” omdat dit intimiteit in verhoudings teenwerk en in ’n huwelik noodlottig kan wees. Intimiteit in die huwelik hang daarvan af dat twee mense bereid is om hul persoonlike identiteit prys te gee en ’n nuwe gesamentlike identiteit aan te neem.

II. Christus het met ’n “getroue liefde” liefgehad

En voor die fees van die pasga het Jesus, omdat Hy geweet het dat sy uur gekom het dat Hy uit hierdie wêreld sou oorgaan na die Vader, en omdat Hy sy eie mense in die wêreld liefgehad het, hulle tot die einde toe liefgehad. –Joh 13:1. Christus het getroue liefde getoon, selfs toe Hy verwerp is. Johannes het geskryf: Hy het na sy eiendom gekom, en sy eie mense het Hom nie aangeneem nie. –Joh 1:11

Matteus het geskryf: Maar dit het alles gebeur, sodat die Skrifte van die profete vervul sou word. Toe het al die dissipels Hom verlaat en gevlug. –Matt 26:56. Dit is een ding om dié lief te hê wat ons terug liefhet. Jesus het gesê dat selfs die tollenaars dit doen. Jesus het liefde betoon aan dié wat Hom gehaat en verraai het, aan dié wat Hom verloën het, en Hy het selfs gebid vir dié wat Hom gekruisig het. Sy liefde is deur ’n verbondsverbintenis volgehou. Hy was …die Lam wat geslag is van die grondlegging van die wêreld af. –Op 13:8. Niks kon Hom van sy ewige doel af laat wyk nie.

Ons samelewing het die begrip van verbond verloor; daarom het ons soveel gebroke huwelike. Selfs baie kerke wat “verbondsteologie” met betrekking tot verlossing aanhang, pas nie dieselfde verbondsbeginsels op die huwelik toe nie. Maleagi stel dit duidelik dat die huwelik ’n verbond is—…tog is sy jou metgesel en die vrou met wie jy ’n verbond gesluit het. –Mal 2:14. Bybelse verbondsliefde is liefde wat blywend is, of dit nou beantwoord word of nie.

Die mees dramatiese openbaring van verbondsliefde vind ons in die Profete. Die boodskap van die profete is hoofsaaklik dié van ’n vurige minnaar, “God”, wat sy ontroue vrou, “Israel”, oproep om na Hom terug te keer—…bekeer julle, bekeer julle van julle verkeerde weë; waarom wil julle sterwe, o huis van Israel? –Eseg 33:11. Jesaja het geskryf: Soek die HERE terwyl Hy nog te vinde is; roep Hom aan terwyl Hy naby is. Laat die goddelose sy weg verlaat en die onregverdige man sy gedagtes; en laat hom terugkeer na die HERE, dan sal Hy hom barmhartig wees; en na onse God, want Hy vergewe menigvuldiglik. –Jes 55:6-7

Hoewel Israel telkens weer teen die Here in opstand gekom het, sien ons tog dat God se liefde vir haar bestendig en onveranderd gebly het. God was getrou aan sy verbondsbelofte, selfs toe sy bruid voor heidense altare neergekniel het. Dit is hierdie kenmerk van getroue verbondsliefde wat die koms van ’n Verlosser teweeggebring het. God het ’n belofte in die tuin van Eden gemaak—En Ek sal vyandskap stel tussen jou en die vrou, en tussen jou saad en haar saad. Hy sal jou die kop vermorsel, en jy sal Hom in die hakskeen byt. –Gen 3:15. Hierdie belofte is sowat vierduisend jaar later in Christus vervul.

Op ons troudag belowe ons om mekaar lief te hê “tot die dood ons skei”. Dit is ’n belofte wat in geloof gemaak word. Niemand kan op hul troudag weet wat daardie belofte oor ’n leeftyd heen kan kos nie. Die koste is onbelangrik vir die verbintenis as daar ’n standhoudende, blywende liefde is, gegrond op God se ewige getrouheid, met Hom as ons getuie.

III. Christus se liefde het lyding omhels

Een kenmerk van ons selfgerigte geslag is die idee dat ek nie in ’n verhouding behoort te hoef ly nie. Dit is ’n produk van ons hedonistiese, plesiersoekende samelewing. Dit vind ook sy weg na ons Anabaptistiese kultuur namate ons al hoe welvarender word en die skeidslyne tussen ons en die wêreld al hoe meer vervaag. Die gevolg van hierdie denkwyse is dat jongmense die huwelik betree met die gedagte: “my maat sal my dien, en ek sal soos ’n prins of prinses kan lewe.”

Ons Anabaptistiese geloof en erfenis is tot in ons tyd bewaar deur mans en vroue wat verstaan het dat ’n verhouding met Christus kruisopname behels. Daar is volop verhale van gesinne wat hul vaderland en alles wat hulle besit het ter wille van die Evangelie agtergelaat het.

Die begrip om lyding in ’n verhouding te omhels, word duidelik in Petrus se brief geleer. Petrus het aan ’n kerk geskryf wat die woedende vuur van vervolging verduur het. Hy het hulle aangemoedig om Christus se voorbeeld te oorweeg: Hy het gely vir ’n saak buite Homself. Omdat Christus dan vir ons na die vlees gely het, moet julle jul ook met dieselfde gesindheid wapen… –1 Pet 4:1. In hoofstuk twee skryf Petrus: Want dit is genade as iemand, omdat hy aan God dink, verdriet verdra deur onregverdig te ly. –1 Pet 2:19. ’n Paar verse later sê hy: Want hiertoe is julle geroep, omdat Christus ook vir julle gely het en julle ’n voorbeeld nagelaat het, sodat julle sy voetstappe kan navolg; –1 Pet 2:21.

Nadat Petrus ons in hoofstuk twee opgeroep het om bereid te wees om Christus se voorbeeld van lyding na te volg, begin hy hoofstuk drie met die woorde: Net so moet julle, vroue, aan julle eie mans onderdanig wees, sodat, as sommige aan die woord ongehoorsaam is, hulle sonder ’n woord deur die wandel van die vroue gewen kan word, wanneer hulle julle rein lewenswandel in die vrees aanskou. –1 Pet 3:1-2. Christene van alle tye het dit as ’n groot eer beskou om ter wille van die goeie te ly. Eers in die afgelope jare is lyding ter wille van die goeie as “mishandeling” beskou. Daar is minstens drie kragte wat ons begrip van lyding op ’n negatiewe manier vorm.

1. ’n Selfsugtige, plesiersoekende samelewing

Een hiervan is reeds hierbo beskryf: die hedonistiese samelewing waarin ons leef, dit wil sê ’n samelewing wat plesier as lewenswyse nastreef.

2. Die gesondheids-, welvaarts- en voorspoedsevangelie

’n Tweede krag is die gesondheids-, welvaarts- en voorspoedsevangelie van baie evangeliese kerke. Die implikasie is dat ons lewens sal oorloop van fisieke welstand en materiële oorvloed as ons kies om Christus te volg. Hierdie begrip berus op die beloftes aan eertydse Israel in die Ou Testament van ’n land wat oorloop van melk en heuning. Ons glo dat hierdie belofte in die kerklike tydperk vervul word deur ’n lewe wat oorloop van die vrug van die Gees: liefde, blydskap, vrede, ensovoorts. Hierdie vrugte kan selfs te midde van lyding oorvloedig wees. Trouens, wanneer ander die vrugte sien te midde van ’n ander persoon se lyding, is dit juis dan die opvallendste en word dit die meeste waardeer.

3. Die feministiese beweging

Die derde invloed wat vandag ons perspektief op lyding vorm, kom van die feministiese beweging, wat met vrymoedigheid verklaar dat geen vrou in ’n huweliksverhouding behoort te ly of enige ontbering behoort te ervaar nie. Daarom het ons ’n samelewing van vroue met hul eie loopbane, wat hul eie salarisse verdien en hul eie bankrekeninge onderhou. Hoe anders is dit tog as die getuienis van gelowige vroue soos Sara, wat …aan Abraham gehoorsaam was en hom heer genoem het. Julle het haar dogters geword as julle goed doen en geen verskrikking vrees nie. –1 Pet 3:6

Lyding ter wille van die verhouding is deur Christus begin en deur duisende getroue Christene dwarsdeur die kerklike tydperk nagevolg. Die woorde van die apostel Petrus en die getuienis van getroue Christene daag ons uit om lyding te omhels as ’n kenteken van die egtheid van ons geloof.

IV. Christus het met ’n heiligende liefde liefgehad

God se plan met ons skepping was dat ons heilig sou wees soos Hy heilig is, sodat ons innige gemeenskap met Hom kon ervaar. Maar die mensdom het teen God in opstand gekom, en daarom het Hy ’n verlosser belowe. Intussen het Hy ’n noodplan ingestel wat bedoel was om te keer dat die mensdom homself vernietig, en dit was “die Wet”.

Dit was egter nooit God se bedoeling dat ons verhouding met Hom deur die wet beheer sou word nie. Hy verlang ’n liefdesverhouding met ons; daarom het Hy sy Seun na ons gestuur en ons met sy liefde oorweldig. Ons beantwoord nou sy liefde, nie uit vrees vir die oordeel nie, maar as ’n liefdesreaksie op sy onweerstaanbare liefde. Hierdie begrip word die duidelikste in Romeine gestel: Want wat vir die wet onmoontlik was, omdat dit kragteloos was deur die vlees [beperk tot wat in die vlees bereik kon word], dit het God gedoen deur sy eie Seun in die gelykheid van die sondige vlees te stuur, en dit ter wille van die sonde, en die sonde in die vlees te veroordeel [die regverdige eise van die wet te bevredig], sodat die reg van die wet vervul kon word in ons wat nie na die vlees wandel nie, maar na die Gees. –Rom 8:3-4

Jesus het deur liefde bereik wat nooit deur die streng vereistes van ’n strafregstelsel bereik kon word nie. Hy het die standaard van geregtigheid hoër gestel. Want Ek sê vir julle: As julle geregtigheid nie oorvloediger is as dié van die skrifgeleerdes en Fariseërs nie, sal julle nooit in die koninkryk van die hemele ingaan nie. –Matt 5:20. Hy het ons gewys hoe om te lewe en lief te hê. Sy selfopofferende dood het aan die strafregtelike eise van die wet voldoen. Deur sy opstanding, hemelvaart en die uitstorting van die Heilige Gees het Hy gelowiges in staat gestel om te lewe en lief te hê soos Hy gedoen het.

Paulus vermaan ons om op dieselfde manier in die huwelik met mekaar om te gaan: Manne, julle moet jul eie vroue liefhê, soos Christus ook die gemeente liefgehad en Homself daarvoor oorgegee het, om dit te heilig, nadat Hy dit gereinig het met die waterbad deur die woord, sodat Hy dit vir Homself kon stel as ’n heerlike gemeente sonder vlek of rimpel of iets dergeliks; maar dat dit heilig en sonder gebrek sou wees. –Ef 5:27. Jesus het aarde toe gekom om vir Homself ’n bruid te verwerf. Sy was nie ’n pragtige, stralende bruid wat gretig op sy koms gewag het nie. Sy was deur sonde ontsier en het in opstand teen Hom geleef—Hy het na sy eiendom gekom, en sy eie mense het Hom nie aangeneem nie. –Joh 1:11. Deur sy geduldige, volhardende liefde het Hy sy bruid verander in ’n heerlike, stralende bruid wat met ontsag voor Hom staan en Hom met vreugde aanbid en verheerlik.

Het jou vrou vlekke en rimpels? Is daar gesindhede wat jy wens anders was? Of is daar vrese en onsekerhede wat haar vryheid en vreugde belemmer? Jy kan eis dat sy verander en haar uitskel omdat sy nie aan jou verwagtinge voldoen nie. Hierdie benadering sou met dié van die wet ooreenstem. Dit sou haar beperkings beklemtoon en haar angs laat toeneem. Of jy kan haar liefhê ondanks haar vlekke en rimpels. Met woorde van medelye en bemoediging kan jy haar aanspoor om haar vrese te bowe te kom, net soos Christus sy bruid deur sy woord heilig. Jesus het getoon dat liefde kan bereik wat harde eise nooit kan nie. Paulus het geleer dat dit ’n grondbeginsel van die huwelik is. Dit is bedoel as ’n verhouding waarin liefde die dryfkrag is.

V. Die groot verborgenheid

Paulus het sy uiteensetting oor die huwelik afgesluit deur te sê: Hierdie verborgenheid is groot; maar ek sê dit met die oog op Christus en die gemeente. –Ef 5:32. ’n Verborgenheid in Bybelse taal is nie iets wat nie begryp kan word nie, maar eerder iets wat slegs verstaan kan word deur dié wat die Waarheid deur geloof ontvang en omhels. Dit word aan opregte Christene geopenbaar; vir ander bly dit verborge.

As gelowiges in Jesus is ons bevoorreg om ’n perspektief op die huwelik te verstaan wat baie mense nie eens kan begin begryp nie: dat selfopofferende liefde die deur na intimiteit oopmaak, dat verbondsliefde die sleutel tot lewenslange vervulling is, dat ons bereidwilligheid om ter wille van die verhouding te ly die egtheid van ons liefde bewys, en laastens, dat onvoorwaardelike liefde die doeltreffendste manier is om verandering in ons huweliksmaat te bevorder.

Hierdie beginsels is deur die tyd beproef en Bybels gegrond. Hulle lê aan die grondslag van die Evangelie en is ’n fundamentele deel van ons Anabaptistiese koninkryksgebaseerde teologie. Wanneer hulle getrou toegepas word, sal hulle enige huwelik verander.

It was 2:30 p.m., Tuesday afternoon.

“Señora!” a chorus of voices hollered from outside our property hedge. “Open the gate!”

“Just wait,” I called back. “It’s not three o’clock yet.”

Disgruntled murmurings sounded from the other side of the hedge. I turned to my wailing baby. Sinking into the rocker to feed her, I closed my eyes to relish each quiet moment before the coming tumult.

**************

We had scarcely settled onto the farm when the neighbor children found us. They appeared—uninvited and unannounced, any time of day—to stay as long as they wished. The first ones soon brought more friends along to join in their play with the foreigner’s children and toys. Play-Doh and table games entertained them but oh, what a commotion ten children could make in a concrete house.

After much exasperation, Ernest (my husband) and I finally came up with a plan…. They could come two afternoons a week, arriving no earlier than three o’clock in the afternoon. On Tuesdays they could stay for supper, but on Thursdays they must leave by 6 p.m.

We also had other rules…. Our children needed to stay within my eyesight and earshot when playing with neighbor children. And NO closed doors. Still, questions niggled my brain. Is this a good thing or a bad one? Will we live to regret it? What if they are a bad influence on our children? My questions formed a prayer, one which God had been hearing from me quite a bit these past months. Lord, give me wisdom and patience with these children today. And if they are a bad influence on our children, Lord, please reveal that to us before our children are harmed.

But what an opportunity! This was one way I could reach the world while being a stay-at-home mom… I read them Bible stories. I taught them the need to respect and obey grownups. I told them they needed to obey me, just as my children were expected to. Transgressors, I warned, would be sent home.

Zinnia did not believe me, until the day she disobeyed and was expelled. I grin now, remembering the little troublemaker perching on the neighbor’s wall, peering over into our farm where her cousins were happily playing. Once had taught her; after that Zinnia obeyed.

**************

“Señora!” Zinnia’s voice interrupted my reverie. “Is it three o’clock yet?”

I opened one eye to peek at the clock—2:47.

“Not quite!” I hollered out the window. Placing baby into the walker, I headed to the kitchen. What would I feed them tonight?

**************

“Zinnia, I need to look in your purse before you go home.”

It was Tuesday evening again, several months later. We had been missing various small things after Zinnia started bringing a purse along on her visits to our house. Tonight, we would see if our suspicions were correct.

Zinnia’s terror-filled eyes met mine. “Just a minute, Señora. I need to use the bathroom.”

“You can use the bathroom after we look in your purse.”

“No, Señora, I can’t wait…”, her voice trailed off as she rushed to the bathroom.

I sighed. Of course, her purse would be empty when she came back out. Searching the bathroom later that night revealed treasures hidden here and there.

“Let’s chat a little, Zinnia,” I invited the following week. Zinnia sat on the bed, twisting yarn knots on the comforter, her eyes defensive, fearful. My heart yearned for the dear girl. Her mom had left years ago to work in another country, leaving the girls with their Grandma.

“I don’t care about those things you stole, Zinnia,” I began. “But it’s a habit you don’t want to start. God cares about you….”

That was the last time Zinnia, her sister, and their cousins showed up at our place. “Our Grandma doesn’t let us come anymore,” they explained.

Maybe it was Grandma; I think it was God. We had prayed much that He would make it clear if their visits were harmful to our children and if they should stop coming. My heart was torn between love for the neighbor children and protection for our own. This was the way God chose to answer.

“Thank you, God,” I prayed. “We’ll take this as your answer, and not invite them back. Send them over if you want them to come again.”

**************

Several years passed. Now it was Jon, a neighbor boy, frequenting our home.

“Could he come to your house every day after school?” his parents had wondered. “We want him to learn good things, instead of playing with boys in our neighborhood.”

Hmm. So, we’re to raise the boy while both parents work?

“He can come Tuesday and Thursday afternoons,” Ernest decided. “Those are the days I’m more often at home.”

Jon showed up faithfully on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons. Problem was, Ernest couldn’t. Other responsibilities and obligations kept coming up, hindering him from being there like he wanted to.

I did not want to nag my husband… He really wished he could be at home, working with the boys. Should I say something, or not? It didn’t seem ideal to have an unconverted boy working for hours with our son, a new Christian.

I did mention my questions to Ernest, but mostly I made it a matter of prayer.

Jon stopped coming. I was amazed. I felt for Jon, yet once again I thanked God for His answer.

**************

“How can I reach out to my neighbor children without compromising my own?” a friend asked recently. Moving to a new area, she faces the challenge of neighbor children coming over.

There are no simple answers. I have discovered the urgency of prayer, and God’s faithfulness in answering when we cry out to Him for wisdom. His answer to others may well be different from what He worked out for us.

**************

Another sister granted me permission to share their experience in relating with neighbor children:

Alex and his mother live across the road from us and began attending church soon after we moved here. Alex came over almost every day and taught our boys Spanish in short order. The boys dreaded his visits at first, but they soon became great friends. After a while another neighbor boy, Nilton, started coming at times and we thought he seemed decent enough. Then one day a third boy, José, came along. I got a distinctly uncomfortable feeling. I gave them a time limit, but just couldn’t shake the uneasy feeling. So, though I thought I didn’t have time, I decided I would work outside the whole time while they were here. I worked close to them and kept an eye on things and thought everything was fine. They seemed to just be playing together nicely, so I was surprised when they went home before the time was up.

It wasn’t long before my boys came in crying; they felt so bad about what had happened. Alex had asked them to deliver a note to his girlfriend because his mom wouldn’t like it if he did. One of the other boys told them what he does out behind bushes at public school, so he doesn’t get caught. They tried to get my boys to promise not to tell me. They didn’t promise, and I was so thankful! But they were very torn up because they thought Alex would not be their friend anymore.

My husband and I talked with the boys and assured them that they had handled the situation correctly by not promising to keep secrets. Within the hour, Alex’s mom came over to visit and we told her about it. She was very alarmed that her son had tried to pass a note and later took care of the situation with her son. I was glad that the budding relationship he had with the neighbor girl was stopped before it went any farther. Alex’s friendship with our boys has continued but the other two boys discovered that our boys had told us about them and didn’t come over for years after that.

José recently asked our eight-year-old son if he could come over to his house and play. I said no. His grandma came over several days later, offended, and said that José was very sad about it. I explained that I feel I must always be with my boys if he would come over because one time, he had tried to get our son to play an electronic war game with him. The grandma understood and was sad that her grandson was a bad influence. She wanted the best for him. We have invited him to Sunday School, but he doesn’t want that. I just hope that we can always have the type of relationship with our children that they will feel free to come to us and not keep these situations to themselves and feel guilty.

**************

Wise parents seek to remove danger, but not difficulty, from their children’s path. I was recently amazed while reading Judges 3, to discover that God wanted some enemy nations to remain in the land of Canaan. Why? He wanted parents to teach their children war (v. 2). Instead, the children of Israel made friends with the enemy nations and began to intermarry. “It seems we live closer to the world here on the mission field,” one sister shared. Our children are growing up on the front lines, as it were. This can be positive. They have frequent opportunities to “speak with the enemy in the gates,” where they are asked what we believe, and why. But when parents are lax, or their children are rebellious, this closer association with the world can prove tragic.

As we connect with God in prayer for our children, we must also connect with them. No strict safety guidelines will substitute a close relationship with your child. The mother of a child who was abused shared, “The only way your child will tell you what is going on is if you have a close relationship.”

I stagger as I consider our enemy and my own inadequacy as a mother. Suddenly I am seized with urgency to pray for things which never entered my head when our children were still young. Abuse cases exist around us; at times in our very midst. I pray for our children’s protection from the evil which surrounds them and that which rises in their hearts. I pray they will never mar another’s purity. I pray for purity at the marriage altar, both for them and their future spouses.

I pray with urgency, yet with confidence. Because this I know: God loves our children—He cares about their purity and protection even more than we as parents do—He longs for us to partner with Him in raising them to be faithful servants of His—And He wants to show Himself strong on behalf of humble parents who cry out to Him as they train soldiers in enemy territory. For the eyes of the LORD run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to shew himself strong in the behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him… –2 Chronicles 16:9.

Erano le 14:30 di martedì pomeriggio.

«Señora!» gridò in coro un gruppo di voci da fuori la siepe che delimitava la nostra proprietà. «Apri il cancello!»

«Aspettate un attimo», risposi. «Non sono ancora le tre.»

Dall’altro lato della siepe si levarono mormorii scontenti. Mi voltai verso la mia bambina che piangeva. Sprofondai nella sedia a dondolo per darle da mangiare e chiusi gli occhi, assaporando ogni momento di quiete prima del tumulto imminente.

**************

Ci eravamo appena sistemati nella fattoria quando i bambini dei vicini ci trovarono. Comparivano, senza invito né preavviso e a qualsiasi ora del giorno, e restavano quanto volevano. Ben presto i primi portarono altri amici, che si unirono ai loro giochi con i figli e i giocattoli della straniera. Il Play-Doh e i giochi da tavolo li intrattenevano, ma, oh, che baccano potevano fare dieci bambini in una casa di cemento!

Dopo molte esasperazioni, Ernest (mio marito) e io escogitammo finalmente un piano…. Potevano venire due pomeriggi alla settimana, non prima delle tre. Il martedì potevano fermarsi a cena, ma il giovedì dovevano andarsene entro le 18.

Stabilimmo anche altre regole…. I nostri figli dovevano restare a portata di vista e di orecchio mentre giocavano con i bambini dei vicini. E niente porte chiuse. Eppure, alcune domande continuavano a tormentarmi. È una cosa buona o cattiva? Finiremo per pentircene? E se fossero una cattiva influenza per i nostri figli? Le mie domande si trasformarono in una preghiera, una che Dio mi aveva sentito rivolgergli spesso negli ultimi mesi. Signore, dammi saggezza e pazienza con questi bambini oggi. E se sono una cattiva influenza per i nostri figli, Signore, ti prego, rivelacelo prima che i nostri figli ne subiscano il danno.

Ma che opportunità! Era un modo per raggiungere il mondo pur restando una mamma a casa… Leggevo loro storie della Bibbia. Insegnavo loro che dovevano rispettare e ubbidire agli adulti. Dicevo loro che dovevano ubbidire a me, proprio come ci si aspettava che facessero i miei figli. Avvertivo che i trasgressori sarebbero stati rimandati a casa.

Zinnia non mi credette, finché un giorno disubbidì e fu mandata via. Ora sorrido, ricordando quella piccola peste appollaiata sul muro del vicino, che sbirciava nella nostra fattoria, dove i suoi cugini giocavano felici. Una volta le avevo insegnato la lezione; da allora Zinnia ubbidì.

**************

«Señora!» La voce di Zinnia interruppe i miei pensieri. «Sono già le tre?»

Aprii un occhio per sbirciare l’orologio: le 2:47.

«Non ancora!» gridai dalla finestra. Misi la bambina nel girello e mi diressi in cucina. Che cosa avrei dato loro da mangiare quella sera?

**************

«Zinnia, prima che tu vada a casa devo guardare nella tua borsa.»

Era di nuovo martedì sera, diversi mesi dopo. Da quando Zinnia aveva cominciato a portare una borsa con sé quando veniva a casa nostra, ci mancavano vari piccoli oggetti. Quella sera avremmo scoperto se i nostri sospetti erano fondati.

Gli occhi di Zinnia, pieni di terrore, incontrarono i miei. «Solo un minuto, Señora. Devo andare in bagno.»

«Puoi andare in bagno dopo che avremo guardato nella tua borsa.»

«No, Señora, non posso aspettare…», la sua voce si spense mentre correva in bagno.

Sospirai. Naturalmente, quando sarebbe uscita, la sua borsa sarebbe stata vuota. Quella notte, più tardi, cercando in bagno, trovai tesori nascosti qua e là.

«Facciamo due chiacchiere, Zinnia», le proposi la settimana seguente. Zinnia era seduta sul letto e attorcigliava i nodi di filato sulla trapunta; i suoi occhi erano sulla difensiva, impauriti. Il mio cuore desiderava tanto aiutare quella cara ragazza. Sua madre era partita anni prima per lavorare in un altro paese, lasciando le bambine con la nonna.

«Non mi importa di quelle cose che hai rubato, Zinnia», cominciai. «Ma è un’abitudine che non vuoi prendere. Dio si prende cura di te…».

Quella fu l’ultima volta che Zinnia, sua sorella e i loro cugini vennero a casa nostra. «La nonna non ci lascia più venire», spiegarono.

Forse era stata la nonna; io penso che fosse stato Dio. Avevamo pregato molto perché ci facesse capire chiaramente se le loro visite fossero dannose per i nostri figli e se dovessero smettere di venire. Il mio cuore era diviso tra l’amore per i bambini dei vicini e il desiderio di proteggere i nostri. Questo fu il modo in cui Dio scelse di rispondere.

«Grazie, Dio», pregai. «Prenderemo questo come la tua risposta e non li inviteremo di nuovo. Se vuoi che tornino, mandali tu.»

**************

Passarono diversi anni. Ora era Jon, un bambino del vicinato, a venire spesso a casa nostra.

«Potrebbe venire a casa vostra ogni giorno dopo la scuola?» ci avevano chiesto i suoi genitori. «Vogliamo che impari cose buone, invece di giocare con i ragazzi del nostro quartiere.»

Hmm. Quindi dovremmo crescere noi il bambino mentre entrambi i genitori lavorano?

«Può venire il martedì e il giovedì pomeriggio», decise Ernest. «Sono i giorni in cui sono più spesso a casa.»

Jon si presentava fedelmente il martedì e il giovedì pomeriggio. Il problema era che Ernest non riusciva a esserci. Altri impegni e responsabilità continuavano a presentarsi, impedendogli di essere lì come avrebbe voluto.

Non volevo assillare mio marito… Desiderava davvero essere a casa e lavorare con i ragazzi. Dovevo dirgli qualcosa oppure no? Non sembrava l’ideale che un ragazzo non convertito passasse ore a lavorare con nostro figlio, che era un nuovo cristiano.

Espressi a Ernest i miei dubbi, ma soprattutto ne feci una questione di preghiera.

Jon smise di venire. Ne fui stupita. Mi dispiaceva per Jon, eppure ancora una volta ringraziai Dio per la sua risposta.

**************

«Come posso avvicinarmi ai bambini dei vicini senza compromettere i miei?» mi ha chiesto di recente un’amica. Trasferitasi in una nuova zona, si trova ad affrontare la sfida dei bambini del vicinato che vengono a casa sua.

Non ci sono risposte semplici. Ho scoperto quanto sia urgente pregare e quanto Dio sia fedele nel rispondere quando gridiamo a lui chiedendo saggezza. La sua risposta ad altri potrebbe benissimo essere diversa da quella che ha dato a noi.

**************

Un’altra sorella mi ha dato il permesso di condividere la loro esperienza nel rapporto con i bambini dei vicini:

Alex e sua madre abitano dall’altra parte della strada rispetto a noi e hanno cominciato a frequentare la chiesa poco dopo il nostro trasferimento qui. Alex veniva quasi ogni giorno e in breve tempo insegnò lo spagnolo ai nostri ragazzi. All’inizio i ragazzi temevano le sue visite, ma presto diventarono grandi amici. Dopo un po’, un altro ragazzo del vicinato, Nilton, cominciò a venire ogni tanto e ci sembrò abbastanza a posto. Poi, un giorno, arrivò un terzo ragazzo, José. Provai un netto senso di disagio. Stabilii un limite di tempo, ma non riuscivo a scrollarmi di dosso quella sensazione inquietante. Così, anche se pensavo di non avere tempo, decisi di lavorare all’aperto per tutto il tempo in cui sarebbero rimasti. Lavorai vicino a loro e tenni d’occhio la situazione, pensando che andasse tutto bene. Sembrava che stessero semplicemente giocando insieme tranquillamente, perciò fui sorpresa quando se ne andarono prima dello scadere del tempo.

Non passò molto che i miei ragazzi entrarono piangendo; si sentivano davvero molto male per ciò che era successo. Alex aveva chiesto loro di consegnare un biglietto alla sua ragazza, perché sua madre non avrebbe approvato se l’avesse fatto lui. Uno degli altri ragazzi raccontò loro che cosa fa dietro i cespugli della scuola pubblica per non farsi scoprire. Cercarono di convincere i miei ragazzi a promettere che non me l’avrebbero detto. Non lo promisero, e ne fui così grata! Ma erano molto turbati, perché pensavano che Alex non sarebbe più stato loro amico.

Mio marito e io parlammo con i ragazzi e li rassicurammo che avevano gestito correttamente la situazione non promettendo di mantenere segreti. Entro un’ora la madre di Alex venne a trovarci e le raccontammo l’accaduto. Era molto allarmata dal fatto che suo figlio avesse cercato di far recapitare un biglietto e poi affrontò la situazione con lui. Fui contenta che la relazione nascente con la ragazza del vicinato si fosse interrotta prima di andare oltre. L’amicizia di Alex con i nostri ragazzi è continuata, ma gli altri due ragazzi scoprirono che i nostri avevano raccontato tutto e per anni non vennero più da noi.

Di recente José ha chiesto a nostro figlio di otto anni se poteva andare a casa sua a giocare. Gli ho detto di no. Alcuni giorni dopo sua nonna venne da noi, offesa, e disse che José era molto triste per questo. Le spiegai che ritenevo di dover essere sempre presente con i miei ragazzi se lui fosse venuto a casa nostra, perché una volta aveva cercato di convincere nostro figlio a giocare con lui a un videogioco di guerra. La nonna capì e si rattristò sapendo che suo nipote era una cattiva influenza. Voleva il meglio per lui. Lo abbiamo invitato alla scuola domenicale, ma lui non vuole venire. Spero soltanto che possiamo sempre avere con i nostri figli un rapporto tale che si sentano liberi di rivolgersi a noi, senza tenersi per sé queste situazioni e sentirsi in colpa.

**************

I genitori saggi cercano di rimuovere il pericolo, ma non le difficoltà, dal cammino dei propri figli. Di recente mi sono stupita, leggendo Giudici 3, nello scoprire che Dio voleva che alcune nazioni nemiche rimanessero nel paese di Canaan. Perché? Voleva che i genitori insegnassero ai loro figli la guerra (v. 2). Invece, i figli d’Israele fecero amicizia con le nazioni nemiche e cominciarono a sposarsi con loro. «Sembra che qui, nel campo missionario, viviamo più vicini al mondo», ha raccontato una sorella. I nostri figli stanno crescendo, per così dire, in prima linea. Questo può essere positivo. Hanno frequenti occasioni di «parlare con il nemico alle porte», quando viene chiesto loro che cosa crediamo e perché. Ma quando i genitori sono negligenti, o i loro figli sono ribelli, questa maggiore vicinanza al mondo può rivelarsi tragica.

Quando ci rivolgiamo a Dio in preghiera per i nostri figli, dobbiamo anche entrare in contatto con loro. Nessuna rigida regola di sicurezza può sostituire un rapporto stretto con tuo figlio. La madre di un bambino che aveva subito abusi ha raccontato: «L’unico modo in cui tuo figlio ti dirà che cosa sta succedendo è se hai un rapporto stretto con lui».

Mi sento sopraffatta quando penso al nostro nemico e alla mia inadeguatezza come madre. All’improvviso mi prende l’urgenza di pregare per cose che non mi erano mai passate per la testa quando i nostri figli erano ancora piccoli. Intorno a noi si verificano casi di abuso; a volte proprio in mezzo a noi. Prego che i nostri figli siano protetti dal male che li circonda e da quello che sorge nei loro cuori. Prego che non intacchino mai la purezza di un’altra persona. Prego per la purezza all’altare del matrimonio, sia per loro sia per i loro futuri coniugi.

Prego con urgenza, ma con fiducia. Perché questo lo so: Dio ama i nostri figli: ha a cuore la loro purezza e protezione ancor più di noi genitori; desidera che collaboriamo con lui per crescerli affinché siano suoi servitori fedeli; e vuole mostrarsi forte a favore dei genitori umili che gridano a lui mentre addestrano soldati in territorio nemico. Poiché gli occhi del SIGNORE percorrono tutta la terra, per mostrare la sua forza a favore di coloro il cui cuore è integro verso di lui… –2 Cronache 16:9.

And I sought for a man among them, that should make up the hedge, and stand in the gap before me for the land, that I should not destroy it: but I found none. –Ezekiel 22:30

The account of the little Dutch boy who heroically stuck his finger in the hole in the dike comes to mind as we consider such a verse. He couldn’t leave the spot for fear of erosion, so he waited the long night through until someone came along in the morning to rescue him from his plight. Many men have performed astounding feats on impulse when the moment so required. Lives were rescued, towns were saved, and enemies defeated because someone filled a role that was needed. Books are written, and monuments erected in honor of those whose benefaction has touched us. These are considered the heroes of history and they are remembered for their staunch bravery and steadfast faithfulness.

But the gaps in life are not always so obvious and the results not always measurable. Solomon informs us of the account of …a little city, and few men within it; and there came a great king against it, and besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it: Now there was found in it a poor wise man, and he by his wisdom delivered the city; yet no man remembered that same poor man. –Ecc 9:14-15. Though we have many thorough descriptions in the Bible of pious men who stood in the gap for God, there are, no doubt, hordes of others who overcame tremendous odds on a spiritual level yet received no recognition in this life.

The problem lies not so much in that, standing in the gap is beyond our capabilities or finances, but in the reality that often the job bears no title, ordination, or recognition. It is to be filled by volunteers with enough vision and care to sacrifice their own agenda for the sole cause of filling the hole in the hedge. It often does not lie within the realm of the physical, but within the borders of the spiritual. While the poor we have with us always and spiritual nobility will stoop to help them, we must consider that God probably has more in mind here than needing someone to organize bread lines and soup kitchens. He is looking for a man clad in a robe of “purple principles” that won’t be shed when the temperatures get hot.

King Darius signed the fateful degree that was designed to escort Daniel to a luncheon with the lions. Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime. –Dan 6:10. What a slight thing it would have been for Daniel to close the shutters before he prayed. But Daniel was not filling the gap by his presence in the high governmental position that he held. The gap lay in the dearth of godly witnesses in Babylon. Thus, the hole between heaven and earth was to be fulfilled by prayer at the open window while sacrificing his “seat in the senate.”

The underlying reason that so many gaps exist and there are so few men to fill them is because we often get our personal, earthly vision of circumstances confused with the eternal purposes of God. We are busily occupied with good things and feeling quite useful. Martha was zealously active in filling what she perceived as the imminent gap in the household, while Mary was sitting in the eternal one. It is incredibly easy to get caught up in the activity trap of a busy life. We may give intensive care to efficiently climb to the top of the ladder, only to discover that it is leaning against the wrong wall. Many people are very busy, but not very effective. Many have labored industriously for years in the Lord’s work, only to arrive at the finish line and realize that the things, which mattered most, had eluded them. Some, while giving their lives to serve others, allowed their marriage to suffer, or their children to disrespect them. Others have given “Corban” to their church while neglecting their relationship with their own parents.

The man in the gap must be wise, and wisdom must understand wherein the true gap lies. In this we must be driven by a purposed, biblical vision. Life will afford many opportunities to abandon our course. If we actively seek to live the expectations handed to us by our family, friends, associates, church agendas, and life’s circumstances, we will be driven by people rather than biblical principles. While this may seem legitimate on the surface, we may reap the bitter disappointment of finding ourselves dangling at the end of the wrong rope.

So, what does the gap of God’s concern look like? Some would say that this gap consists where any need arises. The poor we have with us always and certainly herein is an opportunity to do good. But the better part chosen by Mary had nothing to do with helping the poor or feeding the hungry. Likewise, the woman with the precious alabaster box of ointment of spikenard could have sold it and supplied the poor for quite a while with the sum of its value. But the real gap could not be filled by caressing the cripple, but by crowning the Christ. In the Garden of Eden there was no gap, for man walked in perfect harmony with his Creator. It was sin that created the gap and rankled the relationship. Also, there will be no breach at the end of time when the Lamb receives His bride. Until then, we have a large gap that exists because this earth refuses to glorify its Creator. To stand in that gap must be the chief purpose of all who aspire to bear His name.

This calls for a complete transformation in relationship to our God. The atonement of Christ’s blood makes it judicially possible. The comfort of the Holy Spirit makes it emotionally satisfying, but it is in the realm of our surrender and glorification of God that animates the scene. The Prodigal Son is a prime example of a soul who had brought a world of trouble upon himself by forsaking the position that he held as a son of his father. At the bottom of his restoration was nothing more than a re-establishing of the father-son relationship which had existed from his birth.

It appears to me that God is not so much looking for souls with their hands waving in the air shouting, “Here am I send me!” Rather His eyes search for the humble souls who bow their wills before the Almighty and recognize Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created. –Revelation 4:11. There is no lack for Sons of Sceva who imagine they are filling an important role in their willingness to broadcast the “Jesus” that they have heard of. In 1997, some 800,000 men arrived at a Promise Keepers rally in Washington D.C in response to the theme of “Standing in the Gap.” These men may have had good intentions of representing God to a nation in swift departure from spiritual underpinnings, but it takes more than just a willing heart. God doesn’t need of a large mass of bodies to stuff into a hole. He is looking for qualified men, and few have been promoted to such a position.

If all God wanted was men to show up at a rally or publicly proclaim their faith on the streets, He, no doubt, could have found many desiring such a good work. But to stand in the gap between God and the world will only be sanctioned by God for those who deserve to be there. It is the universal pride of man that drives man to believe that he must only desire to be useful and then he will be used. In God’s house there are some vessels to honor and some to dishonor, yet to deserve an honorable place is much more difficult than to desire one.

It is very common in our day to receive mail bearing the message, “Get the credit you deserve.” It is no secret that the credit that many deserve is zero credit. But we have all been impacted by the subliminal message that everybody deserves credit. Our society is promoting that all immoral, imprudent, and improvident people deserve the same care as the moral and industrious. If the slothful individual deserves a good wage and the spendthrift deserves financial security, then the Apostle Paul certainly has no right to lay any qualifications upon the widows who should receive support from the church. Neither has he any right to reject any sincere soul who desires the office of a Bishop, just because he does not meet the qualifications. But God noticed a few souls …in Sardis which have not defiled their garments; and they shall walk with me in white: for they are worthy. –Rev 3:4

These are men in the gap. Not because they had energy to burn, but because they had a vision for purity. This was no mere accident, for men who wish to attain to preeminence with God must do it by…

…Purpose

By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter; Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season; Esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt: for he had respect unto the recompence of the reward. By faith he forsook Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king: for he endured, as seeing him who is invisible. –Heb 11:24-27

A true vision for the work of God will come with a price tag. The rich young ruler would have loved to be a ruler in the kingdom of Christ as well as on his estate, but he couldn’t hold both. This principle provided the first hurdle for him and for everyone else who would desire such a noble work. As a young man, Moses made his decision and chose his loyalties. He was prepared to be rejected by Egypt, but he never dreamed he would also be so flippantly discarded by his own people.

It was forty years in the lonely furnace that purged his pride and pruned his prowess. There he graduated from the seminary of silence, equipped and prepared to stand in the gap as the meekest man on the face of the earth. He became an intercessor for men to God. As an advocate of men and of God, he preached and prayed, he walked and wept, he lived and loved his God and his brethren. All this while, he deemed himself inadequate for the position. While the children of Israel were at the very core of his heart, his fear and focus never left his God. When we seek to be respected by men, our purpose is clouded over and our position in the gap forfeited. Many good pastors, parents, and pilgrims have made this mistake and received their script from their wife, their children, their friends, or their church. Perhaps it seems like the loving, caring, and most respectful thing to do. But God requires absolute fidelity and there can be no compromise. What a man “wants to be” is driven by his visionary purpose, but what he “turns out to be” rests upon his…

…Priorities

This is a true saying, If a man desire the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work. A bishop then must be blameless, the husband of one wife, vigilant, sober, of good behaviour, given to hospitality, apt to teach; Not given to wine, no striker, not greedy of filthy lucre; but patient, not a brawler, not covetous; One that ruleth well his own house, having his children in subjection with all gravity; –1Ti 3:1-4. Our purpose forms our destination, but our priorities pave the road to get us there.

Unfortunately, some men are promoted to the ministry by popular opinion, but God chooses his men based upon their priorities and eternal qualifications. Men who are governed by their possessions, passions, or position will be useless to serve for God’s purpose. They love to be called Pastor, Reverend, or Father. They love to be esteemed as zealous, knowledgeable, steadfast, or compassionate. For am I now seeking the favor of men, or of God? Or am I striving to please men? If I were still pleasing men, I should not be a servant of Christ. –Gal 1:10 ASV

Fortunately, God is not a respecter of persons, and a stone fit for the wall will not be left in the way. The aged, the poor, the maimed, and the halt are all prime candidates for the position of filling the gap. Those with broken dreams, broken bodies, and broken hearts can stand unhindered in the hedge beside Noah, Abraham, Joseph, Moses, Daniel, Esther, Ruth and a countless battalion of others. These are all stellar representatives of God to this world. They all have turned their back on frivolity, fame, familiarity, and fortune and have become the heroes of heaven. They stand shoulder to shoulder in the hedge and form the “Embassy of the Eternal.” They loved, while others hated. They gave all, while others received. They were mocked and misunderstood, reviled and ridiculed, weary and weeping.

For we are unto God a sweet savour of Christ, in them that are saved, and in them that perish: To the one we are the savour of death unto death; and to the other the savour of life unto life. And who is sufficient for these things? –2 Co 2:15-16. Those whose sole purpose and priorities are governed by God.

Dan Aku mencari di antara mereka seorang yang hendak mendirikan tembok dan berdiri di celah di hadapan-Ku demi negeri itu, supaya Aku tidak memusnahkannya; tetapi Aku tidak menemukannya. –Yehezkiel 22:30

Kisah anak laki-laki Belanda kecil yang dengan gagah berani menyumbat lubang pada tanggul dengan jarinya terlintas di benak kita saat mempertimbangkan ayat seperti ini. Ia tidak bisa meninggalkan tempat itu karena takut tanggul akan terkikis, maka ia bertahan sepanjang malam sampai seseorang datang pada pagi hari untuk menyelamatkannya dari kesulitannya. Banyak pria telah melakukan tindakan luar biasa secara spontan ketika keadaan menuntutnya. Nyawa diselamatkan, kota-kota diselamatkan, dan musuh dikalahkan karena seseorang mengisi peran yang dibutuhkan. Buku-buku ditulis dan monumen didirikan untuk menghormati mereka yang jasanya telah menyentuh kita. Mereka dianggap sebagai pahlawan sejarah dan dikenang karena keberanian mereka yang teguh serta kesetiaan mereka yang kokoh.

Namun, celah-celah dalam kehidupan tidak selalu begitu jelas dan hasilnya tidak selalu dapat diukur. Salomo menyampaikan kisah tentang …sebuah kota kecil dengan sedikit penduduk di dalamnya; datanglah seorang raja besar menyerangnya, mengepungnya, dan mendirikan benteng-benteng besar untuk melawannya. Di dalamnya terdapat seorang miskin yang bijaksana, dan dengan kebijaksanaannya ia menyelamatkan kota itu; tetapi tidak seorang pun mengingat orang miskin itu. –Pkh 9:14-15. Meskipun Alkitab memberi kita banyak uraian terperinci tentang orang-orang saleh yang berdiri di celah bagi Allah, tidak diragukan lagi ada banyak sekali orang lain yang mengatasi rintangan besar di tingkat rohani, tetapi tidak menerima pengakuan dalam kehidupan ini.

Masalahnya bukan terutama karena berdiri di celah melampaui kemampuan atau keuangan kita, melainkan karena kenyataannya, pekerjaan itu sering kali tidak memiliki jabatan, penahbisan, atau pengakuan. Pekerjaan itu harus dilakukan oleh sukarelawan yang memiliki cukup visi dan kepedulian untuk mengorbankan agenda mereka sendiri demi satu-satunya tujuan, yaitu menutup lubang pada pagar. Sering kali pekerjaan itu bukan berada dalam ranah jasmani, melainkan dalam batas-batas rohani. Meskipun orang miskin selalu ada bersama kita dan orang yang luhur secara rohani akan merendahkan diri untuk menolong mereka, kita harus mempertimbangkan bahwa mungkin Allah memikirkan hal yang lebih besar di sini daripada sekadar membutuhkan seseorang untuk mengatur antrean roti dan dapur umum. Dia mencari seorang pria yang mengenakan jubah “prinsip-prinsip ungu” yang tidak akan ditanggalkannya ketika suhu meningkat.

Raja Darius menandatangani dekret yang menentukan nasib Daniel, yang dirancang untuk mengantarnya ke jamuan makan siang bersama singa-singa. Ketika Daniel mengetahui bahwa surat itu telah ditandatangani, ia pergi ke rumahnya. Jendela-jendela kamar atasnya terbuka menghadap Yerusalem. Tiga kali sehari ia berlutut, berdoa, dan mengucap syukur kepada Allahnya, seperti yang biasa dilakukannya sebelumnya. –Dan 6:10. Betapa sepele rasanya jika Daniel menutup jendela sebelum berdoa. Namun Daniel tidak sedang mengisi celah dengan kehadirannya dalam jabatan tinggi pemerintahan yang dipegangnya. Celah itu adalah kelangkaan saksi-saksi saleh di Babel. Jadi, lubang antara surga dan bumi harus ditutup dengan doa di dekat jendela yang terbuka, sementara ia mengorbankan “kursinya di senat.”

Alasan mendasar mengapa begitu banyak celah ada dan begitu sedikit pria yang mengisinya adalah karena kita sering mencampuradukkan visi pribadi kita yang duniawi tentang keadaan dengan tujuan-tujuan kekal Allah. Kita sibuk melakukan hal-hal baik dan merasa cukup berguna. Marta dengan penuh semangat sibuk mengisi apa yang ia anggap sebagai celah mendesak di rumah tangga, sedangkan Maria duduk di tempat yang kekal. Sangat mudah terjebak dalam perangkap aktivitas kehidupan yang sibuk. Kita mungkin mencurahkan perhatian penuh untuk naik ke puncak tangga seefisien mungkin, hanya untuk mendapati tangga itu bersandar pada dinding yang salah. Banyak orang sangat sibuk, tetapi tidak terlalu efektif. Banyak orang telah bekerja keras selama bertahun-tahun dalam pekerjaan Tuhan, hanya untuk sampai di garis akhir dan menyadari bahwa hal-hal yang paling penting telah luput dari mereka. Ada yang mengabdikan hidupnya untuk melayani orang lain, tetapi membiarkan pernikahannya menderita atau anak-anaknya tidak menghormatinya. Yang lain telah memberikan “Korban” kepada gereja mereka sementara mengabaikan hubungan mereka sendiri dengan orang tua mereka.

Orang yang berdiri di celah harus bijaksana, dan kebijaksanaan harus memahami di mana letak celah yang sesungguhnya. Dalam hal ini kita harus digerakkan oleh visi alkitabiah yang memiliki tujuan. Kehidupan akan menyediakan banyak kesempatan untuk meninggalkan jalan kita. Jika kita secara aktif berusaha menjalani harapan yang dibebankan kepada kita oleh keluarga, teman, rekan, agenda gereja, dan keadaan hidup, kita akan digerakkan oleh orang-orang, bukan oleh prinsip-prinsip alkitabiah. Meskipun di permukaan hal ini mungkin tampak masuk akal, kita bisa menuai kekecewaan pahit ketika mendapati diri kita tergantung di ujung tali yang salah.

Jadi, seperti apakah celah yang menjadi perhatian Allah? Ada yang mengatakan bahwa celah ini muncul setiap kali ada kebutuhan. Orang miskin selalu ada bersama kita dan tentu saja ini merupakan kesempatan untuk berbuat baik. Namun, bagian yang lebih baik yang dipilih Maria tidak ada hubungannya dengan menolong orang miskin atau memberi makan orang lapar. Demikian pula, perempuan yang memiliki kotak pualam berisi minyak narwastu yang berharga itu bisa saja menjualnya dan mencukupi kebutuhan orang miskin untuk waktu yang cukup lama dengan hasil penjualannya. Namun, celah yang sesungguhnya tidak dapat ditutup dengan membelai orang lumpuh, melainkan dengan memahkotai Kristus. Di Taman Eden tidak ada celah, sebab manusia hidup dalam keselarasan sempurna dengan Penciptanya. Dosalah yang menciptakan celah dan merusak hubungan itu. Selain itu, pada akhir zaman tidak akan ada keretakan ketika Sang Anak Domba menerima mempelai perempuan-Nya. Sampai saat itu, ada celah besar yang tetap ada karena bumi ini menolak memuliakan Penciptanya. Berdiri di celah itu harus menjadi tujuan utama semua orang yang ingin menyandang nama-Nya.

Hal ini menuntut perubahan menyeluruh dalam hubungan kita dengan Allah. Pendamaian melalui darah Kristus memungkinkan hal itu secara hukum. Penghiburan Roh Kudus membuatnya memuaskan secara emosional, tetapi yang menghidupkan adegan itu adalah penyerahan diri kita dan pemuliaan Allah. Anak yang Hilang adalah contoh utama jiwa yang mendatangkan banyak masalah bagi dirinya sendiri dengan meninggalkan kedudukannya sebagai anak ayahnya. Dasar pemulihannya tidak lebih dari pemulihan kembali hubungan ayah-anak yang telah ada sejak ia lahir.

Menurut saya, Allah tidak begitu mencari jiwa-jiwa yang melambaikan tangan ke udara sambil berseru, “Ini aku, utuslah aku!” Sebaliknya, mata-Nya mencari jiwa-jiwa rendah hati yang menundukkan kehendak mereka di hadapan Yang Mahakuasa dan mengakui “Ya Tuhan, Engkau layak menerima kemuliaan, hormat, dan kuasa, sebab Engkau telah menciptakan segala sesuatu, dan karena kehendak-Mu semuanya itu ada dan diciptakan.” –Wahyu 4:11. Tidak kekurangan anak-anak Skewa yang membayangkan bahwa mereka sedang mengisi peran penting karena bersedia menyiarkan “Yesus” yang telah mereka dengar. Pada tahun 1997, sekitar 800.000 pria tiba di sebuah pertemuan Promise Keepers di Washington D.C. sebagai tanggapan terhadap tema “Berdiri di Celah.” Orang-orang ini mungkin berniat baik untuk mewakili Allah kepada suatu bangsa yang dengan cepat meninggalkan landasan rohaninya, tetapi dibutuhkan lebih dari sekadar hati yang bersedia. Allah tidak membutuhkan sejumlah besar orang untuk dijejalkan ke dalam sebuah lubang. Dia mencari pria-pria yang memenuhi syarat, dan hanya sedikit yang telah diangkat ke kedudukan seperti itu.

Jika yang diinginkan Allah hanyalah pria-pria yang hadir di sebuah pertemuan atau menyatakan iman mereka di jalan-jalan secara terbuka, tentu Dia dapat menemukan banyak orang yang menginginkan pekerjaan baik seperti itu. Namun, berdiri di celah antara Allah dan dunia hanya akan diperkenankan oleh Allah bagi mereka yang layak berada di sana. Kesombongan manusia yang universal mendorong manusia untuk percaya bahwa ia hanya perlu ingin berguna, lalu ia akan dipakai. Di rumah Allah ada bejana untuk kehormatan dan ada bejana untuk kehinaan, tetapi untuk layak menerima tempat terhormat jauh lebih sulit daripada sekadar menginginkan tempat itu.

Sangat lazim pada zaman kita menerima surat yang membawa pesan, “Dapatkan pengakuan yang layak Anda terima.” Bukan rahasia bahwa pengakuan yang layak diterima banyak orang adalah tidak mendapat pengakuan sama sekali. Namun, kita semua telah terpengaruh oleh pesan tersirat bahwa setiap orang layak mendapat pengakuan. Masyarakat kita mengajarkan bahwa semua orang yang tidak bermoral, tidak bijaksana, dan tidak cakap mengelola keuangan layak menerima perhatian yang sama seperti orang yang bermoral dan rajin. Jika orang malas layak mendapat upah yang baik dan orang boros layak mendapat keamanan finansial, maka Rasul Paulus tentu tidak berhak menetapkan persyaratan apa pun bagi janda-janda yang seharusnya menerima bantuan dari gereja. Ia juga tidak berhak menolak jiwa tulus mana pun yang menginginkan jabatan penilik jemaat hanya karena orang itu tidak memenuhi persyaratannya. Namun Allah memperhatikan beberapa jiwa …di Sardis yang tidak mencemarkan pakaian mereka; mereka akan berjalan bersama-Ku dengan pakaian putih, sebab mereka layak. –Why 3:4

Merekalah pria-pria di celah. Bukan karena mereka memiliki energi yang melimpah, tetapi karena mereka memiliki visi tentang kemurnian. Ini bukanlah kebetulan belaka, sebab pria yang ingin mencapai kedudukan tinggi di hadapan Allah harus melakukannya melalui…

…Tujuan

Karena iman, Musa, setelah dewasa, menolak disebut anak putri Firaun. Ia memilih untuk menderita bersama umat Allah daripada menikmati kesenangan dosa yang sementara. Ia menganggap penghinaan karena Kristus lebih berharga daripada harta Mesir, sebab ia memandang upah yang akan diterimanya. Karena iman ia meninggalkan Mesir tanpa takut akan murka raja, sebab ia bertahan seolah-olah melihat Dia yang tidak kelihatan. –Ibr 11:24-27

Visi sejati untuk pekerjaan Allah akan disertai harga yang harus dibayar. Pemimpin muda yang kaya itu tentu ingin menjadi penguasa dalam kerajaan Kristus sekaligus atas tanah miliknya, tetapi ia tidak dapat mempertahankan keduanya. Prinsip ini merupakan rintangan pertama baginya dan bagi setiap orang lain yang menginginkan pekerjaan mulia seperti itu. Sebagai seorang muda, Musa mengambil keputusan dan memilih kesetiaannya. Ia siap ditolak oleh Mesir, tetapi tidak pernah membayangkan bahwa ia juga akan begitu saja disingkirkan oleh bangsanya sendiri.

Empat puluh tahun dalam dapur peleburan yang sunyi memurnikan kesombongannya dan memangkas kehebatannya. Di sana ia lulus dari seminari kesunyian, diperlengkapi dan dipersiapkan untuk berdiri di celah sebagai orang paling lemah lembut di muka bumi. Ia menjadi pendoa syafaat bagi manusia di hadapan Allah. Sebagai pembela manusia dan Allah, ia berkhotbah dan berdoa, berjalan dan menangis, hidup dan mengasihi Allah serta saudara-saudaranya. Selama itu, ia menganggap dirinya tidak layak untuk kedudukan tersebut. Meskipun anak-anak Israel berada tepat di pusat hatinya, rasa takut dan perhatiannya tidak pernah berpaling dari Allahnya. Ketika kita berusaha dihormati manusia, tujuan kita menjadi kabur dan kedudukan kita di celah pun hilang. Banyak pendeta, orang tua, dan peziarah yang baik telah melakukan kesalahan ini dan menerima arahan dari istri, anak-anak, teman-teman, atau gereja mereka. Mungkin hal itu tampak seperti tindakan yang penuh kasih, kepedulian, dan penghormatan. Namun Allah menuntut kesetiaan mutlak dan tidak ada kompromi. Apa yang “ingin dicapai” seseorang digerakkan oleh tujuan visionernya, tetapi akan menjadi seperti apa dirinya bergantung pada…

…Prioritas

Perkataan ini benar: Jika seseorang menginginkan jabatan penilik jemaat, ia menginginkan pekerjaan yang baik. Karena itu, seorang penilik jemaat haruslah tidak bercela, suami dari satu istri, mampu menguasai diri, bijaksana, sopan, suka memberi tumpangan, cakap mengajar; bukan peminum, bukan pemukul, bukan pencinta uang yang kotor, melainkan lemah lembut, tidak suka bertengkar, dan tidak serakah. Ia harus mengatur rumah tangganya dengan baik, dan anak-anaknya harus tunduk kepadanya dengan segala hormat; –1Tim 3:1-4. Tujuan membentuk tempat tujuan kita, tetapi prioritaslah yang membuka jalan untuk mencapainya.

Sayangnya, beberapa pria diangkat ke pelayanan berdasarkan pendapat umum, tetapi Allah memilih orang-orang-Nya berdasarkan prioritas dan kualifikasi kekal mereka. Pria yang dikendalikan oleh harta benda, hawa nafsu, atau kedudukan mereka tidak akan berguna untuk melayani tujuan Allah. Mereka suka dipanggil Pendeta, Yang Terhormat, atau Bapa. Mereka suka dihargai sebagai orang yang bersemangat, berpengetahuan, teguh, atau penuh belas kasih. Apakah sekarang aku sedang mencari perkenanan manusia atau Allah? Ataukah aku berusaha menyenangkan manusia? Jika aku masih berusaha menyenangkan manusia, aku bukanlah hamba Kristus. –Gal 1:10 ASV

Syukurlah, Allah tidak memandang muka, dan batu yang cocok untuk tembok tidak akan dibiarkan tergeletak di jalan. Orang lanjut usia, orang miskin, orang cacat, dan orang lumpuh semuanya merupakan calon utama untuk mengisi celah. Mereka yang memiliki mimpi yang hancur, tubuh yang cacat, dan hati yang remuk dapat berdiri tanpa hambatan di samping pagar bersama Nuh, Abraham, Yusuf, Musa, Daniel, Ester, Rut, dan tak terhitung banyaknya orang lainnya. Mereka semua adalah wakil-wakil Allah yang cemerlang bagi dunia ini. Mereka semua telah berpaling dari kesia-siaan, ketenaran, keakraban, dan kekayaan, lalu menjadi pahlawan surga. Mereka berdiri bahu-membahu di sisi pagar dan membentuk “Kedutaan Yang Kekal.” Mereka mengasihi, sementara yang lain membenci. Mereka memberi segalanya, sementara yang lain menerima. Mereka diejek dan disalahpahami, dicela dan dicemooh, letih dan menangis.

Sebab bagi Allah kami adalah bau harum Kristus, baik di antara mereka yang diselamatkan maupun di antara mereka yang binasa. Bagi yang satu kami adalah bau kematian yang membawa kematian, dan bagi yang lain bau kehidupan yang membawa kehidupan. Siapakah yang sanggup melakukan semuanya itu? –2Kor 2:15-16. Merekalah orang-orang yang tujuan dan prioritasnya semata-mata dikendalikan oleh Allah.
