It was 2:30 p.m., Tuesday afternoon.

“Señora!” a chorus of voices hollered from outside our property hedge. “Open the gate!”

“Just wait,” I called back. “It’s not three o’clock yet.”

Disgruntled murmurings sounded from the other side of the hedge. I turned to my wailing baby. Sinking into the rocker to feed her, I closed my eyes to relish each quiet moment before the coming tumult.

**************

We had scarcely settled onto the farm when the neighbor children found us. They appeared—uninvited and unannounced, any time of day—to stay as long as they wished. The first ones soon brought more friends along to join in their play with the foreigner’s children and toys. Play-Doh and table games entertained them but oh, what a commotion ten children could make in a concrete house.

After much exasperation, Ernest (my husband) and I finally came up with a plan…. They could come two afternoons a week, arriving no earlier than three o’clock in the afternoon. On Tuesdays they could stay for supper, but on Thursdays they must leave by 6 p.m.

We also had other rules…. Our children needed to stay within my eyesight and earshot when playing with neighbor children. And NO closed doors. Still, questions niggled my brain. Is this a good thing or a bad one? Will we live to regret it? What if they are a bad influence on our children? My questions formed a prayer, one which God had been hearing from me quite a bit these past months. Lord, give me wisdom and patience with these children today. And if they are a bad influence on our children, Lord, please reveal that to us before our children are harmed.

But what an opportunity! This was one way I could reach the world while being a stay-at-home mom… I read them Bible stories. I taught them the need to respect and obey grownups. I told them they needed to obey me, just as my children were expected to. Transgressors, I warned, would be sent home.

Zinnia did not believe me, until the day she disobeyed and was expelled. I grin now, remembering the little troublemaker perching on the neighbor’s wall, peering over into our farm where her cousins were happily playing. Once had taught her; after that Zinnia obeyed.

**************

“Señora!” Zinnia’s voice interrupted my reverie. “Is it three o’clock yet?”

I opened one eye to peek at the clock—2:47.

“Not quite!” I hollered out the window. Placing baby into the walker, I headed to the kitchen. What would I feed them tonight?

**************

“Zinnia, I need to look in your purse before you go home.”

It was Tuesday evening again, several months later. We had been missing various small things after Zinnia started bringing a purse along on her visits to our house. Tonight, we would see if our suspicions were correct.

Zinnia’s terror-filled eyes met mine. “Just a minute, Señora. I need to use the bathroom.”

“You can use the bathroom after we look in your purse.”

“No, Señora, I can’t wait…”, her voice trailed off as she rushed to the bathroom.

I sighed. Of course, her purse would be empty when she came back out. Searching the bathroom later that night revealed treasures hidden here and there.

“Let’s chat a little, Zinnia,” I invited the following week. Zinnia sat on the bed, twisting yarn knots on the comforter, her eyes defensive, fearful. My heart yearned for the dear girl. Her mom had left years ago to work in another country, leaving the girls with their Grandma.

“I don’t care about those things you stole, Zinnia,” I began. “But it’s a habit you don’t want to start. God cares about you….”

That was the last time Zinnia, her sister, and their cousins showed up at our place. “Our Grandma doesn’t let us come anymore,” they explained.

Maybe it was Grandma; I think it was God. We had prayed much that He would make it clear if their visits were harmful to our children and if they should stop coming. My heart was torn between love for the neighbor children and protection for our own. This was the way God chose to answer.

“Thank you, God,” I prayed. “We’ll take this as your answer, and not invite them back. Send them over if you want them to come again.”

**************

Several years passed. Now it was Jon, a neighbor boy, frequenting our home.

“Could he come to your house every day after school?” his parents had wondered. “We want him to learn good things, instead of playing with boys in our neighborhood.”

Hmm. So, we’re to raise the boy while both parents work?

“He can come Tuesday and Thursday afternoons,” Ernest decided. “Those are the days I’m more often at home.”

Jon showed up faithfully on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons. Problem was, Ernest couldn’t. Other responsibilities and obligations kept coming up, hindering him from being there like he wanted to.

I did not want to nag my husband… He really wished he could be at home, working with the boys. Should I say something, or not? It didn’t seem ideal to have an unconverted boy working for hours with our son, a new Christian.

I did mention my questions to Ernest, but mostly I made it a matter of prayer.

Jon stopped coming. I was amazed. I felt for Jon, yet once again I thanked God for His answer.

**************

“How can I reach out to my neighbor children without compromising my own?” a friend asked recently. Moving to a new area, she faces the challenge of neighbor children coming over.

There are no simple answers. I have discovered the urgency of prayer, and God’s faithfulness in answering when we cry out to Him for wisdom. His answer to others may well be different from what He worked out for us.

**************

Another sister granted me permission to share their experience in relating with neighbor children:

Alex and his mother live across the road from us and began attending church soon after we moved here. Alex came over almost every day and taught our boys Spanish in short order. The boys dreaded his visits at first, but they soon became great friends. After a while another neighbor boy, Nilton, started coming at times and we thought he seemed decent enough. Then one day a third boy, José, came along. I got a distinctly uncomfortable feeling. I gave them a time limit, but just couldn’t shake the uneasy feeling. So, though I thought I didn’t have time, I decided I would work outside the whole time while they were here. I worked close to them and kept an eye on things and thought everything was fine. They seemed to just be playing together nicely, so I was surprised when they went home before the time was up.

It wasn’t long before my boys came in crying; they felt so bad about what had happened. Alex had asked them to deliver a note to his girlfriend because his mom wouldn’t like it if he did. One of the other boys told them what he does out behind bushes at public school, so he doesn’t get caught. They tried to get my boys to promise not to tell me. They didn’t promise, and I was so thankful! But they were very torn up because they thought Alex would not be their friend anymore.

My husband and I talked with the boys and assured them that they had handled the situation correctly by not promising to keep secrets. Within the hour, Alex’s mom came over to visit and we told her about it. She was very alarmed that her son had tried to pass a note and later took care of the situation with her son. I was glad that the budding relationship he had with the neighbor girl was stopped before it went any farther. Alex’s friendship with our boys has continued but the other two boys discovered that our boys had told us about them and didn’t come over for years after that.

José recently asked our eight-year-old son if he could come over to his house and play. I said no. His grandma came over several days later, offended, and said that José was very sad about it. I explained that I feel I must always be with my boys if he would come over because one time, he had tried to get our son to play an electronic war game with him. The grandma understood and was sad that her grandson was a bad influence. She wanted the best for him. We have invited him to Sunday School, but he doesn’t want that. I just hope that we can always have the type of relationship with our children that they will feel free to come to us and not keep these situations to themselves and feel guilty.

**************

Wise parents seek to remove danger, but not difficulty, from their children’s path. I was recently amazed while reading Judges 3, to discover that God wanted some enemy nations to remain in the land of Canaan. Why? He wanted parents to teach their children war (v. 2). Instead, the children of Israel made friends with the enemy nations and began to intermarry. “It seems we live closer to the world here on the mission field,” one sister shared. Our children are growing up on the front lines, as it were. This can be positive. They have frequent opportunities to “speak with the enemy in the gates,” where they are asked what we believe, and why. But when parents are lax, or their children are rebellious, this closer association with the world can prove tragic.

As we connect with God in prayer for our children, we must also connect with them. No strict safety guidelines will substitute a close relationship with your child. The mother of a child who was abused shared, “The only way your child will tell you what is going on is if you have a close relationship.”

I stagger as I consider our enemy and my own inadequacy as a mother. Suddenly I am seized with urgency to pray for things which never entered my head when our children were still young. Abuse cases exist around us; at times in our very midst. I pray for our children’s protection from the evil which surrounds them and that which rises in their hearts. I pray they will never mar another’s purity. I pray for purity at the marriage altar, both for them and their future spouses.

I pray with urgency, yet with confidence. Because this I know: God loves our children—He cares about their purity and protection even more than we as parents do—He longs for us to partner with Him in raising them to be faithful servants of His—And He wants to show Himself strong on behalf of humble parents who cry out to Him as they train soldiers in enemy territory. For the eyes of the LORD run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to shew himself strong in the behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him… –2 Chronicles 16:9.

मंगलवार की दोपहर, 2:30 बजे थे।

“सेन्योरा!” हमारे आँगन की बाड़ के बाहर से कई आवाज़ें एक साथ चिल्लाईं। “फाटक खोलिए!”

“ज़रा इंतज़ार करो,” मैंने जवाब दिया। “अभी तीन बजे नहीं हुए हैं।”

बाड़ के दूसरी ओर से नाराज़गी भरी बड़बड़ाहट सुनाई दी। मैं अपने रोते हुए शिशु की ओर मुड़ी। उसे दूध पिलाने के लिए झूलने वाली कुर्सी पर बैठते हुए मैंने आँखें बंद कर लीं, ताकि आने वाली हलचल से पहले के हर शांत पल का आनंद ले सकूँ।

**************

हम अभी-अभी खेत वाले घर में बसे ही थे कि पड़ोस के बच्चे हमें ढूँढ़ते हुए आ पहुँचे। वे बिना बुलाए और बिना बताए, दिन के किसी भी समय आ जाते और जितनी देर चाहें, ठहरते। पहले आने वाले बच्चे जल्द ही और दोस्तों को साथ ले आए, जो विदेशियों के बच्चों और खिलौनों के साथ खेलने में शामिल हो गए। प्ले-डो और मेज़ पर खेले जाने वाले खेल उनका मनोरंजन करते, लेकिन दस बच्चे एक कंक्रीट के घर में कितना शोर मचा सकते थे!

बहुत खीझने के बाद, अर्नेस्ट (मेरे पति) और मैंने आखिरकार एक योजना बनाई… वे सप्ताह में दो दोपहर आ सकते थे और दोपहर के तीन बजे से पहले नहीं पहुँच सकते थे। मंगलवार को वे रात के खाने तक रुक सकते थे, लेकिन गुरुवार को उन्हें शाम 6 बजे तक चले जाना था।

हमारे कुछ और नियम भी थे… पड़ोस के बच्चों के साथ खेलते समय हमारे बच्चे मेरी नज़र और सुनने की पहुँच में रहें। और दरवाज़े बंद नहीं होंगे। फिर भी, कुछ सवाल मेरे मन में खटकते रहे। क्या यह अच्छी बात है या बुरी? क्या हमें इस पर पछताना पड़ेगा? अगर उनका हमारे बच्चों पर बुरा प्रभाव पड़ा तो? मेरे सवाल एक प्रार्थना बन गए—ऐसी प्रार्थना जिसे परमेश्वर इन बीते महीनों में मुझसे बार-बार सुन रहे थे। प्रभु, आज इन बच्चों के साथ व्यवहार करने के लिए मुझे बुद्धि और धीरज दीजिए। और यदि उनका हमारे बच्चों पर बुरा प्रभाव पड़ रहा है, तो प्रभु, कृपया हमारे बच्चों को नुकसान पहुँचने से पहले हमें यह दिखा दीजिए।

लेकिन यह कितना बड़ा अवसर था! घर पर रहने वाली माँ होते हुए दुनिया तक पहुँचने का यह एक तरीका था… मैं उन्हें बाइबल की कहानियाँ पढ़कर सुनाती थी। मैं उन्हें सिखाती थी कि बड़ों का आदर करना और उनकी आज्ञा मानना ज़रूरी है। मैं उनसे कहती थी कि उन्हें मेरी आज्ञा भी माननी होगी, ठीक वैसे ही जैसे मेरे बच्चों से अपेक्षा की जाती थी। मैंने चेतावनी दी थी कि नियम तोड़ने वालों को घर भेज दिया जाएगा।

ज़िनिया को मेरी बात पर विश्वास नहीं हुआ—उस दिन तक, जब उसने अवज्ञा की और उसे घर भेज दिया गया। अब उस नन्ही शरारती को पड़ोसी की दीवार पर बैठकर हमारे खेत वाले घर में झाँकते हुए याद करके मैं मुस्कराती हूँ, जहाँ उसकी चचेरी बहनें खुशी-खुशी खेल रही थीं। एक बार की सीख उसके लिए काफ़ी थी; उसके बाद ज़िनिया ने आज्ञा मानी।

**************

“सेन्योरा!” ज़िनिया की आवाज़ ने मेरी तंद्रा तोड़ दी। “क्या तीन बजे हो गए?”

मैंने घड़ी देखने के लिए एक आँख खोली—2:47।

“अभी नहीं!” मैंने खिड़की से चिल्लाकर कहा। बच्चे को वॉकर में बिठाकर मैं रसोई की ओर चली। आज रात उन्हें क्या खिलाऊँगी?

**************

“ज़िनिया, तुम्हारे घर जाने से पहले मुझे तुम्हारा पर्स देखना है।”

कई महीने बाद, फिर से मंगलवार की शाम थी। जब से ज़िनिया हमारे घर आते समय पर्स साथ लाने लगी थी, तब से हमारी कई छोटी-मोटी चीज़ें गायब हो रही थीं। आज रात हम देखेंगे कि हमारा शक सही था या नहीं।

ज़िनिया की आतंक से भरी आँखें मेरी आँखों से मिलीं। “बस एक मिनट, सेन्योरा। मुझे बाथरूम जाना है।”

“तुम पर्स देखने के बाद बाथरूम जा सकती हो।”

“नहीं, सेन्योरा, मैं रुक नहीं सकती…” बाथरूम की ओर भागते हुए उसकी आवाज़ धीमी पड़ गई।

मैंने आह भरी। ज़ाहिर है, जब वह वापस आएगी तो उसका पर्स खाली होगा। उस रात बाद में बाथरूम की तलाशी लेने पर यहाँ-वहाँ छिपाकर रखी हुई चीज़ें मिलीं।

“ज़िनिया, आओ, थोड़ी बात करें,” मैंने अगले हफ़्ते उससे कहा। ज़िनिया बिस्तर पर बैठी थी और बिस्तर की चादर पर धागे की गाँठों को मरोड़ रही थी; उसकी आँखों में बचाव और डर झलक रहा था। उस प्यारी बच्ची के लिए मेरा दिल तड़प उठा। उसकी माँ कई साल पहले दूसरे देश में काम करने चली गई थी और लड़कियों को उनकी दादी के पास छोड़ गई थी।

“ज़िनिया, तुम्हारी चुराई हुई उन चीज़ों की मुझे चिंता नहीं है,” मैंने बात शुरू की। “लेकिन यह ऐसी आदत है जिसे तुम शुरू नहीं करना चाहोगी। परमेश्वर को तुम्हारी परवाह है…”

ज़िनिया, उसकी बहन और उनकी चचेरी बहनें आखिरी बार उसी दिन हमारे घर आई थीं। “हमारी दादी अब हमें आने नहीं देतीं,” उन्होंने बताया।

शायद यह दादी थीं; मुझे लगता है कि यह परमेश्वर थे। हमने बहुत प्रार्थना की थी कि यदि उनकी मुलाकातें हमारे बच्चों के लिए हानिकारक हों और उन्हें आना बंद कर देना चाहिए, तो परमेश्वर यह बात स्पष्ट कर दें। पड़ोस के बच्चों के लिए प्रेम और अपने बच्चों की रक्षा के बीच मेरा दिल बँटा हुआ था। परमेश्वर ने इसी तरह जवाब देना चुना।

“धन्यवाद, परमेश्वर,” मैंने प्रार्थना की। “हम इसे आपका जवाब मानेंगे और उन्हें फिर नहीं बुलाएँगे। यदि आप चाहते हैं कि वे दोबारा आएँ, तो उन्हें भेज दीजिए।”

**************

कई साल बीत गए। अब पड़ोस का एक लड़का, जॉन, अक्सर हमारे घर आने लगा।

“क्या वह स्कूल के बाद हर दिन आपके घर आ सकता है?” उसके माता-पिता ने पूछा था। “हम चाहते हैं कि वह अच्छी बातें सीखे, हमारे पड़ोस के लड़कों के साथ खेलने के बजाय।”

हम्म। तो क्या हम दोनों माता-पिता के काम पर रहने के दौरान इस लड़के को पालें?

“वह मंगलवार और गुरुवार की दोपहर आ सकता है,” अर्नेस्ट ने तय किया। “इन दिनों मेरे घर पर रहने की संभावना ज़्यादा होती है।”

जॉन मंगलवार और गुरुवार की दोपहर नियमित रूप से आने लगा। समस्या यह थी कि अर्नेस्ट घर पर नहीं रह पाता था। दूसरी ज़िम्मेदारियाँ और काम आ जाते, जिससे वह वहाँ नहीं रह पाता, जबकि वह ऐसा करना चाहता था।

मैं अपने पति को बार-बार टोकना नहीं चाहती थी… वह सचमुच घर पर रहकर लड़कों के साथ काम करना चाहता था। क्या मुझे कुछ कहना चाहिए या नहीं? यह बात मुझे ठीक नहीं लगती थी कि एक अविश्वासी लड़का घंटों हमारे बेटे के साथ काम करे, जो अभी-अभी मसीही बना था।

मैंने अपने सवाल अर्नेस्ट के सामने रखे ज़रूर, लेकिन ज़्यादातर मैंने इस बात को प्रार्थना का विषय बनाया।

जॉन ने आना बंद कर दिया। मुझे आश्चर्य हुआ। मुझे जॉन के लिए दुख हुआ, फिर भी एक बार फिर मैंने परमेश्वर को उनके जवाब के लिए धन्यवाद दिया।

**************

“मैं अपने बच्चों के साथ समझौता किए बिना पड़ोस के बच्चों तक कैसे पहुँचूँ?” हाल ही में एक मित्र ने पूछा। नए इलाके में आने के बाद, उसे पड़ोस के बच्चों के घर आने की चुनौती का सामना करना पड़ रहा है।

इसके कोई आसान जवाब नहीं हैं। मैंने प्रार्थना की ज़रूरत की गंभीरता और यह जाना है कि जब हम बुद्धि के लिए परमेश्वर को पुकारते हैं, तो वह विश्वासयोग्यता से जवाब देते हैं। दूसरों को उनका जवाब शायद उस जवाब से अलग हो जो उन्होंने हमारे लिए ठहराया।

**************

एक और बहन ने पड़ोस के बच्चों से मेलजोल के अपने अनुभव को साझा करने की मुझे अनुमति दी:

एलेक्स और उसकी माँ सड़क के उस पार रहते हैं और हमारे यहाँ आने के कुछ ही समय बाद चर्च आने लगे। एलेक्स लगभग हर दिन हमारे घर आने लगा और कुछ ही समय में उसने हमारे लड़कों को स्पैनिश सिखा दी। शुरू में लड़कों को उसके आने से डर लगता था, लेकिन जल्द ही वे बहुत अच्छे दोस्त बन गए। कुछ समय बाद पड़ोस का एक और लड़का, निल्टन, कभी-कभी आने लगा और हमें लगा कि वह ठीक-ठाक है। फिर एक दिन तीसरा लड़का, होसे, उसके साथ आया। मुझे साफ़ तौर पर बेचैनी महसूस हुई। मैंने उनके लिए समय तय कर दिया, लेकिन मन की बेचैनी दूर नहीं हुई। इसलिए, हालाँकि मुझे लगा कि मेरे पास समय नहीं है, मैंने तय किया कि जब तक वे यहाँ होंगे, मैं बाहर काम करूँगी। मैं उनके पास ही काम करती रही और उन पर नज़र रखी; मुझे लगा कि सब ठीक है। वे बस साथ मिलकर अच्छे से खेलते दिख रहे थे, इसलिए जब समय पूरा होने से पहले ही वे घर चले गए तो मुझे हैरानी हुई।

इसके कुछ ही देर बाद मेरे लड़के रोते हुए अंदर आए; जो हुआ था, उससे वे बहुत दुखी थे। एलेक्स ने उनसे अपनी प्रेमिका को एक चिट्ठी पहुँचाने को कहा था, क्योंकि उसकी माँ को यह पसंद नहीं आता। दूसरे लड़कों में से एक ने उन्हें बताया कि वह सरकारी स्कूल में झाड़ियों के पीछे क्या करता है, ताकि पकड़ा न जाए। उन्होंने मेरे लड़कों से वादा करने को कहा कि वे मुझे नहीं बताएँगे। उन्होंने वादा नहीं किया, और इसके लिए मैं बहुत आभारी थी! लेकिन वे बहुत परेशान थे, क्योंकि उन्हें लगा कि एलेक्स अब उनका दोस्त नहीं रहेगा।

मेरे पति और मैंने लड़कों से बात की और उन्हें भरोसा दिलाया कि राज़ रखने का वादा न करके उन्होंने सही किया था। एक घंटे के भीतर एलेक्स की माँ मिलने आईं और हमने उन्हें सब कुछ बताया। वह इस बात से बहुत घबरा गईं कि उनके बेटे ने चिट्ठी पहुँचाने की कोशिश की थी, और बाद में उन्होंने अपने बेटे के साथ इस मामले को संभाला। मुझे खुशी हुई कि पड़ोस की लड़की के साथ उसका उभरता रिश्ता आगे बढ़ने से पहले ही रुक गया। एलेक्स की हमारे लड़कों से दोस्ती बनी रही, लेकिन बाकी दोनों लड़कों को पता चल गया कि हमारे लड़कों ने हमें उनके बारे में बता दिया था, इसलिए वे कई सालों तक हमारे घर नहीं आए।

हाल ही में होसे ने हमारे आठ साल के बेटे से पूछा कि क्या वह उसके घर खेलने आ सकता है। मैंने मना कर दिया। कई दिन बाद उसकी दादी नाराज़ होकर आईं और कहा कि होसे इस बात से बहुत दुखी है। मैंने समझाया कि यदि वह हमारे घर आएगा तो मुझे हमेशा अपने लड़कों के साथ रहना होगा, क्योंकि एक बार उसने हमारे बेटे से उसके साथ इलेक्ट्रॉनिक युद्ध वाला खेल खेलने को कहा था। दादी समझ गईं और उन्हें दुख हुआ कि उनका पोता बुरा प्रभाव डाल रहा था। वह उसके लिए सबसे अच्छा चाहती थीं। हमने उसे संडे स्कूल में आने का न्योता दिया है, लेकिन वह नहीं आना चाहता। मुझे बस उम्मीद है कि हमारे बच्चों के साथ हमारा रिश्ता हमेशा ऐसा बना रहे कि वे खुलकर हमारे पास आ सकें और ऐसी बातें अपने तक न रखें या अपराधबोध महसूस न करें।

**************

समझदार माता-पिता अपने बच्चों के रास्ते से खतरे हटाने की कोशिश करते हैं, कठिनाइयाँ नहीं। हाल ही में न्यायियों 3 पढ़ते हुए मुझे यह जानकर आश्चर्य हुआ कि परमेश्वर चाहते थे कि कनान देश में कुछ शत्रु जातियाँ बनी रहें। क्यों? वह चाहते थे कि माता-पिता अपने बच्चों को युद्ध करना सिखाएँ (पद 2)। इसके बजाय, इस्राएल के बच्चे शत्रु जातियों से मित्रता करने लगे और उनके साथ विवाह करने लगे। “ऐसा लगता है कि मिशन-क्षेत्र में हम दुनिया के ज़्यादा करीब रहते हैं,” एक बहन ने बताया। हमारे बच्चे मानो अग्रिम मोर्चे पर बड़े हो रहे हैं। इसमें सकारात्मक पक्ष भी है। उन्हें अक्सर “फाटक पर शत्रु से बात करने” के अवसर मिलते हैं, जहाँ उनसे पूछा जाता है कि हम क्या मानते हैं और क्यों। लेकिन जब माता-पिता लापरवाह होते हैं, या उनके बच्चे विद्रोही होते हैं, तो दुनिया से यह निकटता विनाशकारी साबित हो सकती है।

जब हम अपने बच्चों के लिए प्रार्थना में परमेश्वर से जुड़ते हैं, तो हमें उनसे भी जुड़े रहना चाहिए। सुरक्षा के कितने ही सख़्त नियम आपके बच्चे के साथ घनिष्ठ रिश्ते की जगह नहीं ले सकते। जिस बच्चे के साथ दुर्व्यवहार हुआ था, उसकी माँ ने कहा, “आपका बच्चा आपको क्या हो रहा है, यह तभी बताएगा जब आपका उसके साथ घनिष्ठ रिश्ता होगा।”

जब मैं अपने शत्रु और एक माँ के रूप में अपनी अपर्याप्तता के बारे में सोचती हूँ, तो मैं भीतर तक हिल जाती हूँ। अचानक मुझे उन बातों के लिए प्रार्थना करने की तीव्र आवश्यकता महसूस होती है, जो हमारे बच्चे छोटे थे तब मेरे मन में कभी नहीं आईं। हमारे आसपास, कभी-कभी हमारे अपने बीच में भी, दुर्व्यवहार के मामले होते हैं। मैं अपने बच्चों की रक्षा के लिए प्रार्थना करती हूँ—उन बुराइयों से जो उन्हें घेरे हुए हैं और उन बुराइयों से भी जो उनके अपने दिलों में उठती हैं। मैं प्रार्थना करती हूँ कि वे कभी किसी दूसरे की पवित्रता को कलंकित न करें। मैं विवाह-वेदिका पर पवित्रता के लिए, उनके और उनके भावी जीवनसाथियों—दोनों के लिए प्रार्थना करती हूँ।

मैं तत्परता से प्रार्थना करती हूँ, फिर भी विश्वास के साथ। क्योंकि मैं यह जानती हूँ: परमेश्वर हमारे बच्चों से प्रेम करते हैं—उन्हें उनकी पवित्रता और सुरक्षा की हम माता-पिता से भी अधिक चिंता है—वह चाहते हैं कि हम उन्हें उनके विश्वासयोग्य सेवक बनाने में उनके साथ भागीदार हों—और वह उन विनम्र माता-पिताओं की ओर से अपना सामर्थ्य प्रकट करना चाहते हैं, जो शत्रु के क्षेत्र में सैनिकों को प्रशिक्षित करते हुए उन्हें पुकारते हैं। क्योंकि यहोवा की दृष्टि सारी पृथ्वी पर फिरती रहती है, ताकि जिनका मन उसकी ओर निष्कपट है, उनके बल की सहायता करे… –2 इतिहास 16:9।

The cold, grey days of winter are being transformed into the warm, sunny days of spring. The first flowers of the year are persistently pushing their way up out of the cold earth towards the warmth of the sun. It never seems to get old—this exciting feeling in the springtime air. There’s the warmth and light of sunny days. There’s the cheery, lilting music of the song birds as they once more take up housekeeping with seemingly boundless energy. And we are again blessed with another season to plant seeds with the expectation of another crop of food to enjoy.

This year I will turn 48 years of age. My how that sounds old to me. I remember that as a youth I thought that folks who were 50 were old. Now I am almost there. For me, this is a clear reminder that we all are getting older and that we will not live forever. Next, comes a number of sobering thoughts: “What have I done for the furtherance of God’s Kingdom? Am I remaining faithful to Him in all that I do? Lord, what wilt thou have me to do—this year?” Let’s, each one, prayerfully seek the Lord about His present and future will for our lives. Let’s encourage and exhort each other to remain faithful in relationship with, and in service for, our Master.

In this issue we have an excellent article on marriage, which we felt can take the place of an article on Discipleship this time. When we meet with couples who have struggled with extreme marriage problems for years, we usually find that something is not working in a godly way at a foundational level. We feel that this marriage article is quite thorough in its evaluation of building and maintaining a Biblical foundation. Lord willing, we plan to have ongoing articles relating to this subject.

We are scheduled to share a series of meetings in Lebanon County, Pennsylvania, this coming July. Please pass this on to others who may be interested. Also, mark your calendar to save the date.

If you wish to receive updated information once all details are finalized, please contact “The Berean Voice” by phone at (330) 439-9547 or by email at subscribe@bereanvoice.org. Холодные, серые зимние дни сменяются тёплыми, солнечными весенними днями. Первые цветы года упорно пробиваются из холодной земли к солнечному теплу. Кажется, это волнующее весеннее чувство в воздухе никогда не приедается. Вот тепло и свет солнечных дней. Вот весёлая, переливчатая музыка певчих птиц, которые с, кажется, неиссякаемой энергией вновь обустраивают свои гнёзда. И снова мы благословлены ещё одним сезоном, чтобы посеять семена в надежде получить новый урожай пищи, которой можно будет наслаждаться.

В этом году мне исполнится 48 лет. Как же старо это звучит для меня. Помню, в юности я думал, что люди в возрасте 50 лет — старики. Теперь я почти достиг этого возраста. Для меня это ясное напоминание о том, что все мы стареем и не будем жить вечно. Далее приходят несколько отрезвляющих мыслей: «Что я сделал для распространения Царства Божьего? Остаюсь ли я верен Ему во всём, что делаю? Господи, что Ты хочешь, чтобы я делал в этом году?» Давайте каждый в молитве будем искать у Господа, какова Его воля для нашей жизни — ныне и в будущем. Будем поддерживать и ободрять друг друга, чтобы оставаться верными в отношениях с нашим Господином и в служении Ему.

В этом выпуске у нас есть превосходная статья о браке, которой, как мы сочли, в этот раз можно заменить статью об ученичестве. Когда мы встречаемся с супругами, которые годами боролись с серьёзными проблемами в браке, обычно выясняется, что на основополагающем уровне что-то устроено не по-Божьему. Мы считаем, что в этой статье о браке весьма обстоятельно рассматриваются создание и поддержание библейского основания. Если будет на то воля Господа, мы планируем и дальше публиковать статьи на эту тему.

В июле этого года у нас запланирована серия встреч в округе Лебанон, штат Пенсильвания. Несколько церквей в этом районе объединяют усилия, чтобы провести это мероприятие, и забронировали Fairview Reception Center. Просим молиться об этих встречах: чтобы исполнилась воля Божья; чтобы Бог направлял выступающих во время подготовки; и чтобы Бог укрепил церковь благодаря этому труду. Пожалуйста, передайте эту информацию другим, кому она может быть интересна. Также отметьте эту дату в календаре.

Если вы хотите получать обновлённую информацию после того, как будут уточнены все подробности, свяжитесь с «The Berean Voice» по телефону (330) 439-9547 или по электронной почте subscribe@bereanvoice.org. Поскольку будут предоставляться питание и места ограничены, для участия в этом мероприятии потребуется регистрация. Ниже приведены предварительные названия серии и отдельных выступлений, однако они ещё могут измениться.

«Библейский взгляд на проблемы психического, эмоционального, супружеского и сексуального насилия»

  1. Понимание сердца — корень ВСЕХ проблем
  2. Евангелие — Божий ответ на ВСЕ проблемы духа и души (психики) человека
  3. Как психология и мирские философии влияют на нас сегодня
  4. Практическое ученичество — действенная помощь людям в изменении
  5. Библейский взгляд на психические расстройства
  6. Библейская оценка вопросов усыновления и приёмного воспитания детей
  7. Понимание эффекта плацебо и безопасное применение психотропных препаратов
  8. Библейское понимание нравственного падения, порнографии и сексуального насилия (только для взрослых)
  9. Чистота — от рождения до обращения, а затем — к браку или жизни без брака (только для родителей)
  10. Предотвращение проблем и работа с ними в благочестивых семьях
  11. Предотвращение всех жизненных трудностей и помощь в их преодолении в поместной церкви

26–28 июля 2019 года

Место проведения: Fairview Reception Center | 141 Jackson Rd | Lebanon, PA 17042

I am Ted. I was born a male and I know I am a male. My skin color is white, and I know I am white. My parents are white, my grandparents were white, and I have no reason to suspect my other ancestors were anything other than white. These are foundational, irrefutable truths about myself. I do not think I am anything other than what I am. Nor do I desire to be anything other than what I am.

I am a Christian. In order to better define my faith—as there are many who profess Christianity—I am a “biblical” Christian. I believe that the Bible is the Word of God, that it is to be taken literally, and that it instructs a pattern and way of life that all believers should embrace. At the age of 24—after having lived a life of my own choosing and while searching for God who, if He was real, I wanted to know—I turned to Him and I was born again. My transformation as a new creation in Christ began immediately and it continues to this day. My faith in and relationship to Jesus Christ are as foundational and irrefutable as my gender and race.

I am writing in response to that which had been extensively covered by the secular media during the Spring and Summer of 2015: a man who reportedly, throughout his life, had considered himself a female and who had been “transitioning” into a woman; a white woman who had insisted that race is “fluid” and that she is black; and the redefinition of marriage by the Supreme Court of the United States of America affecting, as well, the definition of “family” for an entire nation. These are topics which simply cannot be minimized or otherwise ignored.

The white woman lacked much public support for her explanation of race. In fact, she was significantly ridiculed for her stance. This was not true, however, regarding gender identification or “gay” marriage and family issues, and one must wonder why. If a “genetically/physiologically-constructed” male can be accepted by others as a woman simply because that’s what he thinks he is, and if a man can “marry” a man and a woman can “marry” a woman and be accepted as a married couple by others under the premise of equal rights and because that’s what they want to do, why can’t a white woman be accepted as a black woman when she is convinced that she is black?

The question raised is one of reality. Even though I may think I am the greatest pianist and music composer of all times, the evidence simply does not support that conviction. Even though a white woman says she is black, the evidence likewise does not support that conviction. Also true is that of a man who says he is a woman. The genetic and physiological evidence does not support that conviction. Without the redefinition of marriage, two people of the same sex cannot be married. And regardless of definition, they cannot reproduce on their own, one of God’s primary purposes for marriage.

Without God, man does what is right in his own eyes. So-called “progressive thinking” is simply man’s attempt, given his rejection of God, at better understanding the world and better addressing and solving its problems. Essentially, “anything goes” based upon the latest of ideas.

A biblical Christian, however, believes that God has designed, has created, and is very much involved in the universe … even in the individual lives of people who live in it. There are absolutes. There is a distinction between right and wrong. There are moral values and—something that we frequently forget in these modern times—there is an eternity ahead. As a result of progressive thinking, Darwinism now replaces Creationism, within much of our education system, students as well as teachers who profess faith in the God of the Bible are ridiculed and are otherwise discriminated against, millions of pre-born babies (the politically correct prefer calling them “fetuses”) have been legally dismembered, burnt, crushed, suctioned and pharmacologically murdered (aborted), and no-fault divorce has ravaged the families of our nation. Just look at those things that used to be considered wrong or evil which are now a normal part of our “progressing” society.

And what about eternity? Doesn’t that matter anymore, either?

In response to the Supreme Court’s ruling on gay marriage, then-President Barack Obama, clearly one of our nation’s more powerful, progressive thinkers, indicated his desire that “religious people” respond accordingly by modifying their definition of marriage as well. Believing in the God of the Bible as the Creator of the universe and as the One who designed and ordained marriage as a life-long covenant between one man and one woman, I respectfully decline Mr. Obama’s request. As the world in its own fashion deviates from the design and will of God, a true believer in Christ is called to follow Him. Jesus said, Enter through the narrow gate. For wide is the gate and broad is the road that leads to destruction, and many enter through it. But small is the gate and narrow the road that leads to life, and only a few find it. –Mat 7:13-14 NIV

I am Ted. I am a white male. I am a Christian who desires not to belittle, mock, or otherwise mistreat those with whom I may disagree, but there will be disagreements. I am called to love God and to love my neighbor as myself, regardless of who my neighbor might be. My ultimate hope is not found in this world. It is found in eternity with Christ. And my prayer for others is that they, too, may come to know Him, receive forgiveness of their sins, be transformed into the people God so desires, and spend an eternity with Him. This is not a popular message found in today’s liberal media. But for those who are interested, for those who are seeking something much better than what this world has to offer, God has an answer: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. –Joh 3:16

Jeg heter Ted. Jeg ble født som mann, og jeg vet at jeg er mann. Hudfargen min er hvit, og jeg vet at jeg er hvit. Foreldrene mine er hvite, besteforeldrene mine var hvite, og jeg har ingen grunn til å tro at de øvrige forfedrene mine var noe annet enn hvite. Dette er grunnleggende, uomtvistelige sannheter om meg selv. Jeg tror ikke at jeg er noe annet enn det jeg er. Jeg ønsker heller ikke å være noe annet enn det jeg er.

Jeg er kristen. For å definere troen min tydeligere – siden det er mange som bekjenner seg til kristendommen – er jeg en «bibeltro» kristen. Jeg tror at Bibelen er Guds ord, at den skal forstås bokstavelig, og at den gir anvisninger for et livsmønster og en livsførsel som alle troende bør slutte seg til. Da jeg var 24 år – etter å ha levd et liv etter eget forgodtbefinnende og mens jeg søkte Gud, som jeg ønsket å bli kjent med dersom han var virkelig – vendte jeg meg til ham, og jeg ble født på ny. Forvandlingen min til en ny skapning i Kristus begynte umiddelbart og pågår fremdeles. Min tro på og mitt forhold til Jesus Kristus er like grunnleggende og uomtvistelige som kjønnet og rasen min.

Jeg skriver som svar på det som hadde fått omfattende omtale i sekulære medier våren og sommeren 2015: en mann som angivelig gjennom hele livet hadde oppfattet seg selv som kvinne, og som hadde vært i ferd med å «skifte» kjønn; en hvit kvinne som hadde insistert på at rase er «flytende», og at hun er svart; og USAs høyesteretts omdefinering av ekteskapet, som også påvirket definisjonen av «familie» for en hel nasjon. Dette er temaer som rett og slett ikke kan bagatelliseres eller ignoreres på annen måte.

Den hvite kvinnen fikk liten offentlig støtte for sin forklaring på rase. Hun ble faktisk latterliggjort i betydelig grad for standpunktet sitt. Slik var det imidlertid ikke når det gjaldt kjønnsidentitet eller spørsmål om «homofilt» ekteskap og familie, og man må spørre seg hvorfor. Hvis andre kan godta en «genetisk/fysiologisk konstruert» mann som kvinne bare fordi det er det han mener han er, og hvis en mann kan «gifte seg» med en mann og en kvinne kan «gifte seg» med en kvinne og bli godtatt av andre som et ektepar under påskudd av like rettigheter og fordi det er det de ønsker å gjøre, hvorfor kan ikke en hvit kvinne godtas som svart kvinne når hun er overbevist om at hun er svart?

Spørsmålet som reises, handler om virkelighet. Selv om jeg skulle tro at jeg er tidenes største pianist og komponist, gir bevisene rett og slett ikke støtte til den overbevisningen. Selv om en hvit kvinne sier at hun er svart, gir bevisene heller ikke støtte til den overbevisningen. Det samme gjelder en mann som sier at han er kvinne. De genetiske og fysiologiske bevisene gir ikke støtte til den overbevisningen. Uten omdefineringen av ekteskapet kan to personer av samme kjønn ikke inngå ekteskap. Og uansett hvordan ekteskapet defineres, kan de ikke få barn på egen hånd, noe som er ett av Guds viktigste formål med ekteskapet.

Uten Gud gjør mennesket det som er rett i egne øyne. Såkalt «progressiv tenkning» er ganske enkelt menneskets forsøk, etter å ha forkastet Gud, på å forstå verden bedre og bedre håndtere og løse problemene dens. I bunn og grunn betyr det at «alt er tillatt», basert på de nyeste ideene.

En bibeltro kristen tror imidlertid at Gud har utformet og skapt universet, og at han er svært aktivt involvert i det … også i enkeltmenneskenes liv. Det finnes absolutte sannheter. Det finnes et skille mellom rett og galt. Det finnes moralske verdier, og – noe vi ofte glemmer i vår moderne tid – en evighet ligger foran oss. Som følge av progressiv tenkning har darwinismen nå erstattet kreasjonismen i store deler av utdanningssystemet vårt; elever så vel som lærere som bekjenner seg til troen på Bibelens Gud, blir latterliggjort og diskriminert på andre måter; millioner av ufødte barn (de politisk korrekte foretrekker å kalle dem «fostre») er blitt lovlig partert, brent, knust, sugd ut og drept med legemidler (abortert); og skilsmisse uten skyld har herjet familiene i landet vårt. Tenk bare på alt det som før ble regnet som galt eller ondt, men som nå er en normal del av vårt «fremskrittssamfunn».

Og hva med evigheten? Betyr ikke den noe lenger heller?

Som svar på Høyesteretts avgjørelse om homofilt ekteskap ga daværende president Barack Obama, som tydeligvis er en av landets mektigere progressive tenkere, uttrykk for at han ønsket at «religiøse mennesker» også skulle svare på en passende måte ved å endre sin definisjon av ekteskapet. Fordi jeg tror på Bibelens Gud som universets skaper og som den som utformet og innstiftet ekteskapet som en livslang pakt mellom én mann og én kvinne, avslår jeg respektfullt Obamas anmodning. Når verden på sin egen måte avviker fra Guds plan og vilje, er den som virkelig tror på Kristus, kalt til å følge ham. Jesus sa: Gå inn gjennom den trange port. For vid er porten og bred er veien som fører til fortapelsen, og mange går inn gjennom den. Men trang er porten og smal er veien som fører til livet, og få er de som finner den. – Matt 7:13–14 NIV

Jeg heter Ted. Jeg er en hvit mann. Jeg er kristen og ønsker ikke å nedvurdere, håne eller på annen måte behandle dem jeg måtte være uenig med, dårlig, men uenighet vil forekomme. Jeg er kalt til å elske Gud og elske min neste som meg selv, uansett hvem min neste måtte være. Mitt endelige håp finnes ikke i denne verden. Det finnes i evigheten sammen med Kristus. Og min bønn for andre er at også de må lære ham å kjenne, få tilgivelse for syndene sine, bli forvandlet til de menneskene Gud så inderlig ønsker at de skal være, og tilbringe evigheten sammen med ham. Dette er ikke et populært budskap i dagens liberale medier. Men for dem som er interessert, for dem som søker noe langt bedre enn det denne verden har å tilby, har Gud et svar: For så høyt har Gud elsket verden at han ga sin eneste Sønn, for at hver den som tror på ham, ikke skal gå fortapt, men ha evig liv. – Joh 3:16

And I sought for a man among them, that should make up the hedge, and stand in the gap before me for the land, that I should not destroy it: but I found none. –Ezekiel 22:30

The account of the little Dutch boy who heroically stuck his finger in the hole in the dike comes to mind as we consider such a verse. He couldn’t leave the spot for fear of erosion, so he waited the long night through until someone came along in the morning to rescue him from his plight. Many men have performed astounding feats on impulse when the moment so required. Lives were rescued, towns were saved, and enemies defeated because someone filled a role that was needed. Books are written, and monuments erected in honor of those whose benefaction has touched us. These are considered the heroes of history and they are remembered for their staunch bravery and steadfast faithfulness.

But the gaps in life are not always so obvious and the results not always measurable. Solomon informs us of the account of …a little city, and few men within it; and there came a great king against it, and besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it: Now there was found in it a poor wise man, and he by his wisdom delivered the city; yet no man remembered that same poor man. –Ecc 9:14-15. Though we have many thorough descriptions in the Bible of pious men who stood in the gap for God, there are, no doubt, hordes of others who overcame tremendous odds on a spiritual level yet received no recognition in this life.

The problem lies not so much in that, standing in the gap is beyond our capabilities or finances, but in the reality that often the job bears no title, ordination, or recognition. It is to be filled by volunteers with enough vision and care to sacrifice their own agenda for the sole cause of filling the hole in the hedge. It often does not lie within the realm of the physical, but within the borders of the spiritual. While the poor we have with us always and spiritual nobility will stoop to help them, we must consider that God probably has more in mind here than needing someone to organize bread lines and soup kitchens. He is looking for a man clad in a robe of “purple principles” that won’t be shed when the temperatures get hot.

King Darius signed the fateful degree that was designed to escort Daniel to a luncheon with the lions. Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime. –Dan 6:10. What a slight thing it would have been for Daniel to close the shutters before he prayed. But Daniel was not filling the gap by his presence in the high governmental position that he held. The gap lay in the dearth of godly witnesses in Babylon. Thus, the hole between heaven and earth was to be fulfilled by prayer at the open window while sacrificing his “seat in the senate.”

The underlying reason that so many gaps exist and there are so few men to fill them is because we often get our personal, earthly vision of circumstances confused with the eternal purposes of God. We are busily occupied with good things and feeling quite useful. Martha was zealously active in filling what she perceived as the imminent gap in the household, while Mary was sitting in the eternal one. It is incredibly easy to get caught up in the activity trap of a busy life. We may give intensive care to efficiently climb to the top of the ladder, only to discover that it is leaning against the wrong wall. Many people are very busy, but not very effective. Many have labored industriously for years in the Lord’s work, only to arrive at the finish line and realize that the things, which mattered most, had eluded them. Some, while giving their lives to serve others, allowed their marriage to suffer, or their children to disrespect them. Others have given “Corban” to their church while neglecting their relationship with their own parents.

The man in the gap must be wise, and wisdom must understand wherein the true gap lies. In this we must be driven by a purposed, biblical vision. Life will afford many opportunities to abandon our course. If we actively seek to live the expectations handed to us by our family, friends, associates, church agendas, and life’s circumstances, we will be driven by people rather than biblical principles. While this may seem legitimate on the surface, we may reap the bitter disappointment of finding ourselves dangling at the end of the wrong rope.

So, what does the gap of God’s concern look like? Some would say that this gap consists where any need arises. The poor we have with us always and certainly herein is an opportunity to do good. But the better part chosen by Mary had nothing to do with helping the poor or feeding the hungry. Likewise, the woman with the precious alabaster box of ointment of spikenard could have sold it and supplied the poor for quite a while with the sum of its value. But the real gap could not be filled by caressing the cripple, but by crowning the Christ. In the Garden of Eden there was no gap, for man walked in perfect harmony with his Creator. It was sin that created the gap and rankled the relationship. Also, there will be no breach at the end of time when the Lamb receives His bride. Until then, we have a large gap that exists because this earth refuses to glorify its Creator. To stand in that gap must be the chief purpose of all who aspire to bear His name.

This calls for a complete transformation in relationship to our God. The atonement of Christ’s blood makes it judicially possible. The comfort of the Holy Spirit makes it emotionally satisfying, but it is in the realm of our surrender and glorification of God that animates the scene. The Prodigal Son is a prime example of a soul who had brought a world of trouble upon himself by forsaking the position that he held as a son of his father. At the bottom of his restoration was nothing more than a re-establishing of the father-son relationship which had existed from his birth.

It appears to me that God is not so much looking for souls with their hands waving in the air shouting, “Here am I send me!” Rather His eyes search for the humble souls who bow their wills before the Almighty and recognize Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created. –Revelation 4:11. There is no lack for Sons of Sceva who imagine they are filling an important role in their willingness to broadcast the “Jesus” that they have heard of. In 1997, some 800,000 men arrived at a Promise Keepers rally in Washington D.C in response to the theme of “Standing in the Gap.” These men may have had good intentions of representing God to a nation in swift departure from spiritual underpinnings, but it takes more than just a willing heart. God doesn’t need of a large mass of bodies to stuff into a hole. He is looking for qualified men, and few have been promoted to such a position.

If all God wanted was men to show up at a rally or publicly proclaim their faith on the streets, He, no doubt, could have found many desiring such a good work. But to stand in the gap between God and the world will only be sanctioned by God for those who deserve to be there. It is the universal pride of man that drives man to believe that he must only desire to be useful and then he will be used. In God’s house there are some vessels to honor and some to dishonor, yet to deserve an honorable place is much more difficult than to desire one.

It is very common in our day to receive mail bearing the message, “Get the credit you deserve.” It is no secret that the credit that many deserve is zero credit. But we have all been impacted by the subliminal message that everybody deserves credit. Our society is promoting that all immoral, imprudent, and improvident people deserve the same care as the moral and industrious. If the slothful individual deserves a good wage and the spendthrift deserves financial security, then the Apostle Paul certainly has no right to lay any qualifications upon the widows who should receive support from the church. Neither has he any right to reject any sincere soul who desires the office of a Bishop, just because he does not meet the qualifications. But God noticed a few souls …in Sardis which have not defiled their garments; and they shall walk with me in white: for they are worthy. –Rev 3:4

These are men in the gap. Not because they had energy to burn, but because they had a vision for purity. This was no mere accident, for men who wish to attain to preeminence with God must do it by…

…Purpose

By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter; Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season; Esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt: for he had respect unto the recompence of the reward. By faith he forsook Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king: for he endured, as seeing him who is invisible. –Heb 11:24-27

A true vision for the work of God will come with a price tag. The rich young ruler would have loved to be a ruler in the kingdom of Christ as well as on his estate, but he couldn’t hold both. This principle provided the first hurdle for him and for everyone else who would desire such a noble work. As a young man, Moses made his decision and chose his loyalties. He was prepared to be rejected by Egypt, but he never dreamed he would also be so flippantly discarded by his own people.

It was forty years in the lonely furnace that purged his pride and pruned his prowess. There he graduated from the seminary of silence, equipped and prepared to stand in the gap as the meekest man on the face of the earth. He became an intercessor for men to God. As an advocate of men and of God, he preached and prayed, he walked and wept, he lived and loved his God and his brethren. All this while, he deemed himself inadequate for the position. While the children of Israel were at the very core of his heart, his fear and focus never left his God. When we seek to be respected by men, our purpose is clouded over and our position in the gap forfeited. Many good pastors, parents, and pilgrims have made this mistake and received their script from their wife, their children, their friends, or their church. Perhaps it seems like the loving, caring, and most respectful thing to do. But God requires absolute fidelity and there can be no compromise. What a man “wants to be” is driven by his visionary purpose, but what he “turns out to be” rests upon his…

…Priorities

This is a true saying, If a man desire the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work. A bishop then must be blameless, the husband of one wife, vigilant, sober, of good behaviour, given to hospitality, apt to teach; Not given to wine, no striker, not greedy of filthy lucre; but patient, not a brawler, not covetous; One that ruleth well his own house, having his children in subjection with all gravity; –1Ti 3:1-4. Our purpose forms our destination, but our priorities pave the road to get us there.

Unfortunately, some men are promoted to the ministry by popular opinion, but God chooses his men based upon their priorities and eternal qualifications. Men who are governed by their possessions, passions, or position will be useless to serve for God’s purpose. They love to be called Pastor, Reverend, or Father. They love to be esteemed as zealous, knowledgeable, steadfast, or compassionate. For am I now seeking the favor of men, or of God? Or am I striving to please men? If I were still pleasing men, I should not be a servant of Christ. –Gal 1:10 ASV

Fortunately, God is not a respecter of persons, and a stone fit for the wall will not be left in the way. The aged, the poor, the maimed, and the halt are all prime candidates for the position of filling the gap. Those with broken dreams, broken bodies, and broken hearts can stand unhindered in the hedge beside Noah, Abraham, Joseph, Moses, Daniel, Esther, Ruth and a countless battalion of others. These are all stellar representatives of God to this world. They all have turned their back on frivolity, fame, familiarity, and fortune and have become the heroes of heaven. They stand shoulder to shoulder in the hedge and form the “Embassy of the Eternal.” They loved, while others hated. They gave all, while others received. They were mocked and misunderstood, reviled and ridiculed, weary and weeping.

For we are unto God a sweet savour of Christ, in them that are saved, and in them that perish: To the one we are the savour of death unto death; and to the other the savour of life unto life. And who is sufficient for these things? –2 Co 2:15-16. Those whose sole purpose and priorities are governed by God.

«E busquei entre eles um homem que levantasse o muro e se pusesse na brecha diante de mim, em favor da terra, para que eu não a destruísse; mas não encontrei nenhum. –Ezequiel 22:30

A história do pequeno menino holandês que heroicamente enfiou o dedo no buraco do dique vem à mente quando consideramos um versículo como esse. Ele não podia sair dali, temendo a erosão, então passou a longa noite esperando, até que alguém apareceu pela manhã para livrá-lo de sua aflição. Muitos homens realizaram feitos extraordinários por impulso quando o momento assim exigiu. Vidas foram resgatadas, cidades foram salvas e inimigos foram derrotados porque alguém desempenhou um papel necessário. Livros são escritos e monumentos erguidos em honra daqueles cujo benefício nos tocou. Eles são considerados os heróis da história e são lembrados por sua firme coragem e fidelidade inabalável.

Mas as brechas da vida nem sempre são tão evidentes, e os resultados nem sempre são mensuráveis. Salomão nos relata a história de …uma pequena cidade, com poucos homens nela; e veio contra ela um grande rei, cercou-a e construiu grandes baluartes contra ela. Ora, havia nela um homem pobre e sábio, que por sua sabedoria livrou a cidade; contudo, ninguém se lembrou daquele homem pobre. –Ec 9:14-15. Embora a Bíblia nos ofereça muitas descrições detalhadas de homens piedosos que se puseram na brecha por Deus, sem dúvida há multidões de outros que venceram enormes desafios no plano espiritual e, ainda assim, não receberam reconhecimento nesta vida.

O problema não está tanto em que pôr-se na brecha esteja além de nossas capacidades ou recursos financeiros, mas no fato de que, muitas vezes, essa tarefa não tem título, ordenação nem reconhecimento. Ela deve ser realizada por voluntários com visão e dedicação suficientes para sacrificarem seus próprios planos pela única causa de tapar a brecha no muro. Muitas vezes, isso não pertence ao âmbito físico, mas aos limites do espiritual. Embora sempre tenhamos os pobres conosco, e a nobreza espiritual se disponha humildemente a ajudá-los, devemos considerar que provavelmente Deus tem em mente aqui algo além de precisar de alguém para organizar filas de distribuição de pão e refeitórios populares. Ele procura um homem vestido com um manto de «princípios púrpura» que não será despido quando as temperaturas subirem.

O rei Dario assinou o decreto fatídico destinado a levar Daniel a um almoço com os leões. Quando Daniel soube que o escrito estava assinado, entrou em sua casa e, com as janelas do seu quarto abertas na direção de Jerusalém, ajoelhou-se três vezes ao dia, orou e deu graças diante do seu Deus, como costumava fazer. –Dn 6:10. Que coisa insignificante teria sido Daniel fechar as persianas antes de orar! Mas Daniel não estava tapando a brecha apenas por sua presença no alto cargo governamental que ocupava. A brecha estava na escassez de testemunhas piedosas na Babilônia. Assim, a abertura entre o céu e a terra devia ser preenchida pela oração junto à janela aberta, enquanto ele sacrificava seu «assento no Senado».

A razão fundamental de existirem tantas brechas e tão poucos homens para tapá-las é que muitas vezes confundimos nossa visão pessoal e terrena das circunstâncias com os propósitos eternos de Deus. Estamos ocupados com coisas boas e nos sentimos bastante úteis. Marta agia com zelo para preencher aquilo que percebia como a necessidade iminente da casa, enquanto Maria estava sentada junto àquilo que era eterno. É incrivelmente fácil cair na armadilha da atividade de uma vida agitada. Podemos nos dedicar intensamente a subir com eficiência até o topo da escada, apenas para descobrir que ela está apoiada na parede errada. Muitas pessoas estão muito ocupadas, mas não são muito eficazes. Muitos trabalharam diligentemente durante anos na obra do Senhor, apenas para chegar à linha de chegada e perceber que as coisas mais importantes lhes escaparam. Alguns, ao dedicarem a vida ao serviço dos outros, deixaram o casamento sofrer ou permitiram que os filhos lhes faltassem ao respeito. Outros entregaram «Corbã» à sua igreja, negligenciando o relacionamento com os próprios pais.

O homem na brecha precisa ser sábio, e a sabedoria precisa compreender onde se encontra a verdadeira brecha. Nisso, devemos ser guiados por uma visão bíblica e determinada. A vida nos oferecerá muitas oportunidades para abandonarmos nosso rumo. Se buscarmos ativamente viver de acordo com as expectativas que nos são impostas por nossa família, nossos amigos, colegas, programas da igreja e circunstâncias da vida, seremos guiados por pessoas, e não por princípios bíblicos. Embora isso possa parecer legítimo à primeira vista, talvez colhamos a amarga decepção de nos vermos pendurados na ponta da corda errada.

Então, como é a brecha que preocupa a Deus? Alguns diriam que essa brecha aparece sempre que surge uma necessidade. Sempre temos os pobres conosco e, certamente, nisso há uma oportunidade de fazer o bem. Mas a melhor parte escolhida por Maria nada tinha a ver com ajudar os pobres ou alimentar os famintos. Da mesma forma, a mulher que possuía o precioso vaso de alabastro com perfume de nardo poderia tê-lo vendido e, com o valor obtido, sustentado os pobres por bastante tempo. Mas a brecha real não podia ser tapada acariciando o aleijado, mas coroando o Cristo. No Jardim do Éden não havia brecha, pois o homem vivia em perfeita harmonia com seu Criador. Foi o pecado que criou a brecha e perturbou o relacionamento. Também não haverá ruptura no fim dos tempos, quando o Cordeiro receber sua noiva. Até lá, há uma grande brecha, que existe porque esta terra se recusa a glorificar seu Criador. Pôr-se nessa brecha deve ser o propósito principal de todos os que aspiram a levar o nome dele.

Isso exige uma transformação completa em nosso relacionamento com Deus. A expiação pelo sangue de Cristo torna isso judicialmente possível. O consolo do Espírito Santo torna isso emocionalmente satisfatório, mas é no âmbito da nossa rendição e da glorificação de Deus que a cena ganha vida. O Filho Pródigo é um exemplo notável de uma alma que trouxe sobre si um mundo de problemas ao abandonar a posição que ocupava como filho de seu pai. Na base de sua restauração estava nada mais que o restabelecimento do relacionamento entre pai e filho que existia desde o seu nascimento.

Parece-me que Deus não está tanto à procura de almas que agitem as mãos no ar e gritem: «Eis-me aqui, envia-me!» Em vez disso, seus olhos procuram as almas humildes que submetem sua vontade diante do Todo-Poderoso e reconhecem: «Digno és, Senhor, de receber glória, honra e poder, porque criaste todas as coisas, e por tua vontade elas existem e foram criadas.» –Apocalipse 4:11. Não faltam filhos de Ceva que imaginam estar desempenhando um papel importante ao se disporem a anunciar o «Jesus» de quem ouviram falar. Em 1997, cerca de 800 mil homens chegaram a um encontro dos Promise Keepers em Washington, D.C., em resposta ao tema «Pôr-se na brecha». Esses homens talvez tivessem boas intenções ao representar Deus perante uma nação que se afastava rapidamente de seus fundamentos espirituais, mas é preciso mais do que um coração disposto. Deus não precisa de uma grande massa de corpos para enfiar numa brecha. Ele procura homens qualificados, e poucos foram promovidos a tal posição.

Se tudo o que Deus quisesse fosse que homens comparecessem a um encontro ou proclamassem publicamente sua fé nas ruas, sem dúvida poderia encontrar muitos desejosos de realizar uma boa obra desse tipo. Mas pôr-se na brecha entre Deus e o mundo só será autorizado por Deus para aqueles que merecem estar ali. É o orgulho universal do homem que o leva a acreditar que basta desejar ser útil para então ser usado. Na casa de Deus, há vasos para honra e vasos para desonra; no entanto, merecer um lugar honroso é muito mais difícil do que desejá-lo.

Em nossos dias, é muito comum receber correspondência com a mensagem: «Receba o reconhecimento que merece». Não é segredo que o reconhecimento que muitos merecem é nenhum. Mas todos fomos influenciados pela mensagem subliminar de que todos merecem reconhecimento. Nossa sociedade promove a ideia de que todas as pessoas imorais, imprudentes e imprevidentes merecem o mesmo cuidado que as pessoas morais e trabalhadoras. Se o indivíduo preguiçoso merece um bom salário e o gastador merece segurança financeira, então o apóstolo Paulo certamente não tem o direito de impor qualificações às viúvas que devem receber ajuda da igreja. Tampouco tem o direito de rejeitar qualquer alma sincera que deseje o cargo de bispo, apenas por não cumprir os requisitos. Mas Deus observou algumas almas …em Sardes que não contaminaram suas vestes; e andarão comigo vestidas de branco, pois são dignas. –Ap 3:4

Esses são homens na brecha. Não porque tivessem energia de sobra, mas porque tinham uma visão de pureza. Isso não foi mero acaso, pois os homens que desejam alcançar preeminência diante de Deus precisam fazê-lo por meio de…

…Propósito

Pela fé, Moisés, sendo já adulto, recusou ser chamado filho da filha de Faraó, escolhendo antes ser maltratado com o povo de Deus do que desfrutar por algum tempo os prazeres do pecado, considerando o opróbrio de Cristo riqueza maior do que os tesouros do Egito, pois tinha em vista a recompensa. Pela fé, abandonou o Egito, não temendo a ira do rei, pois perseverou como quem vê aquele que é invisível. –Hb 11:24-27

Uma verdadeira visão da obra de Deus virá com um preço. O jovem rico teria adorado ser governante no reino de Cristo e também em sua propriedade, mas não podia ficar com os dois. Esse princípio foi o primeiro obstáculo para ele e para todos os outros que desejariam uma obra tão nobre. Ainda jovem, Moisés tomou sua decisão e escolheu a quem seria leal. Estava preparado para ser rejeitado pelo Egito, mas jamais imaginou que seria também tão levianamente descartado pelo próprio povo.

Foram quarenta anos na fornalha solitária que purificaram seu orgulho e podaram sua capacidade. Ali, concluiu o seminário do silêncio, equipado e preparado para se pôr na brecha como o homem mais manso da face da terra. Tornou-se intercessor dos homens diante de Deus. Como defensor dos homens e de Deus, pregava e orava, caminhava e chorava, vivia e amava seu Deus e seus irmãos. Durante todo esse tempo, considerava-se inadequado para a posição. Embora os filhos de Israel estivessem no âmago de seu coração, seu temor e sua atenção nunca se afastaram de Deus. Quando procuramos ser respeitados pelos homens, nosso propósito fica obscurecido e perdemos nossa posição na brecha. Muitos bons pastores, pais e peregrinos cometeram esse erro e receberam suas orientações da esposa, dos filhos, dos amigos ou da igreja. Talvez pareça a atitude mais amorosa, atenciosa e respeitosa. Mas Deus exige fidelidade absoluta, e não pode haver concessões. Aquilo que um homem «quer ser» é determinado por seu propósito visionário, mas aquilo em que ele «acaba se tornando» depende de suas…

…Prioridades

Esta é uma palavra fiel: se alguém deseja o episcopado, deseja uma boa obra. É necessário, pois, que o bispo seja irrepreensível, marido de uma só mulher, vigilante, sóbrio, de bom comportamento, hospitaleiro, apto para ensinar; não dado ao vinho, não violento, não ávido de lucro desonesto, mas moderado, não briguento, não avarento; que governe bem a própria casa e mantenha os filhos em sujeição, com toda a dignidade; –1Tm 3:1-4. Nosso propósito determina nosso destino, mas são nossas prioridades que pavimentam o caminho até lá.

Infelizmente, alguns homens são promovidos ao ministério pela opinião popular, mas Deus escolhe seus homens com base em suas prioridades e qualificações eternas. Homens governados por suas posses, paixões ou posição serão inúteis para servir ao propósito de Deus. Gostam de ser chamados de Pastor, Reverendo ou Pai. Gostam de ser considerados zelosos, sábios, firmes ou compassivos. Porventura, procuro agora o favor dos homens ou o de Deus? Ou procuro agradar aos homens? Se ainda estivesse agradando aos homens, não seria servo de Cristo. –Gl 1:10 ASV

Felizmente, Deus não faz acepção de pessoas, e uma pedra adequada para o muro não será deixada de lado. Os idosos, os pobres, os mutilados e os coxos são todos candidatos ideais para preencher a brecha. Os que têm sonhos desfeitos, corpos feridos e corações partidos podem pôr-se sem impedimentos na brecha ao lado de Noé, Abraão, José, Moisés, Daniel, Ester, Rute e um incontável batalhão de outros. Todos eles são representantes notáveis de Deus para este mundo. Deram as costas à frivolidade, à fama, à familiaridade e à fortuna, e tornaram-se heróis do céu. Permanecem ombro a ombro na brecha e formam a «Embaixada do Eterno». Amaram enquanto outros odiaram. Deram tudo enquanto outros receberam. Foram escarnecidos e incompreendidos, insultados e ridicularizados, cansados e chorosos.

Porque somos para Deus o bom perfume de Cristo, entre os que se salvam e entre os que se perdem: para estes, cheiro de morte para morte; para aqueles, cheiro de vida para vida. E quem é suficiente para estas coisas? –2Co 2:15-16. São aqueles cujo único propósito e cujas prioridades são governados por Deus.

I am Ted. I was born a male and I know I am a male. My skin color is white, and I know I am white. My parents are white, my grandparents were white, and I have no reason to suspect my other ancestors were anything other than white. These are foundational, irrefutable truths about myself. I do not think I am anything other than what I am. Nor do I desire to be anything other than what I am.

I am a Christian. In order to better define my faith—as there are many who profess Christianity—I am a “biblical” Christian. I believe that the Bible is the Word of God, that it is to be taken literally, and that it instructs a pattern and way of life that all believers should embrace. At the age of 24—after having lived a life of my own choosing and while searching for God who, if He was real, I wanted to know—I turned to Him and I was born again. My transformation as a new creation in Christ began immediately and it continues to this day. My faith in and relationship to Jesus Christ are as foundational and irrefutable as my gender and race.

I am writing in response to that which had been extensively covered by the secular media during the Spring and Summer of 2015: a man who reportedly, throughout his life, had considered himself a female and who had been “transitioning” into a woman; a white woman who had insisted that race is “fluid” and that she is black; and the redefinition of marriage by the Supreme Court of the United States of America affecting, as well, the definition of “family” for an entire nation. These are topics which simply cannot be minimized or otherwise ignored.

The white woman lacked much public support for her explanation of race. In fact, she was significantly ridiculed for her stance. This was not true, however, regarding gender identification or “gay” marriage and family issues, and one must wonder why. If a “genetically/physiologically-constructed” male can be accepted by others as a woman simply because that’s what he thinks he is, and if a man can “marry” a man and a woman can “marry” a woman and be accepted as a married couple by others under the premise of equal rights and because that’s what they want to do, why can’t a white woman be accepted as a black woman when she is convinced that she is black?

The question raised is one of reality. Even though I may think I am the greatest pianist and music composer of all times, the evidence simply does not support that conviction. Even though a white woman says she is black, the evidence likewise does not support that conviction. Also true is that of a man who says he is a woman. The genetic and physiological evidence does not support that conviction. Without the redefinition of marriage, two people of the same sex cannot be married. And regardless of definition, they cannot reproduce on their own, one of God’s primary purposes for marriage.

Without God, man does what is right in his own eyes. So-called “progressive thinking” is simply man’s attempt, given his rejection of God, at better understanding the world and better addressing and solving its problems. Essentially, “anything goes” based upon the latest of ideas.

A biblical Christian, however, believes that God has designed, has created, and is very much involved in the universe … even in the individual lives of people who live in it. There are absolutes. There is a distinction between right and wrong. There are moral values and—something that we frequently forget in these modern times—there is an eternity ahead. As a result of progressive thinking, Darwinism now replaces Creationism, within much of our education system, students as well as teachers who profess faith in the God of the Bible are ridiculed and are otherwise discriminated against, millions of pre-born babies (the politically correct prefer calling them “fetuses”) have been legally dismembered, burnt, crushed, suctioned and pharmacologically murdered (aborted), and no-fault divorce has ravaged the families of our nation. Just look at those things that used to be considered wrong or evil which are now a normal part of our “progressing” society.

And what about eternity? Doesn’t that matter anymore, either?

In response to the Supreme Court’s ruling on gay marriage, then-President Barack Obama, clearly one of our nation’s more powerful, progressive thinkers, indicated his desire that “religious people” respond accordingly by modifying their definition of marriage as well. Believing in the God of the Bible as the Creator of the universe and as the One who designed and ordained marriage as a life-long covenant between one man and one woman, I respectfully decline Mr. Obama’s request. As the world in its own fashion deviates from the design and will of God, a true believer in Christ is called to follow Him. Jesus said, Enter through the narrow gate. For wide is the gate and broad is the road that leads to destruction, and many enter through it. But small is the gate and narrow the road that leads to life, and only a few find it. –Mat 7:13-14 NIV

I am Ted. I am a white male. I am a Christian who desires not to belittle, mock, or otherwise mistreat those with whom I may disagree, but there will be disagreements. I am called to love God and to love my neighbor as myself, regardless of who my neighbor might be. My ultimate hope is not found in this world. It is found in eternity with Christ. मैं टेड हूँ। मेरा जन्म पुरुष के रूप में हुआ और मैं जानता हूँ कि मैं पुरुष हूँ। मेरी त्वचा का रंग गोरा है और मैं जानता हूँ कि मैं गोरा हूँ। मेरे माता-पिता गोरे हैं, मेरे दादा-दादी गोरे थे, और मेरे पास यह संदेह करने का कोई कारण नहीं है कि मेरे अन्य पूर्वज गोरे के अलावा कुछ और थे। ये अपने बारे में बुनियादी, अकाट्य सत्य हैं। मैं यह नहीं सोचता कि मैं जो हूँ, उससे कुछ और हूँ। न ही मेरी इच्छा है कि मैं जो हूँ, उससे कुछ और बनूँ।

मैं एक ईसाई हूँ। अपने विश्वास को बेहतर ढंग से परिभाषित करने के लिए—क्योंकि बहुत से लोग ईसाई होने का दावा करते हैं—मैं एक “बाइबिल-आधारित” ईसाई हूँ। मेरा विश्वास है कि बाइबल परमेश्वर का वचन है, कि उसे शाब्दिक रूप से लिया जाना चाहिए, और यह जीवन की ऐसी रीति और शैली सिखाती है जिसे सभी विश्वासियों को अपनाना चाहिए। 24 वर्ष की आयु में—अपनी मर्ज़ी से जीवन बिताने के बाद और उस परमेश्वर की खोज करते हुए, जिसे यदि वह सचमुच है तो मैं जानना चाहता था—मैं उसकी ओर मुड़ा और नए सिरे से जन्मा। मसीह में नई सृष्टि के रूप में मेरा रूपांतरण तुरंत शुरू हुआ और आज तक जारी है। यीशु मसीह में मेरा विश्वास और उनके साथ मेरा संबंध मेरे लिंग और नस्ल जितने ही बुनियादी और अकाट्य हैं।

मैं उस विषय पर प्रतिक्रिया में लिख रहा हूँ जिस पर 2015 की वसंत और गर्मियों के दौरान धर्मनिरपेक्ष मीडिया में व्यापक रूप से चर्चा हुई थी: एक ऐसा पुरुष जिसने कथित तौर पर जीवन भर स्वयं को स्त्री माना था और जो स्त्री बनने के लिए “संक्रमण” कर रहा था; एक गोरी महिला जिसने ज़ोर देकर कहा था कि नस्ल “लचीली” है और वह अश्वेत है; तथा संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका के सर्वोच्च न्यायालय द्वारा विवाह की पुनर्परिभाषा, जिसने पूरे देश के लिए “परिवार” की परिभाषा को भी प्रभावित किया। ये ऐसे विषय हैं जिन्हें किसी भी तरह कम करके नहीं आँका जा सकता या अनदेखा नहीं किया जा सकता।

गोरी महिला को नस्ल के बारे में उसकी व्याख्या के लिए बहुत कम सार्वजनिक समर्थन मिला। वास्तव में, उसके रुख के लिए उसका काफ़ी मज़ाक उड़ाया गया। लेकिन लिंग-पहचान या “समलैंगिक” विवाह और परिवार के मुद्दों के मामले में ऐसा नहीं हुआ, और यह सोचने की बात है कि क्यों। यदि “आनुवंशिक/शारीरिक रूप से निर्मित” पुरुष को दूसरे लोग केवल इसलिए स्त्री के रूप में स्वीकार कर सकते हैं कि वह स्वयं को वैसा समझता है, और यदि समान अधिकारों के आधार पर तथा इसलिए कि वे ऐसा करना चाहते हैं, एक पुरुष दूसरे पुरुष से “विवाह” कर सकता है और एक महिला दूसरी महिला से “विवाह” कर सकती है और दूसरे उन्हें विवाहित जोड़े के रूप में स्वीकार कर सकते हैं, तो किसी गोरी महिला को अश्वेत महिला के रूप में क्यों स्वीकार नहीं किया जा सकता, जबकि उसे पूरा विश्वास है कि वह अश्वेत है?

यहाँ उठाया गया प्रश्न वास्तविकता का है। भले ही मैं सोचूँ कि मैं अब तक का सबसे महान पियानोवादक और संगीतकार हूँ, प्रमाण उस विश्वास का समर्थन नहीं करते। भले ही कोई गोरी महिला कहे कि वह अश्वेत है, प्रमाण उसी तरह उस विश्वास का समर्थन नहीं करते। यही बात उस पुरुष के बारे में भी सच है जो कहता है कि वह स्त्री है। आनुवंशिक और शारीरिक प्रमाण उस विश्वास का समर्थन नहीं करते। विवाह की पुनर्परिभाषा के बिना, समान लिंग के दो लोगों का विवाह नहीं हो सकता। और परिभाषा चाहे जो हो, वे अपने आप संतान उत्पन्न नहीं कर सकते—जो विवाह के लिए परमेश्वर के प्रमुख उद्देश्यों में से एक है।

परमेश्वर के बिना, मनुष्य वही करता है जो उसकी अपनी दृष्टि में सही है। तथाकथित “प्रगतिशील सोच” दरअसल परमेश्वर को अस्वीकार करने के बाद मनुष्य का दुनिया को बेहतर ढंग से समझने और उसकी समस्याओं का बेहतर समाधान करने का प्रयास है। मूलतः, नवीनतम विचारों के आधार पर “सब कुछ चलता है।”

लेकिन एक बाइबिल-आधारित ईसाई विश्वास करता है कि परमेश्वर ने ब्रह्मांड की रूपरेखा बनाई है, उसे रचा है और उसमें पूरी तरह सक्रिय हैं… यहाँ तक कि उसमें रहने वाले लोगों के व्यक्तिगत जीवन में भी। कुछ बातें निरपेक्ष हैं। सही और गलत में अंतर है। नैतिक मूल्य हैं और—ऐसी बात जिसे हम इन आधुनिक समयों में अक्सर भूल जाते हैं—आगे अनंतकाल है। प्रगतिशील सोच के परिणामस्वरूप, हमारी शिक्षा-व्यवस्था के बड़े हिस्से में सृष्टिवाद की जगह अब डार्विनवाद ने ले ली है; बाइबल के परमेश्वर में विश्वास का दावा करने वाले विद्यार्थियों और शिक्षकों का मज़ाक उड़ाया जाता है और उनके साथ अन्य प्रकार का भेदभाव किया जाता है; लाखों अजन्मे शिशुओं को (राजनीतिक रूप से सही भाषा पसंद करने वाले उन्हें “भ्रूण” कहना पसंद करते हैं) कानूनी रूप से अंग-भंग करके, जलाकर, कुचलकर, चूषण द्वारा और औषधियों से मार डाला गया है (गर्भपात); और बिना किसी दोष के तलाक ने हमारे देश के परिवारों को तहस-नहस कर दिया है। ज़रा उन बातों को देखिए जिन्हें पहले गलत या बुरा माना जाता था, लेकिन जो अब हमारे “प्रगतिशील” समाज का सामान्य हिस्सा बन चुकी हैं।

और अनंतकाल का क्या? क्या अब उसका भी कोई महत्व नहीं रहा?

समलैंगिक विवाह पर सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के फैसले के जवाब में, तत्कालीन राष्ट्रपति बराक ओबामा—जो स्पष्ट रूप से हमारे देश के अधिक शक्तिशाली प्रगतिशील विचारकों में से एक हैं—ने इच्छा जताई कि “धार्मिक लोग” भी विवाह की अपनी परिभाषा में बदलाव करके उसी के अनुरूप प्रतिक्रिया दें। बाइबल के परमेश्वर को ब्रह्मांड का सृष्टिकर्ता और उस सत्ता के रूप में मानते हुए जिसने विवाह की रचना की और उसे एक पुरुष और एक स्त्री के बीच जीवनभर के वाचा-संबंध के रूप में स्थापित किया, मैं श्री ओबामा के अनुरोध को सम्मानपूर्वक अस्वीकार करता हूँ। जिस तरह दुनिया अपने ढंग से परमेश्वर की रूपरेखा और इच्छा से भटकती है, मसीह के सच्चे विश्वासी को उनका अनुसरण करने के लिए बुलाया गया है। यीशु ने कहा, सँकरे फाटक से प्रवेश करो। क्योंकि चौड़ा है वह फाटक और विस्तृत है वह मार्ग जो विनाश की ओर ले जाता है, और बहुत से लोग उससे प्रवेश करते हैं। परन्तु छोटा है वह फाटक और सँकरा है वह मार्ग जो जीवन की ओर ले जाता है, और थोड़े ही लोग उसे पाते हैं। –मत्ती 7:13-14 एनआईवी

मैं टेड हूँ। मैं गोरा पुरुष हूँ। मैं एक ईसाई हूँ, और मेरी इच्छा है कि जिन लोगों से मेरा मतभेद हो, उन्हें नीचा न दिखाऊँ, उनका मज़ाक न उड़ाऊँ और उनके साथ किसी भी तरह दुर्व्यवहार न करूँ; फिर भी मतभेद होंगे। मुझे परमेश्वर से प्रेम करने और अपने पड़ोसी से अपने समान प्रेम करने के लिए बुलाया गया है, चाहे मेरा पड़ोसी कोई भी हो। मेरी अंतिम आशा इस संसार में नहीं है। वह मसीह के साथ अनंतकाल में है। और दूसरों के लिए मेरी प्रार्थना है कि वे भी उन्हें जान पाएँ, अपने पापों की क्षमा पाएँ, उन लोगों में रूपांतरित हों जैसा परमेश्वर उन्हें बनाना चाहता है, और उनके साथ अनंतकाल बिताएँ। आज के उदारवादी मीडिया में यह लोकप्रिय संदेश नहीं है। लेकिन जो लोग रुचि रखते हैं, जो इस संसार की पेशकश से कहीं बेहतर कुछ खोज रहे हैं, उनके लिए परमेश्वर के पास एक उत्तर है: क्योंकि परमेश्वर ने जगत से ऐसा प्रेम किया कि उसने अपना एकलौता पुत्र दे दिया, ताकि जो कोई उस पर विश्वास करे, वह नष्ट न हो, बल्कि अनन्त जीवन पाए। –यूहन्ना 3:16
