I am Ted. I was born a male and I know I am a male. My skin color is white, and I know I am white. My parents are white, my grandparents were white, and I have no reason to suspect my other ancestors were anything other than white. These are foundational, irrefutable truths about myself. I do not think I am anything other than what I am. Nor do I desire to be anything other than what I am.

I am a Christian. In order to better define my faith—as there are many who profess Christianity—I am a “biblical” Christian. I believe that the Bible is the Word of God, that it is to be taken literally, and that it instructs a pattern and way of life that all believers should embrace. At the age of 24—after having lived a life of my own choosing and while searching for God who, if He was real, I wanted to know—I turned to Him and I was born again. My transformation as a new creation in Christ began immediately and it continues to this day. My faith in and relationship to Jesus Christ are as foundational and irrefutable as my gender and race.

I am writing in response to that which had been extensively covered by the secular media during the Spring and Summer of 2015: a man who reportedly, throughout his life, had considered himself a female and who had been “transitioning” into a woman; a white woman who had insisted that race is “fluid” and that she is black; and the redefinition of marriage by the Supreme Court of the United States of America affecting, as well, the definition of “family” for an entire nation. These are topics which simply cannot be minimized or otherwise ignored.

The white woman lacked much public support for her explanation of race. In fact, she was significantly ridiculed for her stance. This was not true, however, regarding gender identification or “gay” marriage and family issues, and one must wonder why. If a “genetically/physiologically-constructed” male can be accepted by others as a woman simply because that’s what he thinks he is, and if a man can “marry” a man and a woman can “marry” a woman and be accepted as a married couple by others under the premise of equal rights and because that’s what they want to do, why can’t a white woman be accepted as a black woman when she is convinced that she is black?

The question raised is one of reality. Even though I may think I am the greatest pianist and music composer of all times, the evidence simply does not support that conviction. Even though a white woman says she is black, the evidence likewise does not support that conviction. Also true is that of a man who says he is a woman. The genetic and physiological evidence does not support that conviction. Without the redefinition of marriage, two people of the same sex cannot be married. And regardless of definition, they cannot reproduce on their own, one of God’s primary purposes for marriage.

Without God, man does what is right in his own eyes. So-called “progressive thinking” is simply man’s attempt, given his rejection of God, at better understanding the world and better addressing and solving its problems. Essentially, “anything goes” based upon the latest of ideas.

A biblical Christian, however, believes that God has designed, has created, and is very much involved in the universe … even in the individual lives of people who live in it. There are absolutes. There is a distinction between right and wrong. There are moral values and—something that we frequently forget in these modern times—there is an eternity ahead. As a result of progressive thinking, Darwinism now replaces Creationism, within much of our education system, students as well as teachers who profess faith in the God of the Bible are ridiculed and are otherwise discriminated against, millions of pre-born babies (the politically correct prefer calling them “fetuses”) have been legally dismembered, burnt, crushed, suctioned and pharmacologically murdered (aborted), and no-fault divorce has ravaged the families of our nation. Just look at those things that used to be considered wrong or evil which are now a normal part of our “progressing” society.

And what about eternity? Doesn’t that matter anymore, either?

In response to the Supreme Court’s ruling on gay marriage, then-President Barack Obama, clearly one of our nation’s more powerful, progressive thinkers, indicated his desire that “religious people” respond accordingly by modifying their definition of marriage as well. Believing in the God of the Bible as the Creator of the universe and as the One who designed and ordained marriage as a life-long covenant between one man and one woman, I respectfully decline Mr. Obama’s request. As the world in its own fashion deviates from the design and will of God, a true believer in Christ is called to follow Him. Jesus said, Enter through the narrow gate. For wide is the gate and broad is the road that leads to destruction, and many enter through it. But small is the gate and narrow the road that leads to life, and only a few find it. –Mat 7:13-14 NIV

I am Ted. I am a white male. I am a Christian who desires not to belittle, mock, or otherwise mistreat those with whom I may disagree, but there will be disagreements. I am called to love God and to love my neighbor as myself, regardless of who my neighbor might be. My ultimate hope is not found in this world. It is found in eternity with Christ. And my prayer for others is that they, too, may come to know Him, receive forgiveness of their sins, be transformed into the people God so desires, and spend an eternity with Him. This is not a popular message found in today’s liberal media. But for those who are interested, for those who are seeking something much better than what this world has to offer, God has an answer: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. –Joh 3:16

Sou Ted. Nasci do sexo masculino e sei que sou do sexo masculino. Minha cor de pele é branca, e sei que sou branco. Meus pais são brancos, meus avós eram brancos, e não tenho razão para suspeitar que meus outros ancestrais fossem algo diferente de brancos. Essas são verdades fundamentais e irrefutáveis sobre mim. Não acho que sou algo diferente do que sou. Tampouco desejo ser algo diferente do que sou.

Sou cristão. Para definir melhor minha fé — já que muitos professam o cristianismo —, sou um cristão “bíblico”. Creio que a Bíblia é a Palavra de Deus, que deve ser interpretada literalmente e que ensina um padrão e um modo de vida que todos os fiéis devem abraçar. Aos 24 anos — depois de ter vivido uma vida segundo minhas próprias escolhas e enquanto buscava a Deus, que, se fosse real, eu queria conhecer — voltei-me para Ele e nasci de novo. Minha transformação em uma nova criatura em Cristo começou imediatamente e continua até hoje. Minha fé em Jesus Cristo e meu relacionamento com Ele são tão fundamentais e irrefutáveis quanto meu gênero e minha raça.

Escrevo em resposta ao que foi amplamente abordado pela mídia secular durante a primavera e o verão de 2015: um homem que, segundo relatos, ao longo da vida se considerara mulher e que estava “fazendo a transição” para se tornar mulher; uma mulher branca que insistia que a raça é “fluida” e que ela é negra; e a redefinição do casamento pela Suprema Corte dos Estados Unidos da América, que também afetou a definição de “família” para uma nação inteira. São temas que simplesmente não podem ser minimizados nem ignorados de outra forma.

A mulher branca não recebeu muito apoio público para sua explicação sobre raça. Na verdade, sua posição foi muito ridicularizada. Isso não ocorreu, porém, no caso da identificação de gênero ou das questões relativas ao casamento “gay” e à família, e é preciso perguntar por quê. Se um homem “construído geneticamente/fisiologicamente” pode ser aceito pelos outros como mulher simplesmente porque é isso que pensa ser, e se um homem pode “casar-se” com um homem e uma mulher pode “casar-se” com uma mulher, sendo aceitos pelos outros como um casal casado sob a premissa da igualdade de direitos e porque é isso que querem fazer, por que uma mulher branca não pode ser aceita como mulher negra quando está convencida de que é negra?

A questão levantada é a da realidade. Ainda que eu pense ser o maior pianista e compositor musical de todos os tempos, as evidências simplesmente não sustentam essa convicção. Ainda que uma mulher branca diga que é negra, as evidências tampouco sustentam essa convicção. O mesmo vale para um homem que diz ser mulher. As evidências genéticas e fisiológicas não sustentam essa convicção. Sem a redefinição do casamento, duas pessoas do mesmo sexo não podem se casar. E, independentemente da definição, não podem procriar por conta própria, um dos propósitos primordiais de Deus para o casamento.

Sem Deus, o homem faz o que lhe parece certo. O chamado “pensamento progressista” é simplesmente a tentativa do homem, dado que rejeita a Deus, de compreender melhor o mundo e de abordar e solucionar melhor seus problemas. Em essência, “vale tudo”, com base nas ideias mais recentes.

Um cristão bíblico, porém, acredita que Deus projetou e criou o universo e está muito envolvido nele … até mesmo na vida individual das pessoas que nele vivem. Há absolutos. Há uma distinção entre o certo e o errado. Há valores morais e — algo que frequentemente esquecemos nestes tempos modernos — há uma eternidade pela frente. Como resultado do pensamento progressista, o darwinismo agora substitui o criacionismo; em grande parte do nosso sistema educacional, alunos e professores que professam fé no Deus da Bíblia são ridicularizados e também discriminados; milhões de bebês ainda não nascidos (os politicamente corretos preferem chamá-los de “fetos”) foram legalmente desmembrados, queimados, esmagados, aspirados e assassinados farmacologicamente (abortados); e o divórcio sem culpa devastou as famílias de nossa nação. Basta olhar para aquilo que costumava ser considerado errado ou mau e que agora é parte normal da nossa sociedade “em progresso”.

E quanto à eternidade? Isso também já não importa?

Em resposta à decisão da Suprema Corte sobre o casamento gay, o então presidente Barack Obama, claramente um dos pensadores progressistas mais poderosos de nossa nação, manifestou o desejo de que as “pessoas religiosas” respondessem de acordo, modificando também sua definição de casamento. Crendo no Deus da Bíblia como Criador do universo e como Aquele que projetou e instituiu o casamento como uma aliança para toda a vida entre um homem e uma mulher, declino respeitosamente do pedido do Sr. Obama. À medida que o mundo, à sua maneira, se afasta do desígnio e da vontade de Deus, o verdadeiro crente em Cristo é chamado a segui-Lo. Jesus disse: Entrem pela porta estreita. Pois larga é a porta e amplo o caminho que leva à destruição, e muitos entram por ele. Mas estreita é a porta e apertado o caminho que leva à vida, e poucos o encontram. –Mt 7:13-14 NVI

Sou Ted. Sou um homem branco. Sou cristão e desejo não menosprezar, ridicularizar nem maltratar de outra forma aqueles de quem posso discordar, mas haverá discordâncias. Sou chamado a amar a Deus e a amar o próximo como a mim mesmo, seja quem for meu próximo. Minha esperança definitiva não está neste mundo. Está na eternidade com Cristo. E minha oração pelos outros é que também venham a conhecê-Lo, recebam o perdão de seus pecados, sejam transformados nas pessoas que Deus tanto deseja que sejam e passem a eternidade com Ele. Essa não é uma mensagem popular na mídia liberal de hoje. Mas, para os interessados, para os que buscam algo muito melhor do que aquilo que este mundo tem a oferecer, Deus tem uma resposta: Porque Deus amou tanto o mundo que deu o seu Filho unigênito, para que todo aquele que nele crê não pereça, mas tenha a vida eterna. –Jo 3:16

I thought the tank was almost full when we left home, and… Oh no!” wailed Carol again. “Dad put the cell phone on the counter for me to take along, and I forgot that also!”

This seems almost impossible to me!” she mournfully uttered from the back seat.

As the girls lapsed into silence, the old Chevy seemed to shake in protest as a long row of trucks whizzed by. “You know,” said Gloria, “I was just remembering Brother Lester’s message this evening. Makes the trusting heart His home.

Milla tras milla pasaba velozmente mientras Carol conducía el viejo Chevy por la concurrida autopista interestatal rumbo a casa. Entre momentos de silencio y conversación, Carol y sus dos hermanas, Elaine y Gloria, alzaban la voz en canto, dando gracias y alabanzas a su Creador. ¡Qué agradecidas estaban por la oportunidad de pasar la velada con sus amigos en la iglesia de Pine Creek y recibir otro mensaje inspirador de la Palabra de Dios!

De pronto, su viaje tranquilo se vio interrumpido por señales de problemas. «¿Qué puede estar pasando ahora con este auto?», dijo Carol preocupada mientras llevaba el auto detenido al borde de la carretera. «¡Ay, no, chicas, nos hemos quedado sin gasolina! Esta tarde tenía tanta prisa que olvidé revisar el indicador. Pensé que el tanque estaba casi lleno cuando salimos de casa, y… ¡Ay, no!», volvió a lamentarse Carol. «Papá dejó el teléfono celular sobre el mostrador para que me lo llevara, ¡y también me olvidé de eso!»

«¿Y ahora qué vamos a hacer?», exclamó Elaine. «¡Aquí estamos, varadas en la oscuridad, sin gasolina, sin teléfono y a siete millas de nuestra salida! Y otra cosa: hoy en día la gente no se detiene rápidamente para ofrecer ayuda. Saben que casi todo el mundo lleva un teléfono. ¡Esto me parece casi imposible!», dijo con tristeza desde el asiento trasero.

Cuando las chicas guardaron silencio, el viejo Chevy pareció sacudirse en señal de protesta mientras una larga fila de camiones pasaba a toda velocidad. «Saben», dijo Gloria, «justo estaba recordando el mensaje del hermano Lester esta tarde. ¡Cómo podemos olvidarlo tan pronto! Tal vez Dios permitió que esto nos sucediera para que nuestra fe aumente al poner nuestra confianza en Él. Llevemos esto al Señor en oración. Busquemos un milagro de la mano de Dios».

Juntas, las chicas inclinaron la cabeza y suplicaron al Señor protección y ayuda.

«¿Saben? Ya me siento mejor», dijo Elaine sonriendo. «Estaba muy preocupada y temerosa, pero desde que oramos y pusimos todo en manos de Dios, tengo confianza en que Él cuidará de nosotras. Me alegra tanto que tenemos un Dios que escucha todos nuestros clamores. ¿Qué haríamos sin su consolador Espíritu Santo? Cantemos otra vez».

«Las alegrías fluyen como un río,
desde que vino el Consolador;
permanece con nosotros para siempre,
y hace de un corazón confiado su morada.
¡Bendita quietud, santa quietud,
bendita seguridad en mi alma!
En el mar tempestuoso, Jesús me habla,
¡y las olas dejan de agitarse!»

-Manie P. Ferguson, siglo XIX

Mientras las chicas cantaban una canción tras otra, sus corazones se conmovían profundamente. ¡Qué tranquilas y en paz se sentían, aunque estaban varadas en una carretera oscura, a trece millas de casa! Pasaban autos y camiones uno tras otro sin detenerse. Entonces vieron que una camioneta, con dos motocicletas todoterreno en la parte trasera, reducía la velocidad. Se apartó de la carretera varios cientos de pies más adelante y comenzó a retroceder lentamente. Las voces de las chicas se apagaron y, en silencio, clamaron desesperadamente a Dios desde lo más profundo de sus corazones. Cuando la camioneta se detuvo, se bajaron dos hombres corpulentos y de pelo largo. Carol bajó la ventanilla mientras se acercaba un hombre con una chaqueta de franela a cuadros rojos.

«¿Qué problema tienen, chicas?», preguntó él, echando un vistazo al auto.

«Nos hemos quedado sin gasolina», respondió Carol rápidamente.

«Bueno, diría que tenemos mucha suerte. Llevamos un bidón de gasolina. ¿Cuánto les falta para llegar?»

«Unas trece millas».

«Bien. Echaremos parte de nuestra gasolina en su tanque y podrán seguir su camino. No hace falta que nos paguen».

«¡Oh, muchas gracias!», respondió Carol. «Estábamos orando para que Dios nos enviara ayuda, ¡y Él hizo mucho más de lo que jamás habríamos imaginado! Muchas gracias».

«Sí, sí», respondió el hombre con brusquedad. «Tienen mucha suerte de que hayamos pasado por aquí. Nos alegra poder ayudarlas».

Varios minutos después, las chicas reanudaron el camino. «Saben», dijo Carol, «cuando vi que esa camioneta se detenía, sentí miedo y alivio al mismo tiempo. Empecé a reprocharme otra vez por no llevar conmigo ese teléfono celular. Pero entonces le pedí a Dios que me ayudara a confiar plenamente en Él y a no tener miedo. Después de todo, ¿acaso no es mucho más confiable que cualquier teléfono celular? Esto ha fortalecido mucho mi fe. ¡Qué diferente podría haber sido todo si hubiéramos dependido únicamente de nuestros teléfonos celulares o de la “buena suerte”, como la llamaron esos hombres! Sin duda, entristece muchísimo el corazón de nuestro Padre que no pongamos nuestra confianza en Él».

«Es justo lo que predicó el hermano Lester esta tarde», añadió Gloria. «¿Recuerdan algunos de esos versículos? Esperé pacientemente al SEÑOR, y él se inclinó a mí y oyó mi clamor… Puso en mi boca un cántico nuevo, una alabanza a nuestro Dios… Bienaventurado el hombre que pone en el SEÑOR su confianza y no se vuelve a los soberbios ni a los que se desvían tras la mentira. –Sal 40:1-4. ¡Esto me hace tan feliz que solo quiero seguir cantando y dando gracias al Señor!»

Una vez más, las chicas alzaron la voz en canto:

«Su ojo siempre está mirando,
su oído atento a escuchar;
su amor es suficiente
para calmar el temor más profundo.
Confía en Él en la luz y en la sombra;
confía en Él, no tengas miedo:
camina muy cerca de ti;
su mano te guiará a salvo;
sus alas te protegerán;
¡confía, no tengas miedo!»

-Charles H. Gabriel, 1856-1932

Maili baada ya maili zilipita kwa kasi Carol alipokuwa akiendesha Chevy ya zamani kwenye barabara kuu yenye magari mengi akielekea nyumbani. Kati ya vipindi vya ukimya na mazungumzo, Carol na dada zake wawili, Elaine na Gloria, waliinua sauti zao katika wimbo, wakimshukuru na kumsifu Muumba wao. Walishukuru sana kwa nafasi ya kutumia jioni pamoja na marafiki zao katika Kanisa la Pine Creek na kupokea ujumbe mwingine wenye kutia moyo kutoka katika Neno la Mungu.

Ghafla, safari yao ya amani ilikatizwa na dalili za tatizo. “Sasa, gari hili lina shida gani?” Carol aliuliza kwa wasiwasi kwa sauti, huku akiielekeza gari lililokwama kando ya barabara. “Lo, hapana, dada zangu, tumekwishaishiwa petroli! Nilikuwa na haraka sana jioni hii hivi kwamba nilisahau kuangalia kipima mafuta. Nilidhani tanki lilikuwa karibu kujaa tulipoondoka nyumbani, na… Lo, hapana!” Carol aliomboleza tena. “Baba aliweka simu ya mkononi kaunta ili niichukue, nami nikasahau hiyo pia!”

“Sasa tufanye nini?” Elaine akasema kwa mshangao. “Tumekwama hapa gizani, hatuna petroli wala simu, na bado tuna maili saba kufika kwenye njia yetu ya kutokea! Na jambo lingine, siku hizi watu hawasimami haraka ili kutoa msaada. Wanajua kwamba karibu kila mtu ana simu. Hili linaonekana kuwa jambo lisilowezekana kwangu!” alisema kwa huzuni akiwa kwenye kiti cha nyuma.

Wasichana waliponyamaza, Chevy ya zamani ilionekana kutikisika kana kwamba inapinga huku msururu mrefu wa malori ukipita kwa kasi. “Unajua,” Gloria alisema, “nilikuwa nikikumbuka ujumbe wa Ndugu Lester jioni hii. Tunawezaje kusahau haraka hivyo! Labda Mungu ameruhusu jambo hili litupate ili imani yetu iongezeke tunapomtegemea Yeye. Tuliombee jambo hili kwa Bwana. Tutazame muujiza utokao mkononi mwa Mungu.”

Wasichana waliinua vichwa vyao pamoja na kumsihi Bwana awalinde na kuwasaidia.

“Unajua, tayari ninajisikia vizuri zaidi,” Elaine alisema huku akitabasamu. “Nilikuwa na wasiwasi na hofu nyingi, lakini kwa kuwa tumeomba na kumkabidhi Mungu kila kitu, nina uhakika kwamba atatulinda. Ninafurahi sana kuwa tuna Mungu anayesikia kilio chetu chote. Tungefanya nini bila Roho wake Mtakatifu mwenye kutufariji? Tuimbe tena.”

“Furaha hutiririka kama mto,
Tangu Mfariji alipokuja;
Anakaa nasi milele,
Na kuufanya moyo wa tumaini makao yake.
Utulivu wa baraka, utulivu mtakatifu,
Hakika njema rohoni mwangu!
Juu ya bahari yenye dhoruba Yesu husema nami,
Nayo mawimbi hutulia!”

-Manie P. Ferguson, karne ya 19

Wasichana walipoimba wimbo baada ya wimbo, mioyo yao iliguswa sana. Walijihisi watulivu na wenye amani, ingawa walikuwa wamekwama kwenye barabara kuu yenye giza, maili kumi na tatu kutoka nyumbani. Gari baada ya gari, na lori baada ya lori, yalipita kwa kasi bila kusimama. Kisha waliona lori dogo la kuchukulia mizigo, lenye pikipiki mbili za ardhini nyuma, likipunguza mwendo. Lilitoka barabarani umbali wa futi mia kadhaa mbele yao, kisha likaanza kurudi nyuma polepole. Sauti za wasichana zilitulia na kuwa kimya huku wakimlilia Mungu kwa dhati kutoka ndani kabisa ya mioyo yao. Lori liliposimama, wanaume wawili wenye nguvu na nywele ndefu waliruka kutoka ndani. Carol alishusha kioo chake huku mwanamume aliyevaa koti la flana lenye miraba mekundu akilikaribia.

“Kuna shida gani hapa, dada zangu?” aliuliza huku akilitazama gari.

“Tumeishiwa petroli,” Carol akajibu haraka.

“Basi, ningesema tuna bahati sana. Tuna kopo la petroli pamoja nasi. Bado mnahitaji kwenda umbali gani?”

“Takriban maili kumi na tatu.”

“Vizuri. Tutamimina petroli yetu kwenye tanki lenu tu, kisha mnaweza kuendelea na safari yenu. Hamhitaji kulipa.”

“Lo, asanteni sana,” Carol akajibu. “Tulikuwa tukiomba Mungu atutumie msaada, naye amefanya zaidi ya tulivyoweza kufikiria! Asanteni sana.”

“Ndiyo, ndiyo,” mwanamume huyo akajibu kwa sauti nzito, “mna bahati sana kwamba tumepita hapa. Tunafurahi tu kuwasaidia.”

Baada ya dakika kadhaa, wasichana waliendelea na safari yao tena. “Unajua,” Carol alisema, “nilipoona lori lile likisimama, niliogopa na kufurahi kwa wakati mmoja. Nilianza tena kujilaumu kwa kutokuwa na simu yangu ya mkononi. Lakini kisha nikamwomba Mungu anisaidie nimtumaini kabisa na nisiogope. Kwa kweli, je, Yeye si wa kutegemewa zaidi kuliko simu yoyote ya mkononi? Jambo hili limeimarisha sana imani yangu. Mambo yangekuwa tofauti sana kama tungalitegemea tu simu zetu za mkononi au ‘bahati nzuri,’ kama wale wanaume walivyoiita. Lazima humhuzunisha sana Baba yetu tunaposhindwa kumtumaini.”

“Ni kama vile Ndugu Lester alivyohubiri jioni hii,” Gloria akaongeza. “Mnayakumbuka baadhi ya mistari hiyo? Nalimngoja Bwana kwa saburi, akaniinamia akakisikia kilio changu … Akatia wimbo mpya kinywani mwangu, naam, sifa kwa Mungu wetu… Heri mtu yule amfanyaye Bwana kuwa tumaini lake, wala hawaheshimu wenye kiburi, wala wale wanaoelekea kwenye uongo. –Zab 40:1-4. Hili linanifurahisha sana hivi kwamba ninataka kuendelea kuimba na kumshukuru Bwana!”

Tena, wasichana waliinua sauti zao katika wimbo:

“Jicho lake daima hutazama,
Sikio lake husikia kwa makini;
Upendo wake watosheleza kabisa
Kutuliza hofu kuu kabisa.
Basi mtumaini kwenye mwangaza na kivuli;
Mtumaini, msiogope:
Anatembea karibu nawe;
Mkono wake utakuongoza salama;
Mabawa yake yatakuficha salama;
Basi mtumaini! Msiogope.”

I am Ted. I was born a male and I know I am a male. My skin color is white, and I know I am white. My parents are white, my grandparents were white, and I have no reason to suspect my other ancestors were anything other than white. These are foundational, irrefutable truths about myself. I do not think I am anything other than what I am. Nor do I desire to be anything other than what I am.

I am a Christian. In order to better define my faith—as there are many who profess Christianity—I am a “biblical” Christian. I believe that the Bible is the Word of God, that it is to be taken literally, and that it instructs a pattern and way of life that all believers should embrace. At the age of 24—after having lived a life of my own choosing and while searching for God who, if He was real, I wanted to know—I turned to Him and I was born again. My transformation as a new creation in Christ began immediately and it continues to this day. My faith in and relationship to Jesus Christ are as foundational and irrefutable as my gender and race.

I am writing in response to that which had been extensively covered by the secular media during the Spring and Summer of 2015: a man who reportedly, throughout his life, had considered himself a female and who had been “transitioning” into a woman; a white woman who had insisted that race is “fluid” and that she is black; and the redefinition of marriage by the Supreme Court of the United States of America affecting, as well, the definition of “family” for an entire nation. These are topics which simply cannot be minimized or otherwise ignored.

The white woman lacked much public support for her explanation of race. In fact, she was significantly ridiculed for her stance. This was not true, however, regarding gender identification or “gay” marriage and family issues, and one must wonder why. If a “genetically/physiologically-constructed” male can be accepted by others as a woman simply because that’s what he thinks he is, and if a man can “marry” a man and a woman can “marry” a woman and be accepted as a married couple by others under the premise of equal rights and because that’s what they want to do, why can’t a white woman be accepted as a black woman when she is convinced that she is black?

The question raised is one of reality. Even though I may think I am the greatest pianist and music composer of all times, the evidence simply does not support that conviction. Even though a white woman says she is black, the evidence likewise does not support that conviction. Also true is that of a man who says he is a woman. The genetic and physiological evidence does not support that conviction. Without the redefinition of marriage, two people of the same sex cannot be married. And regardless of definition, they cannot reproduce on their own, one of God’s primary purposes for marriage.

Without God, man does what is right in his own eyes. So-called “progressive thinking” is simply man’s attempt, given his rejection of God, at better understanding the world and better addressing and solving its problems. Essentially, “anything goes” based upon the latest of ideas.

A biblical Christian, however, believes that God has designed, has created, and is very much involved in the universe … even in the individual lives of people who live in it. There are absolutes. There is a distinction between right and wrong. There are moral values and—something that we frequently forget in these modern times—there is an eternity ahead. As a result of progressive thinking, Darwinism now replaces Creationism, within much of our education system, students as well as teachers who profess faith in the God of the Bible are ridiculed and are otherwise discriminated against, millions of pre-born babies (the politically correct prefer calling them “fetuses”) have been legally dismembered, burnt, crushed, suctioned and pharmacologically murdered (aborted), and no-fault divorce has ravaged the families of our nation. Just look at those things that used to be considered wrong or evil which are now a normal part of our “progressing” society.

And what about eternity? Doesn’t that matter anymore, either?

In response to the Supreme Court’s ruling on gay marriage, then-President Barack Obama, clearly one of our nation’s more powerful, progressive thinkers, indicated his desire that “religious people” respond accordingly by modifying their definition of marriage as well. Believing in the God of the Bible as the Creator of the universe and as the One who designed and ordained marriage as a life-long covenant between one man and one woman, I respectfully decline Mr. Obama’s request. As the world in its own fashion deviates from the design and will of God, a true believer in Christ is called to follow Him. Jesus said, Enter through the narrow gate. For wide is the gate and broad is the road that leads to destruction, and many enter through it. But small is the gate and narrow the road that leads to life, and only a few find it. –Mat 7:13-14 NIV

I am Ted. I am a white male. I am a Christian who desires not to belittle, mock, or otherwise mistreat those with whom I may disagree, but there will be disagreements. I am called to love God and to love my neighbor as myself, regardless of who my neighbor might be. My ultimate hope is not found in this world. It is found in eternity with Christ. And my prayer for others is that they, too, may come to know Him, receive forgiveness of their sins, be transformed into the people God so desires, and spend an eternity with Him. This is not a popular message found in today’s liberal media. But for those who are interested, for those who are seeking something much better than what this world has to offer, God has an answer: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. –Joh 3:16

Saya Ted. Saya dilahirkan sebagai laki-laki dan saya tahu bahwa saya laki-laki. Warna kulit saya putih, dan saya tahu bahwa saya berkulit putih. Orang tua saya berkulit putih, kakek-nenek saya berkulit putih, dan saya tidak punya alasan untuk menduga bahwa leluhur saya yang lain bukan orang kulit putih. Semua ini adalah kebenaran mendasar tentang diri saya yang tak terbantahkan. Saya tidak berpikir bahwa saya adalah sesuatu selain diri saya. Saya juga tidak ingin menjadi sesuatu selain diri saya.

Saya seorang Kristen. Untuk menjelaskan iman saya dengan lebih baik—karena banyak orang mengaku sebagai penganut Kristen—saya adalah seorang Kristen “Alkitabiah”. Saya percaya bahwa Alkitab adalah Firman Allah, bahwa Alkitab harus dipahami secara harfiah, dan bahwa Alkitab mengajarkan pola dan cara hidup yang harus dianut oleh semua orang percaya. Pada usia 24 tahun—setelah menjalani hidup menurut pilihan saya sendiri dan ketika mencari Allah, yang ingin saya kenal jika Dia benar-benar ada—saya berpaling kepada-Nya dan saya dilahirkan kembali. Perubahan diri saya menjadi ciptaan baru di dalam Kristus segera dimulai dan terus berlangsung hingga hari ini. Iman saya kepada Yesus Kristus dan hubungan saya dengan-Nya sama mendasar dan tak terbantahkannya dengan gender dan ras saya.

Saya menulis sebagai tanggapan atas hal-hal yang telah banyak diberitakan oleh media sekuler selama musim semi dan musim panas tahun 2015: seorang pria yang konon sepanjang hidupnya menganggap dirinya perempuan dan yang telah “bertransisi” menjadi seorang wanita; seorang wanita kulit putih yang bersikeras bahwa ras itu “cair” dan bahwa dirinya berkulit hitam; serta pendefinisian ulang pernikahan oleh Mahkamah Agung Amerika Serikat, yang juga berdampak pada definisi “keluarga” bagi seluruh bangsa. Topik-topik ini sama sekali tidak bisa dianggap sepele atau diabaikan begitu saja.

Wanita kulit putih itu tidak mendapat banyak dukungan publik atas penjelasannya tentang ras. Bahkan, ia mendapat banyak ejekan karena pendiriannya. Namun, hal ini tidak terjadi dalam persoalan identifikasi gender atau pernikahan “gay” dan keluarga, sehingga orang patut bertanya-tanya mengapa. Jika seorang pria yang “secara genetik/fisiologis terbentuk” sebagai laki-laki dapat diterima orang lain sebagai wanita hanya karena itulah yang menurutnya merupakan dirinya, dan jika seorang pria dapat “menikahi” pria lain dan seorang wanita dapat “menikahi” wanita lain lalu diterima orang lain sebagai pasangan suami istri atas dasar kesetaraan hak dan karena itulah yang ingin mereka lakukan, mengapa seorang wanita kulit putih tidak dapat diterima sebagai wanita kulit hitam ketika ia yakin bahwa dirinya berkulit hitam?

Pertanyaan yang diajukan adalah tentang realitas. Sekalipun saya mungkin berpikir bahwa saya adalah pianis dan komponis musik terhebat sepanjang masa, bukti yang ada sama sekali tidak mendukung keyakinan itu. Sekalipun seorang wanita kulit putih mengatakan bahwa dirinya berkulit hitam, bukti yang ada juga tidak mendukung keyakinan itu. Hal yang sama berlaku bagi seorang pria yang mengatakan bahwa dirinya wanita. Bukti genetik dan fisiologis tidak mendukung keyakinan itu. Tanpa pendefinisian ulang pernikahan, dua orang berjenis kelamin sama tidak dapat menikah. Dan apa pun definisinya, mereka tidak dapat memiliki keturunan dengan kemampuan mereka sendiri, padahal hal itu merupakan salah satu tujuan utama Allah bagi pernikahan.

Tanpa Allah, manusia melakukan apa yang benar menurut pandangannya sendiri. Apa yang disebut “pemikiran progresif” hanyalah upaya manusia, setelah menolak Allah, untuk memahami dunia dengan lebih baik serta menangani dan memecahkan persoalan-persoalannya dengan lebih baik. Pada dasarnya, “apa saja boleh”, berdasarkan gagasan-gagasan terbaru.

Namun, seorang Kristen Alkitabiah percaya bahwa Allah telah merancang dan menciptakan alam semesta serta sangat terlibat di dalamnya … bahkan dalam kehidupan pribadi orang-orang yang hidup di dalamnya. Ada hal-hal yang mutlak. Ada perbedaan antara benar dan salah. Ada nilai-nilai moral dan—sesuatu yang sering kita lupakan pada zaman modern ini—ada kekekalan yang menanti. Sebagai akibat dari pemikiran progresif, Darwinisme kini menggantikan Kreasionisme; di sebagian besar sistem pendidikan kita, para siswa maupun guru yang mengaku beriman kepada Allah dalam Alkitab diejek dan mengalami diskriminasi dalam berbagai bentuk; jutaan bayi yang belum lahir (orang-orang yang ingin terdengar benar secara politis lebih suka menyebut mereka “janin”) telah secara sah dicabik-cabik, dibakar, diremukkan, disedot, dan dibunuh dengan obat-obatan (digugurkan); dan perceraian tanpa kesalahan telah menghancurkan keluarga-keluarga di bangsa kita. Lihat saja hal-hal yang dahulu dianggap salah atau jahat, tetapi kini menjadi bagian normal dari masyarakat kita yang “terus maju”.

Lalu bagaimana dengan kekekalan? Apakah itu juga tidak lagi penting?

Menanggapi putusan Mahkamah Agung tentang pernikahan gay, Presiden Barack Obama saat itu, yang jelas merupakan salah satu pemikir progresif paling berkuasa di bangsa kita, menyatakan keinginannya agar “orang-orang beragama” juga menanggapi dengan semestinya dengan mengubah definisi pernikahan mereka. Karena percaya kepada Allah dalam Alkitab sebagai Pencipta alam semesta dan sebagai Pribadi yang merancang serta menetapkan pernikahan sebagai perjanjian seumur hidup antara seorang pria dan seorang wanita, dengan hormat saya menolak permintaan Tuan Obama. Ketika dunia dengan caranya sendiri menyimpang dari rancangan dan kehendak Allah, orang yang sungguh-sungguh percaya kepada Kristus dipanggil untuk mengikuti-Nya. Yesus berkata, Masuklah melalui pintu yang sempit. Karena lebarlah pintu dan luaslah jalan yang menuju kebinasaan, dan banyak orang masuk melaluinya. Tetapi sempitlah pintu dan sesaklah jalan yang menuju kehidupan, dan hanya sedikit orang yang menemukannya. –Mat 7:13-14 NIV

Saya Ted. Saya seorang pria kulit putih. Saya seorang Kristen yang tidak ingin merendahkan, mengejek, atau memperlakukan dengan buruk orang-orang yang mungkin tidak sependapat dengan saya, tetapi perbedaan pendapat pasti akan ada. Saya dipanggil untuk mengasihi Allah dan mengasihi sesama seperti diri saya sendiri, siapa pun sesama saya itu. Pengharapan utama saya tidak ditemukan di dunia ini. Pengharapan itu ditemukan dalam kekekalan bersama Kristus. Dan doa saya bagi orang lain adalah agar mereka juga dapat mengenal-Nya, menerima pengampunan atas dosa-dosa mereka, diubahkan menjadi pribadi-pribadi yang sangat dikehendaki Allah, dan menghabiskan kekekalan bersama-Nya. Ini bukan pesan populer yang ditemukan di media liberal masa kini. Namun, bagi mereka yang tertarik, bagi mereka yang mencari sesuatu yang jauh lebih baik daripada yang ditawarkan dunia ini, Allah memberikan jawabannya: Karena begitu besar kasih Allah akan dunia ini, sehingga Ia telah mengaruniakan Anak-Nya yang tunggal, supaya setiap orang yang percaya kepada-Nya tidak binasa, melainkan beroleh hidup yang kekal. –Yoh 3:16

Mile after mile sped by as Carol drove the old Chevy along the busy interstate highway toward home. Between intervals of silence and conversation, Carol and her two sisters, Elaine and Gloria, lifted their voices in song, giving thanks and praise to their Creator. How thankful they were for the opportunity to spend the evening with their friends at Pine Creek Church and to receive another inspiring message from God’s Word.

Suddenly their smooth travel was interrupted by signs of trouble. “Now what can be wrong with this car?” Carol worried out loud as she guided the stalled car to the side of the road. “Oh, no, girls, we’re out of gas! I was in such a hurry this evening that I forgot to check the gauge. I thought the tank was almost full when we left home, and… Oh no!” wailed Carol again. “Dad put the cell phone on the counter for me to take along, and I forgot that also!”

“Whatever are we going to do now?” exclaimed Elaine. “Here we are, stranded in the dark, no gas, no phone, and seven more miles to our exit! And another thing, people just don’t stop very quickly these days and offer help. They know that most everyone carries a phone. This seems almost impossible to me!” she mournfully uttered from the back seat.

As the girls lapsed into silence, the old Chevy seemed to shake in protest as a long row of trucks whizzed by. “You know,” said Gloria, “I was just remembering Brother Lester’s message this evening. How can we forget so quickly! Maybe God has allowed this to happen to us so our faith might be increased as we place our trust in Him. Let’s take this to the Lord in prayer. Let’s look for a miracle from God’s hand.”

Together the girls bowed their heads and pled for the Lord’s protection and help.

“You know, I feel better already,” smiled Elaine. “I was so worried and fearful, but since we prayed and committed everything to God, I have confidence that He will watch over us. I’m so glad we have a God who hears all of our cries. What would we do without His comforting Holy Spirit? Let’s sing again.”

“Joys are flowing like a river,
Since the Comforter has come;
He abides with us forever,
Makes the trusting heart His home.
Blessed quietness, holy quietness,
Blest assurance in my soul!
On the stormy sea Jesus speaks to me,
And the billows cease to roll!”

-Manie P. Ferguson, 19th century

As the girls sang song after song, their hearts were deeply stirred. How quiet and peaceful they felt, even though they were stranded on a dark highway thirteen miles from home. Car after car, and truck after truck sped by without stopping. Then they noticed a pickup truck, with two dirt bikes on the back, slowing down. It pulled off the road several hundred feet ahead of them, and slowly began to back up. The girls’ voices were stilled in silence as they desperately cried out to God from the bottom of their hearts. When the truck came to a halt, two husky, long-haired men jumped out. Carol rolled her window down as a man wearing a red-checked flannel jacket approached.

“What’s the trouble here, girls?” he asked, glancing over the car.

“We’re out of gas,” Carol quickly replied.

“Well, I’d say we’re pretty lucky. We have a can of gas with us. How far do you need to go yet?”

“About thirteen miles.”

“Good. We’ll just pour some of our gas into your tank and you can be on your way again. No payment necessary.”

“O thank you so much,” responded Carol. “We were praying that God would send us help, and He did more than we could ever have thought! Thanks so much.”

“Yes, yes”, replied the man gruffly, “You’re pretty lucky we came along. We’re just glad to help you out.”

Several minutes later, the girls were on their way again. “You know,” said Carol, “when I saw that truck pull over, I was scared and glad at the same time. I began to scold myself again for not having that cell phone with me. But then I asked God to help me completely trust in Him and not be afraid. After all, isn’t He much more dependable than any cell phone? This has been such a faith booster for me. How different this may have turned out, if we had depended solely on our cell phones or “good luck” as those men called it. It must grieve our Father’s heart tremendously when we do not place our trust in Him.”

“It’s just as Brother Lester preached this evening”, added Gloria. “Remember some of those verses? I waited patiently for the LORD; and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry … And he hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God… Blessed is that man that maketh the LORD his trust, and respecteth not the proud, nor such as turn aside to lies. –Psa 40:1-4. This makes me so happy I just want to keep singing and thanking the Lord!”

Again, the girls raised their voices in song:

“His eye is always watching,
His ear is keen to hear;
His love is all-sufficient
To calm the gravest fear.
Then trust Him in shine and shade;
Trust Him, be not afraid:
He’s walking close beside thee;
His hand will safely guide thee;
His wings securely hide thee;
Then trust! Be not afraid.”

-Charles H. Gabriel, 1856-1932

Mile etter mile suste forbi mens Carol kjørte den gamle Chevyen langs den trafikkerte motorveien hjemover. Mellom perioder med stillhet og samtale løftet Carol og de to søstrene hennes, Elaine og Gloria, stemmene i sang og takket og lovpriste Skaperen sin. Så takknemlige de var for muligheten til å tilbringe kvelden sammen med vennene sine i Pine Creek Church og få høre enda et inspirerende budskap fra Guds ord.

Plutselig ble den jevne kjøreturen avbrutt av tegn på problemer. «Hva kan det nå være galt med bilen?» sa Carol bekymret høyt mens hun styrte den stansede bilen inn til veikanten. «Å nei, jenter, vi er tomme for bensin! Jeg hadde det så travelt i kveld at jeg glemte å sjekke måleren. Jeg trodde tanken nesten var full da vi dro hjemmefra, og … Å nei!» jamret Carol igjen. «Pappa la mobiltelefonen på benken så jeg skulle ta den med, og den glemte jeg også!»

«Hva i all verden skal vi gjøre nå?» utbrøt Elaine. «Her sitter vi, strandet i mørket, uten bensin, uten telefon og med sju mil igjen til avkjørselen vår! Og dessuten er det ikke mange som stopper så raskt nå for tiden for å tilby hjelp. De vet at nesten alle har med seg en telefon. Dette virker nesten umulig for meg!» sa hun sørgmodig fra baksetet.

Da jentene ble stille, så den gamle Chevyen ut til å riste i protest mens en lang rekke lastebiler suste forbi. «Vet dere,» sa Gloria, «jeg kom akkurat til å tenke på budskapet bror Lester holdt i kveld. Hvordan kan vi glemme så fort! Kanskje Gud har latt dette skje med oss for at troen vår skal bli styrket når vi setter vår lit til ham. La oss legge dette fram for Herren i bønn. La oss se etter et mirakel fra Guds hånd.»

Sammen bøyde jentene hodene og ba inderlig om Herrens beskyttelse og hjelp.

«Vet dere, jeg føler meg allerede bedre,» sa Elaine med et smil. «Jeg var så bekymret og redd, men etter at vi ba og overlot alt til Gud, er jeg trygg på at han vil passe på oss. Jeg er så glad for at vi har en Gud som hører alle våre rop. Hva skulle vi gjort uten hans trøstende Hellige Ånd? La oss synge igjen.»

«Gleden strømmer som en elv,
siden Trøsteren kom;
han blir hos oss for evig,
gjør det trofaste hjertet til sitt hjem.
Velsignet stillhet, hellig stillhet,
salig visshet i min sjel!
På det stormfulle hav taler Jesus til meg,
og bølgene stilner!»

-Manie P. Ferguson, 1800-tallet

Mens jentene sang den ene sangen etter den andre, ble hjertene deres dypt beveget. Så stille og fredfulle de følte seg, selv om de var strandet på en mørk motorvei tretten mil hjemmefra. Bil etter bil og lastebil etter lastebil suste forbi uten å stoppe. Så la de merke til en pickup med to terrengmotorsykler på lasteplanet som satte ned farten. Den kjørte ut av veien noen hundre fot foran dem og begynte sakte å rygge. Jentene tiet og ropte fortvilet til Gud av hele sitt hjerte. Da bilen stanset, hoppet to kraftige, langhårede menn ut. Carol rullet ned vinduet mens en mann i en rød- og svartternet flanelljakke nærmet seg.

«Hva er problemet her, jenter?» spurte han og så på bilen.

«Vi er tomme for bensin,» svarte Carol raskt.

«Da vil jeg si at vi er ganske heldige. Vi har en bensinkanne med oss. Hvor langt skal dere ennå?»

«Omtrent tretten mil.»

«Bra. Vi heller bare litt av bensinen vår på tanken deres, så kan dere kjøre videre. Dere trenger ikke betale.»

«Å, tusen takk,» svarte Carol. «Vi ba om at Gud skulle sende oss hjelp, og han gjorde mer enn vi noen gang kunne ha tenkt oss! Tusen takk.»

«Ja, ja,» svarte mannen kort. «Dere er ganske heldige som vi kom forbi. Vi er bare glade for å kunne hjelpe dere.»

Noen minutter senere var jentene på vei igjen. «Vet dere,» sa Carol, «da jeg så den lastebilen kjøre til siden, ble jeg både redd og glad. Jeg begynte igjen å bebreide meg selv for at jeg ikke hadde mobiltelefonen med meg. Men så ba jeg Gud om å hjelpe meg til å stole helt på ham og ikke være redd. Er han tross alt ikke mye mer til å stole på enn en mobiltelefon? Dette har virkelig styrket troen min. Tenk hvor annerledes dette kunne ha endt hvis vi bare hadde stolt på mobiltelefonene våre eller på ‘flaks’, som de mennene kalte det. Det må gjøre Faderen vår veldig vondt når vi ikke setter vår lit til ham.»

«Det er akkurat slik bror Lester forkynte i kveld,» la Gloria til. «Husker dere noen av de versene? Jeg ventet tålmodig på HERREN; han bøyde seg til meg og hørte mitt rop … Han la en ny sang i min munn, en lovsang til vår Gud … Salig er den som setter sin lit til HERREN, og som ikke vender seg til de stolte eller til dem som farer med løgn. –Sal 40:1-4. Dette gjør meg så glad at jeg bare har lyst til å fortsette å synge og takke Herren!»

Igjen løftet jentene stemmene i sang:

«Hans øye våker alltid,
hans øre hører skarpt;
hans kjærlighet er mer enn nok
til å stilne den største frykt.
Så stol på ham i sol og skygge;
stol på ham, vær ikke redd:
han går tett ved din side;
hans hånd vil trygt lede deg;
hans vinger vil skjule deg trygt;
så stol på ham! Vær ikke redd.»

-Charles H. Gabriel, 1856–1932

I am Ted. I was born a male and I know I am a male. My skin color is white, and I know I am white. My parents are white, my grandparents were white, and I have no reason to suspect my other ancestors were anything other than white. These are foundational, irrefutable truths about myself. I do not think I am anything other than what I am. Nor do I desire to be anything other than what I am.

I am a Christian. In order to better define my faith—as there are many who profess Christianity—I am a “biblical” Christian. I believe that the Bible is the Word of God, that it is to be taken literally, and that it instructs a pattern and way of life that all believers should embrace. At the age of 24—after having lived a life of my own choosing and while searching for God who, if He was real, I wanted to know—I turned to Him and I was born again. My transformation as a new creation in Christ began immediately and it continues to this day. My faith in and relationship to Jesus Christ are as foundational and irrefutable as my gender and race.

I am writing in response to that which had been extensively covered by the secular media during the Spring and Summer of 2015: a man who reportedly, throughout his life, had considered himself a female and who had been “transitioning” into a woman; a white woman who had insisted that race is “fluid” and that she is black; and the redefinition of marriage by the Supreme Court of the United States of America affecting, as well, the definition of “family” for an entire nation. These are topics which simply cannot be minimized or otherwise ignored.

The white woman lacked much public support for her explanation of race. In fact, she was significantly ridiculed for her stance. This was not true, however, regarding gender identification or “gay” marriage and family issues, and one must wonder why. If a “genetically/physiologically-constructed” male can be accepted by others as a woman simply because that’s what he thinks he is, and if a man can “marry” a man and a woman can “marry” a woman and be accepted as a married couple by others under the premise of equal rights and because that’s what they want to do, why can’t a white woman be accepted as a black woman when she is convinced that she is black?

The question raised is one of reality. Even though I may think I am the greatest pianist and music composer of all times, the evidence simply does not support that conviction. Even though a white woman says she is black, the evidence likewise does not support that conviction. Also true is that of a man who says he is a woman. The genetic and physiological evidence does not support that conviction. Without the redefinition of marriage, two people of the same sex cannot be married. And regardless of definition, they cannot reproduce on their own, one of God’s primary purposes for marriage.

Without God, man does what is right in his own eyes. So-called “progressive thinking” is simply man’s attempt, given his rejection of God, at better understanding the world and better addressing and solving its problems. Essentially, “anything goes” based upon the latest of ideas.

A biblical Christian, however, believes that God has designed, has created, and is very much involved in the universe … even in the individual lives of people who live in it. There are absolutes. There is a distinction between right and wrong. There are moral values and—something that we frequently forget in these modern times—there is an eternity ahead. As a result of progressive thinking, Darwinism now replaces Creationism, within much of our education system, students as well as teachers who profess faith in the God of the Bible are ridiculed and are otherwise discriminated against, millions of pre-born babies (the politically correct prefer calling them “fetuses”) have been legally dismembered, burnt, crushed, suctioned and pharmacologically murdered (aborted), and no-fault divorce has ravaged the families of our nation. Just look at those things that used to be considered wrong or evil which are now a normal part of our “progressing” society.

And what about eternity? Doesn’t that matter anymore, either?

In response to the Supreme Court’s ruling on gay marriage, then-President Barack Obama, clearly one of our nation’s more powerful, progressive thinkers, indicated his desire that “religious people” respond accordingly by modifying their definition of marriage as well. Believing in the God of the Bible as the Creator of the universe and as the One who designed and ordained marriage as a life-long covenant between one man and one woman, I respectfully decline Mr. Obama’s request. As the world in its own fashion deviates from the design and will of God, a true believer in Christ is called to follow Him. Jesus said, Enter through the narrow gate. For wide is the gate and broad is the road that leads to destruction, and many enter through it. But small is the gate and narrow the road that leads to life, and only a few find it. –Mat 7:13-14 NIV

I am Ted. I am a white male. I am a Christian who desires not to belittle, mock, or otherwise mistreat those with whom I may disagree, but there will be disagreements. I am called to love God and to love my neighbor as myself, regardless of who my neighbor might be. My ultimate hope is not found in this world. It is found in eternity with Christ. Я Тед. Я родился мужчиной и знаю, что я мужчина. У меня белая кожа, и я знаю, что я белый. Мои родители белые, мои бабушки и дедушки были белыми, и у меня нет причин подозревать, что кто-либо из моих других предков был не белым. Это основополагающие, неопровержимые истины обо мне. Я не считаю себя кем-либо иным, кроме того, кто я есть. И не хочу быть кем-либо иным.

Я христианин. Чтобы точнее определить свою веру, ведь многие исповедуют христианство, я назову себя «библейским» христианином. Я верю, что Библия — Слово Божье, что её следует понимать буквально и что в ней изложены образец и уклад жизни, которых должны придерживаться все верующие. В возрасте 24 лет — прожив жизнь по собственному выбору и ища Бога, Которого, если Он реален, я хотел узнать, — я обратился к Нему и родился свыше. Моё преображение в новое творение во Христе началось сразу и продолжается по сей день. Моя вера в Иисуса Христа и мои отношения с Ним столь же основополагающи и неопровержимы, как мой пол и моя раса.

Я пишу в ответ на то, что широко освещалось светскими СМИ весной и летом 2015 года: о мужчине, который, по сообщениям, всю жизнь считал себя женщиной и «переходил» в женщину; о белой женщине, настаивавшей на том, что раса «изменчива» и что она чернокожая; и о переопределении брака Верховным судом Соединённых Штатов Америки, затронувшем также понятие «семьи» для целой страны. Эти темы нельзя преуменьшать или просто игнорировать.

Объяснение белой женщины относительно расы не получило широкой общественной поддержки. Более того, её позицию подвергли серьёзным насмешкам. Однако то же самое нельзя сказать о самоопределении пола или вопросах «гей»-браков и семьи, и невольно задаёшься вопросом почему. Если другие могут признать «генетически/физиологически сформированного» мужчину женщиной просто потому, что он считает себя женщиной, и если мужчина может «жениться» на мужчине, а женщина — «выйти замуж» за женщину, и окружающие могут считать их супружеской парой на том основании, что речь идёт о равных правах и они сами этого хотят, почему нельзя признать белую женщину чернокожей, если она убеждена, что она чернокожая?

Здесь поднимается вопрос о реальности. Пусть я и считаю себя величайшим пианистом и композитором всех времён, факты просто не подтверждают эту уверенность. И хотя белая женщина утверждает, что она чернокожая, факты также не подтверждают эту уверенность. То же верно и в отношении мужчины, который говорит, что он женщина. Генетические и физиологические данные не подтверждают эту уверенность. Без переопределения брака двое людей одного пола не могут состоять в браке. И независимо от определения, они не могут самостоятельно иметь потомство — одну из главных целей брака, установленных Богом.

Без Бога человек поступает так, как считает правильным. Так называемое «прогрессивное мышление» — это всего лишь попытка человека, отвергшего Бога, лучше понять мир и лучше решать его проблемы. По сути, это принцип «всё дозволено», основанный на новейших идеях.

Библейский христианин, однако, верит, что Бог задумал и создал вселенную и принимает в ней самое непосредственное участие… вплоть до жизни каждого человека, живущего в ней. Есть абсолютные истины. Есть различие между добром и злом. Есть нравственные ценности и — о чём мы так часто забываем в наше время, — впереди нас ждёт вечность. В результате прогрессивного мышления дарвинизм теперь вытесняет креационизм; во многих учебных заведениях нашей системы образования учеников и учителей, исповедующих веру в Бога Библии, высмеивают и подвергают иной дискриминации; миллионы ещё не рождённых младенцев (политически корректные предпочитают называть их «плодами») законно расчленяют, сжигают, раздавливают, высасывают и убивают с помощью фармакологических средств (прерывают беременность); а развод без необходимости доказывать вину супруга опустошил семьи нашей страны. Достаточно взглянуть на то, что прежде считалось неправильным или злом, а теперь стало обычной частью нашего «развивающегося» общества.

А как же вечность? Разве она больше не имеет значения?

В ответ на решение Верховного суда о гей-браках тогдашний президент Барак Обама, несомненно один из наиболее влиятельных прогрессивных мыслителей нашей страны, выразил пожелание, чтобы «религиозные люди» тоже отреагировали соответствующим образом и изменили своё определение брака. Веря в Бога Библии как Творца вселенной и Того, Кто задумал и установил брак как пожизненный союз одного мужчины и одной женщины, я с уважением отклоняю просьбу господина Обамы. Когда мир по-своему отступает от замысла и воли Бога, истинный верующий во Христа призван следовать за Ним. Иисус сказал: Входите тесными вратами, потому что широки врата и просторен путь, ведущие к погибели, и многие идут ими; потому что тесны врата и узок путь, ведущие к жизни, и немногие находят их. — Мф. 7:13–14 (NIV)

Я Тед. Я белый мужчина. Я христианин и не хочу унижать, высмеивать или как-либо дурно обращаться с теми, с кем я могу быть не согласен, но разногласия будут. Я призван любить Бога и любить ближнего своего, как самого себя, кем бы ни был мой ближний. Моя главная надежда не в этом мире. Она — в вечности со Христом. И я молюсь о том, чтобы и другие познали Его, получили прощение своих грехов, преобразились в тех людей, какими Бог хочет их видеть, и провели вечность с Ним. Сегодняшние либеральные СМИ не распространяют это популярное послание. Но для тех, кому оно интересно, для тех, кто ищет нечто гораздо лучшее, чем может предложить этот мир, у Бога есть ответ: Ибо так возлюбил Бог мир, что отдал Сына Своего Единородного, дабы всякий верующий в Него не погиб, но имел жизнь вечную. — Ин. 3:16

It was 2:30 p.m., Tuesday afternoon.

“Señora!” a chorus of voices hollered from outside our property hedge. “Open the gate!”

“Just wait,” I called back. “It’s not three o’clock yet.”

Disgruntled murmurings sounded from the other side of the hedge. I turned to my wailing baby. Sinking into the rocker to feed her, I closed my eyes to relish each quiet moment before the coming tumult.

**************

We had scarcely settled onto the farm when the neighbor children found us. They appeared—uninvited and unannounced, any time of day—to stay as long as they wished. The first ones soon brought more friends along to join in their play with the foreigner’s children and toys. Play-Doh and table games entertained them but oh, what a commotion ten children could make in a concrete house.

After much exasperation, Ernest (my husband) and I finally came up with a plan…. They could come two afternoons a week, arriving no earlier than three o’clock in the afternoon. On Tuesdays they could stay for supper, but on Thursdays they must leave by 6 p.m.

We also had other rules…. Our children needed to stay within my eyesight and earshot when playing with neighbor children. And NO closed doors. Still, questions niggled my brain. Is this a good thing or a bad one? Will we live to regret it? What if they are a bad influence on our children? My questions formed a prayer, one which God had been hearing from me quite a bit these past months. Lord, give me wisdom and patience with these children today. And if they are a bad influence on our children, Lord, please reveal that to us before our children are harmed.

But what an opportunity! This was one way I could reach the world while being a stay-at-home mom… I read them Bible stories. I taught them the need to respect and obey grownups. I told them they needed to obey me, just as my children were expected to. Transgressors, I warned, would be sent home.

Zinnia did not believe me, until the day she disobeyed and was expelled. I grin now, remembering the little troublemaker perching on the neighbor’s wall, peering over into our farm where her cousins were happily playing. Once had taught her; after that Zinnia obeyed.

**************

“Señora!” Zinnia’s voice interrupted my reverie. “Is it three o’clock yet?”

I opened one eye to peek at the clock—2:47.

“Not quite!” I hollered out the window. Placing baby into the walker, I headed to the kitchen. What would I feed them tonight?

**************

“Zinnia, I need to look in your purse before you go home.”

It was Tuesday evening again, several months later. We had been missing various small things after Zinnia started bringing a purse along on her visits to our house. Tonight, we would see if our suspicions were correct.

Zinnia’s terror-filled eyes met mine. “Just a minute, Señora. I need to use the bathroom.”

“You can use the bathroom after we look in your purse.”

“No, Señora, I can’t wait…”, her voice trailed off as she rushed to the bathroom.

I sighed. Of course, her purse would be empty when she came back out. Searching the bathroom later that night revealed treasures hidden here and there.

“Let’s chat a little, Zinnia,” I invited the following week. Zinnia sat on the bed, twisting yarn knots on the comforter, her eyes defensive, fearful. My heart yearned for the dear girl. Her mom had left years ago to work in another country, leaving the girls with their Grandma.

“I don’t care about those things you stole, Zinnia,” I began. “But it’s a habit you don’t want to start. God cares about you….”

That was the last time Zinnia, her sister, and their cousins showed up at our place. “Our Grandma doesn’t let us come anymore,” they explained.

Maybe it was Grandma; I think it was God. We had prayed much that He would make it clear if their visits were harmful to our children and if they should stop coming. My heart was torn between love for the neighbor children and protection for our own. This was the way God chose to answer.

“Thank you, God,” I prayed. “We’ll take this as your answer, and not invite them back. Send them over if you want them to come again.”

**************

Several years passed. Now it was Jon, a neighbor boy, frequenting our home.

“Could he come to your house every day after school?” his parents had wondered. “We want him to learn good things, instead of playing with boys in our neighborhood.”

Hmm. So, we’re to raise the boy while both parents work?

“He can come Tuesday and Thursday afternoons,” Ernest decided. “Those are the days I’m more often at home.”

Jon showed up faithfully on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons. Problem was, Ernest couldn’t. Other responsibilities and obligations kept coming up, hindering him from being there like he wanted to.

I did not want to nag my husband… He really wished he could be at home, working with the boys. Should I say something, or not? It didn’t seem ideal to have an unconverted boy working for hours with our son, a new Christian.

I did mention my questions to Ernest, but mostly I made it a matter of prayer.

Jon stopped coming. I was amazed. I felt for Jon, yet once again I thanked God for His answer.

**************

“How can I reach out to my neighbor children without compromising my own?” a friend asked recently. Moving to a new area, she faces the challenge of neighbor children coming over.

There are no simple answers. I have discovered the urgency of prayer, and God’s faithfulness in answering when we cry out to Him for wisdom. His answer to others may well be different from what He worked out for us.

**************

Another sister granted me permission to share their experience in relating with neighbor children:

Alex and his mother live across the road from us and began attending church soon after we moved here. Alex came over almost every day and taught our boys Spanish in short order. The boys dreaded his visits at first, but they soon became great friends. After a while another neighbor boy, Nilton, started coming at times and we thought he seemed decent enough. Then one day a third boy, José, came along. I got a distinctly uncomfortable feeling. I gave them a time limit, but just couldn’t shake the uneasy feeling. So, though I thought I didn’t have time, I decided I would work outside the whole time while they were here. I worked close to them and kept an eye on things and thought everything was fine. They seemed to just be playing together nicely, so I was surprised when they went home before the time was up.

It wasn’t long before my boys came in crying; they felt so bad about what had happened. Alex had asked them to deliver a note to his girlfriend because his mom wouldn’t like it if he did. One of the other boys told them what he does out behind bushes at public school, so he doesn’t get caught. They tried to get my boys to promise not to tell me. They didn’t promise, and I was so thankful! But they were very torn up because they thought Alex would not be their friend anymore.

My husband and I talked with the boys and assured them that they had handled the situation correctly by not promising to keep secrets. Within the hour, Alex’s mom came over to visit and we told her about it. She was very alarmed that her son had tried to pass a note and later took care of the situation with her son. I was glad that the budding relationship he had with the neighbor girl was stopped before it went any farther. Alex’s friendship with our boys has continued but the other two boys discovered that our boys had told us about them and didn’t come over for years after that.

José recently asked our eight-year-old son if he could come over to his house and play. I said no. His grandma came over several days later, offended, and said that José was very sad about it. I explained that I feel I must always be with my boys if he would come over because one time, he had tried to get our son to play an electronic war game with him. The grandma understood and was sad that her grandson was a bad influence. She wanted the best for him. We have invited him to Sunday School, but he doesn’t want that. I just hope that we can always have the type of relationship with our children that they will feel free to come to us and not keep these situations to themselves and feel guilty.

**************

Wise parents seek to remove danger, but not difficulty, from their children’s path. I was recently amazed while reading Judges 3, to discover that God wanted some enemy nations to remain in the land of Canaan. Why? He wanted parents to teach their children war (v. 2). Instead, the children of Israel made friends with the enemy nations and began to intermarry. “It seems we live closer to the world here on the mission field,” one sister shared. Our children are growing up on the front lines, as it were. This can be positive. They have frequent opportunities to “speak with the enemy in the gates,” where they are asked what we believe, and why. But when parents are lax, or their children are rebellious, this closer association with the world can prove tragic.

As we connect with God in prayer for our children, we must also connect with them. No strict safety guidelines will substitute a close relationship with your child. The mother of a child who was abused shared, “The only way your child will tell you what is going on is if you have a close relationship.”

I stagger as I consider our enemy and my own inadequacy as a mother. Suddenly I am seized with urgency to pray for things which never entered my head when our children were still young. Abuse cases exist around us; at times in our very midst. I pray for our children’s protection from the evil which surrounds them and that which rises in their hearts. I pray they will never mar another’s purity. I pray for purity at the marriage altar, both for them and their future spouses.

I pray with urgency, yet with confidence. Because this I know: God loves our children—He cares about their purity and protection even more than we as parents do—He longs for us to partner with Him in raising them to be faithful servants of His—And He wants to show Himself strong on behalf of humble parents who cry out to Him as they train soldiers in enemy territory. For the eyes of the LORD run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to shew himself strong in the behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him… –2 Chronicles 16:9.

Il était 14 h 30, mardi après-midi.

« Señora ! » Un chœur de voix cria depuis l’extérieur de la haie qui entourait notre propriété. « Ouvrez le portail ! »

« Attendez un peu, leur ai-je répondu. Il n’est pas encore trois heures. »

Des murmures mécontents s’élevèrent de l’autre côté de la haie. Je me tournai vers mon bébé qui pleurait. M’enfonçant dans le fauteuil à bascule pour la nourrir, je fermai les yeux afin de savourer chaque instant de calme avant le tumulte à venir.

**************

Nous venions à peine de nous installer à la ferme que les enfants du voisinage nous ont trouvés. Ils arrivaient — sans y être invités ni annoncés, à n’importe quelle heure — et restaient aussi longtemps qu’ils le souhaitaient. Les premiers ne tardèrent pas à amener d’autres amis pour se joindre à leurs jeux avec les enfants et les jouets de l’étrangère. La pâte à modeler et les jeux de société les occupaient, mais, ah, quel vacarme dix enfants pouvaient faire dans une maison en béton !

Après bien des exaspérations, Ernest (mon mari) et moi avons enfin trouvé un plan… Ils pourraient venir deux après-midi par semaine, et n’arriveraient pas avant quinze heures. Le mardi, ils pourraient rester pour le souper, mais le jeudi, ils devraient partir avant 18 h.

Nous avions aussi d’autres règles… Nos enfants devaient rester dans mon champ de vision et à portée de voix lorsqu’ils jouaient avec les enfants du voisinage. Et aucune porte fermée. Pourtant, des questions me trottaient dans la tête. Est-ce une bonne chose ou une mauvaise ? Le regretterons-nous un jour ? Et s’ils exerçaient une mauvaise influence sur nos enfants ? Mes questions se transformaient en prière, une prière que Dieu entendait souvent de ma part ces derniers mois. Seigneur, donne-moi aujourd’hui la sagesse et la patience avec ces enfants. Et s’ils exercent une mauvaise influence sur nos enfants, Seigneur, révèle-le-nous, je t’en prie, avant qu’ils ne leur fassent du mal.

Mais quelle occasion ! C’était une façon pour moi d’atteindre le monde tout en restant mère au foyer… Je leur lisais des histoires bibliques. Je leur enseignais qu’il fallait respecter et obéir aux adultes. Je leur disais qu’ils devaient m’obéir, comme mes propres enfants étaient censés le faire. Je les avertissais que ceux qui enfreindraient les règles seraient renvoyés chez eux.

Zinnia ne m’a pas crue, jusqu’au jour où elle a désobéi et a été renvoyée. Aujourd’hui, je souris en me rappelant la petite chipie perchée sur le mur du voisin, qui regardait par-dessus dans notre ferme où ses cousins jouaient joyeusement. Une fois lui avait suffi ; après cela, Zinnia obéissait.

**************

« Señora ! » La voix de Zinnia interrompit mes pensées. « Est-ce qu’il est déjà trois heures ? »

J’ouvris un œil pour jeter un coup d’œil à l’horloge : 14 h 47.

« Pas encore ! » criai-je par la fenêtre. Après avoir installé le bébé dans le trotteur, je me dirigeai vers la cuisine. Qu’allais-je leur donner à manger ce soir ?

**************

« Zinnia, je dois regarder dans ton sac à main avant que tu rentres chez toi. »

C’était de nouveau mardi soir, plusieurs mois plus tard. Depuis que Zinnia avait commencé à apporter un sac à main lors de ses visites chez nous, il nous manquait diverses petites choses. Ce soir, nous allions vérifier si nos soupçons étaient fondés.

Les yeux emplis de terreur de Zinnia croisèrent les miens. « Juste une minute, Señora. Je dois aller aux toilettes. »

« Tu peux y aller après que nous avons regardé dans ton sac. »

« Non, Señora, je ne peux pas attendre… » Sa voix s’éteignit tandis qu’elle se précipitait aux toilettes.

Je soupirai. Bien sûr, son sac serait vide à son retour. En fouillant les toilettes plus tard dans la soirée, je découvris des trésors cachés çà et là.

« Parlons un peu, Zinnia », lui proposai-je la semaine suivante. Zinnia était assise sur le lit, nouant et dénouant les fils de la couverture, le regard méfiant et craintif. Mon cœur aspirait à aider cette chère petite. Sa mère était partie des années auparavant travailler dans un autre pays, laissant les filles avec leur grand-mère.

« Je ne tiens pas à ces objets que tu as volés, Zinnia, commençai-je. Mais c’est une habitude que tu ne veux pas prendre. Dieu se soucie de toi… »

Ce fut la dernière fois que Zinnia, sa sœur et leurs cousins se présentèrent chez nous. « Notre grand-mère ne nous laisse plus venir », expliquèrent-ils.

C’était peut-être leur grand-mère ; moi, je pense que c’était Dieu. Nous avions beaucoup prié pour qu’Il nous fasse clairement comprendre si leurs visites faisaient du mal à nos enfants et s’ils devaient cesser de venir. Mon cœur était partagé entre l’amour pour les enfants du voisinage et le désir de protéger les nôtres. C’est ainsi que Dieu a choisi de répondre.

« Merci, Dieu, priai-je. Nous prendrons cela comme ta réponse et ne les inviterons pas à revenir. Fais-les venir si tu veux qu’ils reviennent. »

**************

Plusieurs années passèrent. À présent, c’était Jon, un garçon du voisinage, qui venait souvent chez nous.

« Pourrait-il venir chez vous tous les jours après l’école ? » nous avaient demandé ses parents. « Nous voulons qu’il apprenne de bonnes choses au lieu de jouer avec les garçons de notre quartier. »

Hmm. Alors, c’est à nous d’élever le garçon pendant que ses deux parents travaillent ?

« Il peut venir les mardis et jeudis après-midi, décida Ernest. Ce sont les jours où je suis le plus souvent à la maison. »

Jon venait fidèlement les mardis et jeudis après-midi. Le problème, c’est qu’Ernest ne le pouvait pas. D’autres responsabilités et obligations se présentaient sans cesse, l’empêchant d’être là comme il le souhaitait.

Je ne voulais pas harceler mon mari… Il aurait vraiment aimé être à la maison pour travailler avec les garçons. Devais-je dire quelque chose ou non ? Il ne me semblait pas idéal qu’un garçon non converti travaille des heures durant avec notre fils, un nouveau chrétien.

J’ai bien parlé de mes questions à Ernest, mais surtout, j’en ai fait un sujet de prière.

Jon a cessé de venir. J’en ai été étonnée. J’éprouvais de la compassion pour Jon, mais une fois encore, j’ai remercié Dieu pour sa réponse.

**************

« Comment puis-je tendre la main aux enfants du voisinage sans mettre les miens en danger ? » m’a récemment demandé une amie. Venue s’installer dans une nouvelle région, elle est confrontée au défi des enfants du voisinage qui viennent chez elle.

Il n’y a pas de réponses simples. J’ai découvert combien la prière est urgente, ainsi que la fidélité de Dieu, qui répond lorsque nous crions à Lui pour recevoir la sagesse. Sa réponse à d’autres peut très bien être différente de celle qu’Il nous a donnée.

**************

Une autre sœur m’a donné la permission de raconter leur expérience avec les enfants du voisinage :

Alex et sa mère habitent de l’autre côté de la route et ont commencé à aller à l’église peu après notre arrivée ici. Alex venait presque tous les jours et a rapidement appris l’espagnol à nos garçons. Au début, les garçons redoutaient ses visites, mais ils sont vite devenus de grands amis. Au bout d’un certain temps, un autre garçon du voisinage, Nilton, a commencé à venir parfois et nous avons pensé qu’il avait l’air assez bien. Puis, un jour, un troisième garçon, José, est venu avec lui. J’ai ressenti un malaise très net. Je leur ai fixé une limite de temps, mais je n’arrivais pas à chasser mon inquiétude. Alors, même si je pensais ne pas avoir le temps, j’ai décidé de travailler dehors tout le temps qu’ils seraient là. Je travaillais près d’eux et je surveillais ce qui se passait, pensant que tout allait bien. Ils semblaient simplement jouer gentiment ensemble, alors j’ai été surprise lorsqu’ils sont rentrés chez eux avant l’heure prévue.

Peu après, mes garçons sont rentrés en pleurant ; ils se sentaient très mal à cause de ce qui s’était passé. Alex leur avait demandé de remettre un mot à sa petite amie, parce que sa mère n’aurait pas apprécié qu’il le fasse lui-même. L’un des autres garçons leur a raconté ce qu’il faisait derrière les buissons à l’école publique pour ne pas se faire prendre. Ils ont essayé de faire promettre à mes garçons de ne rien me dire. Ils n’ont pas promis, et j’en étais tellement reconnaissante ! Mais ils étaient très bouleversés, car ils pensaient qu’Alex ne serait plus leur ami.

Mon mari et moi avons parlé avec les garçons et leur avons assuré qu’ils avaient bien réagi en refusant de promettre de garder des secrets. Moins d’une heure plus tard, la mère d’Alex est venue nous voir et nous lui avons raconté ce qui s’était passé. Elle était très alarmée d’apprendre que son fils avait essayé de faire passer un mot et elle a ensuite réglé la situation avec lui. J’étais contente que la relation naissante qu’il avait avec la fille du voisinage ait été interrompue avant d’aller plus loin. L’amitié d’Alex avec nos garçons a continué, mais les deux autres garçons ont découvert que nos garçons nous avaient parlé d’eux et ne sont plus venus chez nous pendant des années.

Récemment, José a demandé à notre fils de huit ans s’il pouvait venir chez lui jouer. J’ai dit non. Quelques jours plus tard, sa grand-mère est venue, offensée, et a dit que José en était très triste. J’ai expliqué que je pensais devoir toujours rester avec mes garçons s’il venait, car, une fois, il avait essayé de faire jouer notre fils avec lui à un jeu électronique de guerre. La grand-mère a compris et était triste que son petit-fils soit une mauvaise influence. Elle voulait le meilleur pour lui. Nous l’avons invité à l’école du dimanche, mais cela ne l’intéresse pas. J’espère seulement que nous pourrons toujours avoir avec nos enfants une relation telle qu’ils se sentiront libres de venir nous parler, au lieu de garder ces situations pour eux et de se sentir coupables.

**************

Les parents avisés cherchent à écarter le danger, mais non les difficultés, du chemin de leurs enfants. J’ai récemment été stupéfaite en lisant Juges 3 de découvrir que Dieu voulait que certaines nations ennemies demeurent dans le pays de Canaan. Pourquoi ? Il voulait que les parents enseignent la guerre à leurs enfants (v. 2). Pourtant, les enfants d’Israël se sont liés d’amitié avec les nations ennemies et ont commencé à se marier avec elles. « Il semble que nous vivions plus près du monde ici, sur le champ missionnaire », a confié une sœur. Nos enfants grandissent, pour ainsi dire, en première ligne. Cela peut être positif. Ils ont souvent l’occasion de « parler avec l’ennemi aux portes », lorsqu’on leur demande ce que nous croyons et pourquoi. Mais lorsque les parents manquent de vigilance, ou que leurs enfants se rebellent, cette proximité accrue avec le monde peut avoir des conséquences tragiques.

Lorsque nous nous tournons vers Dieu dans la prière pour nos enfants, nous devons aussi nous rapprocher d’eux. Aucune règle de sécurité stricte ne peut remplacer une relation étroite avec votre enfant. La mère d’un enfant victime d’abus a raconté : « La seule façon pour que votre enfant vous dise ce qui se passe, c’est d’avoir une relation étroite avec lui. »

Je suis bouleversée lorsque je pense à notre ennemi et à ma propre incapacité en tant que mère. Soudain, je suis saisie par l’urgence de prier pour des choses qui ne m’étaient jamais venues à l’esprit lorsque nos enfants étaient encore petits. Des cas de maltraitance existent autour de nous, parfois tout près de nous. Je prie pour que nos enfants soient protégés du mal qui les entoure et de celui qui naît dans leur cœur. Je prie pour qu’ils ne souillent jamais la pureté d’autrui. Je prie pour la pureté au pied de l’autel du mariage, la leur comme celle de leurs futurs conjoints.

Je prie avec urgence, mais avec confiance. Car voici ce que je sais : Dieu aime nos enfants — Il se soucie de leur pureté et de leur protection encore plus que nous, leurs parents — Il désire que nous nous associions à Lui pour les élever afin qu’ils deviennent ses fidèles serviteurs — et Il veut montrer sa puissance en faveur des parents humbles qui crient à Lui tandis qu’ils forment des soldats en territoire ennemi. Car les yeux de l’Éternel parcourent toute la terre afin de se montrer fort en faveur de ceux dont le cœur lui est entièrement dévoué… –2 Chroniques 16:9.
