Before I was converted, I had never heard the term “Anabaptist” and the concept of someone sharing their faith in Jesus with others was foreign to me. After I was converted, I remember thinking about all my friends who didn’t know anything about what had just happened to me. One thing kept going through my mind, “I need to tell them!” When something good happens to someone, they usually tell others. Some people tell one or two, while others feel like telling everyone. That’s what I wanted to do, not for my sake, but for theirs.

Whenever I would see an old friend, I would tell them what had happened to me. They usually said they had heard about it and then tried to get me to settle down and relax. I will be the first to admit, I made mistakes those first years. I noticed that many people didn’t appreciate what I had to say, but what astonished me the most was that the people who claimed to be Christians seemed to be the most offended.

One day I was visiting with an older man who said that he had been a Christian for most his life. During the discussion he pointed up to a lightbulb and said “Do you see that lightbulb? It’s not speaking.” I was shocked. He was telling me that, yes, Jesus says we are the light of the world, but that lights are quiet. They don’t speak. I went home to do a personal Bible study on the matter. Was this true? It wasn’t long before I found verses like, And Jesus went about all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing all manner of sickness and all manner of disease among the people. –Mat 4:23. Also, in Matthew, Jesus says that He was moved with compassion because the people with Him were tired and scattered about. Further on, we read, Then saith he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few; Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest. –Mat 9:37-38

It seems to me that wherever Jesus went, He was talking to people about the kingdom. I have seen people witnessing about God but doing it in an ugly way. That doesn’t mean we shouldn’t witness. If you read the book of Acts, that’s about all you see—believers sharing the Gospel message with others! In one account the authorities captured the disciples and said they could go free if they would be quiet! The disciples, though, said they could not—For we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard. –Act 4:20. Eventually, they were permanently silenced—by death.

I later heard about these people called Anabaptists. I began to read about them, and how they, too would not be silent. I ordered the Martyr’s Mirror and was astounded at what I read. These dear people lived like the disciples that we find in the Bible. They fulfilled the things Jesus said,—And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved. –Mat 10:22. And in Romans, As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter. –Rom 8:36. After some time, I found a church with an Anabaptist vision.

So why am I writing this? Dear brothers and sisters, I believe the fire is going out. I keep hearing some of our Anabaptist people talking about living a quiet and peaceable life. Jesus tells us in the parable of the sower, He also that received seed among the thorns is he that heareth the word; and the care of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, choke the word, and he becometh unfruitful. –Mat 13:22. Could that be where some of us are at? We live in a western culture where money seems easy to obtain, and we become focused on our own wealth and the cares of this world. Let’s be careful that we don’t become like the world, to avoid being persecuted by the world.

One group of Anabaptists was fleeing persecution and moved into a country not yet persecuted. They began a furniture shop to support themselves, but they couldn’t sell any furniture because they were the dreaded Anabaptists. Soon the situation got desperate because they needed money for food. One day a wealthy man walked into the shop. All the workers stopped working. “Maybe this man will buy something, and we can eat!” They thought. An old brother approached the possible client and asked him if he knew Jesus. After a short chat the man stormed out of the store in a fit of anger. Soon some hungry workers asked the old man why he had to scare away their only chance at a sale. He explained that for this man to know Jesus was far more important than them worrying about making a sale. That was the mindset of the early Anabaptists—the Gospel was number one. They couldn’t but speak of the things they’d seen and heard and they, too, were killed all the day long.

I’ve read numerous accounts of early Anabaptist Christians who had been arrested for their faith. The authorities would plead with them to just be quiet! But they refused, just as the disciples did. They too chose death, rather than the quiet life. One young man was arrested that left behind his dear wife expecting their first child. The authorities waited for the child to be born then brought the newborn infant to the new father in prison. They told him he was now a father and could go home and be with his wife and son. They said he could also continue to believe the same way, but he had to keep quiet, and not speak out against sin in the church. The young father refused, so they burnt him at the stake. Being quiet was not an option.

So, what do the Scriptures mean about a quiet and peaceable life? Paul writes to Timothy, I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men; For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty. –1Ti 2:1-2. For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty? Yes, the apostle Paul says this, but what did he mean? Could he have meant that we should be quiet about the Gospel? Or that we should never confront a sinner? Paul is not telling us to do something that he never did, or something that Christ himself never did. In fact, the Scriptures, reveal something quite the opposite.

It seems that the New Testament Christians in the Bible and in the early church were actively spreading the Gospel and were excited about the Church of Jesus Christ. They went about preaching the Gospel: holding meetings in the mountains, in the woods, or anywhere people would come. That was their life. Paul here is saying that we should pray that if we are obeying God by doing things the authorities don’t like, that they will leave us alone as we go about our normal day-to-day activities. As Christians, we should be spreading the truth of God’s Word, and being active for the furtherance of God’s Kingdom. Our prayer should be that the authorities will let us live in peace, while serving the Prince of Peace.

Some Christians try to be the world in their efforts to win the world. Trying to get people to live a happy life, join our club, be free in Christ, go on an exciting mission trip, live life to the fullest, be everything you can be. It’s all about “loving Jesus,” not obeying Him.

What about us? Are we excited to tell people about Jesus even if it will cost us something? For many of us it is quite easy to talk about farming, construction work, deer hunting, and many other things, yet when it comes to the things of God, we don’t have much to say. Are we that scared of persecution? Do we fear the world hating us? Remember what Jesus said, If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you. If ye were of the world, the world would love his own… –Joh 15:18-19. And, Whosoever therefore shall be ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation; of him also shall the Son of man be ashamed, when he cometh in the glory of his Father with the holy angels. –Mar 8:38

It’s easy to be a Christian, where you settle down and live a quiet and peaceable life, never challenging a sinner, never correcting a brother, or never stepping on Satan’s toes, but who said it would be easy? Here in Haiti we, as a church, are trying to follow Jesus no matter what the cost. Just yesterday we had two members tell us they are about to lose their jobs because of the Gospel. Another sister in the church reported that the school where her children attend require uniforms and that the girls must wear pants. She sent her daughter to school in a modest dress, but she was sent home with a note from the principle saying she was not to return to school wearing “that thing.” If ye be reproached for the name of Christ, happy are ye; for the spirit of glory and of God resteth upon you: on their part he is evil spoken of, but on your part he is glorified. –1Pe 4:14

Happiness comes from suffering for righteousness. Biblical suffering comes from obeying Jesus in the face of opposition. Are we too busy arguing over personal opinions of doctrine and being politically correct while the world laughs at us and goes to hell? Let’s be like Jesus and faithful Christians down through the ages, living in a manner so that those around us cannot deny that the power of God is in us. We have something that everyone needs. So, what are we waiting for? Let’s reunite, gather back together, deny ourselves, pick up our crosses and follow him!

Kabla sijamgeukia Mungu, sikuwa nimewahi kusikia neno “Anabaptisti,” na wazo la mtu kushiriki imani yake katika Yesu na wengine lilikuwa geni kwangu. Baada ya kumgeukia Mungu, nakumbuka nilifikiria kuhusu marafiki wangu wote ambao hawakujua chochote kuhusu yale yaliyokuwa yamenitokea. Jambo moja liliendelea kunijia akilini: “Ninahitaji kuwaambia!” Jambo zuri linapomtokea mtu, kwa kawaida huwaambia wengine. Watu wengine huwaambia mtu mmoja au wawili, huku wengine wakitaka kuwaambia kila mtu. Hilo ndilo nililotaka kufanya, si kwa ajili yangu, bali kwa ajili yao.

Kila nilipokutana na rafiki wa zamani, nilimwambia yaliyokuwa yamenitokea. Kwa kawaida walisema walikuwa wamesikia habari zake kisha wakajaribu kunishawishi nitulie na kupumzika. Nitakuwa wa kwanza kukiri kwamba nilifanya makosa katika miaka hiyo ya kwanza. Nilitambua kwamba watu wengi hawakuthamini yale niliyosema, lakini kilichonishangaza zaidi ni kwamba watu waliodai kuwa Wakristo walionekana kukerwa zaidi.

Siku moja nilikuwa nikizungumza na mzee mmoja aliyesema alikuwa Mkristo kwa muda mwingi wa maisha yake. Wakati wa mazungumzo, alielekeza juu kwenye balbu ya taa na kusema, “Unaiona ile balbu? Haizungumzi.” Nilishangaa. Alikuwa ananiambia kwamba, ndiyo, Yesu anasema sisi ni nuru ya ulimwengu, lakini nuru huwa kimya. Hazungumzi. Nilikwenda nyumbani kufanya funzo binafsi la Biblia kuhusu jambo hilo. Je, hili lilikuwa kweli? Haikuchukua muda kabla sijapata mistari kama hii: Naye Yesu alikuwa akizunguka katika Galilaya yote, akifundisha katika masinagogi yao, na kuihubiri Injili ya ufalme, na kuponya magonjwa yote na udhaifu wa kila namna miongoni mwa watu. –Mt 4:23. Pia, katika Mathayo, Yesu anasema aliguswa na huruma kwa sababu watu waliokuwa pamoja naye walikuwa wamechoka na kutawanyika. Baadaye tunasoma, Ndipo akawaambia wanafunzi wake, Mavuno ni mengi kweli, lakini watenda kazi ni wachache; Basi mwombeni Bwana wa mavuno awapeleke watenda kazi katika mavuno yake. –Mt 9:37-38

Inaonekana kwangu kwamba popote Yesu alipokwenda, alikuwa akizungumza na watu kuhusu ufalme. Nimewaona watu wakimshuhudia Mungu kwa njia mbaya. Hilo halimaanishi kwamba hatupaswi kutoa ushuhuda. Ukisoma kitabu cha Matendo, karibu hicho ndicho unachokiona—waumini wakiwashirikisha wengine ujumbe wa Injili! Katika simulizi moja, wenye mamlaka waliwakamata wanafunzi na kusema wangeweza kuondoka huru ikiwa wangekaa kimya! Lakini wanafunzi wakasema hawangeweza—Kwa maana sisi hatuwezi kuacha kuyasema mambo tuliyoyaona na kuyasikia. –Mdo 4:20. Hatimaye, walinyamazishwa kabisa—kwa kifo.

Baadaye nilisikia kuhusu watu hawa walioitwa Anabaptisti. Nilianza kusoma kuwahusu, na jinsi wao pia wasingekaa kimya. Niliagiza kitabu cha Martyr’s Mirror, nami nilistaajabishwa na yale niliyosoma. Watu hawa wapendwa waliishi kama wanafunzi tunaowapata katika Biblia. Walitimiza yale Yesu aliyosema,—Nanyi mtachukiwa na watu wote kwa ajili ya jina langu; lakini mwenye kuvumilia hata mwisho, ndiye atakayeokoka. –Mt 10:22. Na katika Warumi, Kama ilivyoandikwa, Kwa ajili yako tunauawa mchana kutwa; tumehesabiwa kuwa kama kondoo wa kuchinjwa. –Rum 8:36. Baada ya muda, nilipata kanisa lenye maono ya Anabaptisti.

Basi kwa nini ninaandika haya? Ndugu na dada wapendwa, naamini moto unazimika. Ninaendelea kuwasikia baadhi ya watu wetu wa Anabaptisti wakizungumza kuhusu kuishi maisha ya utulivu na amani. Yesu anatuambia katika mfano wa mpanzi, Naye aliyepandwa penye miiba ndiye asikiaye lile neno; na shughuli za dunia hii, na udanganyifu wa mali, hulisonga lile neno, naye huwa haji kuzaa matunda. –Mt 13:22. Je, huenda baadhi yetu tuko katika hali hiyo? Tunaishi katika utamaduni wa Magharibi ambamo pesa zinaonekana kupatikana kwa urahisi, nasi tunajikita katika utajiri wetu wenyewe na shughuli za dunia hii. Tuwe waangalifu tusije tukawa kama ulimwengu ili kuepuka kuteswa na ulimwengu.

Kundi moja la Anabaptisti lilikuwa linakimbia mateso na kuhamia nchi ambayo bado halikuwa likiteswa. Walianzisha duka la samani ili kujikimu, lakini hawakuweza kuuza samani yoyote kwa sababu walikuwa Anabaptisti waliotishwa. Hali ikawa mbaya upesi kwa sababu walihitaji pesa za chakula. Siku moja tajiri mmoja aliingia dukani. Wafanyakazi wote wakaacha kufanya kazi. “Labda mtu huyu atanunua kitu, nasi tutapata chakula!” wakawaza. Ndugu mmoja mzee akamwendea mteja aliyekuwa mtarajiwa na kumuuliza kama anamjua Yesu. Baada ya mazungumzo mafupi, mtu huyo alitoka dukani kwa hasira kali. Muda mfupi baadaye, baadhi ya wafanyakazi waliokuwa na njaa walimuuliza yule mzee kwa nini ilimbidi amfukuze nafasi yao pekee ya kufanya mauzo. Alieleza kwamba kumsaidia mtu huyo amjue Yesu kulikuwa muhimu zaidi kuliko wao kuhangaikia kuuza kitu. Huo ndio uliokuwa mtazamo wa Anabaptisti wa kwanza—Injili ilikuwa jambo la kwanza. Hawakuweza kuacha kusema mambo waliyoyaona na kuyasikia, na wao pia waliuawa mchana kutwa.

Nimesoma simulizi nyingi kuhusu Wakristo wa Anabaptisti wa zamani waliokamatwa kwa ajili ya imani yao. Wenye mamlaka wangewasihi wakae kimya tu! Lakini walikataa, kama vile wanafunzi walivyofanya. Wao pia walichagua kifo badala ya maisha ya utulivu. Kijana mmoja alikamatwa, akiwa ameacha mke wake mpendwa ambaye alikuwa anatarajia mtoto wao wa kwanza. Wenye mamlaka walingoja mtoto azaliwe, kisha wakamleta mtoto mchanga kwa baba yake mpya gerezani. Walimwambia sasa alikuwa baba na angeweza kwenda nyumbani kuwa pamoja na mkewe na mwanawe. Walisema angeweza pia kuendelea kuamini vivyo hivyo, lakini alipaswa kunyamaza na asiseme dhidi ya dhambi kanisani. Baba huyo mchanga alikataa, kwa hiyo wakamchoma kwenye mti wa mateso. Kunyamaza hakukuwa chaguo.

Basi, Maandiko yanamaanisha nini yanaposema kuhusu maisha ya utulivu na amani? Paulo anamwandikia Timotheo, Nawasihi, basi, kwanza ya yote, dua, sala, maombezi, na shukrani zifanyike kwa ajili ya watu wote; kwa ajili ya wafalme na wote wenye mamlaka; ili tuishi maisha ya utulivu na amani katika utauwa wote na heshima. –1Tim 2:1-2. Kwa ajili ya wafalme na wote wenye mamlaka; ili tuishi maisha ya utulivu na amani katika utauwa wote na heshima? Ndiyo, mtume Paulo anasema hivi, lakini alimaanisha nini? Je, huenda alimaanisha kwamba tunapaswa kunyamaza kuhusu Injili? Au kwamba hatupaswi kamwe kumkabili mwenye dhambi? Paulo hatuambii tufanye jambo ambalo yeye mwenyewe hakuwahi kufanya, au jambo ambalo Kristo mwenyewe hakuwahi kufanya. Kwa kweli, Maandiko yanaonyesha jambo lililo kinyume kabisa.

Inaonekana kwamba Wakristo wa Agano Jipya katika Biblia na katika kanisa la kwanza walikuwa wakieneza Injili kwa bidii na walisisimuliwa na Kanisa la Yesu Kristo. Walizunguka wakihubiri Injili: wakifanya mikutano milimani, msituni, au mahali popote ambapo watu wangekuja. Hayo ndiyo yaliyokuwa maisha yao. Hapa Paulo anasema tunapaswa kuomba kwamba ikiwa tunamtii Mungu kwa kufanya mambo ambayo wenye mamlaka hawapendi, watuache tuendelee na shughuli zetu za kawaida za kila siku. Kama Wakristo, tunapaswa kueneza ukweli wa Neno la Mungu, na kuwa watendaji katika kuendeleza Ufalme wa Mungu. Sala yetu inapaswa kuwa kwamba wenye mamlaka wataturuhusu kuishi kwa amani, huku tukimtumikia Mfalme wa Amani.

Baadhi ya Wakristo hujaribu kuwa kama ulimwengu katika juhudi zao za kuuokoa ulimwengu. Hujaribu kuwafanya watu waishi maisha ya furaha, wajiunge na kikundi chetu, wawe huru katika Kristo, waende safari ya kusisimua ya umisheni, wafurahie maisha kikamilifu, wawe kila kitu wanachoweza kuwa. Yote yanahusu “kumpenda Yesu,” si kumtii.

Vipi kuhusu sisi? Je, tunasisimuka kuwaambia watu kuhusu Yesu hata kama itatugharimu kitu? Kwa wengi wetu ni rahisi kabisa kuzungumza kuhusu kilimo, kazi ya ujenzi, uwindaji wa kulungu, na mambo mengine mengi, lakini inapofikia mambo ya Mungu, hatuna mengi ya kusema. Je, tunaogopa sana kuteswa? Tunaogopa ulimwengu utatuchukia? Kumbukeni Yesu alichosema, Ulimwengu ukiwachukia, jueni kwamba ulinichukia mimi kabla ya kuwachukia ninyi. Kama mngekuwa wa ulimwengu, ulimwengu ungewapenda walio wake… –Yn 15:18-19. Na, Basi, mtu yeyote atakayenionea haya mimi na maneno yangu katika kizazi hiki cha uzinzi na cha dhambi, Mwana wa Adamu naye atamwonea haya, atakapokuja katika utukufu wa Baba yake pamoja na malaika watakatifu. –Mk 8:38

Ni rahisi kuwa Mkristo unapokuwa umetulia na kuishi maisha ya utulivu na amani, bila kamwe kumkabili mwenye dhambi, kumrekebisha ndugu, au kukanyaga hata kidogo eneo la Shetani; lakini ni nani aliyesema itakuwa rahisi? Hapa Haiti sisi, kama kanisa, tunajaribu kumfuata Yesu bila kujali gharama yake. Jana tu, washiriki wawili walituambia kwamba wako karibu kupoteza kazi zao kwa sababu ya Injili. Dada mwingine kanisani aliripoti kwamba shule wanayosoma watoto wake inahitaji sare na kwamba wasichana lazima wavae suruali. Alimpeleka binti yake shuleni akiwa amevaa gauni la heshima, lakini alirudishwa nyumbani akiwa na ujumbe kutoka kwa mkuu wa shule ukisema asirudi shuleni akiwa amevaa “kile kitu.” Mkitukanwa kwa ajili ya jina la Kristo, heri yenu; kwa sababu Roho wa utukufu na wa Mungu anawakalia; kwa upande wao anatukanwa, lakini kwa upande wenu hutukuzwa. –1Pet 4:14

Furaha hutokana na kuteseka kwa ajili ya haki. Mateso ya kibiblia hutokana na kumtii Yesu unapokabiliwa na upinzani. Je, tuko bize mno kubishana kuhusu maoni binafsi ya mafundisho na kujaribu kuwa sahihi kisiasa, huku ulimwengu ukitukejeli na kwenda jehanamu? Tuwe kama Yesu na Wakristo waaminifu katika vizazi vyote, tukiishi kwa namna ambayo walio karibu nasi hawawezi kukana kwamba nguvu za Mungu ziko ndani yetu. Tuna kitu ambacho kila mtu anahitaji. Basi, tunangoja nini? Tujumuike tena, tukusanyike pamoja, tujinyime, tuchukue misalaba yetu na kumfuata yeye!

As a man was dying, his thoughts went back.
Will I leave a good mark, that none can attack?
I forsook all, on the alter I went
Keeping nothing back, not even a cent.
I wanted to do, all that was right.
I sometimes prayed, all through the night.
It was easy? I cannot say.
But rather a battle, I fought everyday.
Few understood why I lived this way.
Giving up everything was foolish they’d say.
They couldn’t have seen the peace inside.
A peace that I thought, no one could hide.
A life on the run, was not my desire.
But they wanted my body, to put in the fire.
From cave to cave, I would call home
Knowing one day, I’d never more roam.
As I look back, I wouldn’t change a thing.
It has been a great honor serving my king.
But I must go now, the smoke is too thick.
My body to ashes, as the flames lick.
There is one thing, I need to ask.
Will I die in vain, or will you take up the task?
Jesus is looking for A people today
That will stand the test, and not go astray.
Giving our life is part of the cost.
Will you make that decision, before time is lost?
The church is struggling, the world has come in.
They killed our Jesus, and love their sin.
Let’s not give in, there’s too much at stake.

Alors qu’un homme se mourait, ses pensées remontèrent le temps.
Laisserai-je une bonne trace, que nul ne pourra attaquer ?
J’ai tout abandonné, je suis allé à l’autel,
Sans rien retenir, pas même un centime.
Je voulais faire tout ce qui était juste.
Parfois, je priais toute la nuit.
Était-ce facile ? Je ne saurais le dire.
Mais c’était plutôt un combat, que je menais chaque jour.
Peu comprenaient pourquoi je vivais ainsi.
« Tout abandonner, c’est insensé », disaient-ils.
Ils n’auraient pas pu voir la paix qui m’habitait.
Une paix que je croyais impossible à cacher.
Une vie de fugitif, ce n’était pas mon désir.
Mais ils voulaient mon corps pour le jeter au feu.
De grotte en grotte, je me faisais un foyer,
Sachant qu’un jour, je n’errerais plus jamais.
En regardant en arrière, je ne changerais rien.
Ce fut un grand honneur de servir mon roi.
Mais je dois partir maintenant, la fumée est trop épaisse.
Mon corps réduit en cendres, tandis que les flammes le lèchent.
Il y a une chose que je dois demander.
Vais-je mourir en vain, ou reprendras-tu le flambeau ?
Jésus cherche aujourd’hui un peuple
Qui résistera à l’épreuve sans s’égarer.
Donner notre vie fait partie du prix à payer.
Prendras-tu cette décision avant qu’il ne soit trop tard ?
L’Église est en difficulté, le monde y a pénétré.
Ils ont tué notre Jésus et aiment leur péché.
Ne cédons pas, l’enjeu est trop important.
Mais combattons plutôt ! Un royaume est à conquérir !

–Barry Grant

I am Ted. I was born a male and I know I am a male. My skin color is white, and I know I am white. My parents are white, my grandparents were white, and I have no reason to suspect my other ancestors were anything other than white. These are foundational, irrefutable truths about myself. I do not think I am anything other than what I am. Nor do I desire to be anything other than what I am.

I am a Christian. In order to better define my faith—as there are many who profess Christianity—I am a “biblical” Christian. I believe that the Bible is the Word of God, that it is to be taken literally, and that it instructs a pattern and way of life that all believers should embrace. At the age of 24—after having lived a life of my own choosing and while searching for God who, if He was real, I wanted to know—I turned to Him and I was born again. My transformation as a new creation in Christ began immediately and it continues to this day. My faith in and relationship to Jesus Christ are as foundational and irrefutable as my gender and race.

I am writing in response to that which had been extensively covered by the secular media during the Spring and Summer of 2015: a man who reportedly, throughout his life, had considered himself a female and who had been “transitioning” into a woman; a white woman who had insisted that race is “fluid” and that she is black; and the redefinition of marriage by the Supreme Court of the United States of America affecting, as well, the definition of “family” for an entire nation. These are topics which simply cannot be minimized or otherwise ignored.

The white woman lacked much public support for her explanation of race. In fact, she was significantly ridiculed for her stance. This was not true, however, regarding gender identification or “gay” marriage and family issues, and one must wonder why. If a “genetically/physiologically-constructed” male can be accepted by others as a woman simply because that’s what he thinks he is, and if a man can “marry” a man and a woman can “marry” a woman and be accepted as a married couple by others under the premise of equal rights and because that’s what they want to do, why can’t a white woman be accepted as a black woman when she is convinced that she is black?

The question raised is one of reality. Even though I may think I am the greatest pianist and music composer of all times, the evidence simply does not support that conviction. Even though a white woman says she is black, the evidence likewise does not support that conviction. Also true is that of a man who says he is a woman. The genetic and physiological evidence does not support that conviction. Without the redefinition of marriage, two people of the same sex cannot be married. And regardless of definition, they cannot reproduce on their own, one of God’s primary purposes for marriage.

Without God, man does what is right in his own eyes. So-called “progressive thinking” is simply man’s attempt, given his rejection of God, at better understanding the world and better addressing and solving its problems. Essentially, “anything goes” based upon the latest of ideas.

A biblical Christian, however, believes that God has designed, has created, and is very much involved in the universe … even in the individual lives of people who live in it. There are absolutes. There is a distinction between right and wrong. There are moral values and—something that we frequently forget in these modern times—there is an eternity ahead. As a result of progressive thinking, Darwinism now replaces Creationism, within much of our education system, students as well as teachers who profess faith in the God of the Bible are ridiculed and are otherwise discriminated against, millions of pre-born babies (the politically correct prefer calling them “fetuses”) have been legally dismembered, burnt, crushed, suctioned and pharmacologically murdered (aborted), and no-fault divorce has ravaged the families of our nation. Just look at those things that used to be considered wrong or evil which are now a normal part of our “progressing” society.

And what about eternity? Doesn’t that matter anymore, either?

In response to the Supreme Court’s ruling on gay marriage, then-President Barack Obama, clearly one of our nation’s more powerful, progressive thinkers, indicated his desire that “religious people” respond accordingly by modifying their definition of marriage as well. Believing in the God of the Bible as the Creator of the universe and as the One who designed and ordained marriage as a life-long covenant between one man and one woman, I respectfully decline Mr. Obama’s request. As the world in its own fashion deviates from the design and will of God, a true believer in Christ is called to follow Him. Jesus said, Enter through the narrow gate. For wide is the gate and broad is the road that leads to destruction, and many enter through it. But small is the gate and narrow the road that leads to life, and only a few find it. –Mat 7:13-14 NIV

I am Ted. I am a white male. I am a Christian who desires not to belittle, mock, or otherwise mistreat those with whom I may disagree, but there will be disagreements. I am called to love God and to love my neighbor as myself, regardless of who my neighbor might be. My ultimate hope is not found in this world. It is found in eternity with Christ. And my prayer for others is that they, too, may come to know Him, receive forgiveness of their sins, be transformed into the people God so desires, and spend an eternity with Him. This is not a popular message found in today’s liberal media. But for those who are interested, for those who are seeking something much better than what this world has to offer, God has an answer: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. –Joh 3:16

Jag heter Ted. Jag föddes som man och vet att jag är man. Min hudfärg är vit, och jag vet att jag är vit. Mina föräldrar är vita, mina mor- och farföräldrar var vita, och jag har ingen anledning att misstänka att mina övriga förfäder var något annat än vita. Detta är grundläggande, obestridliga sanningar om mig själv. Jag tror inte att jag är något annat än det jag är. Inte heller önskar jag vara något annat än det jag är.

Jag är kristen. För att bättre definiera min tro – eftersom det finns många som bekänner sig till kristendomen – är jag en ”biblisk” kristen. Jag tror att Bibeln är Guds ord, att den ska tas bokstavligt och att den föreskriver ett levnadsmönster och ett sätt att leva som alla troende bör omfatta. När jag var 24 år – efter att ha levt ett liv efter eget val och medan jag sökte Gud, som jag ville lära känna om han var verklig – vände jag mig till honom och blev född på nytt. Min förvandling till en ny skapelse i Kristus började omedelbart och fortsätter än i dag. Min tro på Jesus Kristus och min relation till honom är lika grundläggande och obestridliga som mitt kön och min ras.

Jag skriver som svar på det som hade rapporterats utförligt i sekulära medier under våren och sommaren 2015: en man som enligt uppgift under hela sitt liv hade betraktat sig själv som kvinna och som hade ”övergått” till att bli kvinna; en vit kvinna som hade hävdat att ras är ”flytande” och att hon är svart; och USA:s högsta domstols omdefinition av äktenskapet, som också påverkar definitionen av ”familj” för en hel nation. Detta är ämnen som helt enkelt inte kan förringas eller på annat sätt ignoreras.

Den vita kvinnan fick föga offentligt stöd för sin förklaring av ras. Faktum är att hon blev utsatt för betydande hån för sin ståndpunkt. Detta gällde däremot inte frågor om könsidentitet eller ”gayäktenskap” och familj, och man måste fråga sig varför. Om en ”genetiskt/fysiologiskt konstruerad” man kan accepteras av andra som kvinna bara för att det är vad han anser sig vara, och om en man kan ”gifta sig” med en man och en kvinna kan ”gifta sig” med en kvinna och av andra accepteras som ett gift par med hänvisning till lika rättigheter och för att det är vad de vill göra, varför kan då inte en vit kvinna accepteras som svart när hon är övertygad om att hon är svart?

Frågan som väcks handlar om verklighet. Även om jag skulle tro att jag är tidernas främste pianist och musikkompositör, stöder bevisen helt enkelt inte den övertygelsen. Även om en vit kvinna säger att hon är svart, stöder bevisen inte heller den övertygelsen. Detsamma gäller en man som säger att han är kvinna. De genetiska och fysiologiska bevisen stöder inte den övertygelsen. Utan omdefinitionen av äktenskapet kan två personer av samma kön inte vara gifta. Och oavsett definition kan de inte fortplanta sig på egen hand, vilket är ett av Guds främsta syften med äktenskapet.

Utan Gud gör människan det som är rätt i hennes egna ögon. Så kallat ”progressivt tänkande” är helt enkelt människans försök, till följd av sitt förkastande av Gud, att bättre förstå världen och bättre ta itu med och lösa dess problem. I grund och botten innebär det att ”allt är tillåtet”, utifrån de senaste idéerna.

En biblisk kristen tror däremot att Gud har utformat och skapat universum och är i högsta grad verksam i det … till och med i enskilda människors liv. Det finns absoluta sanningar. Det finns en skillnad mellan rätt och fel. Det finns moraliska värderingar och – något som vi ofta glömmer i modern tid – en evighet som väntar. Som en följd av progressivt tänkande har darwinismen nu ersatt kreationismen. Inom stora delar av vårt utbildningssystem blir elever såväl som lärare som bekänner sin tro på Bibelns Gud hånade och på annat sätt diskriminerade. Miljontals ofödda barn (de politiskt korrekta föredrar att kalla dem ”foster”) har lagligen stympats, bränts, krossats, utsugits och dödats farmakologiskt (aborterats), och skilsmässa utan krav på att någon part ska ha gjort sig skyldig till något har ödelagt vårt lands familjer. Se bara på sådant som tidigare ansågs vara fel eller ont men som nu är en normal del av vårt ”framåtskridande” samhälle.

Och hur är det med evigheten? Spelar den inte längre någon roll heller?

Som svar på högsta domstolens dom om samkönade äktenskap uttryckte dåvarande president Barack Obama, tydligt en av vår nations mäktigare progressiva tänkare, sin önskan att ”religiösa människor” skulle reagera därefter genom att också ändra sin definition av äktenskapet. Eftersom jag tror på Bibelns Gud som universums skapare och som den som utformade och instiftade äktenskapet som ett livslångt förbund mellan en man och en kvinna, avböjer jag respektfullt Obamas begäran. När världen på sitt eget sätt avviker från Guds plan och vilja, är den som verkligen tror på Kristus kallad att följa honom. Jesus sade: Gå in genom den trånga porten. Ty vid är den port och bred är den väg som leder till fördärvet, och många går in genom den. Men trång är den port och smal är den väg som leder till livet, och få är de som finner den. – Matt 7:13–14 NIV

Jag heter Ted. Jag är en vit man. Jag är kristen och vill inte förringa, håna eller på annat sätt behandla dem illa som jag kanske inte håller med, men meningsskiljaktigheter kommer att finnas. Jag är kallad att älska Gud och att älska min nästa som mig själv, oavsett vem min nästa är. Mitt yttersta hopp finns inte i den här världen. Det finns i evigheten med Kristus. Och min bön för andra är att också de ska lära känna honom, få förlåtelse för sina synder, förvandlas till de människor Gud så gärna vill att de ska vara och tillbringa en evighet med honom. Detta är inte ett populärt budskap i dagens liberala medier. Men för dem som är intresserade, för dem som söker något mycket bättre än vad den här världen har att erbjuda, har Gud ett svar: Ty så älskade Gud världen att han utgav sin enfödde Son, för att var och en som tror på honom inte ska gå förlorad utan ha evigt liv. – Joh 3:16

As a man was dying, his thoughts went back.
Will I leave a good mark, that none can attack?
I forsook all, on the alter I went
Keeping nothing back, not even a cent.
I wanted to do, all that was right.
I sometimes prayed, all through the night.
It was easy? I cannot say.
But rather a battle, I fought everyday.
Few understood why I lived this way.
Giving up everything was foolish they’d say.
They couldn’t have seen the peace inside.
A peace that I thought, no one could hide.
A life on the run, was not my desire.
But they wanted my body, to put in the fire.
From cave to cave, I would call home
Knowing one day, I’d never more roam.
As I look back, I wouldn’t change a thing.
It has been a great honor serving my king.
But I must go now, the smoke is too thick.
My body to ashes, as the flames lick.
There is one thing, I need to ask.
Will I die in vain, or will you take up the task?
Jesus is looking for A people today
That will stand the test, and not go astray.
Giving our life is part of the cost.
Will you make that decision, before time is lost?
The church is struggling, the world has come in.
They killed our Jesus, and love their sin.
Let’s not give in, there’s too much at stake.
But rather let’s fight! There’s a kingdom to take!

–Barry Grant

I am Ted. I was born a male and I know I am a male. My skin color is white, and I know I am white. My parents are white, my grandparents were white, and I have no reason to suspect my other ancestors were anything other than white. These are foundational, irrefutable truths about myself. I do not think I am anything other than what I am. Nor do I desire to be anything other than what I am.

I am a Christian. In order to better define my faith—as there are many who profess Christianity—I am a “biblical” Christian. I believe that the Bible is the Word of God, that it is to be taken literally, and that it instructs a pattern and way of life that all believers should embrace. At the age of 24—after having lived a life of my own choosing and while searching for God who, if He was real, I wanted to know—I turned to Him and I was born again. My transformation as a new creation in Christ began immediately and it continues to this day. My faith in and relationship to Jesus Christ are as foundational and irrefutable as my gender and race.

I am writing in response to that which had been extensively covered by the secular media during the Spring and Summer of 2015: a man who reportedly, throughout his life, had considered himself a female and who had been “transitioning” into a woman; a white woman who had insisted that race is “fluid” and that she is black; and the redefinition of marriage by the Supreme Court of the United States of America affecting, as well, the definition of “family” for an entire nation. These are topics which simply cannot be minimized or otherwise ignored.

The white woman lacked much public support for her explanation of race. In fact, she was significantly ridiculed for her stance. This was not true, however, regarding gender identification or “gay” marriage and family issues, and one must wonder why. If a “genetically/physiologically-constructed” male can be accepted by others as a woman simply because that’s what he thinks he is, and if a man can “marry” a man and a woman can “marry” a woman and be accepted as a married couple by others under the premise of equal rights and because that’s what they want to do, why can’t a white woman be accepted as a black woman when she is convinced that she is black?

The question raised is one of reality. Even though I may think I am the greatest pianist and music composer of all times, the evidence simply does not support that conviction. Even though a white woman says she is black, the evidence likewise does not support that conviction. Also true is that of a man who says he is a woman. The genetic and physiological evidence does not support that conviction. Without the redefinition of marriage, two people of the same sex cannot be married. And regardless of definition, they cannot reproduce on their own, one of God’s primary purposes for marriage.

Without God, man does what is right in his own eyes. So-called “progressive thinking” is simply man’s attempt, given his rejection of God, at better understanding the world and better addressing and solving its problems. Essentially, “anything goes” based upon the latest of ideas.

A biblical Christian, however, believes that God has designed, has created, and is very much involved in the universe … even in the individual lives of people who live in it. There are absolutes. There is a distinction between right and wrong. There are moral values and—something that we frequently forget in these modern times—there is an eternity ahead. As a result of progressive thinking, Darwinism now replaces Creationism, within much of our education system, students as well as teachers who profess faith in the God of the Bible are ridiculed and are otherwise discriminated against, millions of pre-born babies (the politically correct prefer calling them “fetuses”) have been legally dismembered, burnt, crushed, suctioned and pharmacologically murdered (aborted), and no-fault divorce has ravaged the families of our nation. Just look at those things that used to be considered wrong or evil which are now a normal part of our “progressing” society.

And what about eternity? Doesn’t that matter anymore, either?

In response to the Supreme Court’s ruling on gay marriage, then-President Barack Obama, clearly one of our nation’s more powerful, progressive thinkers, indicated his desire that “religious people” respond accordingly by modifying their definition of marriage as well. Believing in the God of the Bible as the Creator of the universe and as the One who designed and ordained marriage as a life-long covenant between one man and one woman, I respectfully decline Mr. Obama’s request. As the world in its own fashion deviates from the design and will of God, a true believer in Christ is called to follow Him. Jesus said, Enter through the narrow gate. For wide is the gate and broad is the road that leads to destruction, and many enter through it. But small is the gate and narrow the road that leads to life, and only a few find it. –Mat 7:13-14 NIV

I am Ted. I am a white male. I am a Christian who desires not to belittle, mock, or otherwise mistreat those with whom I may disagree, but there will be disagreements. I am called to love God and to love my neighbor as myself, regardless of who my neighbor might be. My ultimate hope is not found in this world. It is found in eternity with Christ. And my prayer for others is that they, too, may come to know Him, receive forgiveness of their sins, be transformed into the people God so desires, and spend an eternity with Him. This is not a popular message found in today’s liberal media. But for those who are interested, for those who are seeking something much better than what this world has to offer, God has an answer: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. –Joh 3:16

Sono Ted. Sono nato maschio e so di essere maschio. Il colore della mia pelle è bianco e so di essere bianco. I miei genitori sono bianchi, i miei nonni erano bianchi e non ho motivo di sospettare che i miei altri antenati fossero diversi dal bianco. Queste sono verità fondamentali e inconfutabili su di me. Non penso di essere altro da ciò che sono. Né desidero essere altro da ciò che sono.

Sono cristiano. Per definire meglio la mia fede — dato che sono in molti a professare il cristianesimo — sono un cristiano «biblico». Credo che la Bibbia sia la Parola di Dio, che debba essere presa alla lettera e che indichi un modello e uno stile di vita che tutti i credenti dovrebbero abbracciare. All’età di 24 anni — dopo aver vissuto una vita a modo mio e mentre cercavo Dio, che, se fosse stato reale, desideravo conoscere — mi sono rivolto a Lui e sono nato di nuovo. La mia trasformazione in una nuova creatura in Cristo è iniziata subito e continua ancora oggi. La mia fede in Gesù Cristo e il mio rapporto con Lui sono fondamentali e inconfutabili quanto il mio genere e la mia razza.

Scrivo in risposta a quanto era stato ampiamente trattato dai media laici nella primavera e nell’estate del 2015: un uomo che, a quanto riferito, per tutta la vita si era considerato una donna e che stava «transitando» verso una donna; una donna bianca che aveva insistito sul fatto che la razza è «fluida» e che lei è nera; e la ridefinizione del matrimonio da parte della Corte Suprema degli Stati Uniti d’America, che ha inciso anche sulla definizione di «famiglia» per un’intera nazione. Sono argomenti che semplicemente non possono essere minimizzati o ignorati in altro modo.

La donna bianca non ha ricevuto molto sostegno pubblico per la sua spiegazione della razza. Anzi, la sua posizione è stata oggetto di notevole derisione. Questo, tuttavia, non è accaduto per quanto riguarda l’identificazione di genere o le questioni del matrimonio «gay» e della famiglia, e ci si deve chiedere perché. Se un maschio «costituito geneticamente/fisiologicamente» può essere accettato dagli altri come donna semplicemente perché è ciò che pensa di essere, e se un uomo può «sposare» un uomo e una donna può «sposare» una donna ed essere accettati dagli altri come coppia sposata sulla base dei pari diritti e perché è ciò che vogliono fare, perché una donna bianca non può essere accettata come donna nera quando è convinta di esserlo?

La questione sollevata riguarda la realtà. Anche se potessi pensare di essere il più grande pianista e compositore musicale di tutti i tempi, le prove semplicemente non sostengono tale convinzione. Anche se una donna bianca dice di essere nera, le prove non sostengono nemmeno tale convinzione. Lo stesso vale per un uomo che dice di essere una donna. Le prove genetiche e fisiologiche non sostengono tale convinzione. Senza la ridefinizione del matrimonio, due persone dello stesso sesso non possono essere sposate. E, a prescindere dalla definizione, non possono procreare da sole, uno degli scopi principali che Dio ha per il matrimonio.

Senza Dio, l’uomo fa ciò che è giusto ai suoi occhi. Il cosiddetto «pensiero progressista» è semplicemente il tentativo dell’uomo, dato il suo rifiuto di Dio, di comprendere meglio il mondo e di affrontarne e risolverne meglio i problemi. In sostanza, «tutto è lecito», sulla base delle idee più recenti.

Un cristiano biblico, invece, crede che Dio abbia progettato e creato l’universo e che sia profondamente coinvolto in esso… persino nelle vite dei singoli che vi abitano. Esistono verità assolute. C’è una distinzione tra giusto e sbagliato. Esistono valori morali e — qualcosa che spesso dimentichiamo in questi tempi moderni — ci attende l’eternità. Come risultato del pensiero progressista, il darwinismo ha ormai sostituito il creazionismo; in gran parte del nostro sistema educativo, studenti e insegnanti che professano fede nel Dio della Bibbia vengono derisi e altrimenti discriminati; milioni di bambini non ancora nati (chi vuole essere politicamente corretto preferisce chiamarli «feti») sono stati legalmente smembrati, bruciati, schiacciati, aspirati e uccisi farmacologicamente (abortiti); e il divorzio senza colpa ha devastato le famiglie della nostra nazione. Basta guardare a quelle cose che un tempo erano considerate sbagliate o malvagie e che ora sono una parte normale della nostra società «in progresso».

E l’eternità? Non conta più, nemmeno quella?

In risposta alla sentenza della Corte Suprema sul matrimonio gay, l’allora presidente Barack Obama, chiaramente uno dei pensatori progressisti più influenti della nostra nazione, espresse il desiderio che anche le «persone religiose» rispondessero di conseguenza, modificando la propria definizione di matrimonio. Credendo nel Dio della Bibbia come Creatore dell’universo e come Colui che ha progettato e istituito il matrimonio quale patto per tutta la vita tra un uomo e una donna, declino rispettosamente la richiesta del signor Obama. Mentre il mondo, a modo suo, si allontana dal disegno e dalla volontà di Dio, un vero credente in Cristo è chiamato a seguirLo. Gesù disse: Entrate per la porta stretta. Perché larga è la porta e spaziosa la via che conduce alla perdizione, e molti vi entrano. Ma stretta è la porta e angusta la via che conduce alla vita, e pochi la trovano. –Mt 7:13-14 NIV

Sono Ted. Sono un uomo bianco. Sono un cristiano che desidera non sminuire, deridere o maltrattare in altro modo coloro con cui può essere in disaccordo, ma ci saranno divergenze. Sono chiamato ad amare Dio e ad amare il mio prossimo come me stesso, chiunque sia il mio prossimo. La mia speranza ultima non si trova in questo mondo. Si trova nell’eternità con Cristo. E la mia preghiera per gli altri è che anche loro possano arrivare a conoscerLo, ricevere il perdono dei loro peccati, essere trasformati nelle persone che Dio desidera tanto che siano e trascorrere l’eternità con Lui. Questo non è un messaggio popolare nei media liberali di oggi. Ma per chi è interessato, per chi cerca qualcosa di molto migliore di ciò che questo mondo ha da offrire, Dio ha una risposta: Perché Dio ha tanto amato il mondo da dare il suo Figlio unigenito, affinché chiunque crede in lui non perisca, ma abbia vita eterna. –Gv 3:16

As a man was dying, his thoughts went back.
Will I leave a good mark, that none can attack?
I forsook all, on the alter I went
Keeping nothing back, not even a cent.
I wanted to do, all that was right.
I sometimes prayed, all through the night.
It was easy? I cannot say.
But rather a battle, I fought everyday.
Few understood why I lived this way.
Giving up everything was foolish they’d say.
They couldn’t have seen the peace inside.
A peace that I thought, no one could hide.
A life on the run, was not my desire.
But they wanted my body, to put in the fire.
From cave to cave, I would call home
Knowing one day, I’d never more roam.
As I look back, I wouldn’t change a thing.
It has been a great honor serving my king.
But I must go now, the smoke is too thick.
My body to ashes, as the flames lick.
There is one thing, I need to ask.
Will I die in vain, or will you take up the task?
Jesus is looking for A people today
That will stand the test, and not go astray.
Giving our life is part of the cost.
Will you make that decision, before time is lost?
The church is struggling, the world has come in.
They killed our Jesus, and love their sin.
Let’s not give in, there’s too much at stake.
But rather let’s fight! There’s a kingdom to take!

–Barry Grant

כשאדם עמד למות, מחשבותיו חזרו לאחור.
האם אשאיר אחריי חותם טוב, שאיש לא יוכל לערער עליו?
ויתרתי על הכול, ועל המזבח הנחתי את עצמי,
לא שמרתי דבר לעצמי, אפילו לא אגורה.
רציתי לעשות את כל מה שנכון.
לפעמים התפללתי כל הלילה.
האם זה היה קל? איני יכול לומר.
אך זו הייתה מלחמה, ונלחמתי בה מדי יום.
מעטים הבינו מדוע חייתי כך.
הם אמרו שלוותר על הכול זו שטות.
הם לא יכלו לראות את השלווה שבתוכי.
שלווה שחשבתי שאיש לא יוכל להסתיר.
חיים במנוסה לא היו רצוני.
אך הם רצו את גופי, כדי להשליכו לאש.
ממערה למערה, כך קראתי למקום בית.
בידיעה שיום אחד כבר לא אשוטט עוד.
כשאני מביט לאחור, לא הייתי משנה דבר.
היה זה כבוד גדול לשרת את מלכי.
אבל עכשיו עליי ללכת, העשן סמיך מדי.
גופי יהפוך לאפר, כשהלהבות ילקקו אותו.
יש דבר אחד שעליי לשאול.
האם אמות לשווא, או שתיטלו על עצמכם את המשימה?
ישוע מחפש כיום עם

מסירת חיינו היא חלק מן המחיר.

הכנסייה נאבקת, והעולם נכנס פנימה.

Many of us, in our youth, have fantasized about the ideal marriage. We have envisioned being married to someone who loves us unconditionally and who cheerfully accommodates our every peculiarity. In Ephesians 5:22-33 we find just such a marriage. Here the Apostle Paul compares the husband and wife relationship with that of the intimate relationship between Jesus Christ and His bride, the Church. He transitions so easily from the relationship between husband and wife to that of Christ and His bride that we are left wondering which one his primary focus was. In verse 22, he instructs wives to …submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord. Then in verse 25, he instructs husbands to …love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church….

Paul summarizes this passage by stating that This is a great mystery: but I speak concerning Christ and the church. –Eph 5:32. This striking parallelism leads us to believe that marriage is intended to fully reflect the intense, self-sacrificing relationship that Christ demonstrated in securing a bride for himself. This imagery is so powerful that we can only believe that from the time of creation, God designed marriage to reflect his passionate love for us.

Paul wrote, Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it; –Eph 5:25. As we observe the life of Jesus during his brief stay here on earth, we see nothing but self-sacrifice for the benefit of others. We find not a hint of self-serving. It is this selfless laying down of His life that makes the Gospel so powerfully attractive to so many.

In 2 Cor 5:14, Paul wrote, For the love of Christ constraineth us…. This is the nature of the Gospel. We are compelled by Christ’s great love for us to love him in return. This reciprocal love results in a life of devoted service that we sometimes call obedience. If you as a husband desire to have a wife that delights in devoted service to you, learn to love like Christ loved.

I. Christ loved with a “sacrificial love”

Philippians chapter two is sometimes referred to as the “great kenosis” of Christ. The Greek word kenoo found in verse seven (But made himself of no reputation), means “to pour out”. In coming to earth, Jesus laid aside his position with the Father and entered life on planet earth through a questionable conception (humanly speaking) as the son of a humble, virgin, peasant girl. That is the reputation that he adopted. He chose to identify with fallen humanity although he had every right to claim equality with God.

In the Garden of Gethsemane, Jesus demonstrated “sacrificial love” when he …prayed, saying, O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt. –Mat 26:39. Through His life and sacrificial death, he showed us that intimacy in relationship can only be found by losing ourselves in that relationship. The great bane of our day is self-love and self-absorption. Paul wrote to Timothy …that in the last days perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves… –2Ti 3:1-2

We see this prophecy being fulfilled with the advent of social networking. While it claims to be a platform where individuals can connect, it actually is a platform for the promotion of self. This obsession with self is “perilous” because it militates against intimacy in relationship and can be fatal in a marriage relationship. Intimacy in marriage is contingent upon two individuals being willing to relinquish their personal identity and assume a new joint identity.

II. Christ loved with a “faithful love”

Now before the feast of the passover, when Jesus knew that his hour was come that he should depart out of this world unto the Father, having loved his own which were in the world, he loved them unto the end. –Joh 13:1. Christ demonstrated faithful love, even in the face of rejection. John wrote that He came unto his own, and his own received him not. –Joh 1:11

Matthew wrote, But all this was done, that the scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled. Then all the disciples forsook him, and fled. –Mat 26:56. It is one thing to love those who love us in return. Jesus said that even the publicans do that much. Jesus demonstrated love to those who hated him, to those who betrayed him, to those who denied him, and he even prayed for those who crucified him. His love was sustained by a covenant commitment. He was …the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world. –Rev 13:8. He allowed nothing to deter him from his eternal purpose.

Our society has lost an understanding of covenant; hence we have so many broken marriages. Even many churches that embrace “covenant theology” in regard to salvation fail to apply those same covenant principles to marriage. Malachi clearly states that marriage is a covenant—…yet is she thy companion, and the wife of thy covenant. –Mal 2:14. Biblical covenant love is a love that is enduring whether or not it is reciprocated.

The most dramatic disclosure of covenant love is found in the Prophets. The message of the prophets is primarily that of a passionate lover “God” calling out to his unfaithful wife “Israel” to return to him—…turn ye, turn ye from your evil ways; for why will ye die, O house of Israel? –Eze 33:11. Isaiah wrote: Seek ye the LORD while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near: Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts: and let him return unto the LORD, and he will have mercy upon him; and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon. –Isa 55:6-7

Although Israel rebelled against the Lord again and again, yet we see God’s love to her as constant and unaltered. God was faithful to his covenant promise even though His bride bowed the knee to pagan altars. It is this quality of faithful covenant love that brought about the coming of a Redeemer. God made a promise in the Garden of Eden—And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel. –Gen 3:15. This promise was fulfilled in Christ some four thousand years later.

On our wedding day we promise to love “till death do us part”. This is a promise made in faith. No one can know on their wedding day what that promise may cost in the span of a lifetime. The cost is irrelevant to the commitment if there is an abiding, enduring love, rooted in the eternal faithfulness of God as our witness.

III. Christ’s love embraced suffering

One characteristic of our self-focused generation is the idea that I should not need to suffer in a relationship. This is a product of our hedonistic, pleasure-seeking society. It finds its way into our Anabaptist culture as we become increasingly affluent and as the lines of separation between us and the world become increasingly obscure. The product of this mind-set is that we have young people going into marriage thinking that “my partner will serve me, and I will be able to live like a prince or a princess.”

Our Anabaptist faith and heritage has been preserved to our day by men and women who understood that a relationship with Christ involves cross-bearing. Stories abound of families who abandoned their homeland and all that they had for the sake of the Gospel.

The concept of embracing suffering in relationship is clearly taught in Peter’s epistle. Peter was writing to a church that was enduring the raging fire of persecution. He was encouraging them to consider Christ’s example of suffering for a cause outside of themselves. Forasmuch then as Christ hath suffered for us in the flesh, arm yourselves likewise with the same mind… –1Pe 4:1. In chapter two, Peter writes: For this is thankworthy, if a man for conscience toward God endure grief, suffering wrongfully. –1Pe 2:19. Several verses later he states: For even hereunto were ye called: because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps: –1Pe 2:21.

After calling us to be willing to emulate Christ’s example of suffering in chapter two, Peter moves into chapter three by saying, Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives; While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear. –1Pe 3:1-2. This suffering for well-doing has been regarded as a high honor with Christians of all ages. Only in recent years has suffering for well-doing been regarded as “abuse”. There are at least three forces are shaping our understanding of suffering in a negative way.

1. A Selfish, Pleasure-Seeking Society

One has already been described above, which is the hedonistic (devotion to pleasure as a way of life) society in which we live.

2. The Health, Wealth, and Prosperity Gospel

A second one is the health, wealth, and prosperity gospel of many evangelical churches. The implication is that if we choose to follow Christ our lives will be overflowing with physical well-being and material abundance. This understanding is based on the promises to ancient Israel in the Old Testament of a land flowing with milk and honey. We believe this promise is fulfilled in the church age with a life that is overflowing with the fruit of the Spirit of love, joy, peace, etc. It is possible for these fruit can to abound in the midst of suffering. In fact, when others observe fruit amid another individual’s suffering, that is when it is the most noticeable and the most appreciated.

3. The Feminist Movement

The third influence that today shapes our perspective on suffering comes from the feminist movement that boldly declares that no woman should suffer or experience privation of any kind in a marriage relationship. Hence, we have a society of women with their own careers, drawing their own salary, and maintaining their own bank account. How very different from the testimony of women of faith like Sarah who …obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement. –1Pe 3:6

Suffering for the benefit of relationship has been initiated by Christ and emulated by thousands of faithful Christians throughout the church age. We are challenged by the words of the Apostle Peter and by the witness of faithful Christians to embrace suffering as a badge of the authenticity of our faith.

IV. Christ loved with a sanctifying love

God’s plan in creating us was that we would be holy as he is holy so we can experience intimate fellowship with him. But mankind rebelled against God, so he promised a redeemer. In the interim he introduced a contingency plan that was intended to prevent mankind from destroying themselves, and that was “the Law”.

However, it was never God’s intent that our relationship with him should be governed by law. He desires a love relationship with us, so he sent his Son to us and overwhelmed us with his love. We now reciprocate his love, not through fear of judgment, but as a love response to his compelling love. This concept is most clearly stated in Romans For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh [limited to what could be accomplished in the flesh], God sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh [satisfied the righteous demands of the law]: That the righteousness of the law [the full and complete fulfillment of the law] might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit. –Rom 8:3-4

Jesus accomplished through love what could never be accomplished through the strict demands of a penal code. He raised the bar on righteousness. For I say unto you, That except your righteousness shall exceed the righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees, ye shall in no case enter into the kingdom of heaven. –Mat 5:20. He showed us how to live and how to love. His sacrificial death satisfied the penal demands of the law. Through his resurrection, ascension, and the outpouring of the Holy Spirit he has empowered believers to live and to love as he did.

Paul admonishes us to relate in marriage in this same way: Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it; That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word, That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish. –Eph 5:27. Jesus came to earth to secure a bride for himself. She was not a beautiful, radiant bride that was eagerly awaiting his arrival. She was defaced by sin and living in rebellion against him—He came unto his own, and his own received him not. –Joh 1:11. Through his patient, persistent love he transformed his bride into a glorious radiant bride that stands in awe of him and joyfully worships and adores him.

Does your wife have spots and wrinkles? Are there some attitudes that you wish were different? Or are there fears and insecurities that hinder her freedom and joy? You could demand that she change and berate her for not living up to your expectations. This approach would be comparable to that of the law. It would serve to amplify her limitations and increase her anxieties. Or you could love her in spite of her spots and wrinkles. With words of compassion and encouragement you could motivate her to rise above her fears, just like Christ sanctifies his bride by his word. Jesus demonstrated that love can accomplish what harsh demands never can. Paul taught that this is a fundamental principle of marriage. It is intended to be a relationship in which the compelling force is love.

V. The great mystery

Paul concluded his treatise on marriage by saying: This is a great mystery: but I speak concerning Christ and the church. –Eph 5:32. A mystery in Biblical language in not something that cannot be comprehended, but rather something that can only be understood by those who by faith receive and embrace the Truth. It is revealed to sincere Christians; it is veiled to others.

As believers in Jesus we are privileged to understand a perspective of marriage that many cannot begin to comprehend: that sacrificial love opens the door to intimacy, that covenant love is the key to life-long fulfillment, that our willingness to suffer for the relationship proves the authenticity of our love, and finally, that the most effective way to expedite change in our spouse is unconditional love.

These principles are time-proven and Biblically-based. They are foundational to the Gospel and are a fundamental part of our Anabaptist kingdom-based theology. Where faithfully applied they will transform any marriage.

Muchos de nosotros, en nuestra juventud, hemos fantaseado con el matrimonio ideal. Nos hemos imaginado casados con alguien que nos ama incondicionalmente y que acepta con alegría todas nuestras peculiaridades. En Efesios 5:22-33 encontramos precisamente un matrimonio así. Aquí el apóstol Pablo compara la relación entre esposo y esposa con la relación íntima entre Jesucristo y su novia, la Iglesia. Pasa con tanta facilidad de la relación entre esposo y esposa a la de Cristo y su novia que nos quedamos preguntándonos cuál era su enfoque principal. En el versículo 22, instruye a las esposas a …sométanse a sus propios esposos, como al Señor. Luego, en el versículo 25, instruye a los esposos a …amen a sus esposas, así como Cristo también amó a la iglesia….

Pablo resume este pasaje diciendo que Este es un gran misterio; pero yo hablo con respecto a Cristo y a la iglesia. –Ef 5:32. Este llamativo paralelismo nos lleva a creer que el matrimonio está destinado a reflejar plenamente la intensa relación de entrega propia que Cristo demostró al asegurar una novia para sí. Esta imagen es tan poderosa que solo podemos creer que, desde el momento de la creación, Dios diseñó el matrimonio para reflejar su amor apasionado por nosotros.

Pablo escribió: Esposos, amen a sus esposas, así como Cristo también amó a la iglesia y se entregó por ella; –Ef 5:25. Al observar la vida de Jesús durante su breve estancia aquí en la tierra, no vemos más que entrega propia en beneficio de los demás. No encontramos ni rastro de egoísmo. Es esta entrega desinteresada de su vida lo que hace que el Evangelio sea tan poderosamente atractivo para tantos.

En 2 Co 5:14, Pablo escribió: Porque el amor de Cristo nos constriñe…. Esta es la naturaleza del Evangelio. El gran amor de Cristo por nosotros nos impulsa a amarlo a cambio. Este amor recíproco da como resultado una vida de servicio devoto, que a veces llamamos obediencia. Si usted, como esposo, desea tener una esposa que se deleite en servirle con devoción, aprenda a amar como Cristo amó.

I. Cristo amó con un «amor sacrificial»

Al capítulo dos de Filipenses a veces se le llama la «gran kenosis» de Cristo. La palabra griega kenoo, que aparece en el versículo siete (se despojó a sí mismo), significa «derramar». Al venir a la tierra, Jesús dejó a un lado su posición junto al Padre y entró en la vida en el planeta Tierra mediante una concepción cuestionable (desde el punto de vista humano), como hijo de una humilde joven campesina y virgen. Esa fue la reputación que adoptó. Eligió identificarse con la humanidad caída, aunque tenía todo el derecho de reclamar igualdad con Dios.

En el huerto de Getsemaní, Jesús demostró «amor sacrificial» cuando …oró, diciendo: Padre mío, si es posible, pase de mí esta copa; pero no sea como yo quiero, sino como tú quieras. –Mt 26:39. Mediante su vida y su muerte sacrificial, nos mostró que la intimidad en una relación solo se encuentra al perderse uno mismo en esa relación. El gran flagelo de nuestros días es el amor propio y la ensimismación. Pablo escribió a Timoteo: …que en los últimos días vendrán tiempos peligrosos. Porque los hombres serán amadores de sí mismos… –2 Ti 3:1-2

Vemos cumplirse esta profecía con la llegada de las redes sociales. Aunque afirman ser una plataforma donde las personas pueden conectarse, en realidad son una plataforma para la promoción de uno mismo. Esta obsesión con uno mismo es «peligrosa» porque atenta contra la intimidad en las relaciones y puede ser fatal en el matrimonio. La intimidad matrimonial depende de que dos personas estén dispuestas a renunciar a su identidad personal y adoptar una nueva identidad compartida.

II. Cristo amó con un «amor fiel»

Antes de la fiesta de la Pascua, cuando Jesús sabía que había llegado su hora de partir de este mundo al Padre, habiendo amado a los suyos que estaban en el mundo, los amó hasta el fin. –Jn 13:1. Cristo demostró un amor fiel, incluso ante el rechazo. Juan escribió que Vino a los suyos, y los suyos no lo recibieron. –Jn 1:11

Mateo escribió: Pero todo esto sucedió para que se cumplieran las Escrituras de los profetas. Entonces todos los discípulos lo abandonaron y huyeron. –Mt 26:56. Una cosa es amar a quienes nos aman a cambio. Jesús dijo que incluso los publicanos hacen eso. Jesús demostró amor a quienes lo odiaban, a quienes lo traicionaron, a quienes lo negaron, e incluso oró por quienes lo crucificaron. Su amor se sostenía en un compromiso de pacto. Él era …el Cordero inmolado desde la fundación del mundo. –Ap 13:8. No permitió que nada lo apartara de su propósito eterno.

Nuestra sociedad ha perdido la comprensión del pacto; de ahí que haya tantos matrimonios rotos. Incluso muchas iglesias que aceptan la «teología del pacto» en cuanto a la salvación no aplican esos mismos principios del pacto al matrimonio. Malaquías afirma claramente que el matrimonio es un pacto: …ella es tu compañera y la esposa de tu pacto. –Mal 2:14. El amor bíblico de pacto es un amor que perdura, sea o no correspondido.

La revelación más dramática del amor de pacto se encuentra en los Profetas. El mensaje de los profetas es principalmente el de un amante apasionado, «Dios», que llama a su esposa infiel, «Israel», para que vuelva a él: …Vuélvanse, vuélvanse de sus malos caminos; pues ¿por qué morirán, casa de Israel? –Ez 33:11. Isaías escribió: Busquen al SEÑOR mientras puede ser hallado; llámenlo en tanto que está cercano. Deje el impío su camino, y el hombre injusto sus pensamientos; y vuélvase al SEÑOR, quien tendrá misericordia de él; y a nuestro Dios, porque él perdonará abundantemente. –Is 55:6-7

Aunque Israel se rebeló contra el Señor una y otra vez, vemos que el amor de Dios por ella permanecía constante e inalterado. Dios fue fiel a su promesa del pacto, aunque su novia se arrodillara ante altares paganos. Fue esta cualidad del amor fiel de pacto la que hizo posible la venida de un Redentor. Dios hizo una promesa en el huerto del Edén: Y pondré enemistad entre ti y la mujer, y entre tu descendencia y la descendencia suya; esta te herirá en la cabeza, y tú la herirás en el talón. –Gn 3:15. Esta promesa se cumplió en Cristo unos cuatro mil años después.

El día de nuestra boda prometemos amarnos «hasta que la muerte nos separe». Esta es una promesa hecha con fe. Nadie puede saber el día de su boda cuánto podría costarle esa promesa a lo largo de una vida. El costo es irrelevante para el compromiso si hay un amor firme y perdurable, arraigado en la fidelidad eterna de Dios como testigo nuestro.

III. El amor de Cristo abrazó el sufrimiento

Una característica de nuestra generación centrada en sí misma es la idea de que no debería tener que sufrir en una relación. Esto es producto de nuestra sociedad hedonista, que busca el placer. Se abre paso en nuestra cultura anabautista a medida que nos volvemos cada vez más prósperos y que las líneas de separación entre nosotros y el mundo se vuelven cada vez más difusas. El resultado de esta mentalidad es que los jóvenes se casan pensando que «mi pareja me servirá y podré vivir como un príncipe o una princesa».

Nuestra fe y herencia anabautistas se han preservado hasta nuestros días gracias a hombres y mujeres que entendieron que una relación con Cristo implica llevar la cruz. Abundan las historias de familias que abandonaron su tierra natal y todo lo que tenían por causa del Evangelio.

El concepto de abrazar el sufrimiento en una relación se enseña claramente en la epístola de Pedro. Pedro escribía a una iglesia que soportaba el fuego abrasador de la persecución. Los animaba a considerar el ejemplo de Cristo, que sufrió por una causa ajena a sí mismo. Puesto que Cristo padeció por nosotros en la carne, ármense también ustedes del mismo pensamiento… –1 P 4:1. En el capítulo dos, Pedro escribe: Porque esto merece aprobación, si alguno por causa de la conciencia delante de Dios soporta agravios padeciendo injustamente. –1 P 2:19. Unos versículos después afirma: Pues para esto fueron llamados, porque también Cristo padeció por nosotros, dejándonos ejemplo, para que sigan sus pasos: –1 P 2:21.

Después de llamarnos en el capítulo dos a estar dispuestos a imitar el ejemplo de sufrimiento de Cristo, Pedro pasa al capítulo tres diciendo: Asimismo ustedes, esposas, sométanse a sus propios esposos, para que, si algunos no obedecen a la palabra, también sean ganados sin palabra por la conducta de sus esposas, al observar su conducta casta y respetuosa. –1 P 3:1-2. Los cristianos de todas las épocas han considerado un gran honor sufrir por hacer el bien. Solo en años recientes se ha considerado «maltrato» sufrir por hacer el bien. Hay al menos tres fuerzas que están moldeando de manera negativa nuestra comprensión del sufrimiento.

1. Una sociedad egoísta y en busca del placer

Una ya se describió anteriormente: la sociedad hedonista (la devoción al placer como forma de vida) en la que vivimos.

2. El evangelio de la salud, la riqueza y la prosperidad

Una segunda fuerza es el evangelio de la salud, la riqueza y la prosperidad de muchas iglesias evangélicas. La implicación es que, si elegimos seguir a Cristo, nuestras vidas rebosarán de bienestar físico y abundancia material. Esta comprensión se basa en las promesas hechas al antiguo Israel en el Antiguo Testamento de una tierra que mana leche y miel. Creemos que esta promesa se cumple en la era de la iglesia con una vida que rebosa del fruto del Espíritu: amor, gozo, paz, etc. Es posible que estos frutos abunden en medio del sufrimiento. De hecho, cuando otros observan fruto en medio del sufrimiento de otra persona, es cuando más se nota y más se aprecia.

3. El movimiento feminista

La tercera influencia que hoy moldea nuestra perspectiva sobre el sufrimiento proviene del movimiento feminista, que declara audazmente que ninguna mujer debería sufrir ni experimentar privaciones de ningún tipo en el matrimonio. Por eso tenemos una sociedad de mujeres con sus propias carreras, que cobran su propio sueldo y mantienen su propia cuenta bancaria. ¡Qué diferente es esto del testimonio de mujeres de fe como Sara, quien …obedeció a Abraham, llamándolo señor; de ella ustedes son hijas, si hacen el bien y no tienen miedo de ninguna amenaza. –1 P 3:6

Cristo inició el sufrimiento en beneficio de una relación, y miles de cristianos fieles lo han imitado a lo largo de la era de la iglesia. Las palabras del apóstol Pedro y el testimonio de cristianos fieles nos desafían a abrazar el sufrimiento como insignia de la autenticidad de nuestra fe.

IV. Cristo amó con un amor santificador

El plan de Dios al crearnos era que fuéramos santos como él es santo, para que pudiéramos experimentar una comunión íntima con él. Pero la humanidad se rebeló contra Dios, así que él prometió un redentor. Mientras tanto, introdujo un plan alternativo destinado a impedir que la humanidad se destruyera a sí misma: «la Ley».

Sin embargo, nunca fue la intención de Dios que nuestra relación con él se rigiera por la ley. Él desea una relación de amor con nosotros, así que nos envió a su Hijo y nos colmó con su amor. Ahora correspondemos a su amor, no por temor al juicio, sino como respuesta amorosa a su amor que nos impulsa. Este concepto se expresa con mayor claridad en Romanos: Porque lo que la ley no podía hacer, por cuanto era débil por la carne [limitada a lo que podía lograrse en la carne], Dios, enviando a su propio Hijo en semejanza de carne de pecado, y por el pecado, condenó al pecado en la carne [satisfizo las justas exigencias de la ley], para que la justicia de la ley [el cumplimiento pleno y completo de la ley] se cumpliera en nosotros, que no andamos conforme a la carne, sino conforme al Espíritu. –Ro 8:3-4

Jesús logró mediante el amor lo que jamás podría lograrse mediante las estrictas exigencias de un código penal. Elevó el estándar de justicia. Porque les digo que, si su justicia no supera la de los escribas y fariseos, de ninguna manera entrarán en el reino de los cielos. –Mt 5:20. Nos mostró cómo vivir y cómo amar. Su muerte sacrificial satisfizo las exigencias penales de la ley. Mediante su resurrección, ascensión y el derramamiento del Espíritu Santo, ha capacitado a los creyentes para vivir y amar como él lo hizo.

Pablo nos exhorta a relacionarnos de esta misma manera en el matrimonio: Esposos, amen a sus esposas, así como Cristo también amó a la iglesia y se entregó por ella, para santificarla y limpiarla con el lavamiento del agua por la palabra, a fin de presentársela a sí mismo como una iglesia gloriosa, que no tuviese mancha ni arruga ni cosa semejante, sino que fuese santa y sin defecto. –Ef 5:27. Jesús vino a la tierra para asegurar una novia para sí. Ella no era una novia hermosa y radiante que esperaba con ansias su llegada. Estaba desfigurada por el pecado y vivía en rebelión contra él: Vino a los suyos, y los suyos no lo recibieron. –Jn 1:11. Mediante su amor paciente y persistente, transformó a su novia en una novia gloriosa y radiante que lo contempla con reverencia y lo adora y venera con alegría.

¿Tiene manchas y arrugas su esposa? ¿Hay algunas actitudes que desearía que fueran diferentes? ¿O hay temores e inseguridades que limitan su libertad y alegría? Usted podría exigir que cambie y reprenderla por no estar a la altura de sus expectativas. Este enfoque sería comparable al de la ley. Serviría para acentuar sus limitaciones y aumentar sus ansiedades. O podría amarla a pesar de sus manchas y arrugas. Con palabras de compasión y ánimo, podría motivarla a superar sus temores, así como Cristo santifica a su novia mediante su palabra. Jesús demostró que el amor puede lograr lo que las exigencias severas nunca podrán. Pablo enseñó que este es un principio fundamental del matrimonio. Está destinado a ser una relación en la que la fuerza que impulsa sea el amor.

V. El gran misterio

Pablo concluyó su tratado sobre el matrimonio diciendo: Este es un gran misterio; pero yo hablo con respecto a Cristo y a la iglesia. –Ef 5:32. En el lenguaje bíblico, un misterio no es algo que no pueda comprenderse, sino algo que solo pueden entender quienes reciben y abrazan la Verdad por fe. Se revela a los cristianos sinceros; permanece velado para los demás.

Como creyentes en Jesús, tenemos el privilegio de comprender una perspectiva del matrimonio que muchos ni siquiera pueden empezar a comprender: que el amor sacrificial abre la puerta a la intimidad; que el amor de pacto es la clave para una plenitud duradera; que nuestra disposición a sufrir por la relación demuestra la autenticidad de nuestro amor; y, finalmente, que la manera más eficaz de acelerar el cambio en nuestro cónyuge es el amor incondicional.

Estos principios han sido probados por el tiempo y se basan en la Biblia. Son fundamentales para el Evangelio y forman parte esencial de nuestra teología anabautista basada en el reino. Cuando se aplican fielmente, transformarán cualquier matrimonio.
